recipes.caption:
Fish Kobiraji- Big Bengali Feast S2 Ep 1 

Recipe ➡️

Fish Fry:
Bhetki fillets – 600 g (6–7 pieces); 1 medium onion; 1 handful coriander bunch with roots; ½ handful of parsley bunch, 3–4 green chillies; 1-inch ginger; 5–6 garlic cloves; ⅓ rd tsp Bengali garam masala; ¼ tsp MSG; ⅓ tsp sugar; ½ tsp black pepper; 1 tsp lime juice; 1 egg; 2½ tbsp flour; breadcrumbs; salt; eggs for egg wash.

Blend onion, ginger, garlic, coriander, parsley, green chillies, salt, MSG, garam masala and lime juice into a smooth paste. Marinate fish and refrigerate 3–4 hours. Add egg, flour, salt and pepper; mix and refrigerate another 15–20 mins. Dip once in egg wash and once in breadcrumbs, using one dry hand for breadcrumbs and one wet hand for egg wash. Fry on medium-high heat until golden.

Note: if you are using panko, crush them first. 

Egg Coverage:
2 eggs; 3 tbsp all purpose flour; 1 tbsp cornflour; 1 tsp chilli flakes; ⅓ tsp black pepper; salt; pinch of carom seeds; coriander leaves; vegetable oil; 2–3 eggs for dipping.

Beat 1 egg with maida and cornflour. Add 3 more eggs, chilli flakes, salt and pepper; whisk and rest 20–30 mins—don’t skip. 

Separately beat 2–3 eggs with salt and pepper. This is used for dipping the fries. 

Heat a large pan on low-medium. Dip fingertips in the coverage batter and move to and fro over the oil to create a web. It needn’t be perfect. 

Sprinkle coriander and carom seeds over it. Dip the fish fry in egg wash, place on the web and fold it over the fish. 

Fry until golden and crisp. Drain on tissue paper and serve with kashundi.

Recipe Inspiration: @bongeats Eats 

#Fishkobiraji #kolkata #Durgapujo2026 #BigBengaliFeast BurpingBengalis

Bhetki fillets – 600 g (6–7 pieces)
1 medium onion
1 handful coriander bunch with roots
½ handful of parsley bunch
3–4 green chillies
1-inch ginger
5–6 garlic cloves
⅓ tsp Bengali garam masala
¼ tsp MSG
⅓ tsp sugar
½ tsp black pepper
1 tsp lime juice
1 egg
2½ tbsp flour
breadcrumbs
salt
eggs for egg wash
2 eggs
3 tbsp all purpose flour
1 tbsp cornflour
1 tsp chilli flakes
⅓ tsp black pepper
salt
pinch of carom seeds
coriander leaves
vegetable oil
2–3 eggs for dipping
recipes.recipe_method:
Blend onion, ginger, garlic, coriander, parsley, green chillies, salt, MSG, garam masala and lime juice into a smooth paste.
Marinate fish and refrigerate 3–4 hours.
Add egg, flour, salt and pepper; mix and refrigerate another 15–20 mins.
Dip once in egg wash and once in breadcrumbs, using one dry hand for breadcrumbs and one wet hand for egg wash.
Fry on medium-high heat until golden.
Beat 1 egg with maida and cornflour.
Add 3 more eggs, chilli flakes, salt and pepper; whisk and rest 20–30 mins—don’t skip.
Separately beat 2–3 eggs with salt and pepper. This is used for dipping the fries.
Heat a large pan on low-medium.
Dip fingertips in the coverage batter and move to and fro over the oil to create a web.
Sprinkle coriander and carom seeds over it.
Dip the fish fry in egg wash, place on the web and fold it over the fish.
Fry until golden and crisp.
Drain on tissue paper and serve with kashundi.

recipes.recipe_method:

recipes.title: Squash & Hot Honey Rigatoni
recipes.author: rubys.food
recipes.text: easy squash & hot honey rigatoni 💓💓 serves 3 1 large squash (any kind will work) 1 bulb garlic 1 handful sage leaves 3 tsp butter 1 large white onion 300g pasta 200ml cream 2-3 ladles pasta water 1 buratta hot honey & sage to top (i just make my own hot honey from honey, chilli flakes & olive oil) olive oil salt & pepper 1. preheat the oven to 180c (or use an air fryer). chop the squash into slices and cut the top off the garlic, put in a tray with a few leaves of sage and drizzle with olive oil, salt & pepper. roast for 35 mins until soft. 2. meanwhile, chop your onion. melt the butter in a frying pan, then add a couple leaves of sage for 1 min, followed by the onions. cook until soft. 3. cook your pasta, saving at least 2 ladles of pasta water for the sauce (you can adjust depending on how thick you want the sauce). 4. once the sqaush is roasted, remove the skin and add to a blender with the roasted garlic, sage, onions & cream. blend until smooth, season then add the pasta water 1 ladle at a time, blending until glossy. pour the sauce over your pasta and top with buratta, hot honey & crispy sage if you likeee xxx
recipes.caption:
Easy squash & hot honey rigatoni 💓💓

Serves 3
1 large squash (any kind will work)
1 bulb garlic
1 handful sage leaves
3 tsp butter
1 large white onion
300g pasta
200ml cream
2-3 ladles pasta water
1 buratta
Hot honey & sage to top (I just make my own hot honey from honey, chilli flakes & olive oil)
Olive oil
Salt & pepper 

1. Preheat the oven to 180c (or use an air fryer). Chop the squash into slices and cut the top off the garlic, put in a tray with a few leaves of sage and drizzle with olive oil, salt & pepper. Roast for 35 mins until soft.
2. Meanwhile, chop your onion. Melt the butter in a frying pan, then add a couple leaves of sage for 1 min, followed by the onions. Cook until soft.
3. Cook your pasta, saving at least 2 ladles of pasta water for the sauce (you can adjust depending on how thick you want the sauce).
4. Once the sqaush is roasted, remove the skin and add to a blender with the roasted garlic, sage, onions & cream. Blend until smooth, season then add the pasta water 1 ladle at a time, blending until glossy. Pour the sauce over your pasta and top with buratta, hot honey & crispy sage if you likeee xxx
recipes.recipe_ingredients:
1 large squash (any kind will work)
1 bulb garlic
1 handful sage leaves
3 tsp butter
1 large white onion
300g pasta
200ml cream
2-3 ladles pasta water
1 buratta
Hot honey & sage to top
Olive oil
Salt & pepper
recipes.recipe_method:
Preheat the oven to 180c (or use an air fryer).
Chop the squash into slices and cut the top off the garlic, put in a tray with a few leaves of sage and drizzle with olive oil, salt & pepper.
Roast for 35 mins until soft.
Meanwhile, chop your onion.
Melt the butter in a frying pan, then add a couple leaves of sage for 1 min, followed by the onions.
Cook until soft.
Cook your pasta, saving at least 2 ladles of pasta water for the sauce (you can adjust depending on how thick you want the sauce).
Once the sqaush is roasted, remove the skin and add to a blender with the roasted garlic, sage, onions & cream.
Blend until smooth, season then add the pasta water 1 ladle at a time, blending until glossy.
Pour the sauce over your pasta and top with buratta, hot honey & crispy sage if you likeee xxx

recipes.title: High-Protein Upma
recipes.author: deepinsights21
recipes.text: upma… but make it high-protein 💪 the trick: blend cottage cheese smooth and cook your rava in it. same soft, fluffy uppittu — just creamier, richer, and loaded with protein. breakfast just got an upgrade ✨ blend: 1 cup cottage cheese 1/2 cup greek with about 4 cups water, till completely smooth. tempering: heat 2 tbsp oil or ghee — 1 tsp mustard seeds (let them crackle), 1 tsp chana dal, 1 tsp urad dal, curry leaves, 2 chopped green chillies, 1 tsp grated ginger, a pinch of hing. add 1 chopped onion, sauté till soft. pour in the cottage cheese blend + salt, bring to a gentle boil. rain in 1 cup rava slowly, stirring non-stop so no lumps. cover, cook on low 2–3 minutes till soft and fluffy. serve hot, straight off the stove ♨
recipes.caption:
Upma… but make it HIGH-PROTEIN 💪
The trick: blend cottage cheese smooth and cook your rava in it. Same soft, fluffy uppittu — just creamier, richer, and loaded with protein. Breakfast just got an upgrade ✨
Blend: 1 cup cottage cheese 1/2 cup greek@yogurt with about 4 cups water, till completely smooth.
Tempering: heat 2 tbsp oil or ghee — 1 tsp mustard seeds (let them crackle), 1 tsp chana dal, 1 tsp urad dal, curry leaves, 2 chopped green chillies, 1 tsp grated ginger, a pinch of hing. Add 1 chopped onion, sauté till soft.
Pour in the cottage cheese blend + salt, bring to a gentle boil. Rain in 1 cup rava slowly, stirring non-stop so no lumps. Cover, cook on low 2–3 minutes till soft and fluffy.
Serve hot, straight off the stove ♨#Upma #Uppittu #HighProteinBreakfast #CottageCheese
recipes.recipe_ingredients:
1 cup cottage cheese
1/2 cup greek yogurt
4 cups water
2 tbsp oil or ghee
1 tsp mustard seeds
1 tsp chana dal
1 tsp urad dal
curry leaves
2 chopped green chillies
1 tsp grated ginger
pinch of hing
1 chopped onion
salt
1 cup rava
recipes.recipe_method:
Blend: 1 cup cottage cheese 1/2 cup greek yogurt with about 4 cups water, till completely smooth.
Tempering: heat 2 tbsp oil or ghee — 1 tsp mustard seeds (let them crackle), 1 tsp chana dal, 1 tsp urad dal, curry leaves, 2 chopped green chillies, 1 tsp grated ginger, a pinch of hing.
Add 1 chopped onion, sauté till soft.
Pour in the cottage cheese blend + salt, bring to a gentle boil.
Rain in 1 cup rava slowly, stirring non-stop so no lumps.
Cover, cook on low 2–3 minutes till soft and fluffy.
Serve hot, straight off the stove

recipes.caption:
SABUDANA RATALA WAFFLES

My heart beats for sabudana khichadi. It beats really fast for Sabudana Wada. And now it’s doing cartwheels for these Sabudana Sweet Potato Waffles!!!
Also, in my house we eat khichadi with dahi & sugar. 
How do you eat it? I love weird combos!
Pohe with grated cheese & limboo is another 😂
And best is sheera & Bedekar loncha!
You can make these with left over sabudana khichadi + boiled ratala or just soak the sabudana and follow the recipe!!
Off to discuss my Shakti Infradian Rhythm Workshop for @joinedgecity and FYI these waffles are also great for your Luteal Phase because of the complex carb and the easily digested starch from sabudana!
Time to FEED THE GODDESS WITHIN sisters!

SABUDANA SWEET POTATO WAFFLES
Ingredients-
1 cup sabudana, soaked
1 cup sweet potato (boiled & mashed)
1 tsp cumin seeds
1 tsp green chillies (finely chopped)
¼ cup coriander leaves 
1/3 cup peanuts (roasted & crushed)
1 tsp salt or kala namak
1 tsp tup/ghee

Method-

Prep- Soak sabudana in water for 5 hours (soak in water for 30 min, drain and put a plate on top), roast ⅓ cup peanuts and peel them, boil 2 sweet potatoes, peel and mash them. Or use leftover sabudana khichadi.
Mix- Add soaked sabudana, mashed sweet potatoes, cumin seeds, finely chopped green chillies, coriander leaves, peanuts, salt and ghee to a bowl and mix it well.
Add some more ghee if needed to form the mix into balls.
Cook-
Put some tup on the waffle maker and take one of the balls and place it on the waffle maker. Cook the waffles for 7-8 minutes or until lightly golden. And serve with dahi-saakar or any chutney.

recipes.caption:
These are viral for a reason! They are just THAT GOOD 😮‍💨🔥

What You’ll Need:

For the chicken:
	•	1 lb ground chicken
	•	1 tbsp yellow mustard
	•	1 tsp of each: garlic powder, onion powder, chili powder
	•	½ tsp of each: paprika, kosher salt, black pepper
	•	¼ cup buttermilk or milk (for brushing)
	•	8 small flour tortillas (street style)
	•	Neutral oil for frying (about ¼ inch in skillet)

For the crust:
	•	1 cup all-purpose flour
	•	1 tsp aluminum-free baking powder
	•	1 tsp paprika
	•	1 tsp kosher salt
	•	¼–½ tsp cayenne (adjust to heat preference)
	•	½ tsp of each: garlic powder, onion powder, black pepper 

For the oil:
	•	1 tbsp brown sugar
	•	1 tsp cayenne
	•	½ tsp of each: garlic powder, onion powder, chili powder, salt
	•	¼ tsp black pepper
	•	4 tablespoons neutral oil

Instructions:

In a bowl, combine ground chicken, mustard, garlic powder, onion powder, chili powder, paprika, salt, and pepper. Mix until just combined.

In a shallow bowl, whisk together flour, baking powder, paprika, cayenne, garlic powder, onion powder, salt, and pepper.

Drizzle 1–2 tablespoons of milk into the flour mixture. Use your fingers to rub and toss it through the flour to create craggly bits. This is what gives you that textured crunch.

Press a thin, even layer of the chicken mixture onto one side of each tortilla.

Lightly brush the chicken side with milk and firmly press into the seasoned flour mixture.

Heat about ¼ inch of neutral oil in a skillet over medium heat. Place tacos chicken-side down. Press gently and cook 4-5 minutes, until deeply golden and crispy.

Flip and cook 1–2 minutes more, until chicken is fully cooked and tortilla is lightly toasted.
Transfer to a wire rack or paper towel-lined plate.

In another skillet warm up 4 tbsp oil on medium heat for 2-3 minutes. Add in the seasonings for the oil and mix until the sugar dissolves. Remove from heat and brush generously over the crispy chicken side of each taco.

Top each taco with a drizzle of sauce, pickles & kale slaw. Optional: finish with a light drizzle of honey.

recipes.comment_recipe:
CARAMELISED ONION & FIG JAM PUFF PASTRY BITES 🥐✨

Sweet, savoury, cheesy and perfectly flaky! An easy, elegant appetizer for your next gathering. 🤌🏻

INGREDIENTS(Makes 12–16 bites)

* 1 sheet puff pastry, thawed
* 2 medium onions, thinly sliced
* 1 tbsp butter
* 1 tbsp olive oil
* ½ tsp salt, or to taste
* ¼ tsp black pepper
* 100–120 g brie cheese, cut into small pieces
* 3–4 tbsp fig jam
* Fresh chives, finely chopped
* Red chilli flakes, for garnish (grinded)

Method:

1. Prepare the pastry: Preheat oven to 400°F (200°C). Cut puff pastry into squares/ circles using a cookie cutter and lay on a baking tray. Add parchment paper at the bottom. 
2. Bake: Bake for 10–12 minutes until puffed and lightly golden. Gently press down the centres to create little cups.
3. Caramelise the onions: Heat butter and olive oil in a pan. Add sliced onions and sea salt. Cook on medium-low heat for 15 minutes, stirring occasionally, until soft, golden and caramelised. Add black pepper.
4. Fill: Add a spoonful of caramelised onions to each pastry cup, followed by a small piece of brie and about ½ tsp fig jam.
5. Bake again: Return to the oven for 5–8 minutes, until the brie melts and the pastry is golden and crisp.
6. Garnish: Finish with freshly chopped chives and a pinch of red chilli flakes.

✨ Hosting tip: Caramelise the onions and prebake the pastry cups ahead of time. Assemble and bake just before serving for the best texture!

recipes.author: diningwithdhoot
recipes.text: mushroom galouti kebab 🍄✨ served these on our conch shell plate - it’s so aesthetic & pretty 🤌🏻 melt in your mouth, deeply spiced & absolutely packed with flavour — this one is pure royalty on a plate 🤌🏻 mushroom galouti kebab 🍄✨ • wash 100g mushrooms & boil in salted water for 4-5 mins. drain & set aside. • heat 1 tbsp oil in a kadhai, add 2 sliced onions & caramelise till 80% done. add ¼ cup cashews & cook together. blend into a smooth paste. • add the paste back to the kadhai & cook with 1 tsp coriander powder, 1 tsp red chilli powder, 1 tsp garam masala, 1 tsp jeera powder & 1 tsp salt. mix well & switch off the flame. • add 1-2 tbsp besan to bind — add more if the mixture is too loose. shape into tikkis & pan fry on both sides on a hot tawa till golden & crispy. • for the mini parathas, roll out an atta or maida roti & cut out small circles using a katori. pan fry on both sides with a little oil till golden. • to serve, place the kebab on the mini paratha, top with sliced onion & green chutney & enjoy ✨ [dining with dhoot, mushroom galouti kebab, galouti kebab, mushroom recipes, lucknowi food, kebab recipes, indian street food, comfort food, vegetarian recipes]
recipes.caption:
Mushroom Galouti Kebab 🍄✨

Served these on our @setthetable_in conch shell plate - it’s so aesthetic & pretty 🤌🏻 

Melt in your mouth, deeply spiced & absolutely packed with flavour — this one is pure royalty on a plate 🤌🏻

Mushroom Galouti Kebab 🍄✨
• Wash 100g mushrooms & boil in salted water for 4-5 mins. Drain & set aside.
• Heat 1 tbsp oil in a kadhai, add 2 sliced onions & caramelise till 80% done. Add ¼ cup cashews & cook together. Blend into a smooth paste.
• Add the paste back to the kadhai & cook with 1 tsp coriander powder, 1 tsp red chilli powder, 1 tsp garam masala, 1 tsp jeera powder & 1 tsp salt. Mix well & switch off the flame.
• Add 1-2 tbsp besan to bind — add more if the mixture is too loose. Shape into tikkis & pan fry on both sides on a hot tawa till golden & crispy.
• For the mini parathas, roll out an atta or maida roti & cut out small circles using a katori. Pan fry on both sides with a little oil till golden.
• To serve, place the kebab on the mini paratha, top with sliced onion & green chutney & enjoy ✨

recipes.recipe_method:
Wash 100g mushrooms & boil in salted water for 4-5 mins. Drain & set aside.
Heat 1 tbsp oil in a kadhai, add 2 sliced onions & caramelise till 80% done. Add ¼ cup cashews & cook together. Blend into a smooth paste.
Add the paste back to the kadhai & cook with 1 tsp coriander powder, 1 tsp red chilli powder, 1 tsp garam masala, 1 tsp jeera powder & 1 tsp salt. Mix well & switch off the flame.
Add 1-2 tbsp besan to bind — add more if the mixture is too loose. Shape into tikkis & pan fry on both sides on a hot tawa till golden & crispy.
For the mini parathas, roll out an atta or maida roti & cut out small circles using a katori. Pan fry on both sides with a little oil till golden.
To serve, place the kebab on the mini paratha, top with sliced onion & green chutney

GUT HEALTHY MULTIGRAIN PORRIDGE

recipes.caption:
MOST REQUESTED RECIPE AS A PRIVATE CHEF

Every single client asks me for this one, and it’s such an easy one to make. You literally bang everything in a bowl and mix it with water.

I make these super seed crackers as soon as I arrive at a client’s house because they’re so versatile - they’re a canapé base, something for dips, or a crunchy salad topper, and they’re really high in fibre. The fennel, coriander and caraway seeds are what give them so much flavour.

I love seeds, so I always have loads in the house. For this batch I used pumpkin, sunflower, hemp, whole linseeds and poppy seeds, but the @waitrose seed mix works really well too. If you don’t have many seeds in, you can just use 250g of one. The only thing that matters is the chia, milled flax and psyllium husk, because they’re what hold it all together.

SUPER SEED CRACKER

250g seed mix
2 tsp caraway seeds
2 tsp fennel seeds
3 tsp coriander seeds
3 tsp chia seeds
3 tsp milled flax
2 tsp psyllium husk
3 pinches of salt
200ml water

Mix everything together, then leave it for 10 minutes. This is the important bit. The chia, flax and psyllium turn into a gel, which binds the seeds and makes it much easier to spread. If you don’t have psyllium, just add a bit more milled flax.

Spread it thinly over a lined baking tray and bake at 150C for 40 minutes. Let it cool, then break it into shards.

It makes a huge sheet that should last ages, but I’ve already managed to munch my way through most of it, hence the very small jar at the end. They’re brilliant if you’re meal prepping, and they keep well in an airtight jar.

250g seed mix
2 tsp caraway seeds
2 tsp fennel seeds
3 tsp coriander seeds
3 tsp chia seeds
3 tsp milled flax
2 tsp psyllium husk
3 pinches of salt
200ml water
recipes.recipe_method:
Mix everything together, then leave it for 10 minutes.
Spread it thinly over a lined baking tray and bake at 150C for 40 minutes.
Let it cool, then break it into shards.

recipes.recipe_ingredients:
150 g uncooked short grain rice
2 chicken thighs, deboned
1/2 tsp black pepper powder
5 -6 dried shiitake mushrooms, rehydrated and sliced
150 ml mushroom soaking liquid
45 g fresh shiitake mushrooms
45 g shimeji mushrooms
5 ginger slices
1 green onion, chopped (garnish)
2 tbsp Shaoxing cooking wine
1 tbsp light soy sauce
2 tsp dark soy sauce
1/4 tsp white pepper powder
10 g rock sugar
2 tbsp sesame oil
recipes.recipe_method:
Soak the dried shiitake mushrooms in 150ml water overnight until fully plump. If you’re short on time, soak them in hot water for 30 minutes. Squeeze out the excess liquid, then slice the mushrooms. Keep the soaking liquid for later.
Debone the chicken thighs and make a few shallow cuts on the meat side to even out the thickness. Lightly season the meat side with black pepper.
Place the chicken skin side down in a cold pan, then turn the heat to medium. You don’t need to add oil because the chicken skin will render its own fat.
Once the skin starts to sizzle, cook for 4-5 minutes until the skin is golden and crispy. Flip and pan-fry the meat side for about 2 minutes. The chicken doesn’t need to be fully cooked at this stage as we will continue to stir-fry later. Remove from the pan and chop into bite-sized pieces.
In the same pan, add the ginger slices, dried shiitake, fresh shiitake and shimeji mushrooms. Stir-fry for 2-3 minutes until softened and fragrant.
Add the sliced chicken back into the pan. Pour in Shaoxing wine, light soy sauce, dark soy sauce, white pepper, rock sugar and sesame oil. Stir-fry for another 2-3 minutes until the chicken is cooked through and everything is coated in a glossy sauce.
Add the washed and drained rice into your rice cooker. Top with the chicken and mushroom stir-fry, then pour in the reserved mushroom soaking liquid. Cook as you normally would for rice, usually around 30 minutes, depending on your rice cooker.
Once cooked, gently fluff the rice and garnish with chopped spring onions. Serve immediately. Enjoy!

recipes.title: Instant Pot Pasta
recipes.author: mariumhosein
recipes.text: method: 1. add pasta to the instant pot. 1 lb. i’m using cavatappi 2. pour in 5 cups water or stock (adds flavor and protein)—the pasta should be mostly submerged. add salt. 3. do not stir too much; just gently press the pasta down so it’s covered. 4. close the lid and set to high pressure for 4 minutes. 5. when it finishes, do a quick release immediately. be careful because pasta water can foam. 6. open and stir. if there’s a little excess liquid, let it sit for 1–2 minutes or drain it. 7. this made my pasta perfectly soft. but if you like your pasta with a bite do 3 mins. cavatappi is fairly thick, so 4 minutes gives you al dente-ish pasta. if you’re going to toss it with a hot sauce and let it cook a little more, i’d do 3 minutes. if you’re making it for a baked pasta/casserole, definitely do 3 minutes so it doesn’t get mushy.
recipes.caption:
Method:

1. Add pasta to the Instant Pot. 1 lb. I’m using Cavatappi
2. Pour in 5 cups water or stock (adds flavor and protein)—the pasta should be mostly submerged. Add salt.
3. Do not stir too much; just gently press the pasta down so it’s covered.
4. Close the lid and set to High Pressure for 4 minutes.
5. When it finishes, do a quick release immediately. Be careful because pasta water can foam.
6. Open and stir. If there’s a little excess liquid, let it sit for 1–2 minutes or drain it.
7. This made my pasta perfectly soft. But if you like your pasta with a bite do 3 mins. 

Cavatappi is fairly thick, so 4 minutes gives you al dente-ish pasta. If you’re going to toss it with a hot sauce and let it cook a little more, I’d do 3 minutes.

If you’re making it for a baked pasta/casserole, definitely do 3 minutes so it doesn’t get mushy.
recipes.recipe_ingredients:
1 lb pasta (Cavatappi)
5 cups water or stock
salt
recipes.recipe_method:
Add pasta to the Instant Pot.
Pour in 5 cups water or stock (adds flavor and protein)—the pasta should be mostly submerged. Add salt.
Do not stir too much; just gently press the pasta down so it’s covered.
Close the lid and set to High Pressure for 4 minutes.
When it finishes, do a quick release immediately.
Open and stir. If there’s a little excess liquid, let it sit for 1–2 minutes or drain it.

recipes.text: you bring smoky fig bruschetta once and suddenly it’s your permanent party assignment 🍂🍯 sweet caramelized figs get a smoky kick, layered over creamy farmer cheese and finished with rosemary hot honey for the perfect balance of sweet, savory, and spicy. easy, chef-y, and perfect for fall hosting or wine nights with friends. save this recipe and tag the friend bringing the wine 🍷 smoky fig bruschetta with rosemary hot honey serves 4–6 ingredients 👇 1 baguette, sliced and toasted 1 garlic clove 6–8 fresh figs, halved or quartered 1 tbsp olive oil pinch of flaky sea salt 1 cup lifeway farmer cheese zest of 1 lemon freshly cracked black pepper aged prosciutto (optional, for topping) crushed pistachios (optional, for crunch) rosemary hot honey 🔥🍯 (comment hot honey and i’ll dm the recipe to you) instructions: slice and toast the baguette until golden and crisp. rub each crostini with garlic. add hot honey to a skillet. add figs cut side down, cook 2–3 minutes until caramelized. place a sprig of rosemary into the pan, and torch it until it’s smoking. place the lid onto the pan to infuse the smoke flavor into the figs. in a bowl, mix farmer cheese with lemon zest, a drizzle of olive oil, salt, and pepper until smooth. spread whipped farmer cheese on toasted baguette slices. top with caramelized figs, crispy prosciutto, and pistachios if using. drizzle with rosemary hot honey right before serving. cheers!🍂
recipes.caption:
You bring Smoky Fig Bruschetta once and suddenly it’s your permanent party assignment 🍂🍯

Sweet caramelized figs get a smoky kick, layered over creamy Farmer Cheese and finished with rosemary hot honey for the perfect balance of sweet, savory, and spicy.

Easy, chef-y, and perfect for fall hosting or wine nights with friends.

Save this recipe and tag the friend bringing the wine 🍷

Smoky Fig Bruschetta with Rosemary Hot Honey
Serves 4–6
Ingredients 👇

1 baguette, sliced and toasted
1 garlic clove
6–8 fresh figs, halved or quartered
1 tbsp olive oil
Pinch of flaky sea salt
1 cup Lifeway Farmer Cheese
Zest of 1 lemon
Freshly cracked black pepper
Aged prosciutto (optional, for topping)
Crushed pistachios (optional, for crunch)
Rosemary Hot Honey 🔥🍯 (comment Hot Honey and I’ll dm the recipe to you)

Instructions:

Slice and toast the baguette until golden and crisp. Rub each crostini with garlic. 

Add hot honey to a skillet. Add figs cut side down, cook 2–3 minutes until caramelized. 

Place a sprig of rosemary into the pan, and torch it until it’s smoking. Place the lid onto the pan to infuse the smoke flavor into the figs. 

In a bowl, mix Farmer Cheese with lemon zest, a drizzle of olive oil, salt, and pepper until smooth.

Spread whipped Farmer Cheese on toasted baguette slices. Top with caramelized figs, crispy prosciutto, and pistachios if using.

Drizzle with Rosemary Hot Honey right before serving. Cheers!🍂

recipes.text: superfood amaranth ( rajgira or ramdana) parathas! 🫓💚 protein, fiber & iron-rich lunchbox! 🌸 6:00 am prayer, lunchbox & some protein goodness – episode 50 ❤️🙏 as a mom of 2 growing kids, i always try to add more nutrition to everyday meals! ❤️ today i made these soft, delicious rajgira (amaranth), sweet potato & cottage cheese parathas — a wholesome combination of protein, fiber, iron and calcium! perfect for breakfast, kids’ lunchboxes or the whole family! 😍 🥣 ingredients (makes7-8 paranthas) * 1 cup rajgira (amaranth) flour * 1 cup whole-wheat flour (atta) * 1 cup cottage cheese or grated paneer * 1 cup boiled & mashed sweet potato * fresh coriander leaves * 1 tsp cumin powder * 1 tsp ajwain powder * 1 tbsp sesame seeds * hing, black pepper & salt to taste * water as needed * ghee or oil for cooking 👩‍🍳 method 1️⃣ mix all ingredients and knead into a soft dough using a little water as needed. rest for 15–20 minutes. 2️⃣ roll a dough ball, apply ghee or oil, fold and roll again. 3️⃣ cook both sides on low-medium heat with ghee until golden. apply a little butter if desired. 4️⃣ pack with curd, chutney or homemade ketchup! ❤️ 🌿 why amaranth is a superfood! 💪 protein: supports growth and muscle development. ❤️ iron: helps support healthy blood and energy metabolism. 🌾 fiber: supports digestion and gut health. 🦴 calcium & magnesium: important for growing bones and muscles. ✨ approx. 8-9 g protein per paratha no maida, just wholesome homemade goodness! ❤️ 💌 save this nutritious
recipes.caption:
Superfood Amaranth ( Rajgira or Ramdana) Parathas! 🫓💚 Protein, Fiber & Iron-Rich Lunchbox!
🌸 6:00 AM Prayer, Lunchbox & Some Protein Goodness – Episode 50 ❤️🙏

As a mom of 2 growing kids, I always try to add more nutrition to everyday meals! ❤️

Today I made these soft, delicious Rajgira (Amaranth), Sweet Potato & Cottage Cheese Parathas — a wholesome combination of protein, fiber, iron and calcium! Perfect for breakfast, kids’ lunchboxes or the whole family! 😍

🥣 Ingredients (Makes7-8 paranthas)

* 1 cup rajgira (amaranth) flour
* 1 cup whole-wheat flour (atta)
* 1 cup cottage cheese or grated paneer
* 1 cup boiled & mashed sweet potato
* Fresh coriander leaves
* 1 tsp cumin powder
* 1 tsp ajwain powder
* 1 tbsp sesame seeds
* Hing, black pepper & salt to taste
* Water as needed
* Ghee or oil for cooking

👩‍🍳 Method

1️⃣ Mix all ingredients and knead into a soft dough using a little water as needed. Rest for 15–20 minutes.

2️⃣ Roll a dough ball, apply ghee or oil, fold and roll again.

3️⃣ Cook both sides on low-medium heat with ghee until golden. Apply a little butter if desired.

4️⃣ Pack with curd, chutney or homemade ketchup! ❤️

🌿 Why Amaranth Is a Superfood!

💪 Protein: Supports growth and muscle development.

❤️ Iron: Helps support healthy blood and energy metabolism.

🌾 Fiber: Supports digestion and gut health.

🦴 Calcium & Magnesium: Important for growing bones and muscles.

✨ Approx. 8-9 g protein per paratha 

No maida, just wholesome homemade goodness! ❤️

💌 Save this nutritious lunchbox idea and share it with another mom!

recipes.title: Pickled Carrots
recipes.author: thesoulfulplates
recipes.text: honestly, it's better than plain carrot in a salad. crunchy, tangy, and ready by tomorrow. carrot pickle → cut 3-4 medium carrots into sticks and pack them in a clean jar → add ½ tbsp mustard seeds, 4-6 garlic cloves, 3-4 green chillies and 1 tbsp pink salt → pour in ½-1 cup apple cider vinegar → fill the jar with lukewarm water → optional: 1 tbsp jaggery or sugar to balance the acidity (i skipped it, but it's good) → let it cool, close the lid, and burp the jar once in a while → ready to eat after 24 hours. store in the fridge. tips → use a clean, dry jar → keep the carrots fully submerged in the liquid → always use a dry spoon to take it out → keep it in the fridge and finish within 1-2 weeks → taste gets better on day 2 save this for the next time something is going to waste in your fridge. 🫙
recipes.caption:
Honestly, it's better than plain carrot in a salad. Crunchy, tangy, and ready by tomorrow.

Carrot pickle
→ Cut 3-4 medium carrots into sticks and pack them in a clean jar
→ Add ½ tbsp mustard seeds, 4-6 garlic cloves, 3-4 green chillies and 1 tbsp pink salt
→ Pour in ½-1 cup apple cider vinegar
→ Fill the jar with lukewarm water
→ Optional: 1 tbsp jaggery or sugar to balance the acidity (I skipped it, but it's good)
→ Let it cool, close the lid, and burp the jar once in a while
→ Ready to eat after 24 hours. Store in the fridge.

Tips
→ Use a clean, dry jar
→ Keep the carrots fully submerged in the liquid
→ Always use a dry spoon to take it out
→ Keep it in the fridge and finish within 1-2 weeks
→ Taste gets better on day 2

Save this for the next time something is going to waste in your fridge. 🫙

recipes.title: Jalapeño Cream Cheese Pinwheels
recipes.author: ashleymarkleeats
recipes.text: these viral jalapeño cream cheese pinwheels are so easy and so yummy 🧀🌶️ ingredients: 1 sheet puff pastry 4oz cream cheese sliced jalapeño peppers 1 cup shredded mozzarella cheese 1 egg (for egg wash) hot honey (optional) instructions: roll out the puff pastry dough and spread with a layer of cream cheese evenly over the surface. then add a layer of jalapenos and shredded cheese. roll tightly into a log (allow to set in freezer for 10-15 minutes if needed to firm up) and slice into 7-8 pinwheels. place pinwheels on a parchment-lined baking sheet. brush the tops with beaten egg, then bake at 400°f for 18-20 minutes until golden and flaky. allow to cool slightly, drizzle with hot honey and enjoy! 😋
recipes.caption:
these viral jalapeño cream cheese pinwheels are so easy and so yummy 🧀🌶️

Ingredients:
1 sheet @bakejusrol puff pastry
4oz @phillycreamchs cream cheese 
@mezzetta sliced jalapeño peppers
1 cup shredded mozzarella cheese
1 egg (for egg wash)
@mikeshothoney hot honey (optional)

Instructions:
Roll out the puff pastry dough and spread with a layer of cream cheese evenly over the surface. Then add a layer of jalapenos and shredded cheese. Roll tightly into a log (allow to set in freezer for 10-15 minutes if needed to firm up) and slice into 7-8 pinwheels. Place pinwheels on a parchment-lined baking sheet. Brush the tops with beaten egg, then bake at 400°F for 18-20 minutes until golden and flaky. Allow to cool slightly, drizzle with hot honey and enjoy! 😋

recipes.text: craving a real aglio e olio? it should never leave a puddle of oil on your plate. the secret is slow cooking minced garlic in cold olive oil and finishing the pasta right in the pan for a smooth, creamy sauce. come to ameretti to taste how it is truly meant to be made.

recipes.recipe_ingredients:
olive oil
garlic
chili flakes
pasta
pasta cooking water
parsley
grated cheese
recipes.recipe_method:
Pour cold olive oil into a pan, add minced garlic and chili flakes, and cook slowly to infuse the oil and avoid bitterness.
Boil the pasta until half-cooked.
Transfer the half-cooked pasta to the pan and toss it in the garlic-chili oil so it finishes cooking in the pan (about 70% of the cooking) and absorbs the flavors.
Add a splash of starchy pasta water and toss to create a smooth, creamy sauce.
Plate and top with chopped parsley and grated cheese.

recipes.title: Miso Salmon
recipes.author: xomelissatovar
recipes.text: my fav weeknight dinner that reheats perfectly the next day! miso salmon (can also use cod or sablefish): - 1/4 cup miso paste - 1/4 cup mirin - 2 tbsp maple syrup or sugar - 2 tbsp low sodium soy sauce - 1 tbsp sesame oil - grated fresh ginger *optional broil on middle rack for 10-15 mins. i like to turn my rack halfway through so it crusts evenly along the top. *the longer you marinate the salmon the deeper the flavor will be! lately i don’t have time so i do 30 mins. you can also sprinkle with pepper and sea salt on top before broiling if you like it on the saltier side!

recipes.recipe_ingredients:
heavy cream
yogurt or kefir (a spoonful, as starter culture)
ice water
salt
recipes.recipe_method:
Pour the heavy cream into a bowl, add a spoonful of yogurt or kefir, and mix gently.
Cover with a kitchen towel and let it ferment at room temperature for 24 to 48 hours until thick and scoopable.
Whip the cultured cream with an electric hand mixer until it separates into solid butter and liquid buttermilk; save the buttermilk.
Transfer the butter to a bowl of ice water and knead by hand to wash out the remaining buttermilk.
Add salt and mix it in.
Shape the butter into a log, wrap it in parchment paper, and store.

asparagus
butter
salt
fresh lemon juice
cold butter (several tablespoons)
fresh herbs (dill or parsley)
recipes.recipe_method:
Blanch the asparagus spears in boiling water.
Finish the asparagus in a pan with butter and salt over medium heat.
Add fresh lemon juice and bring it to a bubble, then remove the asparagus and set it aside.
With the heat off, whisk in the cold butter piece by piece until it emulsifies with the lemon juice into a thick, creamy sauce.
Season with salt and stir in fresh herbs such as dill or parsley.
Spoon the sauce generously over the plated asparagus.

Tomato Chilli Oil Noodles Recipe
Ingredients
2 servings of frozen udon (1 just is not enough for me)
2 cloves of garlic, minced
1 small knob ginger, minced
1 heaped tbsp tomato paste
1 tbsp light soy sauce
1 tbsp black rice vinegar (or any other vinegar)
1 tbsp mirin (or 2 tsp sweetener of choice)
1 tbsp sesame oil
1 tbsp shoaxing wine (or any clear cooking wine, or skip)
1-2 tsp chilli oil (or as much as you like)
1 tsp chilli powder/gochugaru (or more if you want)
1 lime, juiced (or 1/2 lemon) 
2 spring onions, finely sliced, to garnish
Handful of coriander, roughly chopped, to garnish

Method
1. Prepare your noodles according to the package instructions. (I place my frozen udon in a colander and pour boiling water over it to soften). 
2. Heat a large frying pan over medium heat with a drizzle of oil. Add the garlic and ginger and cook for 3 mins, until fragrant. 
3. Add the tomato paste and fry for 2 mins. Add the chilli powder (or skip) and fry for another 2-3 minutes. 
4. Add the sauce and bring to a simmer. Add the cooked noodles and cook for 1-2 minutes, until the sauce has been absorbed. 
5. Turn off the heat. Add the lime juice and garnish with spring onions and coriander. 
6. Serve :)

recipes.title: Hoisin Chicken Fried Rice
recipes.author: themrskathsymes
recipes.text: hoisin chicken is good but hoisin chicken fried rice is better 🤌 super fast and easy for any night of the week. save for your next fried rice fix. serves 2. difficulty ⭐️ you will need the following. 📌 2 portions of cold cooked rice 📌 2 diced chicken breasts 📌 2 minced garlic cloves 📌 small chunk of grated ginger 📌 2 eggs lightly beaten 📌 2 spring onions, white and green parts separated the sauce: add the following to a bowl and mix well. 📌 2 tbsp hoisin sauce 📌 2 tsp light soy sauce 📌 1 tsp dark soy sauce 📌 1 tsp oyster sauce 📌 1 tsp rice vinegar 📌 add the chicken to a bowl, add the following mix well and leave to marinate while you get everything else ready. 📌 1 tsp cornflour 📌 1 tsp light soy sauce 📌 1 tsp oil 🔥 heat a wok add 1 tbsp oil, once hot add the chicken, stir fry for 3-4 minutes until golden and no longer pink. remove to a plate. 🔥 add a splash more oil, add the eggs and lightly scramble. push to one side and add the white part of the spring onions, the garlic and ginger. stir fry for 30 seconds. 🔥 add the rice, break it up and stir fry for 1-2 minutes. add the chicken back in. 🔥 add the sauce and stir fry, toss for 2-3 minutes. add the green part of the spring onions, stir fry, toss for a further 1-2 minutes. remove from the heat and drizzle with optional sesame oil. serve and enjoy 😉 there you have it done. easy as that!
recipes.caption:
Hoisin Chicken is good but Hoisin Chicken Fried Rice is better 🤌 

Super fast and easy for any night of the week. Save for your next fried rice fix. 

Serves 2. Difficulty ⭐️

You will need the following. 

📌 2 portions of cold cooked rice 
📌 2 diced chicken breasts 
📌 2 minced garlic cloves 
📌 Small chunk of grated ginger 
📌 2 eggs lightly beaten 
📌 2 spring onions, white and green parts separated 

The sauce: Add the following to a bowl and mix well. 

📌 2 tbsp hoisin sauce 
📌 2 tsp light soy sauce 
📌 1 tsp dark soy sauce 
📌 1 tsp oyster sauce 
📌 1 tsp rice vinegar 

📌 Add the chicken to a bowl, add the following mix well and leave to marinate while you get everything else ready. 

📌 1 tsp cornflour 
📌 1 tsp light soy sauce 
📌 1 tsp oil 

🔥 Heat a wok add 1 tbsp oil, once hot add the chicken, stir fry for 3-4 minutes until golden and no longer pink. Remove to a plate. 

🔥 Add a splash more oil, add the eggs and lightly scramble. Push to one side and add the white part of the spring onions, the garlic and ginger. Stir fry for 30 seconds. 

🔥 Add the rice, break it up and stir fry for 1-2 minutes. Add the chicken back in.

🔥 Add the sauce and stir fry, toss for 2-3 minutes. Add the green part of the spring onions, stir fry, toss for a further 1-2 minutes. Remove from the heat and drizzle with optional sesame oil. Serve and enjoy 😉 

There you have it done. Easy as that!
recipes.recipe_ingredients:
2 portions of cold cooked rice
2 diced chicken breasts
2 minced garlic cloves
Small chunk of grated ginger
2 eggs lightly beaten
2 spring onions, white and green parts separated
2 tbsp hoisin sauce
2 tsp light soy sauce
1 tsp dark soy sauce
1 tsp oyster sauce
1 tsp rice vinegar
1 tsp cornflour
1 tsp light soy sauce
1 tsp oil
recipes.recipe_method:
Heat a wok add 1 tbsp oil, once hot add the chicken, stir fry for 3-4 minutes until golden and no longer pink. Remove to a plate.
Add a splash more oil, add the eggs and lightly scramble. Push to one side and add the white part of the spring onions, the garlic and ginger. Stir fry for 30 seconds.
Add the rice, break it up and stir fry for 1-2 minutes. Add the chicken back in.
Add the sauce and stir fry, toss for 2-3 minutes. Add the green part of the spring onions, stir fry, toss for a further 1-2 minutes. Remove from the heat and drizzle with optional sesame oil. Serve and enjoy 😉

recipes.recipe_ingredients:
TOFU
1 block silken or soft tofu drained (around 400g block)
SAUCE
1 1/2 tbsp neutral oil
1 scallion thinly sliced, some green parts saved for garnish

recipes.recipe_method:
PREPARE THE TOFU
Carefully drain the tofu and place it on a heat-safe plate or shallow bowl that fits inside your steamer. Slice the top of the tofu into a checkered grid pattern, but do not cut all the way through the base so the tofu stays together.
STEAM THE TOFU
Steam the tofu over medium high heat for 5-6 minutes or until warmed through. Carefully drain any excess liquid released by the tofu after steaming.
MAKE THE SAUCE
Heat the neutral oil in a small pan over medium heat. Add the scallion and grated ginger, then cook for 1-2 minutes or until aromatic. Pour the hot scallion ginger oil into a bowl.
In the bowl, mix the soy sauce, Chinese black vinegar, brown sugar, chili oil, vegetarian oyster sauce, and Chinese 5 spice powder. Taste and adjust to your liking.
FINISH AND SERVE
Pour the sauce over the steamed tofu. Garnish with scallions or cilantro, sesame seeds, and extra chili oil, if desired.

#cottagecheese #jalapenocheddar #biscuits #highprotein
recipes.recipe_ingredients:
1 large egg, at room temperature
1 cup full-fat cottage cheese, small curd
2 tablespoons cream cheese, softened
1 teaspoon apple cider vinegar
1 cup all-purpose flour
2 teaspoons baking powder
1/4 teaspoon salt
1/2 cup shredded cheddar cheese, plus more for topping
1 jalapeño, finely chopped, plus slices for topping
recipes.recipe_method:
1. Preheat the oven to 400°F. Line a baking sheet with parchment paper.
2. In a medium bowl, whisk the egg lightly. Add the cottage cheese, cream cheese, and apple cider vinegar and whisk until mostly smooth. Some small curds are fine.
3. Stir the shredded cheddar and chopped jalapeño into the wet mixture.
4. In a separate bowl, whisk together the flour, baking powder, and salt.
5. Add the flour mixture to the cottage cheese mixture and fold gently with a spatula just until combined. Do not overmix.
6. Using a large cookie scoop or two spoons, portion the dough into 8 equal mounds and drop onto the prepared baking sheet, spacing them evenly. Lightly press the tops to flatten slightly.
7. Top each biscuit with a pinch of shredded cheddar and a slice of jalapeño.
8. Bake for 18 to 24 minutes, until the biscuits are puffed, golden, and set through the centre.
9. Let cool completely before storing. Keep in an airtight container in the refrigerator for up to 4 days, or freeze for up to 2 months. Reheat in a 350°F oven until warmed through.

1 lb ground meat of choice ( i used ground boneless chicken thighs )
1 tsp garlic powder 
1 tsp onion powder 
1 tbsp red chili flakes 
10 Mini tacos
Salt to taste
1 tbsp black pepper

4 tbsp oil for cooking

Red onion ( diced )
Tomatoes ( diced )
Lettuce ( diced )
Jalapeños 
Banana peppers 

For the burger taco sauce:

1 cup mayonnaise 
1/2 cup ketchup 
1 tsp black pepper 
1 tablespoons cajun seasoning 
1/2 tsp garlic powder 
1 tsp sliced jalapeños ( optional )

Instructions: Season the minced chicken with salt, pepper, red chili flakes, garlic and onion powder. Mix and make small ball.

In a skillet add oil on medium high heat, place the chicken on the skillet and smash it down with the help of a flat surface. Flip after 3 minutes ,Add shredded cheese on top  of the burger patty and cover it with the taco. Press and let it cook for 5-6 minutes or until the patty is fully cooked. 

Flip the taco , add cheese slices on top of the patty. Cover the skillet so the cheese can melt. Make sure the stove is on low heat otherwise the taco can burn from bottom.

Once cheese is melted, add lettuce, tomato , onion, jalapeños, banana peppers. Drizzle some burger sauce on top and enjoy!

recipes.caption:
Caramelized Onion and Garlic Spaghetti 🔥

Comment “Recipe” and I’ll send you the full recipe card for free!!

For ALL of you asking about the app I made, search “Osta” on the App Store or Google Play 🫶😁

Minimal effort, max comfort. Sweet, savory, a little spicy... this one hits every note.

Tip: Best served with with chicken, shrimp, or tofu 🫡 

Ingredients:

-1 large onion, thinly sliced
-4 garlic cloves, minced
-2 tbsp chili crisp 
-1 cup of cream or coconut milk, room temperature
-1 tbsp soy sauce, optional
-1/2 cup fresh Parmesan cheese, grated
-8 oz (225g) pasta of your choice
-2 tbsp butter
-1 tbsp olive oil
-Seasonings (1 tsp each): paprika, garlic powder, salt, pepper, italian seasoning

1. Slice your onion like it owes you money, mince that garlic (use fresh please), and measure out all your seasoning. Bring a cup of cream or coconut milk to room temperature.
2. Heat 2 tbsp butter + 1 tbsp olive oil in a large skillet over medium. Add in the onions and let them vibe for 15–20 minutes, stirring occasionally, until golden and jammy. If they start sticking, hit ‘em with a splash of water.
3. While your onions are caramelizing like sweet little angels, boil a pot of salted water and cook the pasta until al dente. Drain, but don’t forget to save some of that pasta water — it’s liquid gold.
4. When the onions are deeply golden, stir in your minced garlic and all the seasonings. Let it all bloom for a minute, then add the chili crisp and saute for a minute. Pour in your cream (or coconut milk). Let it simmer and get cozy for a few minutes then add the grated Parmesan cheese. 
5. Add your pasta to the sauce and toss to coat. Use that reserved pasta water to loosen things up if it’s too thick — you’re going for silky, not sticky.
6. Serve hot with an extra spoon of chili crisp on top for a spicy kick and maybe a sprinkle of fresh parsley if you’re feelin’ fancy.

recipes.caption:
It’s cheesy, sweet & salty EVERYTHING you could possibly want in a GRILLED CHEESE.

This Fig & caramelized hot honey grilled cheese passes all the grilled cheese tests for me! Made with 2 different types of cheeses- Gruyere & Havarti & coated in a cinnamon sugar butter mixture.

For the caramelized onions:
Avocado oil
1 small red or white onion sliced
1 tbsp balsamic vinegar pinch of salt
For the grilled cheese:
2 slices of sourdough bread or bread of choice
2 tbsp softened butter mixed with cinnamon & sugar
Fig jam
Sliced figs
Shredded Gruyere cheese about 1/2 cup
Sliced havarti cheese
Fresh thyme leaves
Flaky sea salt
Hot honey
Balsamic glaze
In a skillet on medium heat pour in the avocado oil about 2-3 tbsp. Put the onions in with a pinch of salt & turn to medium-low. You want the onions to cook low & slow here so they release their natural sugars.
Add a splash of water if the pan seems too try & stir every few minutes. Once the onions are soft about 10 minutes pour in 1 tbsp balsamic vinegar. Mix for a couple of min then turn off heat.

Preheat oven to 350 degrees. Butter opposite sides of bread then flip over to spread on the fig jam. Add the shredded cheese, caramelized onions, figs, thyme, sliced havarti, sea salt, hot honey & balsamic glaze. Carefully close the sandwich & transfer to a skillet on medium heat. Press bread down with the back of the pan & cook until golden then flip & cook the other side making sure the outer bread doesn’t burn. Transfer to the oven for 5 min to make sure it’s all cheesy. Slice in half & enjoy by itself or with your fave fall soup!

Enjoy!

recipes.author: thespicystory
recipes.text: i am sharing one of my favourite recipes to make for fasting - lauki & paneer muthiyas.😍 they make for a perfect snack or even lunch with dahi wali green chutney that you can enjoy in the fast too. even if you are not fasting, it is a recipe to try.🌱 recipe 👇🏻 1 small lauki/bottle gourd 1/4 cup paneer, grated 2 cups rajgira flour 1 tsp cumin seeds sendha namak, to taste pepper, to taste 1-2 green chillies, finely chopped 2 tbsp fresh coriander, finely chopped 1 tsp ginger, finely chopped lauki squeezed water, if required for tadka - 2 tsp oil 1 tsp cumin seeds 2 sprig curry leaves 1 green chillies, chopped lemon juice from 1 lemon method 👇🏻 peel and grate lauki and squeeze out the water. add in a bowl or paraat and mix in with paneer, rajgira flour, cumin seeds, rock salt, pepper, green chillies, fresh coriander, ginger and lauki squeezed water as required. knead a soft dough and shape into muthiyas. steam for 12-15 mins and the cool it down. cut and keep aside. heat oil in a pan. add cumin seeds, curry leaves, green chilli and add the muthiyas. cook for 2-3 mins, add lemon juice and enjoy.
recipes.caption:
I am sharing one of my favourite recipes to make for fasting - Lauki & Paneer Muthiyas.😍

They make for a perfect snack or even lunch with dahi wali green chutney that you can enjoy in the fast too. Even if you are not fasting, it is a recipe to try.🌱

Recipe 👇🏻
1 small Lauki/Bottle Gourd
1/4 cup Paneer, grated
2 cups Rajgira flour
1 tsp cumin seeds
Sendha Namak, to taste
Pepper, to taste
1-2 green chillies, finely chopped
2 tbsp fresh coriander, finely chopped
1 tsp ginger, finely chopped
Lauki squeezed water, if required 
For tadka -
2 tsp oil
1 tsp cumin seeds
2 sprig curry leaves
1 green chillies, chopped
Lemon juice from 1 lemon 

Method 👇🏻
Peel and grate lauki and squeeze out the water. Add in a bowl or paraat and mix in with paneer, rajgira flour, cumin seeds, rock salt, pepper, green chillies, fresh coriander, ginger and Lauki squeezed water as required.
Knead a soft dough and shape into muthiyas. Steam for 12-15 mins and the cool it down. Cut and keep aside.
Heat oil in a pan. Add cumin seeds, curry leaves, green chilli and add the muthiyas. Cook for 2-3 mins, add lemon juice and enjoy.

recipes.text: chocolate orange truffle bites 🧡 ingredients (makes 24): 8 medjool dates, pitted 3 tbsp raw cacao powder 3 tbsp pumpkin seeds 2 tbsp tahini zest of 1 orange (save a bit for topping) + 1 tbsp fresh orange juice pinch of sea salt 40g 85% dark chocolate, melted (for drizzling) method: soak dates in boiling water for a 5 minutes to soften them then drain. blitz everything other than the dark chocolate in a food processor use a silicon spatula to press the mixture into an ice-cube tray (if you don’t have one, put in the fridge to firm up then roll into balls) melt the dark chocolate and drizzle over the top of your tray top with your orange zest and pop in the freezer to firm up once they’re set, pop out of the trays and sprinkle with flaky sea salt keep in the freezer for a pick me up whenever you want! per 3 bites, you’ll get 3g protein and 1.7mg iron (11.5% rda) enjoy!

recipes.title: Greek Yogurt Blueberry Pastry
recipes.author: eatswithjamie
recipes.text: 5 ways to use greek yogurt ep. 4: blueberry pastry make this gluten-free pastry with a few simple ingredients! it’s high in protein from greek yogurt and is perfect for breakfast or a snack. 2 medium rice paper sheets 1 extra large egg 1/4 tsp baking powder 2 - 3 tbsp thick greek yogurt (flavored or plain) a small handful or blueberries a generous amount of honey or agave directions: -preheat oven to 375 f -whisk the egg and baking powder together -soak one rice paper sheet quickly in the mixture and brush off any excess. dip another sheet in and layer it on top of the soaked rice paper sheet. -spread greek yogurt on to the rice paper sheet, add blueberries on top, and drizzle some honey. fold 4 sides of the pastry in. -bake the pastries at 375 f for 20-25 minutes on parchment paper or air fry for 10 minutes tip: don’t add too many blueberries otherwise the pastry will be soggy!
recipes.caption:
5 Ways to use Greek Yogurt EP. 4: Blueberry Pastry 

Make this gluten-free pastry with a few simple ingredients! It’s high in protein from Greek yogurt and is perfect for breakfast or a snack. 

2 medium rice paper sheets
1 extra large egg
1/4 tsp baking powder
2 - 3 tbsp thick Greek yogurt (flavored or plain)
A small handful or blueberries 
A generous amount of honey or agave

Directions: 
-preheat oven to 375 F
-whisk the egg and baking powder together
-soak one rice paper sheet quickly in the mixture and brush off any excess. Dip another sheet in and layer it on top of the soaked rice paper sheet.
-spread Greek yogurt on to the rice paper sheet, add blueberries on top, and drizzle some honey. Fold 4 sides of the pastry in.
-bake the pastries at 375 F for 20-25 minutes on parchment paper or air fry for 10 minutes 

Tip: don’t add too many blueberries otherwise the pastry will be soggy!

recipes.text: a little break from our usual oatmeal 🎃🤎 made this arroz con leche inspired pumpkin rice pudding for breakfast and it turned out so creamy and cozy! such a good one for fall and something the whole family can have too. follow + comment recipe and i’ll send the recipe straight to your dms! ✨ make sure you follow before commenting so my message lands in your inbox! recipe ⬇️ ½ cup white rice 1 cup water 1 cup whole milk + more if needed ½ tsp cinnamon ⅓ cup pumpkin purée 1–2 tbsp maple syrup ½ tsp vanilla pinch of nutmeg, optional lightly rinse the rice and add it to a pot with the water. cover and simmer for about 10–12 minutes, until most of the water is absorbed. add the milk and cinnamon and cook uncovered on low for another 10–15 minutes, stirring often, until the rice is nice and soft and creamy. stir in the pumpkin, vanilla and maple syrup and cook for another 3–5 minutes. turn off the heat. add a little more milk if you want it creamier it thicken as it cools! for younger toddlers, you can skip the maple syrup and mash in ½ a ripe banana instead. 🍌 you can also stir in some plain greek yogurt once it has cooled down a little for some extra creaminess + protein. this makes about 3–4 toddler servings. store leftovers in the fridge for up to 3 days. just add a splash of milk when reheating since it gets thicker in the fridge.
recipes.caption:
A little break from our usual oatmeal 🎃🤎

Made this Arroz con Leche inspired pumpkin rice pudding for breakfast and it turned out so creamy and cozy! Such a good one for fall and something the whole family can have too.

Follow + Comment RECIPE and I’ll send the recipe straight to your DMs! ✨ Make sure you follow before commenting so my message lands in your inbox!

Recipe ⬇️

½ cup white rice
1 cup water
1 cup whole milk + more if needed
½ tsp cinnamon
⅓ cup pumpkin purée
1–2 tbsp maple syrup
½ tsp vanilla
Pinch of nutmeg, optional

Lightly rinse the rice and add it to a pot with the water. Cover and simmer for about 10–12 minutes, until most of the water is absorbed.

Add the milk and cinnamon and cook uncovered on low for another 10–15 minutes, stirring often, until the rice is nice and soft and creamy.

Stir in the pumpkin, vanilla and maple syrup and cook for another 3–5 minutes. Turn off the heat. Add a little more milk if you want it creamier it thicken as it cools!

For younger toddlers, you can skip the maple syrup and mash in ½ a ripe banana instead. 🍌

You can also stir in some plain Greek yogurt once it has cooled down a little for some extra creaminess + protein.

This makes about 3–4 toddler servings.

Store leftovers in the fridge for up to 3 days. Just add a splash of milk when reheating since it gets thicker in the fridge.

recipes.recipe_method:
Lightly rinse the rice and add it to a pot with the water. Cover and simmer for about 10–12 minutes, until most of the water is absorbed.
Add the milk and cinnamon and cook uncovered on low for another 10–15 minutes, stirring often, until the rice is nice and soft and creamy.
Stir in the pumpkin, vanilla and maple syrup and cook for another 3–5 minutes. Turn off the heat. Add a little more milk if you want it creamier it thicken as it cools!
For younger toddlers, you can skip the maple syrup and mash in ½ a ripe banana instead. 🍌
You can also stir in some plain Greek yogurt once it has cooled down a little for some extra creaminess + protein.
This makes about 3–4 toddler servings.
Store leftovers in the fridge for up to 3 days. Just add a splash of milk when reheating since it gets thicker in the fridge.

recipes.recipe_ingredients:
8 cups (1.9L) water
3/4 cup (155g) small tapioca pearls
1 cup (235ml) whole or 2% milk
3/4 cup (175ml) full-fat canned coconut milk
3 1/2 tablespoons honey, divided (can sub with sugar or maple syrup)
3 medium-sized mangoes (about 775 to 800 grams), see note 1
1 cup sliced strawberries, see headnote
recipes.recipe_method:
Cook Pearls
Add the water to a pot or large saucepan and bring it to boil over high heat. DO NOT add the tapioca pearls when the water is still cold (see note 2). Reduce the heat slightly to medium-high and add the tapioca pearls. Give the pearls a quick stir. Cook the pearls for 15 minutes and turn off the heat. The pearls will be translucent around the exterior with solid white specks in the center. Cover the pot with a lid and let the pearls sit for another 10 to 15 minutes, until the pearls look completely translucent. It's okay if a few pearls here and there still have tiny white specks in the center.
Drain the pearls and rinse them under cold water. Transfer them to a large bowl with cold tap water. Submerging the pearls completely in cold water helps them to cool faster and makes them less sticky. Let that sit while you prepare the other components of the tapioca pudding.
Prepare Mango Puree
Add the milk and coconut milk to a saucepan and bring to a boil. Do not cover the saucepan with a lid because it's very easy for the milk to boil over. Turn off the heat and add 2 tablespoons of honey. (See note 3 for the reasoning behind boiling the milk.) Let the milk cool for 5 to 10 minutes.
Slice a mango along the oblong pit in the center. Using the tip of your knife, make crosswise cuts inside the 2 mango slices to make cubes. Use your fingers to bend the mango slices so that the mango cubes protrude. Then, run the knife below the cubes to slice them off.
Take the piece of mango containing the central pit and use a paring knife to peel off the skin. Then, use the knife to cut off as much flesh from the pit as possible. I generally use the flesh around the pit for the mango puree.
Measure 1 1/4 cups (225 grams) of mango flesh and transfer it to the bowl of a high-speed blender. Add the warmed milk to the blender. Blend everything until smooth. Pour the mango puree into a large bowl.
Finish Tapioca Pudding
Drain the tapioca pearls and drizzle 1 1/2 tablespoons of honey over the pearls. Toss to coat the pearls with the honey. Add the tapioca pearls to the bowl with the mango puree and stir. Next, add the remaining mango cubes/chunks and sliced strawberries to the bowl. Stir to combine. Taste the mango tapioca pudding and add more honey, if necessary.
Chill the mango tapioca pudding for at least 2 hours before serving.

recipes.title: Kerala Crispy Shrimp
recipes.author: jaggus_cafe
recipes.text: crispy shrimp, garlicky shallots, coconut oil magic. one pan kerala comfort that hits different on a cozy afternoon . ingredients for shrimp 500 g small shrimp (chemmeen) 1 tsp salt 1/2 tsp turmeric powder 1 tsp kashmiri chili powder 3/4 tsp black pepper powder for stir fry 4–5 tbsp coconut oil 1/2 tsp mustard seeds 4–6 garlic cloves, crushed 10–12 shallots, thinly sliced curry leaves 1 tsp crushed red chili flakes 2 cups cooked rice (day-old works best) a pinch of fenugreek seed powder (uluva podi) method marinate shrimp with salt, turmeric, chili powder, and pepper. rest 30–45 minutes. heat coconut oil in an iron kadai and fry shrimp for 4–5 minutes until crispy. remove and keep aside. keep about 2 tbsp oil in the pan. splutter mustard seeds, add garlic and sauté till golden. add shallots and cook till golden brown. add curry leaves and chili flakes. add cooked rice and mix well. add fried shrimp and toss gently. finish with a pinch of fenugreek powder. serve hot and enjoy. . . shrimp rice, chemeen choru, kerala shrimp recipe, garlic shrimp rice, coconut oil stir fry, south indian seafood, kerala lunch, spicy shrimp rice, easy shrimp recipe, kerala comfort food . shrimprecipe southindianfood coconutoilcooking malayalifood homecooking seafoodlovers indianfoodreels keralalunch spicyfood foodreels jaggucafe
recipes.caption:
Crispy shrimp, garlicky shallots, coconut oil magic. One pan Kerala comfort that hits different on a cozy afternoon .

Ingredients
For shrimp
500 g small shrimp (chemmeen)
1 tsp salt
1/2 tsp turmeric powder
1 tsp Kashmiri chili powder
3/4 tsp black pepper powder

For stir fry
4–5 tbsp coconut oil
1/2 tsp mustard seeds
4–6 garlic cloves, crushed
10–12 shallots, thinly sliced
Curry leaves
1 tsp crushed red chili flakes
2 cups cooked rice (day-old works best)
A pinch of fenugreek seed powder (uluva podi)

Method
Marinate shrimp with salt, turmeric, chili powder, and pepper. Rest 30–45 minutes.
Heat coconut oil in an iron kadai and fry shrimp for 4–5 minutes until crispy. Remove and keep aside.
Keep about 2 tbsp oil in the pan. Splutter mustard seeds, add garlic and sauté till golden.
Add shallots and cook till golden brown. Add curry leaves and chili flakes.
Add cooked rice and mix well. Add fried shrimp and toss gently.
Finish with a pinch of fenugreek powder. Serve hot and enjoy.

recipes.recipe_ingredients:
1 large white onion (or 2-3 medium onions), diced
2 garlic cloves minced
4 tablespoon olive oil
3 tablespoon butter
salt & black pepper to taste
3 sprigs fresh thyme
1 tablespoon balsamic vinegar
80 ml white wine
1.5 tablespoon plain flour
1 liter vegetable stock
225 g dried pasta
60 ml double cream
60 g mature cheddar cheese (plus extra for grilling the top)
recipes.recipe_method:
1. Peel your onion and slice thinly.
2. Heat the oil in a pan and add the thinly sliced onion. Cook on low, stirring occasionally, for 15 - 20 minutes until softened.
3. Add the salt, pepper, and butter and continue cooking for another 20 minutes. The onions should be beginning to turn a deep golden brown at this point. Stir often.
4. Add the balsamic vinegar, thyme, and minced garlic. Saute for 2 minutes.
5. Add the flour and stir it into the onions. Then, add the white wine and deglaze the pan, cooking for another 5-8 minutes until the wine has cooked down/evaporated.
6. Add the pasta and vegetable stock, stir, and cover the pan to simmer for another 10 minutes or until the pasta has cooked. Stir the pan intermittently to ensure nothing is sticking to the bottom of the pan - add more stock as required.
7. Stir in the cream and grated cheese until the cheese has melted and then serve with more cheese and black pepper to finish.

recipes.title: Soaked Oat Porridge
recipes.author: mackdujour
recipes.text: 👀 do you want to optimize your gut health? it’s porridge season, so here’s a friendly reminder of the best way to get the most from your oats this fall— why you should be soaking your oats before you make oatmeal: • it makes them easier to digest • it permeates them with probiotics • helps neutralize phytic acid — increasing bioavailability for mineral absorption (so your body actually gets the iron, zinc, and magnesium! including a healthy fat also helps here) • reduces cooking time i’ve been cooking oats like this since my kids were babies. it’s so quick and provides more nutrition than cooking oats dry! this recipe scales super easy — i usually 1.5x it for a serving for 4 the actual beat oatmeal: 1 cup oats 2 cups water, divided 2 tbs kefir 1/2 tsp sea salt 2 tbs grass fed butter • soak the oats in kefir + 1 cup of water, at room temp overnight (not in the fridge!). • the next morning, boil one cup of water. add salt and butter until melted. add the oats and stir, reduce to a simmer and simmer for ~10 minutes, until you have perfectly creamy oatmeal • eat as is or top with all your fave fruits, nuts and seeds. *make it vegan by subbing coconut kefir or lemon juice and coconut oil in place of the butter (the fat is important for mineral absorption tho, so don’t skip it!) try it yourself then send to someone else who eats oatmeal and deserves more nutrients! follow for more gut health loving recipes 🥰 • • • • •
recipes.caption:
👀 Do you want to optimize your gut health?

It’s porridge season, so here’s a friendly reminder of the best way to get the most from your oats this fall—

Why you should be soaking your oats before you make oatmeal:

• it makes them easier to digest
• it permeates them with probiotics
• helps neutralize phytic acid — increasing bioavailability for mineral absorption (so your body actually gets the iron, zinc, and magnesium! Including a healthy fat also helps here)
• reduces cooking time 

I’ve been cooking oats like this since my kids were babies. It’s so quick and provides more nutrition than cooking oats dry!

This recipe scales super easy — I usually 1.5x it for a serving for 4

The actual beat oatmeal:

1 cup oats
2 cups water, divided
2 tbs kefir 
1/2 tsp sea salt 
2 tbs grass fed butter

• Soak the oats in kefir + 1 cup of water, at room temp overnight (not in the fridge!).
• The next morning, boil one cup of water. Add salt and butter until melted. Add the oats and stir, reduce to a simmer and simmer for ~10 minutes, until you have perfectly creamy oatmeal
• Eat as is or top with all your fave fruits, nuts and seeds.

*make it vegan by subbing coconut kefir or lemon juice and coconut oil in place of the butter (the fat is important for mineral absorption tho, so don’t skip it!)

Try it yourself then send to someone else who eats oatmeal and deserves more nutrients!

recipes.author: suzuvibes
recipes.text: easy ube mochi bites!💜🍡🤌🏼 made with just 5 ingredients without dairy, microwave or a steamer! the ube coconut condensed milk made the mochi bites 10x better in taste and the looks! just try once and you’ll love it!💜💫 ingredients:💜 - glutinous rice flour- 45g - corn starch- 10g - ube condensed coconut milk- 1/4 cup - water- 2 tablespoons - coconut oil- 1 teaspoon 1. in a non stick pan, add all the ingredients and mix until it’s combined well. 2. place the pan on the stove and cook the mixture on medium heat while stirring it constantly with a non stick spatula. 3. cook it until a soft dough is formed. 4. remove from the heat and let it cool for 5 minutes. 5. while it’s still warm, use hand gloves and knead the mochi by stretching it. knead it until it becomes stretchy. 6. divide it into small balls and coat them with corn starch to prevent sticking. dust off the excess corn starch. 7. dip the mochi balls in coconut condensed milk and cookie crumbs/ desiccated coconut flakes. enjoy!!💜🥥✨
recipes.caption:
Easy Ube mochi bites!💜🍡🤌🏼
Made with just 5 ingredients without dairy, microwave or a steamer! The Ube coconut condensed milk made the mochi bites 10x better in taste and the looks! Just try once and you’ll love it!💜💫

Ingredients:💜
- Glutinous rice flour- 45g
- Corn starch- 10g
- @naturescharm Ube condensed coconut milk- 1/4 cup
- Water- 2 tablespoons 
- Coconut oil- 1 teaspoon 

1. In a non stick pan, Add all the ingredients and mix until it’s combined well.
2. Place the pan on the stove and cook the mixture on medium heat while stirring it constantly with a non stick spatula.
3. Cook it until a soft dough is formed.
4. Remove from the heat and let it cool for 5 minutes.
5. While it’s still warm, use hand gloves and knead the mochi by stretching it. Knead it until it becomes stretchy.

recipes.recipe_method:

recipes.caption:
Garlic Parmesan chicken rangoons 

Ingredients 

For the chicken 

1 lb boneless chickens breast 
1 tsp salt
1/2 tsp black pepper 
1 tsp garlic powder 
1 tsp onion powder 
1/2 tsp paprika powder 
1 bay leaf
1 black cardamom 
1 clove garlic, smashed
2 cups water

For the filling:
Boiled and shredded chicken 
8oz cream cheese, softened 
1/2 cups green onion, finely chopped 
1 tbsp fresh garlic, finely chopped 
1/2 cups freshly grated parmesan cheese
Salt to taste
1/2 tsp black pepper 
1 tsp garlic powder 
1 tsp onion powder 
1 tsp smoked paprika powder 
1/2 tbsp red chili flakes 
1/2 tsp Italian seasoning 
1 tsp parsley, freshly chopped 
2 tsp lemon juice 

To assemble:
Wonton wrappers
1/3 cups water water
Oil (for frying)

For the garlic Parmesan sauce:

1/2 cups mayonnaise 
1/4 cup sour cream
1/3 cup freshly grated Parmesan
1 small garlic clove, finely grated
1 tbsp lemon juice
1 tsp Dijon mustard
1/2 tsp garlic powder
1/4 tsp black pepper
1–2 tbsp milk or heavy cream, to thin
Salt to taste

Method:

Add chicken, seasonings, bay leaf, cardamom, garlic, and water to a pot. Bring to a gentle boil, reduce to medium-low, cover, and simmer 15–18 minutes, or until the chicken reaches 165°F. Remove, cool slightly, and finely shred.
Mix the shredded chicken with cream cheese, green onion, garlic, Parmesan, seasonings, parsley, and lemon juice until well combined. Taste and adjust salt.
For the sauce, mix mayonnaise, sour cream, Parmesan, garlic, lemon juice, Dijon, garlic powder, and black pepper. Add 1–2 tbsp milk or heavy cream until creamy and your desired consistency. Adjust salt and refrigerate.
Place about 1 tbsp filling in the center of each wonton wrapper. Lightly wet the edges with water, fold over, and press firmly to seal. Bring the two outer corners together for a classic rangoon shape.
Heat 2–3 inches of neutral oil to 350°F. Fry wontons in batches for 2–3 minutes, turning occasionally, until golden and crispy. Transfer to a wire rack or paper towel-lined plate and allow the oil to return to 350°F before the next batch.
Serve immediately with the Garlic Parmesan sauce and garnish with fresh parsley and extra Parmesan.

recipes.caption:
I LOVE this kind of dinner- my rice cooker made my dinner while I went and picked up my kids from school AND while waiting for the rice to cool down, I was able to shower my kids before dinner + activities 👌🏻👌🏻 if you want to cut down the active cooking time to 15 minutes, you can just serve salmon and mushroom rice (takikomi gohan) with seaweed on the side - my kids dipped their 🍙 in soy sauce! 

Comment “RECIPE” if you’d like this one sent to your DMs!

JAPANESE SALMON & MUSHROOM RICE

Serving size: 2 adults + 2 kids + leftovers

Ingredients:
2 cups of short or medium grain white rice, rinsed
1 to 2 boneless salmon fillet
4 tbsp of soy sauce
2 tbsp of mirin
1/2 cup of Asparagus, thinly chopped
2 cups of mushrooms, I used beech and shiitake 
3 tbsp of furikake
2 tbsp of sesame oil
water, slightly below the 2 cup line as mushrooms will release water 
Optional: 1 seafood stock powder or coin, crushed or dashi powder

Directions:
1. Thoroughly rinse your short-grain rice until the water turns clear. Place the rinsed rice into the inner pot of your rice cooker and fill the water to right below the 2 cup line - you want to add a little less water as cooking mushrooms will release water. 
2. Add soy sauce, mirin, and seafood stock or dashi powder and give it a good mix. Then add chopped asparagus, salmon fillet, and mushrooms and cook on your normal white rice setting. 
3. When rice is done cooking, open the lid and give it a good mix while fluffing your rice and flaking the salmon. You can also remove the skin. Then add furikake, sesame oil and extra salt as needed. 
4. Top with green onions and sesame seeds and serve with miso soup or you can also make it into an ongiri and serve! Enjoy!

Viral Dumpling Bake Meal Prep

Makes 4 individual bakes

Ingredients (per container)
- 5 to 6 frozen dumplings (potstickers or gyoza)
- 1/2 cup chopped bok choy 
- 1/4 cup canned full-fat coconut milk (add 1/2 cup if you want it more brothy)
- 2 tbsp Trader Joe’s Thai red curry sauce
- 1 tbsp Trader Joe’s Soyaki sauce
- Chili crunch, for topping @momofukugoods 
- Fresh cilantro, chopped, for topping
- Green onion, for topping

Soyaki sauce swaps (if no Trader Joe’s):
- 1 tbsp teriyaki sauce or 1 tbsp soy sauce + 1/2 tsp honey or brown sugar

(Totals: 24 dumplings (1 package) , 2 cups bok choy, 1 cup coconut milk, 1/2 cup red curry sauce, 1/4 cup soyaki or substitute)

Instructions
1. Preheat oven to 375°F.
2. Lightly spray 4 individual glass meal prep containers.
3. Add 1/2 cup bok choy to the bottom of each container.
4. In each container, pour in 1/4 cup coconut milk, 2 tbsp red curry sauce, and 1 tbsp soyaki (or substitute).
5. Stir gently to coat the bok choy.
6. Layer 5 to 6 frozen dumplings on top.
7. Cover containers tightly with foil or lids.
8. Bake for 35 to 40 minutes, until dumplings are tender and sauce is bubbling.
9. Remove foil, then top with chili crunch, cilantro, and green onion.

Reheat
- Microwave 1 to 2 minutes, covered.
- Stir gently before eating to coat dumplings in sauce.

recipes.text: moong dal–lauki paneer chilla ingredients * 1 cup soaked moong dal * ½ lauki, peeled and cut into cubes * 50 g paneer * 1 green chilli * ½ tbsp jeera * ½ tbsp haldi * salt to taste * 12 tbsp besan * chopped onion * chopped capsicum * grated carrot * fresh coriander * oil/ghee for cooking method 1. blend: add soaked moong dal + cubed ½ lauki + paneer + green chilli to a blender. blend until smooth. 2. transfer to a bowl and add jeera, haldi and salt. 3. add 12 tbsp besan and mix well. adjust consistency with a little water if required. 4. heat a tawa and lightly grease it. 5. pour and spread the batter into a chilla. 6. top with chopped onion, capsicum, grated carrot and coriander. 7. cook until golden, flip and cook the other side. 8. serve hot with dahi/green chutney.

Moong Dal–Lauki Paneer Chilla

Ingredients

* 1 cup soaked moong dal
* ½ lauki, peeled and cut into cubes
* 50 g paneer
* 1 green chilli
* ½ tbsp jeera
* ½ tbsp haldi
* Salt to taste
* 12 tbsp besan
* Chopped onion
* Chopped capsicum
* Grated carrot
* Fresh coriander
* Oil/ghee for cooking

Method

1. Blend: Add soaked moong dal + cubed ½ lauki + paneer + green chilli to a blender. Blend until smooth.
2. Transfer to a bowl and add jeera, haldi and salt.
3. Add 12 tbsp besan and mix well. Adjust consistency with a little water if required.
4. Heat a tawa and lightly grease it.
5. Pour and spread the batter into a chilla.
6. Top with chopped onion, capsicum, grated carrot and coriander.
7. Cook until golden, flip and cook the other side.
8. Serve hot with dahi/green chutney.

recipes.title: Potato Skillet Omelet
recipes.author: cooking.with.salouma
recipes.text: potato skillet omelet!! made it for breakfast and it was extremely delicious. make sure you make it too 😉 you’ll need: 1 tbsp olive oil 1 potato 2 eggs 1/2 cup cheddar cheese salt and pepper on a medium heat add the oil to a non stick pan and slice the potato with a peeler and form a thin layer. add salt. when the edges turn golden and crispy, flip the potatoes over. break eggs on them. add black pepper and salt. let it cook for a minute. add the cheese and cover until cheese has melted. fold the omelet. slice and serve. enjoy 😉
recipes.caption:
Potato Skillet Omelet!!
Made it for breakfast and it was extremely delicious. Make sure you make it too 😉

You’ll need:
1 tbsp olive oil 
1 potato
2 eggs
1/2 cup cheddar cheese 
Salt and pepper

On a medium heat add the oil to a non stick pan and slice the potato with a peeler and form a thin layer. Add salt. When the edges turn golden and crispy, flip the potatoes over. Break eggs on them. Add black pepper and salt. Let it cook for a minute.
Add the cheese and cover until cheese has melted. Fold the omelet. Slice and serve. 
Enjoy 😉

recipes.recipe_ingredients:
1 cup long grain white rice*, rinsed well
2 cups chicken broth, low sodium preferred, extra to moisten at the end
2-3 garlic cloves, minced
3 – 4 Tbsp melted butter
1½ lb chicken breast, cut in bite-sized pieces
1 ½ – 2 tsp Italian seasoning
½ tsp onion powder
½ tsp garlic powder
½ tsp paprika
½ tsp sea salt
½ tsp pepper
½ cup freshly grated parmesan
¼ cup heavy cream, technically optional, but adds richness and creaminess
2 cups chopped baby spinach, measured before chopping
recipes.recipe_method:
Preheat oven to 375°F.
Add rice, broth, butter and minced garlic to a 9×13 inch baking pan and stir to combine. I use the 2 cups, and then later after baking, if it feels a bit too dry, add in the extra ¼ cup or a bit more if desired.
Add the cubed chicken over top and sprinkle seasonings Gently stir to combine. (*You can also add the spinach at this time if preferred. After original testing, I did it before baking and found liked it a bit better this way because the spinach bakes with all the flavors and seasoning.)
Cover the pan with foil and seal very tight. Bake for 50-60 minutes or until the chicken has reached 165°F and the rice is tender. Check in at the 45 minute mark and adjust as needed.
Once cooked, stir in the parmesan and cream if using and allow to melt. Add the spinach and stir it in, let it sit for several minutes to wilt.
Allow the dish to rest for several minutes before serving. Serve with fresh chopped herbs (thyme, sage, or parsley are faves) and more parmesan.

recipes.text: part 9 🧀 cheesy courgette loaf 🥒 i love a cup of tea when my little one is down for a nap but lately i’ve been spending the first 10 minutes of nap time boiling my kettle and quickly prepping a snack to go in the oven. follow for more easy and pocket friendly snack ideas that are healthy! save this recipe for your next batch prep! ingredients: - 2 eggs - 1 grated courgette with liquid squeezed out - 1 cup cheddar cheese, grated - 1 cup self raising flour - 1tsp baking powder - 1/2 cup of milk method: - grate your courgette and squeeze out the excess liquid - add all your ingredients to a bowl and mix well (i also added 1tsp of salt and some black pepper at this point) - bake at 180°c (350°f) for 35-45 minutes or until golden and cooked through. let me know if you make it! enjoy!

recipes.text: undercover iron ep. 13: black sesame brownie bites ingredients: - 8 medjool dates, pitted (if you can’t find medjool get large ones and pre-soak) - 3 tbsp cacao powder - 3 tbsp black sesame paste (or black tahini) - 50g cashews - 30g oats - 100g 85% dark chocolate - 1 tsp coconut oil (optional) - pinch flaky sea salt - sesame seeds to top method: 1. blend together dates, cacao, black sesame tahini, cashews, oats and 25g of the dark chocolate 2. press mixture into ice cube tray (i used one with 24 mini cubes). if you don’t have one then press into the base of a small baking tin 3. melt remaining 75g dark chocolate with 1 tsp coconut oil (optional but makes the topping a bit softer) 4. pour over the black sesame base and top with black sesame seeds and a sprinkle of flaky salt then put in the fridge to set solid 5. once they’re set they’re ready to eat! 6. remember: if wanting to optimise iron, combine with a vitamin c rich snack accompanying snack e.g. kiwi, orange, strawberries
