If you have any Greek yogurt left over from the week, this is your sign to turn it into these insanely delicious refined sugar-free brownie batter cookies! You guys went crazy over my chocolate chip Greek yogurt cookies, so naturally, I had to make a double-chocolate version and they did not disappoint! 

These cookies have crispy edges, soft and gooey centers, and all the rich, fudgy flavor of a brownie, but they’re made with better-for-you ingredients. YES, PLEASE!!

Comment LINK and I’ll send the recipe straight to your DMs, or visit lovelydelites.com through the link in my bio.

Be sure to SAVE, SHARE, and TAG me when you try them! 🤎

* 1 ½ cups all-purpose flour
* ¼ cup cocoa powder (Dutch-process is preferred)
* 1 teaspoon baking soda
* ¼ teaspoon baking powder
* ½ teaspoon kosher salt
* ½ cup coconut sugar
* ⅓ cup coconut oil (softened but not melted)
* ¼ cup runny tahini
* ⅓ cup 2% plain Greek yogurt
* 1 large egg
* 2 teaspoons vanilla extract
* 1 teaspoon instant espresso powder
* ½ cup semi-sweet chocolate chips
* ½ cup chopped dark chocolate
* Flaky sea salt (for finishing)

Preheat the oven to 350°F and line a baking sheet with parchment. In a medium bowl, whisk together the flour, cocoa powder, baking soda, baking powder and salt. In a separate large bowl, beat the softened coconut oil and coconut sugar until well combined and slightly fluffy. Mix in the tahini, Greek yogurt, egg, vanilla and espresso powder until smooth. Combine ingredients and don’t over mix!!!
Scoop the dough into roughly 2-tablespoon portions, flatten lightly with your fingers. These spread a little during baking time. Press a few extra pieces of chopped chocolate into the tops. Bake for 9–11 minutes, or until the edges are puffed and set but the centers still look slightly soft and underdone. Don’t wait for the centers to look completely baked. Sprinkle immediately with flaky sea salt and enjoy!!

recipes.caption:
Eating Simpler Diaries ep12: Zucchini Ragi Button Noodles

Inspired by the viral carrot button noodles, but gave them my own little wholesome twist with zucchini, edamame & ragi! 🤍

Ingredients:
• Zucchini
• Edamame
• Ragi flour
• All-purpose flour
• Olive oil
• Red pepper flakes
• Red chilli powder
• Dried basil
• Salt

How to make this (Recipe):

Boil the zucchini and edamame until tender and blend them into a smooth paste. Save that cooking water!

Mix ragi flour and all-purpose flour with salt, then gradually add the zucchini-edamame paste to form a soft dough. I did not use any water to knead, just the paste.

Roll into tiny balls and press the center to make little button shapes, almost like making tiny dhoklis!

Boil the buttons in the same reserved veggie water until cooked.

For the sauce, heat a little olive oil with red pepper flakes, red chilli powder and basil. Add the remaining zucchini-edamame paste and cook it down until creamy.

Toss in the cooked button noodles and let everything come together. Finish with a drizzle of olive oil, chilli flakes and basil. 

🌱 Protein: edamame + ragi
🥒 Fiber: zucchini + edamame + ragi

Soft, chewy little buttons with simple ingredients!

recipes.caption:
Made a batch of frozen taquitos for my kids’ school lunches. Into the freezer they go for busy mornings. I’ll share how I pack them in a lunchbox soon!

Spiced Pork Taquitos
Makes about 30–35

• 2 lb ground pork
• 2 tsp kosher salt
• 1 tbsp paprika
• 1–2 tsp ancho or regular chili powder
• 2 tsp garlic powder
• 1 tsp onion powder
• 1 tsp cumin
• 1 tsp dried oregano
• 1/2 tsp ground coriander
• 1 tbsp tomato paste
• 1/3 cup water
• 3 cups shredded Mexican-style cheese
• 30–35 tortillas, preferably a corn/masa + flour blend
• 1 egg + 1 tbsp water
• Oil spray

Make the filling:
1. Brown the pork over medium-high heat, breaking into small crumbles. Add salt and spices, cook 30–60 seconds.
2. Stir in tomato paste, cook 30 seconds, then add the water. Simmer until mostly cooked down and moist but not wet.
3. Off heat, sprinkle cheese evenly over the pork. Let sit a few minutes so it melts and binds the filling.

Assemble:
1. Wrap tortillas in a damp towel and microwave about 2 minutes until soft and pliable. Keep covered while you work.
2. Whisk the egg with 1 tbsp water. Add 2–3 tbsp filling to each tortilla with a slotted spoon, letting excess grease drip off. Roll tightly, brush the final edge with egg wash, and seal.

Freeze:
Place seam-side down on a sheet pan and freeze about 2 hours until firm. Transfer to a freezer bag. Freeze up to 3 months.

Air fry from frozen:
Preheat to 350°F for 2 minutes. Spray taquitos lightly with oil and cook 5 minutes. Flip, spray again, and cook another 5–7 minutes, until crisp, golden, and heated through.

🩷 These taste extra delicious with homemade masa flour tortillas! I walk through my full method for making them inside Our Daily Staples. Check out my pinned post to see it.

recipes.caption:
Hype or Hoax – Episode 198

✅ Worth the Hype (9.5/10)

Fudgy Brownie Cheesecake Bars — I think the best thing I’ve ever made! Worth the washing up, and worth the wait in the fridge and freezer. Run, don’t walk—this was incredible. Features a fudgy brownie base, a creamy cheesecake center, and a chocolate layer on top.

Full Recipe (Makes 6 good-sized bars)
Brownie Base:
* Almond flour — 150g (approx. 1.5 cups)
* Cocoa powder — 30g (approx. 1/3 cup)
* Sugar-free maple syrup — 30g (approx. 2 tbsp)
* Coconut oil — 20ml (approx. 1.3 tbsp)
* Unsweetened almond milk — 3 tbsp
* Vanilla extract — 5ml (approx. 1 tsp)
Cheesecake Layer:
* Light cream cheese — 250g (approx. 1 cup)
* Sweetener — 10g (approx. 2 tsp)
* Vanilla extract — 1 tbsp (approx. 15ml)
* Lemon juice — a squeeze
Chocolate Topping:
* Cocoa powder — 40g (approx. 2/5 cup / ~5 tbsp)
* Sugar-free maple syrup — 20g (approx. 1.3 tbsp)
* Coconut oil — 1 tbsp (approx. 15ml)
* Unsweetened almond milk — 2 tbsp

Method:
1. Brownie Base: Mix the base ingredients together, press into a lined tray, and freeze for 10 minutes.
2. Cheesecake Layer: Mix the cheesecake ingredients together, spread over the base, and freeze for 45 minutes.
3. Chocolate Topping: Mix the topping ingredients together, spread over the top layer, and refrigerate for at least 30 minutes.
4. Slice into 6 decent-sized bars and enjoy.

Macros & Fibre (per bar)
* Calories: 275 cals
* Protein: 10g
* Carbs: 9g
* Fat: 20g
* Fibre: 5g (Estimated)

Verdict
9.5/10 — Easily one of the best things ever made. It’s entirely worth the washing up and the wait in the fridge and freezer. Run, don’t walk—this is incredible, vastly more satisfying than standard treats, and hits the spot completely.

Full credit to @nora.dora99 for the inspiration — go show them some love. 🤍

Heat oil in a pan and saute the crushed aromatics, sliced ginger, and chopped scallions.

recipes.recipe_ingredients:
12 tbsp unsalted butter (170g)
3/4 cup + 1 tbsp light brown sugar, packed (163g)
125g extra ripe banana (about one and a quarter medium-sized banana, and around 1/2 cup once mashed)
1 tsp vanilla bean paste
1/2 tsp instant coffee dissolved in 1/2 teaspoon water – optional
3/4 tsp salt
1/2 tsp baking soda
1 1/2 cup + 2 tbsp all purpose flour (210g)
4 oz dark chocolate, chopped (113g)
4 oz milk chocolate, chopped (113g)
recipes.recipe_method:
1. Line 2 light colored 18″x13″ baking sheets with parchment paper (you can also use one sheet and bake the cookies in batches if you don't have two)
2. Add the butter to a light-colored saucepan. Place on the stove on medium-low heat, and cook until the butter has melted. Continue cooking, stirring occasionally, until the butter has turned brown. First it will melt and become very frothy, but then it will stop sizzling and you will see brown specks and a nice, toasty smell. Be careful not to overcook, as brown butter can burn very quickly
3. Add the brown butter to a mixing bowl (scrape in all the brown specks on the bottom of the pan, too!). Add the brown sugar, mashed banana, vanilla bean paste and instant coffee dissolved in water. Whisk until the ingredients are combined and smooth (almost like a caramel)
4. Mix in the salt and baking soda until just combined
5. Sift in the flour and add the chopped chocolate. Use a rubber spatula to gently fold the ingredients together until you see no more streaks of flour, and the chocolate is evenly dispersed. Avoid over-mixing the dough
6. Use a 2 tbsp cookie scoop to scoop the cookie dough onto the prepared baking sheets, keeping at least 2-3″ between the scoops. Level off the cookie scoops so the cookie balls aren't too big, and you should have 16 cookies divided between the two sheets
7. Optionally, you can press in some more chocolate chunks on top of the cookies, and sprinkle some flaky sea salt. I also like adding a thin slice of banana on top of each cookie
8. Rest the scooped cookies for 20-30 minutes at room temperature (or the fridge if you want thicker cookies)
9. Pre-heat your oven to 370F (conventional / no fan) while the cookies are resting
10. Bake the cookies in the pre-heated oven for ~8-10 minutes, until the edges are set but the centers are still slightly soft to touch
11. Remove the cookies from the oven, and use a 4″ cake ring to "scoot" the cookies into perfect circles while they're still hot. Let the cookies rest on the baking sheets until they're set
12. Serve and enjoy!

recipes.title: Walnut Dressing
recipes.author: thechutneylife
recipes.text: this dressing is your solution to needing a simple and delicious way to get all the incredible benefits of ! it keeps well in the fridge for a few days and makes for a great spread in sandwiches or scattered over any roasted vegetables! here’s what you’ll need: ½ cup california walnuts, toasted and cooled ¼ cup cilantro, tender leaves and stems 1 tbsp chili oil 1 tbsp soy sauce 2 cloves garlic 2 tsp sesame oil ½ a lime, juiced 2 tsp honey pinch of salt 6 carrots instructions: 1. chop the walnuts into bite size pieces, toast them on a skillet carefully on low heat until they are fragrant then let them cool. 2. add walnuts, cilantro, chili oil, garlic, sesame oil, lime juice, honey and salt into a small food processor and pulse until the everything looks like a uniform crumble. this will resemble a thicker pesto vs a typical dressing. set aside. 3. wash the carrots & peel off the outer skin. use a vegetable peeler to create ribbons and place into a large mixing bowl. 4. add the walnut mixture to the carrot ribbons and toss gently with your hands. taste and adjust (you can add more chili oil for spice or a squeeze more lime for more acidity). 5. serve immediately for the crunchiest texture but it will keep well for a few days in the fridge as it softens slightly. a one-ounce serving provides 18g of total fat, “healthy fats” including 2.5g of monounsaturated fat and 13g of polyunsaturated fat (of which 2.5 grams is plant-based omega-3 ala), as well as 1.5g of saturated fat.
recipes.caption:
This dressing is your solution to needing a simple and delicious way to get all the incredible benefits of @cawalnuts! It keeps well in the fridge for a few days and makes for a great spread in sandwiches or scattered over any roasted vegetables! 
 
Here’s what you’ll need:
½ cup California walnuts, toasted and cooled
¼ cup cilantro, tender leaves and stems
1 tbsp chili oil 
1 tbsp soy sauce
2 cloves garlic 
2 tsp sesame oil
½ a lime, juiced
2 tsp honey
Pinch of salt
6 carrots
 
Instructions:
1. Chop the walnuts into bite size pieces, toast them on a skillet carefully on low heat until they are fragrant then let them cool. 
2. Add walnuts, cilantro, chili oil, garlic, sesame oil, lime juice, honey and salt into a small food processor and pulse until the everything looks like a uniform crumble. This will resemble a thicker pesto vs a typical dressing. Set aside. 
3. Wash the carrots & peel off the outer skin.  Use a vegetable peeler to create ribbons and place into a large mixing bowl.
4. Add the walnut mixture to the carrot ribbons and toss gently with your hands. Taste and adjust (you can add more chili oil for spice or a squeeze more lime for more acidity). 
5. Serve immediately for the crunchiest texture but it will keep well for a few days in the fridge as it softens slightly.
 
A one-ounce serving provides 18g of total fat, “healthy fats” including 2.5g of monounsaturated fat and 13g of polyunsaturated fat (of which 2.5 grams is plant-based omega-3 ALA), as well as 1.5g of saturated fat.

½ cup California walnuts, toasted and cooled
¼ cup cilantro, tender leaves and stems
1 tbsp chili oil
1 tbsp soy sauce
2 cloves garlic
2 tsp sesame oil
½ a lime, juiced
2 tsp honey
Pinch of salt
6 carrots
recipes.recipe_method:
Chop the walnuts into bite size pieces, toast them on a skillet carefully on low heat until they are fragrant then let them cool.
Add walnuts, cilantro, chili oil, garlic, sesame oil, lime juice, honey and salt into a small food processor and pulse until the everything looks like a uniform crumble. This will resemble a thicker pesto vs a typical dressing. Set aside.
Wash the carrots & peel off the outer skin.  Use a vegetable peeler to create ribbons and place into a large mixing bowl.
Add the walnut mixture to the carrot ribbons and toss gently with your hands. Taste and adjust (you can add more chili oil for spice or a squeeze more lime for more acidity).
Serve immediately for the crunchiest texture but it will keep well for a few days in the fridge as it softens slightly.

recipes.caption:
Crispy garlic parmesan chicken rolls 🌯 

Ingredients 

For the chicken:

2 lb boneless chicken breast, cut into small pieces 
Salt to taste
1 tsp black pepper 
1 tbsp garlic powder 
1 tsp onion powder 
2 tsp paprika powder 
1/2 tsp cumin powder 
1 tbsp lemon juice 
1 tbsp oil (for marinating)
1 small yellow onion, diced
1 red bell pepper, diced
2 tbsp oil for cooking 

For the garlic parmesan sauce:

1 tbsp butter 
1 tbsp garlic, minced 
1 1/2 cup unsweetened heavy whipping cream
1 tbsp cream cheese 
Salt to taste
1/2 tsp black pepper 
1 tsp garlic powder 
1 tsp red chili flakes 
1 cup Parmesan cheese , freshly grated 
1 tsp parsley , finely chopped 

To assemble:
9-10 small flour tortilla wraps
1 cup mozzarella cheese 
Oil for pan frying 

Method:

Season chicken with salt, black pepper, garlic powder, onion powder, paprika, cumin, lemon juice, and oil. Mix well.
Heat 2 tbsp oil in a skillet over medium-high heat. Cook chicken until fully cooked and lightly golden. Add diced onion and bell pepper and sauté for 2–3 minutes until softened. Set aside.
For the sauce, melt butter over medium-low heat. Add garlic and sauté for 30 seconds. Add heavy cream, cream cheese, salt, black pepper, garlic powder, and red chili flakes. Whisk until smooth and simmer until slightly thickened.
Lower the heat and stir in Parmesan until melted and smooth. Turn off the heat and add parsley.
Reserve half the sauce for dipping and mix the remaining half with the chicken. Let cool slightly.
Add a few spoonfuls of filling to each tortilla and sprinkle with mozzarella. Fold in the sides and roll tightly.
Lightly oil a skillet over medium to medium-low heat. Place rolls seam-side down and cook, turning until golden and crispy on all sides. Add more oil as needed. Avoid high heat so the tortilla doesn’t brown before the cheese melts.
Sprinkle with fresh parsley and Parmesan and serve immediately with the reserved garlic Parmesan dipping sauce.

recipes.recipe_method:
Cut the raw chicken into bite-size pieces.
Marinate for 30 minutes with soy sauce, rice wine, grated ginger, minced garlic, five-spice powder, salt, brown sugar, and white pepper.
Coat the chicken in egg white, then dredge each piece in coarse tapioca starch.
Spray the air fryer basket with oil, place the coated chicken in a single layer, and spray again.
Air fry at 375°F for 9 minutes.
Flip the pieces, spray again, and cook for 6 more minutes at 400°F until golden and crispy.

recipes.title: Rice Cooker Chicken Rice
recipes.author: yejiskitchenstories
recipes.text: my husband’s favorite home-cooked meal is chicken with ginger scallion sauce, so i turned it into this easy rice cooker chicken rice. everything cooks together, and it’s the kind of one-pot dinner i’ll keep making when i don’t want a lot of dishes. **rice cooker chicken rice** - 2 cups rice, rinsed - 2 cups water - 2 tbsp mirin - 2 tbsp soy sauce - 2 tbsp sesame oil - ½ onion, sliced - 3 chicken thighs **chicken marinade** - 3 tbsp soy sauce - 2 tbsp mirin - 3 tbsp minced garlic - salt and black pepper i marinated the chicken for about 20 minutes to maximize flavor, but if you don’t have time, just adjust the seasoning at the end with extra salt or soy sauce. add the rice, water, mirin, soy sauce, sesame oil, and sliced onion to your rice cooker. place the chicken thighs on top and cook on the regular white rice setting. once everything is done and the chicken is fully cooked, cut it into smaller pieces. add ginger scallion sauce, mix it all together, and serve.
recipes.caption:
My husband’s favorite home-cooked meal is chicken with ginger scallion sauce, so I turned it into this easy rice cooker chicken rice. Everything cooks together, and it’s the kind of one-pot dinner I’ll keep making when I don’t want a lot of dishes.

**Rice Cooker Chicken Rice**
- 2 cups rice, rinsed 
- 2 cups water 
- 2 tbsp mirin 
- 2 tbsp soy sauce 
- 2 tbsp sesame oil 
- ½ onion, sliced 
- 3 chicken thighs 

**Chicken marinade**
- 3 tbsp soy sauce 
- 2 tbsp mirin 
- 3 tbsp minced garlic 
- Salt and black pepper 

I marinated the chicken for about 20 minutes to maximize flavor, but if you don’t have time, just adjust the seasoning at the end with extra salt or soy sauce.

Add the rice, water, mirin, soy sauce, sesame oil, and sliced onion to your rice cooker. Place the chicken thighs on top and cook on the regular white rice setting.

Once everything is done and the chicken is fully cooked, cut it into smaller pieces. Add ginger scallion sauce, mix it all together, and serve.

recipes.title: Healthy Tahini Cookies
recipes.author: lovinglylina
recipes.text: my healthy tahini cookies recipe!👇🏼😍🥠 so chewy, delicious, made of only 3(ish) nutritious ingredients, and super easy to make too!🙌🏼 i always make double batches because they don’t last long at our house!😋 ingredients: (makes ~ 12 cookies) 🍪3 cups almond flour 🍪1 cup tahini (make sure it’s made of 100% sesame) 🍪1/2 cup pure maple syrup or raw honey 🍪1/2 teaspoon baking soda 🍪sprinkle of sea salt optional: sesame seeds for topping directions: 🤎preheat oven to 350 f 🤎mix all ingredients in a bowl until it looks like cookie dough (if it feels too crumbly then add some more tahini) 🤎shape into balls and place on parchment-lined baking sheet 🤎press them down with your fingers or a fork and top with sesame seeds if using 🤎bake for 7 minutes ⚠️yes only 7 minutes! i know they will look raw at first but just leave them to cool down on the baking sheet, don’t move them anywhere until they’re completely cool, they will start to harden slightly but will still be super chewy!👌🏼😋 enjoy & don’t forget to let me know when you make them!😍📸
recipes.caption:
My Healthy Tahini Cookies recipe!👇🏼😍🥠

So chewy, delicious, made of only 3(ish) nutritious ingredients,  and super easy to make too!🙌🏼 I always make double batches because they don’t last long at our house!😋

Ingredients: (makes ~ 12 cookies) 
🍪3 cups almond flour 
🍪1 cup tahini (make sure it’s made of 100% sesame)
🍪1/2 cup pure maple syrup or raw honey 
🍪1/2 teaspoon baking soda
🍪sprinkle of sea salt
Optional: sesame seeds for topping

Directions:
🤎Preheat oven to 350 F 
🤎Mix all ingredients in a bowl until it looks like cookie dough (if it feels too crumbly then add some more tahini) 
🤎Shape into balls and place on parchment-lined baking sheet 
🤎Press them down with your fingers or a fork and top with sesame seeds if using
🤎Bake for 7 minutes 
⚠️Yes ONLY 7 minutes! I know they will look raw at first but just leave them to cool down on the baking sheet, don’t move them anywhere until they’re completely cool, they will start to harden slightly but will still be super chewy!👌🏼😋 

ENJOY & don’t forget to let me know when you make them!😍📸

recipes.text: a little miso goes a long way, melting into the sauce for rich, savoury umami, while doubanjiang adds a gentle kick and thai basil brings it all to life 🌿🔥 you may have noticed i simply switch up the protein, ground beef, tofu, chicken, and it still works every time! 👍🏻🔥 as long as there’s plenty of fresh thai basil, you’re good to go 🌿👌🏻 spicy chicken basil stir-fry 👉🏻 main • chicken thighs, about 300g, cut into small pieces • a handful of thai basil 🌿 (or any basil) 👉🏻 chicken marinade • soy sauce, about 1 tsp (lee kum kee) • sesame oil, about 1 tsp (ottogi) • white pepper powder, about ¼ tsp • potato starch, about 1 tsp 👉🏻 aromatics: • 3 cloves garlic, minced • minced ginger, about 1 tbsp • 3 shallots, sliced • ¼ onion, chopped 👉🏻 sauce & cooking: • doubanjiang, 1 tsp (lee kum kee) • white miso, 1 tsp (hikari) • soy sauce, about 1 tsp (lee kum kee) • sweet soy sauce, about 1 tsp (lee kum kee) 👉🏻 to serve: serve with warm rice, top with a crispy fried egg, then finish with fresh chopped green onions and a sprinkle of crushed toasted sesame seeds 🍚👏🏻😋
recipes.caption:
A little miso goes a long way, melting into the sauce for rich, savoury umami, while doubanjiang adds a gentle kick and Thai basil brings it all to life 🌿🔥

As long as there’s plenty of fresh Thai basil, you’re good to go 🌿👌🏻

Spicy Chicken Basil Stir-Fry

👉🏻 Main
 • Chicken thighs, about 300g, cut into small pieces
 • A handful of Thai basil 🌿 (or any basil)

👉🏻 Chicken Marinade
 • Soy sauce, about 1 tsp (Lee Kum Kee)
 • Sesame oil, about 1 tsp (Ottogi)
 • White pepper powder, about ¼ tsp
 • Potato starch, about 1 tsp

👉🏻 Aromatics:
 • 3 cloves garlic, minced
 • Minced ginger, about 1 tbsp

 Serve with warm rice, top with a crispy fried egg, then finish with fresh chopped green onions and a sprinkle of crushed toasted sesame seeds 🍚👏🏻😋

recipes.caption:
⇩ Full Recipe 🍗 ⇩

Macros per serving:

Protein: 49g
Carbs: 53g
Fat: 10g
Calories: 531

Ingredients per serving (makes 2 servings):

[Chicken]

- 1 lb skinless, boneless, chicken thighs, raw
- 1/2 tsp white pepper
- 1 tsp Chinese five spice powder
- 1.5 tbsp minced garlic
- 1 tbsp minced ginger
- 1 tbsp Shaoxing wine
- 2 tbsp soy sauce
- 3/4 cup coarse potato starch
- 1 egg (egg white only, no yolk)
- 1 second spray cooking oil

[Toppings]

- 1/2 tsp salt
- 1/2 tsp five spice powder
- 1/2 tsp brown sugar
- 1/2 tsp white pepper
- 1 cup Thai basil

How to make it yourself:

1. Dice your chicken thighs into small 1 inch pieces.
2. In a bowl, mix together white pepper, Chinese 5 spice powder, minced garlic, minced ginger, Shaoxing wine, soy sauce, and the egg white of an egg (no yolk) to make your marinade.
3. Add your chicken pieces into the marinade and set aside for 30 minutes or overnight in the refrigerator.
4. Pour your potato starch onto a plate and fully coat your chicken pieces into the potato starch.
5. Coat your air fryer tray with spray oil, place your chicken coated with potato starch into the tray, and lightly spray your chicken with more oil.
6. Cook in your air fryer at 390°F for 13-15 minutes, flipping halfway through or until crispy and golden brown.
7. Add in your Thai basil on top of the cooked chicken and air fryer for another 2-3 minutes.
8. In a bowl, mix together salt, 5 spice powder, brown sugar, and white pepper and sprinkle the seasoning mix on top of your cooked chicken and enjoy!

📩 Save this Taiwanese popcorn chicken recipe to make for later and if you make it, post it and tag me in it! I’d love to see how you liked the recipe! :)

recipes.caption:
Liquid Gold Chicken Bowl 🍗🍚

A comforting bowl of tender shredded chicken, fresh ginger, scallions and coriander, brought together with a hot, savoury broth, soy and oyster sauce. Light, aromatic and deeply comforting — the perfect soul-warming bowl.

Ingredients ( serves 2 )
2 chicken legs + 2 chicken thighs
20 g ginger
25 g scallions
15 g coriander
1–2 whole red chillies
1 tbsp chilli oil
1 tbsp soy sauce
1 tbsp oyster sauce
½ tsp white pepper
Salt, to taste
Cooked rice
Half cube of Stock

Method

Place an inverted small bowl inside a larger bowl and arrange the chicken over it. Add ginger, scallions and red chilli.

Place the bowl in a water bath, cover and steam for 15–20 minutes.

Meanwhile, finely chop ginger, scallions and coriander and mix with chilli oil.

Remove the chicken, then carefully take out the inverted bowl and save those juices — that's the liquid gold. Shred the chicken into strips.

Add 100Mls of hot water and mix it with half a cube of stock and mix it well in the broth.

Mix the flavour bomb with salt, white pepper, soy sauce and oyster sauce. Add the shredded chicken and finish with the hot broth.

Serve over hot rice and enjoy! 🍗🔥

recipes.caption:
SALTED CARAMELISED DATE FRO-YO

Creamy, tangy frozen yoghurt blended with sticky caramelised dates, tahini and a little salt. Served with even more caramelised dates, a good glug of olive oil and a pinch of flaky salt — ridiculously good x

[Ingredients]
500g thick Greek yoghurt
2–3 tbsp honey, plus more to taste
200g Medjool dates, pitted
1 tbsp tahini
Pinch of salt

To serve:
Extra caramelised dates
Extra virgin olive oil
Flaky salt

[Method]
1. Mix the Greek yoghurt with the honey. Spread in a relatively thin, even layer over a lined baking tray or dish, then freeze for around 2–3 hours, or until completely firm.
2. Meanwhile, halve the dates. Warm some olive oil in a frying pan over medium heat, then add the dates and cook for a few minutes, until soft, sticky and beginning to caramelise. Remove from the heat and allow to cool completely.
3. Set aside a few of the caramelised dates for serving, then add the rest to a high-powered blender or food processor with the tahini and a small pinch of salt. Blitz until a crumb is formed. 
4. Break the frozen yoghurt into shards and add to the blender. Blitz until thick, smooth and creamy, but with little pieces of caramelised date still running throughout. You may need to stop and scrape down the sides a few times.
5. Taste and adjust with a little extra honey or salt if needed, then spoon into a freezer-safe dish. Cover and freeze for another 1-2 hours, or until firm but scoopable.
6. Scoop into bowls and serve with a couple of extra caramelised dates, a good glug of olive oil and a pinch of flaky salt. 

Hope you love, 
Manuela x
recipes.recipe_ingredients:
500g thick Greek yoghurt
2–3 tbsp honey, plus more to taste
200g Medjool dates, pitted
1 tbsp tahini
Pinch of salt
Extra caramelised dates
Extra virgin olive oil
Flaky salt
recipes.recipe_method:
Mix the Greek yoghurt with the honey. Spread in a relatively thin, even layer over a lined baking tray or dish, then freeze for around 2–3 hours, or until completely firm.
Meanwhile, halve the dates. Warm some olive oil in a frying pan over medium heat, then add the dates and cook for a few minutes, until soft, sticky and beginning to caramelise. Remove from the heat and allow to cool completely.
Set aside a few of the caramelised dates for serving, then add the rest to a high-powered blender or food processor with the tahini and a small pinch of salt. Blitz until a crumb is formed.
Break the frozen yoghurt into shards and add to the blender. Blitz until thick, smooth and creamy, but with little pieces of caramelised date still running throughout. You may need to stop and scrape down the sides a few times.
Taste and adjust with a little extra honey or salt if needed, then spoon into a freezer-safe dish. Cover and freeze for another 1-2 hours, or until firm but scoopable.
Scoop into bowls and serve with a couple of extra caramelised dates, a good glug of olive oil and a pinch of flaky salt.

recipes.recipe_ingredients:
cauliflower
flour
chickpea flour
spices
water
cornflakes
nutritional yeast
oil spray
creamy herb dip
recipes.recipe_method:
Remove the leaves from a whole head of cauliflower, cut out the stem, break it into florets, and wash them.
Boil the florets until fork-tender.
Mix flour with chickpea flour, spices, and water to create a thick batter.
Crush cornflakes with nutritional yeast for the crunchy outer coating.
Dip each boiled floret in the batter, then in the crumbs.
Place them in an air fryer basket, spray with oil, and cook until crispy.
Serve with a creamy herb dip.

recipes.title: Creamy Malai Broccoli
recipes.author: shameemskitchenrecipe
recipes.text: 🥦creamy & healthy malai broccoli | guilt-free air fryer snack..😋🔥 👉🏻required ingredients 1 cup broccoli florets ½ cup hung curd 1 tsp ginger–garlic paste 1 tsp crushed green chillies 2 tsp cornflour 2 tsp mozzarella cheese (grated) 1 tsp lemon juice 2 tsp fresh cream ½ tsp black pepper powder 1 tsp chaat masala ½ tsp salt (or to taste) 1 tsp kasuri methi (crushed) 1 tsp chilli flakes 1 tsp oregan 📌 steps 👉step 1: in a bowl, mix all the ingredients to make a smooth marinade. 👉step 2: add the broccoli florets and coat them evenly with the marinade. 👉step 3: preheat the air fryer and cook at 180°c for 10–12 minutes. 👉step 4: once soft and lightly golden, remove from the air fryer. 👉step 5: serve hot and enjoy your creamy & healthy malai broccoli
recipes.caption:
🥦Creamy & Healthy Malai Broccoli | Guilt-Free Air Fryer Snack..😋🔥

#broccoli #malaibroccoli #creamy #airfryer #healthysnacking

1 cup broccoli florets
½ cup hung curd
1 tsp ginger–garlic paste
1 tsp crushed green chillies
2 tsp cornflour
2 tsp mozzarella cheese (grated)
1 tsp lemon juice
2 tsp fresh cream
½ tsp black pepper powder

recipes.text: something i needed to address ❤️ if you want recipes that are cheap, fast, and free from diet culture then follow me! chocolate self saucing pudding recipe 🍫 total cost: $3 approx!! ingredients: 1/3 cup brown sugar (you can use white sugar) 1 cup flour (you can use gf flour) 1 tsp baking powder 1/3 cup cocoa pinch of salt 1 egg (or 1 flax egg/ grated apple) 1/2 cup milk (use any milk you like) 3 tbsp oil or melted butter for the sauce: 1/4 cup cocoa powder 3/4 cup brown sugar 2 cups boiling water method: heat oven to 180 degrees celcius. mix together sugar, flour, baking powder, cocoa, and salt. add in the egg, milk and oil and stir until combined. place in an oven proof dish. in another bowl combine the cocoa and sugar. sprinkle over the top of the batter. pour over the hot water. bake for around 35 minutes - the cake should rise to the top and the sauce will be underneath! serve hot! you can also reheat this ❤️

recipes.caption:
Sticky Peanut Chicken Noodles 🥜🌶️

Protein: 60 g | Fibre: 10 g | Plant points: 11

INGREDIENTS (serves 2)

Peanut noodles
• 250 g / 9 oz ready cooked udon noodles
• 50 g / 1 3/4 oz smooth peanut butter
• 1 tbsp white miso
• 1 tbsp soy sauce
• 1 tbsp rice vinegar
• 2 tbsp lime juice
• 2 tsp honey or maple syrup
• 1 tsp fresh ginger, grated
• 70 to 100 ml / 2 1/2 to 3 1/2 fl oz warm water

Sticky chicken
• 400 g / 14 oz lean ground chicken breast
• 1 tbsp extra virgin olive oil
• 2 garlic cloves, grated
• 1 tsp fresh ginger, grated
• 1 tbsp gochujang
• 1 tbsp reduced sodium soy sauce
• 2 tsp rice vinegar
• 2 tsp honey or brown sugar
• 1/2 to 1 tsp chili flakes

Crunchy slaw
• 300 g / 10 1/2 oz cabbage, finely shredded
• 1 large cucumber, about 300 g / 10 1/2 oz, thinly sliced
• 4 scallions, sliced
• 20 g / 3/4 oz cilantro, chopped
• 10 g / 1/3 oz mint, torn
• Juice of 1/2 lime
• 2 tsp rice vinegar
• Pinch sea salt

To finish
• 25 g / 1 oz roasted walnuts, crushed
• Extra cilantro, mint, lime and chili flakes

METHOD

Whisk peanut butter, miso, soy, vinegar, lime, honey and ginger with 70 ml / 2 1/2 fl oz warm water until glossy, adding more water if needed.
Combine cabbage, cucumber and scallions. Keep herbs, lime, vinegar and salt separate until serving.
Mix garlic, ginger, gochujang, soy, vinegar, honey, chili and pepper. Heat oil in a wide skillet, press chicken into a thin layer and leave untouched 2-3 minutes until deeply golden.
Break up chicken, cook 2 to 3 minutes more, then add the gochujang mixture and toss 1 to 2 minutes until sticky and caramelized.
Prepare udon according to package directions, drain, then toss in the same skillet with peanut sauce for 1-2 minutes until glossy.
Toss slaw with herbs, lime, vinegar and salt. Divide noodles between bowls, top with chicken and slaw, then finish with peanuts, herbs, chili and lime.

recipes.title: Gochujang Butter Noodles
recipes.author: _dishcovery
recipes.text: comment “recipe” and i’ll send you the full recipe in your dms. make sure to follow so that i can dm you 🫶 after being completely starstruck by my gochujang butter noodles with caramelized onions, i couldn’t stop thinking about that combination. there was something about the way deeply sweet onions melted into a rich buttery sauce that felt too good not to explore further. so naturally, i went in a totally different direction and landed here. this version swaps the spicy kick for something softer and deeper. the onions slowly caramelize until they’re jammy and golden, the butter adds pure comfort, the white miso brings that savory fermented umami that makes you keep reaching for another bite, and the miso rayu adds a subtle tingle that ties everything together. it’s cozy, rich, and surprisingly simple, with every thick udon noodle coated in a silky sauce that tastes like it took way more effort than it actually did. if you’re looking for an easy noodle dish that feels restaurant-worthy but uses a handful of pantry staples, this one is for you.
recipes.caption:

After being completely starstruck by my gochujang butter noodles with caramelized onions, I couldn’t stop thinking about that combination. There was something about the way deeply sweet onions melted into a rich buttery sauce that felt too good not to explore further. So naturally, I went in a totally different direction and landed here.

This version swaps the spicy kick for something softer and deeper. The onions slowly caramelize until they’re jammy and golden, the butter adds pure comfort, the @wearesaitaku white miso brings that savory fermented umami that makes you keep reaching for another bite, and the @uce.rayu miso rayu adds a subtle tingle that ties everything together. It’s cozy, rich, and surprisingly simple, with every thick udon noodle coated in a silky sauce that tastes like it took way more effort than it actually did.

If you’re looking for an easy noodle dish that feels restaurant-worthy but uses a handful of pantry staples, this one is for you.

udon noodles
starchy noodle water

chives
black sesame seeds
fried onions

recipes.recipe_method:
Add sliced onions to a pan and caramelize them low and slow.
Meanwhile, whisk together honey, soy sauce, and white miso paste in a small cup, then loosen the sauce with starchy noodle water.
Cook the udon noodles separately.
Once the onions are deeply golden, melt butter and pressed garlic into them.
Toss the cooked noodles and miso sauce together until glossy.
Plate and garnish with chopped chives, black sesame seeds, extra fried onions, and a spoonful of miso rayu chili crisp.

recipes.title: Prawn Ginger Scallion Oil Noodles
recipes.author: therealchadli
recipes.text: ep.8 michelin on a minimum wage | prawn, ginger and scallion oil noodles 🍜🦐🫚 ingredients: • 3 portions of knife cut noodles • 200g prawns • greens ends of 4 bunches of green onions/scallions • 4 tbsp of minced ginger • 2 tbsp dark soy • 2 tbsp sweet soy (kecap manis) • 1 packet of ramen seasoning of your choice (or bullion seasoning) • 150ml sesame oil method: 1. heat up water in a pot until it starts boiling. add in your noodles and cook until softened. 2. heat a pan under a medium flame and add in sesame oil. once it’s hot, add your scallions and ginger. cook until slightly charred. 3. add in your shrimp, cook until pink (2-3 mins) then add your dark soy, sweet soy and ramen seasoning. 4. add in your noodles, mix and garnish with some chopped scallions.
recipes.caption:
EP.8 MICHELIN ON A MINIMUM WAGE | Prawn, Ginger and Scallion Oil Noodles 🍜🦐🫚

Ingredients:
•  3 portions of knife cut noodles 
•  200g prawns 
•  Greens ends of 4 bunches of green onions/scallions
•  4 tbsp of minced ginger 
•  2 tbsp dark soy 
•  2 tbsp sweet soy (kecap manis)
•  1 packet of ramen seasoning of your choice (or bullion seasoning)
•  150ml sesame oil 

Method:
1.  Heat up water in a pot until it starts boiling. Add in your noodles and cook until softened.
2.  Heat a pan under a medium flame and add in sesame oil. Once it’s hot, add your scallions and ginger. Cook until slightly charred.
3.  Add in your shrimp, cook until pink (2-3 mins) then add your dark soy, sweet soy and ramen seasoning. 
4.  Add in your noodles, mix and garnish with some chopped scallions.

recipes.title: Spiced-Butter Yogurt Eggs
recipes.author: ana.potard
recipes.text: spiced-butter yogurt eggs 🍳 creamy garlicky yogurt, jammy eggs, avocado and tomatoes, finished with warm spiced butter. i had it for lunch, but it would be just as good for breakfast or brunch! ingredients: 175 g / ¾ cup greek yogurt 1 garlic clove, minced juice of ½ lemon 2–3 tbsp olive oil a small bunch of parsley, chopped salt and pepper 2 soft-boiled eggs, halved ½ avocado, sliced 5–6 cherry tomatoes, halved for the spiced butter: 20 g / 1½ tbsp butter 1 tsp paprika ½ tsp chilli flakes 1 tsp turmeric, optional mix the yogurt with the garlic, lemon juice, olive oil, parsley, salt and pepper. spread it over a plate, then add the eggs, avocado and tomatoes. melt the butter over low heat. add the paprika, chilli flakes and turmeric, then let the spices gently infuse for 1–2 minutes without burning. drizzle the warm spiced butter over everything and serve with plenty of bread for dipping.
recipes.caption:
SPICED-BUTTER YOGURT EGGS 🍳

Creamy garlicky yogurt, jammy eggs, avocado and tomatoes, finished with warm spiced butter. I had it for lunch, but it would be just as good for breakfast or brunch!

Ingredients:

175 g / ¾ cup Greek yogurt
1 garlic clove, minced
Juice of ½ lemon
2–3 tbsp olive oil
A small bunch of parsley, chopped
Salt and pepper

2 soft-boiled eggs, halved
½ avocado, sliced
5–6 cherry tomatoes, halved

For the spiced butter:

20 g / 1½ tbsp butter
1 tsp paprika
½ tsp chilli flakes
1 tsp turmeric, optional

Mix the yogurt with the garlic, lemon juice, olive oil, parsley, salt and pepper. Spread it over a plate, then add the eggs, avocado and tomatoes.

Melt the butter over low heat. Add the paprika, chilli flakes and turmeric, then let the spices gently infuse for 1–2 minutes without burning.

Drizzle the warm spiced butter over everything and serve with plenty of bread for dipping.

recipes.caption:
i really did try to keep it simple but i got carried away as usual sorry 

(for the lemon oats) you’ll need:
- 1 small banana
- zest of 1 lemon
- 1 egg 
- 2tbsp honey / maple syrup
- 1/2 cup oats (about 40g)
- 1 knob of butter

(for the raspberry chia jam):
- 1 cup (a large handful) of fresh / frozen raspberries
- juice of 1/4 of a lemon
- 1 tbsp chia seeds 
- 1tbsp honey

(to serve):
- any yogurt you like!
- fresh strawberries, sliced into rounds
- any nut butter you like (i use almond!

method:
1. begin by roughly mashing the banana with a fork in a shallow bowl.

2. add in the lemon zest, honey, egg and oats and mix until thoroughly combined.

3. melt the butter in a small frying pan on a medium heat and begin to fry the oat mixture.

4. start scrambling it as if you were scrambling eggs!

5. it will begin to cluster so break it up as you go.

6. meanwhile, place the raspberries, lemon juice, chia seeds and honey in a small saucepan and place on a medium to high heat.

7. as soon as the raspberries begin to thaw and release their juices, lower the heat and keep stirring until you form a jam. remove from the heat.

8. once the oats are golden and clustered, remove from the heat.

9. begin to assemble your yogurt bowl by placing your yogurt of choice first and make a small well in the centre.

10. spoon the jam on top right in the centre…

11. then, layer on top the lemon oats into your corner of choice.

12. finish with the sliced strawberries, nut butter of choice and a drizzle of honey if you like…

enjoy!🍋🍋🍋

1tbsp honey

add in the lemon zest, honey, egg and oats and mix until thoroughly combined.
melt the butter in a small frying pan on a medium heat and begin to fry the oat mixture.
start scrambling it as if you were scrambling eggs!
it will begin to cluster so break it up as you go.
meanwhile, place the raspberries, lemon juice, chia seeds and honey in a small saucepan and place on a medium to high heat.
as soon as the raspberries begin to thaw and release their juices, lower the heat and keep stirring until you form a jam. remove from the heat.
once the oats are golden and clustered, remove from the heat.
begin to assemble your yogurt bowl by placing your yogurt of choice first and make a small well in the centre.
spoon the jam on top right in the centre…
then, layer on top the lemon oats into your corner of choice.
finish with the sliced strawberries, nut butter of choice and a drizzle of honey if you like…

recipes.title: Spicy Chicken Rice Noodle Bowl
recipes.author: modernflavour
recipes.text: the most comforting meal in a bowl 🤎 adding this ramen-inspired spicy chicken rice noodle bowl to our weekly rotation! recipe: 1. bring a medium pot of 4 cups chicken broth to a gentle simmer over medium heat. 2. add 2 cloves garlic and 1 tsp jarred ginger. simmer for 5 minutes to infuse the broth. 3. stir in 1 tbsp soy sauce, 1 tsp sesame oil, 1 tsp rice wine vinegar, 1 tbsp chili crisp, and a few cracks of black pepper. 4. add 2 cooked chicken chicken thighs and cook for another 3 to 4 minutes until heated through. 5. meanwhile, cook 100g rice noodles according to the package instructions. drain and divide between two serving bowls. 6. bring a small pot of water to a boil. carefully lower in 2 eggs and cook for 6½ to 7 minutes for jammy yolks. transfer immediately to an ice bath, peel, and cut in half. 7. ladle the hot broth and chicken over the noodles. 8. top each bowl with a soft-boiled egg, fresh cilantro, sesame seeds, and a generous squeeze of fresh lime before serving. follow for more easy recipes you’ll actually make again 🤎
recipes.caption:

recipes.title: Egg Salad Sandwich
recipes.author: helenhtaylor
recipes.text: not my mums bread so not sure how chic this can possible be (pretty delish though)🤣🤷🏼‍♀️ you’ll need: - 3 eggs - 1/2 red onion, finely chopped - a small handful of fresh dill, roughly chopped - 2tsp dijon mustard - 2tbsp mayonnaise - pinch of sea salt & pepper (to serve): - fresh/ toasted sourdough (or any bread) - fresh cucumber, thinly sliced method: 1. place the eggs in cold water and set on a high heat until boiling. as soon as they start boiling, set the timer for 7 mins. 2. meanwhile, finely chop the onion & dill. 3. once the eggs have boiled, either place into an ice bath or drain the water and fill back up with cold water and allow the eggs to sit for a few minutes. 4. carefully peel the shell and place the eggs into a medium sized, wide bowl. 5. roughly mash with a fork and add in the onion, dill, mustard, mayo and seasoning. mix until thoroughly combined. 6. top the mixture on either toasted or fresh bread and finish with some slices of fresh cucumber. enjoy xxx🥚🥒

recipes.caption:
Read below for the reason (and recipe)👇

The hard decisions we have to make when revamping our systems include killing off a couple drinks.

Purple Rice Yogurt has been my favorite drink since we’ve opened our doors, but that doesn’t mean it’ll be everyone else’s favorite. Our sales just didn’t support the additional single-item ingredients and prep work behind it. So after several conversations and internal battles, we have decided to discontinue the Purple Rice Yogurt.

Now I know there are die hard fans of this drink, and it really was so difficult for us to stop serving it, so here’s a present from us - the recipe to the Purple Rice Yogurt (PRY) 📖🎁

Ingredients
- 1/2 cup Coconut Milk
- 1 cup Greek Yogurt
- 1 1/2 cup of ice
- 2 tablespoons simple syrup (honey works too)
- 1/4 cup Black Rice

1. Blend together the coconut milk, yogurt, ice & simple syrup until it reaches a smoothie consistency
2. Add the black rice and pulse at a low speed
3. Pour into a glass and enjoy

Tips:
- Don’t use thick coconut milk. Think the vegan milks you find in the dairy aisle of your local store
- Greek yogurt is a must for the best taste and texture
- You can decrease the simple syrup depending on how sweet you like your drink (I personally use half the amount)
- If your drink is too icy, then add a little more coconut milk and reblend before adding the rice
- To preserve the structure of the rice, it is important to not over blend after adding the rice
- Purple rice can be found at many Asian grocery stores. It sometimes goes by different names, like Black Berry Rice, Black Rice, or Forbidden Rice. A good rule of thumb is to look for the rice with more dark grains instead of the tricolor grains.

And to those that have tried PRY and loved it, thank you for appreciating it while it was here with us 💞 we really lost a good one 😭

Last day you can get it is tonight 5/31/2026 🙇🏻‍♀️

recipes.title: Mango Coconut Oatmeal
recipes.author: helenhtaylor
recipes.text: i’m defrosting my summer breakfast ideas and i love it (next time i promise to attempt your mango art )💛 you’ll need: - 1 egg - 1/2 cup rolled oats - 1 cup any milk (i use whole) - 2tbsp honey / maple syrup - 2tbsp dessicated coconut (to serve): - fresh mango, cubed - dessicated coconut - extra honey (optional) method: 1. begin by placing the egg, oats, milk, honey and coconut in a small saucepan and place on a medium to low heat. 2. whisk continuously until the porridge begins to gain some heat (it will start releasing some steam). 3. lower the heat to the lowest and continue whisking for about 5-6 minutes or until the porridge is beautifully silky and creamy! 4. remove from the heat, serve with freshly sliced mango, a sprinkle of extra coconut and a drizzle of honey… enjoy xxx🥭

recipes.recipe_ingredients:
3.2 oz Nasoya Organic Super Firm Tofu 2 servings, 182 grams
1 cup Kodiak Cakes Power Cakes Flapjack and Waffle Mix
28 gram Truvani Unflavored Plant based protein powder can be sub with Kodiak mix
30 gram Anthony's Vital Wheat Gluten (1/4 cup) can be sub with Kodiak Mix or Sooji
1½ cup Minced Cabbage easy to mince in food processor
1 inch Ginger
3 Thai Green Chili
2 large Galic Cloves
1¼ tsp Salt
¼ tsp Turmeric Powder
2 tsp Cumin Coriander Powder
¼ tsp Garam Masala
½ tsp Red Chili Powder
⅓ cup Fat Free Plain Greek Yogurt, 85 grams
⅓ cup Freshly Chopped Cilantro
For Tempering
2 tbsp Avocado Oil choice of oil with high smoking point
1 tsp Mustard Seeds
1 tbsp White Sesame Seeds
⅛ tsp Asafetida, Hing
4 Curry Leaves
recipes.recipe_method:
Press tofu and pat dry using paper towel to remove as much moisture as possible. Shred 2 servings from the whole block. Place it in a big mixing bowl.
Process cabbage in a food processor, Place it in a big mixing bowl along with shredded tofu.
Process ginger, garlic, thai green chili using food processor, Place it in a big mixing bowl along with cabbage.
In the same mixing bowl, place Kodiak mix, vital wheat gluten, Truvani unflavored protein powder along with salt, turmeric powder, red chili powder, garam masala, cumin coriander powder and greek yogurt.
Mix everything together to form a dough. Divide dough into 4-6 big chunks. The dough should be soft enough to make a cylinder like shapes using your hands. Make 4-5 dough cylinders.
You should not need water to form the dough, but if you have hard time forming the shape and keeping it together feel free to add little water at a time until you get the good consistency of the dough. Take some oil between your palms if it is super sticky.
If using steamer for steaming, start boiling water at the bottom of the steamer. Grease the steamer plate and place dough cylinders in it.
If using Instant Pot, Add 2-4 cups of water in the pot of the Instant Pot. Place Steamer Rack Stand at the bottom of the pot and put IP on saute mode. Let the water come to boil. Place cylinder shaped dough in a greased stainless steel plates/thali, thali with a little less diameter than IP pot diameter.
Place the thali/plate inside the steamer (if using steamer) OR on top of the steamer rack stand inside the Instant Pot.
If using steamer, close the steamer lid tight, and steam on high heat for 20 minutes. If using IP, close the lid, seal the valve, secure/seal the valve and put IP on steam mode for 20 minutes. Once timer goes off, let the pressure release for 15-20 minutes. Release rest of the pressure manually
Once muthiya is steamed, take the thhali/plate out of the steamer/IP, let it cool down for 10-15 minutes.
Once cooled down to handle, cut them in decent size pieces.
Tempering of Muthiya
Heat 2 tbsp oil in a flat wide pan. (non stick would work the best)
Once hot, add mustard seeds and sesame seeds. Once done splattering, add a pinch of asafetida and curry leaves. Then Immediately add cut muthiya and give it a gentle toss.
Keep cooking on medium heat until you reach desired crispiness. Keep tossing them at every few minutes to make sure it gets evenly crispy.
Garnish it with fresh cilantro. Serve it hot with sprinkle of thin sev and side of masala chai!!

recipes.title: Egg White Oats
recipes.author: liftwsarah
recipes.text: high protein breakfast: how to make egg white oats that don’t taste like scrambled eggs. three things go wrong: 1. not enough water don’t cook the oats down completely. you want them still sitting in a little starchy liquid before the egg whites go in, so the whites distribute evenly and thicken gradually instead of catching in the oats and scrambling. 2. heat too high pour egg whites into boiling oats and you have made scrambled eggs. turn the heat right down first. pour them in while whisking, until it’s frothy and combined. then back up to medium and cook until thick. 3. cooking too long once they’re thick and creamy, off the heat. the base (~30g protein, no protein powder):30g oats, 100ml water, 200ml oat milk, pinch of salt, 200g egg whites, 1 tsp vanilla, ⅛ tsp pure stevia (or 20g sweetener of choice)simmer the oats. drop the heat right down. whisk the egg whites in until foamy. back up to medium, whisk until thick. off the heat, then flavour and top however you like. done properly they should be thick, and delicious!! egg white oats e-book full of every recipe i’ve done on my website!
recipes.caption:
High protein breakfast: how to make egg white oats that don’t taste like scrambled eggs.
Three things go wrong:

1. NOT ENOUGH WATER 
don’t cook the oats down completely. You want them still sitting in a little starchy liquid before the egg whites go in, so the whites distribute evenly and thicken gradually instead of catching in the oats and scrambling.

2. HEAT TOO HIGH 
pour egg whites into boiling oats and you have made scrambled eggs. Turn the heat right down first. Pour them in while whisking, until it’s frothy and combined. Then back up to medium and cook until thick.

3. COOKING TOO LONG 
once they’re thick and creamy, off the heat. 

THE BASE (~30g protein, no protein powder):30g oats, 100ml water, 200ml oat milk, pinch of salt, 200g egg whites, 1 tsp vanilla, ⅛ tsp pure stevia (or 20g sweetener of choice)Simmer the oats. Drop the heat right down. Whisk the egg whites in until foamy. Back up to medium, whisk until thick. Off the heat, then flavour and top however you like.
Done properly they should be thick, and delicious!!

recipes.title: Mushroom Onion Roll-Ups
recipes.author: shivangipithisaria
recipes.text: pov: you have an airfryer ep.27 ⭐️ caramelised mushroom roll ups 🍄‍🟫 recipe: https://shivangikooks.com/mushroom-onion-roll-ups/ or comment “shroom” to get the recipe in your dms 🧅
recipes.caption:
pov: you have an airfryer ep.27 ⭐️ caramelised mushroom roll ups 🍄‍🟫

recipe: https://shivangikooks.com/mushroom-onion-roll-ups/

or comment “shroom” to get the recipe in your dms 🧅
recipes.recipe_ingredients:
Mushroom filling
1 pack (200 g) mushrooms
1/4 cup walnuts
5 garlic cloves
2 red onion, sliced
salt and pepper, to taste
1-2 tbsp extra virgin olive oil
1 tbsp soy sauce
1 tsp balsamic vinegar
Garlic butter
3 tbsp salted butter, melted
3 cloves garlic, minced
2 tbsp chopped coriander
1 tsp chilli flakes
1/2 tsp dried or fresh thyme
Green sauce
1/4 cup curd or yogurt
2 tbsp cream cheese
handful of fresh coriander
handful of fresh mint
juice of 1/2 lemon
5 cloves garlic
salt, to taste
1/4 cup ice
More
3 tortilla
recipes.recipe_method:
For the mushroom filling: In a baking tray or baking tin, add mushrooms, walnuts, sliced onions and garlic. Season with salt and pepper and drizzle with olive oil and give everything a good mix to make sure everything is well coated.
Airfry at 180°C for 20–25 minutes, or bake at 190°C for 25–30 minutes, mixing halfway through till the mushrooms and onions are deeply browned and caramelised. Let the mixture cool completely.
Add the roasted mixture to a blender and pulse a few times to get a coarse mixture. Mix in the soy sauce and balsamic vinegar and your rich, umami packed filling is ready.
For the garlic butter: Simply mix melted butter with minced garlic, chopped coriander, chilli flakes and thyme.
Take a tortilla and spread the mushroom filling generously all over it. Roll it tightly from bottom to top to form a log. Using a sharp knife, divide the log into smaller pieces. Thread each piece onto a skewer to make the roll ups, I arranged five roll ups on each skewer but you can add as many as you like.
Brush the garlic butter generously all over the roll ups and airfry at 180°C for 10–15 minutes till the tortilla is crispy and the tops are golden brown. Brush with some more garlic butter immediately after taking them out of the air fryer.
For the green sauce: To serve, I wanted a fresh, tangy and savoury sauce to cut through the rich mushroom filling so I made this simple herby cream cheese sauce. Add fresh coriander, fresh mint, yogurt, cream cheese, lemon juice, garlic, salt and ice to a blender and blend till completely smooth.
Drizzle the green sauce all over the tortilla roll ups and enjoyy!

recipes.caption:
A bowl you’ll never get tired of, whether you prefer to enjoy it with noodles or warm rice, both work beautifully! 😋🍜🍚👌🏻 

You’ve got golden-brown tofu, crunchy bean sprouts, refreshing cucumber, and that creamy, nutty, slightly spicy peanut dressing, then finish it all with fried onions, toasted sesame, and prawn crackers. So much flavour in one bowl! 🤤👌🏻 

👉🏻 Ingredients: 
• ½ block firm tofu, cut into small cubes and dry-seared until golden brown
• A handful of fresh bean sprouts
• 1 small cucumber, sliced
• 1 green onion, chopped

👉🏻 Homemade Peanut Dressing: 
• 2 tbsp peanut butter (Skippy)
• 2 tbsp chili sauce (Din Tai Fung)
• 1 tsp sweet soy sauce (Lee Kum Kee Sweet Soy Sauce for Dim Sum)
• 1 tsp soy sauce (Lee Kum Kee First Draw Authentic)
• ¼ tsp rice vinegar (Din Tai Fung)
• 1 tsp sesame oil (Ottogi)
• 50 ml water 

👉🏻 To Finish: 
Chopped green onions, fried onions, crushed toasted sesame seeds, and prawn crackers 👌🏻

Simple, fresh, nutty, savoury, and so satisfying. 😋
Honestly, this is the kind of bowl I could happily eat again and again! 🥜🍜🍚

NOTE:
• Don’t like raw bean sprouts? Just blanch them briefly before adding. 👌🏻
• Prefer fried tofu instead? Go for it! Both work beautifully 👌🏻

• My Honest Tofu Method: Why My Tofu Always Looks Dry 

1. Open/peel back about ⅛ of the plastic cover.
2. Drain out the original water.
3. Do not remove the tofu from the package.
4. Put the package upside down in a bowl, with the opening facing downward.
5. Store it in the refrigerator overnight.
6. The water/moisture will gradually drain into the bowl.
By tomorrow, or even after 1–2 days, the tofu can lose a substantial amount of excess water, especially if it’s soft or medium tofu.
And then it’s ready to cook! 👌🏻

recipes.title: Mocha Overnight Oats
recipes.author: the_balanced_dish
recipes.text: creamy, chocolatey, and packed with protein—this mocha overnight oats is the perfect make-ahead breakfast for busy mornings. recipe below: 👇 (1 serving) ingredients oats base - ⅓ cup rolled oats - 1 tbsp chia seeds - 1 tbsp cocoa powder - ½ tbsp maple syrup - ½ tsp vanilla extract - 1 shot espresso - ⅓ cup greek yogurt, plain, 2% fat - ⅓ cup 2% milk toppings - ½ cup greek yogurt, plain, 2% fat - 1-2 tbsp semi-sweet chocolate chips - ½ tbsp 2% milk method 1. mix the oats, chia seeds, cocoa powder, maple syrup, vanilla extract, espresso, greek yogurt, and milk in a jar until well combined. 2. cover and refrigerate overnight, or for at least 4 hours. 3. when ready to eat, microwave the chocolate chips and milk for 30 seconds to 1 minute in 20-second bursts, stirring between each burst. 4. top with greek yogurt, drizzle the melted chocolate overtop, and serve. ✅ nutrition info (per serving): 480 kcal; 28g protein; 60g total carbs; 10g fiber; 20g fat enjoy! ❤️
recipes.caption:
Creamy, chocolatey, and packed with protein—this mocha overnight oats is the perfect make-ahead breakfast for busy mornings.  Recipe below: 👇 (1 serving)

INGREDIENTS

Oats base
- ⅓ cup Rolled oats
- 1 tbsp Chia seeds
- 1 tbsp Cocoa powder 
- ½ tbsp Maple syrup
- ½ tsp Vanilla extract
- 1 shot Espresso
- ⅓ cup Greek yogurt, plain, 2% fat
- ⅓ cup 2% Milk

Toppings
- ½ cup Greek yogurt, plain, 2% fat
- 1-2 tbsp Semi-sweet chocolate chips
- ½ tbsp 2% Milk

METHOD

1. Mix the oats, chia seeds, cocoa powder, maple syrup, vanilla extract, espresso, Greek yogurt, and milk in a jar until well combined.
2. Cover and refrigerate overnight, or for at least 4 hours.
3. When ready to eat, microwave the chocolate chips and milk for 30 seconds to 1 minute in 20-second bursts, stirring between each burst.
4. Top with Greek yogurt, drizzle the melted chocolate overtop, and serve.

✅ Nutrition Info (Per Serving):
480 kcal; 28g protein; 60g total carbs; 10g fiber; 20g fat

Enjoy! ❤️

recipes.text: hainanese chicken rice in a rice cooker is one of the dishes i always come back to because it’s actually fool-proof. i’m jasmine, a korean-american mom of 2 & this is my series, lazy girl dinners where i make easy asian-inspired meals the whole family will actually enjoy!! comment “chicken” and i’ll send you the recipe to your inbox! lazy girl dinners, ep 18: hainanese chicken rice (rice cooker) 🍗🍚 ingredients: 5 boneless chicken thighs (skin on preferred) 2 cups chicken broth 1.5 cups rice 4 cloves garlic 2 tsp minced ginger 1 stalk green onion ginger garlic scallion oil💚: 2 stalks green onions, thinly sliced ½ cup neutral oil (i used avocado) 1 tbsp minced ginger ½ tbsp minced garlic salt to taste steps: rinse rice and add to rice cooker with broth, garlic, ginger and green onion stalk (no need to chop the green onions). stir to combine. season chicken with salt, white pepper and a tiny bit of sesame oil. place chicken on top of rice, skin side up if using skin on. set rice cooker to regular cooking function and let it do its thing. when done, remove chicken and cut into 1 inch pieces. fluff rice and plate with chicken generously drizzled with the garlic ginger scallion oil and serve with fresh cucumbers! for the oil: heat oil in a pan, add ginger, garlic and green onions to a jar, pour hot oil over and add salt to taste. linkdm *006*

recipes.title: Steamed Chicken, Chili Scallion Sauce
recipes.author: yourpetpooja
recipes.text: spicy steamed chicken with chili scallion sauce ingredients and way to go about it: for the chicken * 2 chicken breasts * 2–3 slices ginger * 2 scallions / spring onions * 2–3 cloves * 1 tsp whole peppercorns * salt, to taste * water, for poaching for the spicy sauce * 2 tbsp chopped spring onions * 1 tsp ginger-garlic paste * red chilli, chopped (as much as you like) * 2 tbsp hot oil * 1 tbsp soy sauce * 1 tbsp chili oil * 1 tbsp oyster sauce * 1 tsp sesame seeds * 2–3 tbsp reserved chicken stock method 1. in a pot, add water along with ginger, scallions, cloves, peppercorns, and salt. bring it to a gentle simmer. 2. add the chicken breasts and gently poach for about 10 minutes. avoid aggressively boiling the chicken — this keeps it soft and juicy. 3. check if the chicken is cooked by poking it with a chopstick or toothpick. if the juices run clear, it’s done. 4. shred the chicken into chunky pieces or thin threads — however you like it. 5. for the sauce, combine chopped spring onions, ginger-garlic paste, and red chilli in a bowl. pour hot oil over it to make everything fragrant. 6. add soy sauce, chili oil, oyster sauce, sesame seeds, and a little of the reserved chicken stock to bring the sauce together. 7. pour the sauce all over the shredded chicken and serve immediately. your daily protein intake does not have to be boring. try this once and you will not regret it.
recipes.caption:
Spicy Steamed Chicken with Chili Scallion Sauce

Ingredients and way to go about it:

For the Chicken

* 2 chicken breasts
* 2–3 slices ginger
* 2 scallions / spring onions
* 2–3 cloves
* 1 tsp whole peppercorns
* Salt, to taste
* Water, for poaching

For the Spicy Sauce

* 2 tbsp chopped spring onions
* 1 tsp ginger-garlic paste
* Red chilli, chopped (as much as you like)
* 2 tbsp hot oil
* 1 tbsp soy sauce
* 1 tbsp chili oil
* 1 tbsp oyster sauce
* 1 tsp sesame seeds
* 2–3 tbsp reserved chicken stock

Method

1. In a pot, add water along with ginger, scallions, cloves, peppercorns, and salt. Bring it to a gentle simmer.
2. Add the chicken breasts and gently poach for about 10 minutes. Avoid aggressively boiling the chicken — this keeps it soft and juicy.
3. Check if the chicken is cooked by poking it with a chopstick or toothpick. If the juices run clear, it’s done.
4. Shred the chicken into chunky pieces or thin threads — however you like it.
5. For the sauce, combine chopped spring onions, ginger-garlic paste, and red chilli in a bowl. Pour hot oil over it to make everything fragrant.
6. Add soy sauce, chili oil, oyster sauce, sesame seeds, and a little of the reserved chicken stock to bring the sauce together.
7. Pour the sauce all over the shredded chicken and serve immediately.

Your daily protein intake does NOT have to be boring. Try this once and you will not regret it.

recipes.title: Ragi Chocolate Cookies
recipes.author: _let.her.cook__
recipes.text: the soft & chewy high-protein ragi chocolate cookie 🍪🤎 crispy around the edges, soft in the center, and loaded with melty chocolate. made with oats, ragi, and protein, this is the cookie you’ll want to bake on repeat. ingredients * ½ cup oats flour * ½ cup ragi flour * 35 g protein powder (1 sachet) * 3 tbsp unsalted butter (softened) * 5 tbsp milk * ⅓ cup brown sugar * ½ dark chocolate chunks (2 tbsp) * ¼ tsp baking soda * ¼ tsp baking powder * ¼ tsp salt method 🍪 cream the softened butter and brown sugar until light and smooth. 🍪 add the protein powder, milk and mix until well combined. 🍪 add the oats flour, ragi flour, baking soda, baking powder, and salt. mix until a thick cookie dough forms. 🍪 fold in the dark chocolate chunks. 🍪 divide the dough 4 large cookies and place them on a lined baking tray. 🍪 airfry at 145°c for 10-12 minutes, until the edges are lightly golden and the center is just set. 🍪 let the cookies cool for 10 minutes before enjoying—they’ll continue to firm up as they cool
recipes.caption:
The Soft & Chewy High-Protein Ragi Chocolate Cookie 🍪🤎

Crispy around the edges, soft in the center, and loaded with melty chocolate. Made with oats, ragi, and protein, this is the cookie you’ll want to bake on repeat.

Ingredients

* ½ cup oats flour 
* ½ cup ragi flour
* 35 g protein powder (1 sachet)
* 3 tbsp unsalted butter (softened)
* 5 tbsp milk
* ⅓ cup brown sugar
* ½ dark chocolate chunks (2 tbsp)
* ¼ tsp baking soda
* ¼ tsp baking powder
* ¼ tsp salt

Method
🍪 Cream the softened butter and brown sugar until light and smooth.
🍪 Add the protein powder, milk and mix until well combined.
🍪 Add the oats flour, ragi flour, baking soda, baking powder, and salt. Mix until a thick cookie dough forms.
🍪 Fold in the dark chocolate chunks.
🍪 Divide the dough 4 large cookies and place them on a lined baking tray.
🍪 Airfry at 145°C for 10-12 minutes, until the edges are lightly golden and the center is just set.
🍪 Let the cookies cool for 10 minutes before enjoying—they’ll continue to firm up as they cool

recipes.caption:
Iron Matters Series | Episode 3: 5-Minute Oats, Banana & Raisin Pancakes | Neha Poddar
 
Iron plays a vital role in your baby's growth and development. It supports brain development, helps carry oxygen throughout the body, and is especially important from 6 months onwards, when a baby's natural iron stores begin to decrease.
 
If you're looking for an easy, naturally sweet, iron-rich breakfast, this recipe comes together in just 5 minutes and is perfect for busy mornings.
 
For even better iron absorption, pair it with a vitamin C-rich fruit such as orange, steamed guava, strawberries, or kiwi.
 
Oats, Banana & Raisin Pancakes
 
Makes: 3–4 small pancakes
 
Ingredients
 
• 2 tbsp oat flour
• 1 overripe banana
• 5 soaked black raisins
• Ghee for cooking
 
Optional (once introduced and allergens have been tested):
 
• 1 tsp nuts and seeds powder
 
Method
 
• Soak the black raisins until soft.
 
• Add the oat flour, overripe banana, and soaked raisins to a blender. Blend until you have a smooth batter.
 
• Once your baby has had this recipe a few times and all nuts and seeds have been safely introduced, you can blend in 1 teaspoon of nuts and seeds powder for an extra nutritional boost.
 
• Heat a pan on medium flame and lightly grease it with ghee.
 
• Pour small portions of the batter onto the pan and cook until bubbles appear. Flip and cook the other side until golden.
 
• Serve warm with a vitamin C-rich fruit such as orange slices, steamed guava, strawberries, or kiwi to help improve iron absorption.
 
Suitable for babies from 6 months onwards, with the texture adapted to your baby's stage of eating.

Serve warm with a vitamin C-rich fruit such as orange slices, steamed guava, strawberries, or kiwi to help improve iron absorption.

recipes.caption:
This is our Brown Butter Sticky Date Rice Pudding 🤎

And the very first recipe of our Food For Burnout Month.

Because when life feels a bit chaotic, stressful or overwhelming… sometimes what you actually need isn’t a cold chia pudding or smoothie, sometimes you need a warm bowl of something comforting, nourishing and super satisfying.

This one is sooo creamy, cosy, sweetened with sticky caramelized dates and packed with nutrients that support your body through stressful seasons.

Full recipe is now live inside the Recipe Club. Comment BURNOUT below if you’d like to check out more! 

So here’s how this recipe supports stress, burnout & overall nourishment…

Cooked & cooled rice: Contains resistant starch which helps support gut health while also providing those comforting carbohydrates that can feel really grounding during stressful periods.

Egg yolks: Provide all those wonderful healthy fats, choline, selenium and fat-soluble vitamins that help support the brain, nervous system and overall nourishment.

Dates: Rich in natural carbohydrates, potassium and magnesium, making them such a beautiful ingredient for quick energy and deeper nourishment.

Collagen: Provides the amino acids that help support connective tissue, recovery and overall nourishment while making this dessert more satiating and protein rich!

Brown butter: Adds richness, flavour and those satisfying fats that can help make meals feel more grounding and enjoyable.

Warm comfort foods: When we’re stressed, burnt out or overwhelmed, warm soft foods can often feel easier to digest, easier to prepare and more supportive than trying to force ourselves to eat perfectly.

Honestly… this is exactly the kind of recipe I crave when life feels a bit full and I want something that tastes like a hug but still nourishes my body.
recipes.recipe_ingredients:
butter
pitted dates
pre-cooked and cooled white rice
coconut milk
water
cinnamon
vanilla
maple syrup
egg yolks
collagen powder
recipes.recipe_method:
Brown the butter in a cast-iron skillet.
Fry the pitted dates until caramelized.
Add pre-cooked and cooled white rice, coconut milk, water, cinnamon, vanilla, and maple syrup.
Temper whisked egg yolks with the hot mixture, then combine everything back in the pan to thicken into a creamy pudding.
Serve in a bowl topped with the sticky dates, a drizzle of brown butter, and cinnamon.

recipes.title: Tandoori Chicken Breast
recipes.author: depinder_
recipes.text: air fryer tandoori style chicken breast 🌶️ recipe ⬇️ ingredients 4 chicken breasts 1 cup yoghurt juice of half a lime 2 tbsp ginger-garlic paste 1½ tsp kashmiri chilli powder 1 tsp ground cumin 1 tbsp ground coriander 1 tsp garam masala ½ tsp turmeric 1/2 tsp chaat masala 1/2 tsp crushed black pepper salt to taste 1 tbsp ghee or oil 1 tbsp dried fenugreek leaves (kasuri methi), crushed 1 tbsp soy sauce 1 tsp vinegar 1 tbsp chopped mint 1 tbsp chopped coriander method add the chicken to a bowl and make a few shallow cuts into the breast fillets. this helps the marinade penetrate. mix together all the ingredients and mix well. coat the chicken well in the marinade. cover and refrigerate for at least 30 minutes, ideally overnight. place the chicken in a single layer, leaving space between the pieces. air fry for 15-20 min at 190c, turning halfway, until lightly charred and cooked through. cooking time will depend on the size of the piece. serve with lime and a delish salad!
recipes.caption:
Air Fryer Tandoori Style Chicken Breast 🌶️

RECIPE ⬇️
Ingredients
4 chicken breasts
1 cup yoghurt
Juice of half a lime 
2 tbsp ginger-garlic paste
1½ tsp Kashmiri chilli powder
1 tsp ground cumin
1 tbsp ground coriander
1 tsp garam masala
½ tsp turmeric
1/2 tsp chaat masala
1/2 tsp crushed black pepper 
Salt to taste
1 tbsp ghee or oil 
1 tbsp  dried fenugreek leaves (kasuri methi), crushed
1 tbsp soy sauce 
1 tsp vinegar
1 tbsp chopped mint
1 tbsp chopped coriander
Method

Add the chicken to a bowl and make a few shallow cuts into the breast fillets. This helps the marinade penetrate.
Mix together all the ingredients and mix well. 
Coat the chicken well in the marinade. Cover and refrigerate for at least 30 minutes, ideally overnight. 
Place the chicken in a single layer, leaving space between the pieces.
Air fry for 15-20 min at 190C, turning halfway, until lightly charred and cooked through. Cooking time will depend on the size of the piece. 
Serve with lime and a delish salad!

recipes.caption:
in MY opinion* hahahaha no seriously

you’ll need:
- 2 dates
- 1 egg
- 1 cup (240ml) any milk
- 1/2 cup (40g) rolled oats
- pinch of sea salt

(for the peanut toffee sauce):
- 1tbsp smooth peanut butter (or any smooth nut butter!)
- 2tsp honey / maple syrup
- 30ml (2-3tbsp) any milk

(to serve):
- 1 banana
- small knob of butter for frying
- dark chocolate, finely chopped

method:
1. begin by manually tearing the dates into a few pieces and discarding the pip (or you can chop finely but honestly there’s no need).

2. place the dates, egg, milk, oats and sea salt in a small sauce pan and place on a low to medium heat.

3. begin whisking right away continuously until you start to see the oats are releasing a little steam.

4. lower the heat and continue whisking until the oats begin to thicken. you can break up and squash the dates as you go (they will eventually soften enough and break up).

5. meanwhile, melt the butter in a seperate small frying pan on a medium heat. place the banana slices face down onto the pan and fry for a few minutes until golden brown and caramelised.

6. carefully flip over and cook for another couple of minutes.

7. meanwhile, keep whisking the porridge.

8. prepare the toffee sauce by placing the peanut butter, milk and honey in a small bowl and mix until throughly combined (it will come together eventually i promise!).

9. once the oats have thickened to the consistency you like, remove from the heat.

10. serve right away in a medium sized bowl and carefully place the caramelised banana on top.

11. spoon over the peanut sauce wherever you like!

12. sprinkle the dark chocolate all over…

enjoy xxx🍌🍯🍫

#dates #porridge #oatmeal #breakfastideas #breakfast

30ml (2-3tbsp) any milk

recipes.recipe_method:
begin by manually tearing the dates into a few pieces and discarding the pip (or you can chop finely but honestly there’s no need).
place the dates, egg, milk, oats and sea salt in a small sauce pan and place on a low to medium heat.
begin whisking right away continuously until you start to see the oats are releasing a little steam.
lower the heat and continue whisking until the oats begin to thicken. you can break up and squash the dates as you go (they will eventually soften enough and break up).
meanwhile, melt the butter in a seperate small frying pan on a medium heat. place the banana slices face down onto the pan and fry for a few minutes until golden brown and caramelised.
carefully flip over and cook for another couple of minutes.
meanwhile, keep whisking the porridge.
prepare the toffee sauce by placing the peanut butter, milk and honey in a small bowl and mix until throughly combined (it will come together eventually i promise!).
once the oats have thickened to the consistency you like, remove from the heat.
serve right away in a medium sized bowl and carefully place the caramelised banana on top.
spoon over the peanut sauce wherever you like!
sprinkle the dark chocolate all over…

recipes.title: Chocolate Chickpea Truffles
recipes.author: inseason.withgenevieve
recipes.text: the better bite: episode 5 chocolate chickpea truffles. they’re naturally sweetened with medjool dates, made with chickpeas, nut butter + cocoa, then dipped in dark chocolate and finished with cacao nibs for the perfect little crunch. the’re insanely fudgy & chocolatey, and you honestly can’t tell that they are made with chickpeas!! my partner who is a professional french chef couldn’t tell, and he loved them!! ingredients: * 1 can chickpeas, drained (~240g drained weight) * 20g pure unsweetened cocoa powder * 60g smooth peanut or almond butter * 6 pitted medjool dates * 1 tsp vanilla extract * pinch of fine sea salt * 150g dark chocolate (70%+) * 30g cacao nibs method: 1. add the chickpeas, cocoa powder, nut butter, dates, vanilla and salt to a food processor. blend until smooth and fudgy. 2. roll the mixture into small balls and place on a parchment-lined tray. 3. melt the dark chocolate, and mix in the cacao nibs. 4. dip each truffle into the melted chocolate & sprinkle with sea salt, and let them set in the fridge. save this one for your next sweet craving 🤎
recipes.caption:
The Better Bite: Episode 5

Chocolate chickpea truffles. They’re naturally sweetened with Medjool dates, made with chickpeas, nut butter + cocoa, then dipped in dark chocolate and finished with cacao nibs for the perfect little crunch. The’re insanely fudgy & chocolatey, and you honestly can’t tell that they are made with chickpeas!! My partner who is a professional French chef couldn’t tell, and he loved them!! 

Ingredients:
* 1 can chickpeas, drained (~240g drained weight)
* 20g pure unsweetened cocoa powder
* 60g smooth peanut or almond butter
* 6 pitted Medjool dates
* 1 tsp vanilla extract
* Pinch of fine sea salt
* 150g dark chocolate (70%+)
* 30g cacao nibs

Method:
1. Add the chickpeas, cocoa powder, nut butter, dates, vanilla and salt to a food processor. Blend until smooth and fudgy.
2. Roll the mixture into small balls and place on a parchment-lined tray.
3. Melt the dark chocolate, and mix in the cacao nibs.
4. Dip each truffle into the melted chocolate & sprinkle with sea salt, and let them set in the fridge.

Save this one for your next sweet craving 🤎
recipes.recipe_ingredients:
1 can chickpeas, drained (~240g drained weight)
20g pure unsweetened cocoa powder
60g smooth peanut or almond butter
6 pitted Medjool dates
1 tsp vanilla extract
Pinch of fine sea salt
150g dark chocolate (70%+)
30g cacao nibs
recipes.recipe_method:
Add the chickpeas, cocoa powder, nut butter, dates, vanilla and salt to a food processor. Blend until smooth and fudgy.
Roll the mixture into small balls and place on a parchment-lined tray.
Melt the dark chocolate, and mix in the cacao nibs.
Dip each truffle into the melted chocolate & sprinkle with sea salt, and let them set in the fridge.

recipes.title: Savory Bhajiya Waffle
recipes.author: fitvegmomtulsi
recipes.text: who said waffles have to be sweet? 👀🧇 this is my savory bhajiya waffle—all the flavors i love in a traditional bhajiya, but made in the waffle iron for a fun, crispy twist. no standing over a pan of hot oil and no deep frying needed! 🙌 ✨ my base mix: • 2 cups besan (chickpea flour) • ¼ cup rice flour • ¼ cup vital wheat gluten • ¼ cup nutritional yeast • 1–2 tsp ginger-garlic-green chili paste • 1.5 cups greek yogurt • 2 tsp turmeric • 1 tsp black pepper • 1.5 tsp red chili powder • 1 tsp hing (asafoetida) • 1 tbsp olive oil • 2 tbsp black sesame seeds • 1 tbsp baking powder • salt to taste 🥬 load it up with veggies: • 2–3 cups chopped spinach • 1 cup finely chopped onion • swap in zucchini, bottle gourd (dudhi), or methi too! mix everything together, add water slowly as needed—keep the batter thick for crispy waffles—then cook in the waffle iron until golden and crisp. 🔥🧇 a healthier twist doesn’t mean giving up the foods we grew up loving. sometimes it just means getting creative with them. ❤️ would you try a savory bhajiya waffle? tell me yes or no in the comments! 👇 save this recipe for your next chai-time craving ☕️ chickpeaflourrecipes proteinpacked highproteinvegetarian healthysnackideas southasianfood indianfoodlovers wafflemakerrecipes vegetarianindianfood fitvegmom
recipes.caption:
Who said waffles have to be sweet? 👀🧇

This is my savory bhajiya waffle—all the flavors I love in a traditional bhajiya, but made in the waffle iron for a fun, crispy twist. No standing over a pan of hot oil and no deep frying needed! 🙌

✨ My base mix:
• 2 cups besan (chickpea flour)
• ¼ cup rice flour
• ¼ cup vital wheat gluten
• ¼ cup nutritional yeast
• 1–2 tsp ginger-garlic-green chili paste
• 1.5 cups Greek yogurt
• 2 tsp turmeric
• 1 tsp black pepper
• 1.5 tsp red chili powder
• 1 tsp hing (asafoetida)
• 1 tbsp olive oil
• 2 tbsp black sesame seeds
• 1 tbsp baking powder
• Salt to taste

🥬 Load it up with veggies:
• 2–3 cups chopped spinach
• 1 cup finely chopped onion
• Swap in zucchini, bottle gourd (dudhi), or methi too!

Mix everything together, add water slowly as needed—keep the batter thick for crispy waffles—then cook in the waffle iron until golden and crisp. 🔥🧇

A healthier twist doesn’t mean giving up the foods we grew up loving. Sometimes it just means getting creative with them. ❤️
