For the Tofu Chilli Cheese Mixture
7 ounces extra firm tofu, pressed for 15 minutes
1 cup vegan cheese shreds, such as mozzarella or a mix of mozzarella and cheddar
1 tablespoon nutritional yeast, or more, to taste
1/2 teaspoon salt
1/2 teaspoon black pepper
3 green chillies, finely chopped, such as serrano or Indian green chillies
1/4 cup finely chopped red bell pepper
1/4 cup finely chopped red onion, or more, to taste
1/2 cup loosely packed chopped cilantro
1/4 to 1/2 cup chopped greens, such as spinach or baby kale, or 1/4 cup frozen spinach
2 tablespoons hemp seeds, or more, to taste
1/4 teaspoon red pepper flakes, optional, or more, to taste
1/2 teaspoon chaat masala blend, or use lime zest or 1/8 teaspoon kala namak
1/2 cup non-dairy yogurt, cashew cream, or blended silken tofu
1 teaspoon dried oregano, optional
lime juice, as needed
For Topping the Cheese Toast
1/2 cup vegan cheese shreds
1 green chilli, thinly sliced
2 teaspoons oil
7 to 8 slices sourdough, or other sturdy bread, such as multigrain bakery bread
For the Crispy Chilli Lime Tempeh
4 ounces tempeh, grated, crumbled, or finely chopped
2 teaspoons oil
3 cloves garlic, thinly sliced
1/2 teaspoon salt
1/2 teaspoon Kashmiri chili powder
zest of 1/2 lime
recipes.recipe_method:
Make the chilli cheese mixture.
Crumble the tofu into a bowl, then use a fork to break it down further, so there are no large chunks remaining. If you are using miso, mix 1 to 2 teaspoons miso into the yogurt before adding it to the mixture. Add all of the remaining chilli cheese mixture ingredients, and mix very well. Press and mix so the cheese is evenly distributed throughout the tofu mixture.
If the mixture seems dry, add a little more non-dairy yogurt or a squeeze of lime juice. Taste and adjust the seasoning. If you want a cheesier flavor, add more nutritional yeast. Set the mixture aside and slice another green chilli for topping. This mix can be refrigerated for up to three days.
Assemble the toasts (see notes for a grilled cheese version!).
Lightly toast the bread slices. You don't want them deeply browned, but you do want a little crispness. This helps prevent the bread from becoming soggy once topped. Spread the chilli cheese mixture generously onto each slice. For a heartier meal, use a thick layer. For snack-sized toasts, use a thinner layer. Top with a little more vegan cheese, then add sliced green chillies and a few drops of oil over the chillies.
Preheat the oven to 450° F (232° C). Once preheated, switch to low broil. Depending on your oven, this may be around 500° to 525° F (260° to 275° C). Place the prepared toasts directly on a clean baking sheet. Do not use parchment paper, as it may burn under the broiler.
Broil for about 2 minutes, then check. If the cheese has not fully melted and started browning, continue broiling for another 1 to 2 minutes. Once the cheese is melted, golden, and the edges of the toast are lightly browned, remove from the oven.
Airfry: air fry at 370deg F(190 c) for 6-8 minutes
Meanwhile, make the crispy chilli lime tempeh.
Heat a small skillet over medium heat and add the oil. Once the oil is hot, reduce the heat to medium-low and add the garlic. Cook, stirring frequently, until the garlic is crispy and golden, about 2 minutes. Remove the garlic and set aside.
In the same skillet, add the tempeh and increase the heat to medium. Cook until golden brown, stirring every minute or so. This can take 4 to 6 minutes, depending on your skillet and stove.
Add the garlic back to the skillet, and mix well. Turn off the heat, and immediately add the salt, lime zest, and Kashmiri chilli powder. Toss to coat. Transfer the tempeh mixture to a bowl so it doesn't continue cooking and lose the fresh lime zest flavor, and try not to snack on all of it before serving.
Top the chilli cheese toasts with the crispy tempeh and garlic mixture, and serve immediately.

recipes.caption:
Our Healing Chicken Bone Broth 🍋 

This is our go-to broth recipe - intentionally designed to support gut healing.

This broth forms a foundational part of our protocols for patients with intestinal permeability (“leaky gut”), eczema, digestive disorders, autoimmune conditions, inflammation, injury and low immunity.

We use a whole chicken to keep the cooking time down (minimising histamine build-up) while delivering a delicious and nutrient dense broth.

The connective tissue, skin, and bones provide a rich source of zinc, collagen, gelatin, and key amino acids like glycine, proline, and glutamine - nutrients that are all essential for restoring the gut lining, calming inflammation, supporting detoxification, and improving skin and joint health.

Sip it as a warm drink between meals, or use it as a healing base for soups, stews, and slow-cooked meals.

Ingredients
1 whole organic/free-range chicken
8 whole black peppercorns
2 sprigs fresh parsley
2 Tbsp fresh dill
2 tsp sea salt (adjust to taste)
1 tsp turmeric
1 carrot, sliced
1 celery stalk, sliced
1 leek, sliced

Directions

Add all of the ingredients (except the herbs) to a large pot and cover with water. Bring to a gentle boil.

Reduce the heat to low and let it simmer, partially covered, for 90 minutes.

Lift out the chicken carefully and set it aside to cool. (You can shred the meat and set aside to use in meals).

Simmer for another 30 minutes, uncovered.

Stir in the parsley and dill, cover, and turn off the heat. Leave for 10 minutes.

Strain the broth through a sieve, taste and adjust seasoning if needed. Store in the fridge (up to 5 days) or freezer (up to 6 months.

Crust
100g mashed sweet potato
5 tbsp almond flour
1 pinch of salt

Filling
2 egg yolks
2 tbsp Greek yogurt
1 tbsp allulose (or sweetener of choice)

Method

1. Mix mashed sweet potato, almond flour, and salt until combined.

recipes.caption:
Food Scientist Explains: Why You Should Always Boil Your Tofu

By @wendythefoodscientist
15 million people have watched this technique. Thousands have told me it changed everything and made them finally fall in love with tofu. If you've been marinating for hours with disappointing results, this is the method you've been missing.
Here's exactly what happens when you boil tofu in salted water:
1. Water goes out, salt goes in.
Boiling draws out excess moisture from the surface. Water moves from the tofu into the surrounding brine. At the same time, a small amount of salt diffuses into the tofu, seasoning it gently from the inside out without making it salty.

2. The protein network opens up.
Heat slightly loosens the soy protein structure — think of it as relaxing the tofu's pores. This preps it to absorb marinades and sauces in seconds instead of hours. Not minutes. Seconds.

3. Texture improves.
The tofu becomes firmer, cleaner, and far less likely to fall apart during stir-frying, braising, or pan-frying.
One technique. Solves the number one tofu complaint — "it doesn't absorb flavor" — completely.

This method changed so many people's relationship with tofu that I built an entire guide around it.

recipes.recipe_ingredients:
Garlic, Ginger, Jalapeno mixture
6–8 cloves of garlic
2 inch ginger
½ jalapeno with seeds
Corn and Shishito Pepper Kofta
2 teaspoons vegetable oil
6–7 large shishito peppers
400 grams potatoes
1 corn shucked, and corn kernels removed from the cob
1 teaspoon cumin seeds
½ cup corn flour (makai ka atta)
1 teaspoon table salt
1 tablespoon garlic-ginger-jalapeno mixture
1 teaspoon garam masala
Vegetable Oil or avocado oil to fry
Corn Curry
3 tablespoons vegetable oil
1 bay leaf
1 ½ teaspoon cumin seeds
¼ stick cinnamon
2–3 cardamom pods
1 tablespoon garlic-ginger-jalapeno mixture
1 cup red onion, finely chopped
½ cup cashew nuts
2 corn, shucked and boiled
1 cup heavy cream or coconut cream
1 cup water, divided
1 ½ teaspoons table salt
1 teaspoon garam masala
1 teaspoon ground cumin
1 teaspoon ground coriander
2 teaspoons granulated sugar
¾ teaspoon turmeric
Garnish
Heavy cream
Blistered shishito peppers
recipes.recipe_method:
Garlic, Ginger, Jalapeno mixture
1. In a mini food processor, add the garlic, ginger and jalapeno, and grind the mixture until it is finely chopped. Remove into a bowl and set aside.
Corn and Shishito Pepper Kofta
1. In a medium saucepan, on medium heat, add the oil. After a minute, add the shishito peppers. You will start to hear the sizzling of the peppers. Bring the peppers to a char for 2 minutes, and turn them onto the other side, and char for another 2 minutes. Repeat the process until you see brown blisters around the shishito peppers, roughly about 2 more minutes.
2. Set the peppers aside.
3. Peel the potatoes, cut them into halves and boil the potatoes in water for about 15 minutes until they are fork tender. Drain immediately and set aside to cool completely.
4. Grate the corn on a grater in a large mixing plate/bowl to remove all the corn kernels and the juice as well.
5. Grate the boiled potatoes as well.
6. Add the cumin seeds, corn flour, salt, ginger-garlic-jalapeno-mixture, and garam masala.
7. Finely chop 3 blistered shishito peppers and add it to the mixture. Using gloves, mix all the ingredients well to form a cohesive dough.
8. Using a 2 tablespoon scooper, divide the dough into 17~18 balls.
9. Take each ball between the palms of your hands and move your one hand in a clockwise direction and the other hand in an anti-clockwise direction to form a round ball. Set it aside.
10. Repeat for the remaining balls.
11. In a medium saucepan, on medium high heat, add vegetable oil about 3 inches in height from the bottom of the saucepan. Place a plate lined with a paper towel to drain off the excess oil.
12. After 5-7 minutes, test by adding a tiny piece of the dough. If the dough rises up immediately with tiny balls around it, the oil is ready for frying.
13. Fry about 2 to 3 balls at a time for a minute until the bottom size is light brown. Turn the ball around to brown the other side, for another minute. The ball should look medium brown in color. Remove using a spider strainer onto the plate.
14. Repeat the process for all the koftas. Set aside.
Corn Curry
1. In a large skillet, on medium heat, add the vegetable oil.
2. After a minute, add the bay leaf, cumin seeds, cinnamon, cardamom pods, and saute for a minute.
3. Next add the ginger-garlic-jalapeno mixture, along with the red onions and saute for 3 to 5 minutes until the onions turn translucent and light brown in color.
4. Next remove the corn off the cob, and add it to the onion mixture.
5. Add the cashew nuts and saute the mixture for a minute.
6. Add the heavy cream and ½ cup of water and stir to combine.
7. Add all the spices such as salt, garam masala, ground cumin, ground coriander, sugar, and turmeric. Stir to combine and cook the mixture for 2-3 minutes, stirring occasionally.
8. Remove the bay leaf, add the mixture into a high speed blender to get a smooth sauce.
9. Add the sauce back into the pan along with additional ½ cup water, cover with a lid and cook the mixture on medium-low heat for 3 to 5 minutes. Uncover the lid.
10. Plate the curry onto a serving plate. Add the koftas into the curry in a circular pattern. Drizzle with the heavy cream.
11. Decorate with 4 blistered shishito peppers on top of the koftas.
12. Serve with naan immediately.

recipes.text: love my home slippers for many reasons 🤣🩴🦟 anyway, for dinner we had this easy honey garlic shrimp with edamame cilantro lime rice. comment “recipe” to get this sent your way for an easy weeknight / weekend dinner! ps. i opened my cuckoo rice cooker right after the steam release ended (w 2 min left to the cycle) and steamed my bok choy by keeping it in the rice cooker for a total of 4 minutes! i’ve been serving my steamed bok choy with soy sauce + sesame oil + minced garlic + tj’s chili onions and it’s a fam fav!!
recipes.caption:
Love my home slippers for MANY reasons 🤣🩴🦟 anyway, for dinner we had this easy honey garlic shrimp with edamame cilantro lime rice. Comment “RECIPE” to get this sent your way for an easy weeknight / weekend dinner! 

Ps. I opened my cuckoo rice cooker right after the steam release ended (w 2 min left to the cycle) and steamed my bok choy by keeping it in the rice cooker for a total of 4 minutes! I’ve been serving my steamed bok choy with soy sauce + sesame oil + minced garlic + TJ’s chili onions and it’s a fam fav!!
recipes.recipe_ingredients:
rice
water
frozen shelled edamame
sliced beech mushrooms
raw peeled shrimp
minced garlic
honey
butter
fresh bok choy
lime juice
chopped cilantro
green onion
sesame seeds
recipes.recipe_method:
Place the rice, water, frozen shelled edamame, and sliced beech mushrooms in a rice cooker and cook.
Season the raw peeled shrimp with minced garlic and honey.
Sauté the shrimp in a pan with butter and more honey until glazed.
Open the rice cooker mid-cycle and steam the fresh bok choy inside for four minutes.
Mix the cooked rice with lime juice, chopped cilantro, and green onion.
Plate the rice topped with the honey garlic shrimp and bok choy, and finish with sesame seeds.

recipes.caption:
Healthy rice paper dumpling rolls✨

My debut cookbook is officially out now! Link in bio 🤍. 

Filling:▪️1 lb. Ground Chicken (96% lean, not fat free)▪️8 oz. Peeled and Deveined Shrimp, diced small▪️1/2 Cup Red Cabbage, finely chopped▪️1/2 Cup Carrot, finely chopped▪️3 Scallions, sliced▪️2 Tbsp Finely Chopped Fresh Ginger▪️2 Garlic Cloves, finely chopped▪️3 Tbsp Finely Chopped Fresh Cilantro▪️2 Tbsp Soy Sauce▪️2 Tbsp Sesame Oil▪️1+1/2 tsp Kosher Salt▪️1/2 tsp Pepper▪️1 Egg▪️

Sauce:▪️1/4 Cup Warm Water▪️1 Tbsp Fish Sauce▪️1 Tbsp Sugar▪️1 Tbsp Fresh Lime Juice▪️1 Tbsp Finely Chopped Carrot▪️1 Tbsp Finely Chopped Fresh Cilantro▪️

Dumplings:▪️16-18 Sheets Rice Paper▪️2 Tbsp Neutral Oil, plus more as needed▪️

1️⃣ In a large bowl, add all the ingredients for the dumpling filling and mix.
2️⃣ In a small bowl, add all the ingredients for the sauce. Mix until the sugar dissolves and set aside.
3️⃣ Fill a pie dish (or large bowl) with warm water and line a cutting board with damp paper towels. Working one sheet at a time, soak the rice paper in the water for 10 to 15 seconds (it will continue to soften as you work), then place it on the paper towel-lined cutting board. Add about 3 Tbsp of filling to the bottom third of the rice paper and spread it into a rectangle, leaving room along the sides and bottom edge. Fold the bottom edge up over the filling and roll once more so the filling is fully enclosed. Fold in the sides, then continue rolling until sealed. Repeat with the remaining rice paper and filling.
4️⃣ In a large nonstick skillet, heat 2 Tbsp oil over medium heat. Working in batches, add the rolls to the skillet, rubbing the bottoms in the oil and leaving space between each. Cook until golden brown on the first side, 5 to 7 mins. Flip and cook on the second side until golden brown and the internal temperature reaches 165°F, 2 to 4 mins more. Transfer to a plate and repeat with the remaining rolls, adding more oil as needed. The rolls may cook faster as the skillet heats up, so check the bottoms frequently to monitor their progress.
5️⃣ Serve with sauce spooned on top and enjoy!

⏲30 minute prep time / 1 hour total time

Serves 4-6
recipes.recipe_ingredients:
Filling:
1 lb. Ground Chicken (96% lean, not fat free)
8 oz. Peeled and Deveined Shrimp, diced small
1/2 Cup Red Cabbage, finely chopped
1/2 Cup Carrot, finely chopped
3 Scallions, sliced
2 Tbsp Finely Chopped Fresh Ginger
2 Garlic Cloves, finely chopped
3 Tbsp Finely Chopped Fresh Cilantro
2 Tbsp Soy Sauce
2 Tbsp Sesame Oil
1+1/2 tsp Kosher Salt
1/2 tsp Pepper
1 Egg
Sauce:
1/4 Cup Warm Water
1 Tbsp Fish Sauce
1 Tbsp Sugar
1 Tbsp Fresh Lime Juice
1 Tbsp Finely Chopped Carrot
1 Tbsp Finely Chopped Fresh Cilantro
Dumplings:
16-18 Sheets Rice Paper
2 Tbsp Neutral Oil, plus more as needed
recipes.recipe_method:
1. In a large bowl, add all the ingredients for the dumpling filling and mix.
2. In a small bowl, add all the ingredients for the sauce. Mix until the sugar dissolves and set aside.
3. Fill a pie dish (or large bowl) with warm water and line a cutting board with damp paper towels. Working one sheet at a time, soak the rice paper in the water for 10 to 15 seconds (it will continue to soften as you work), then place it on the paper towel-lined cutting board. Add about 3 Tbsp of filling to the bottom third of the rice paper and spread it into a rectangle, leaving room along the sides and bottom edge. Fold the bottom edge up over the filling and roll once more so the filling is fully enclosed. Fold in the sides, then continue rolling until sealed. Repeat with the remaining rice paper and filling.
4. In a large nonstick skillet, heat 2 Tbsp oil over medium heat. Working in batches, add the rolls to the skillet, rubbing the bottoms in the oil and leaving space between each. Cook until golden brown on the first side, 5 to 7 mins. Flip and cook on the second side until golden brown and the internal temperature reaches 165°F, 2 to 4 mins more. Transfer to a plate and repeat with the remaining rolls, adding more oil as needed. The rolls may cook faster as the skillet heats up, so check the bottoms frequently to monitor their progress.
5. Serve with sauce spooned on top and enjoy!

recipes.title: Zucchini Waffles
recipes.author: anadovada
recipes.text: how to get kids to eat veggies with zero drama? 🤫👇 waffle prepping is one of my ultimate mom hacks! these zucchini waffles freeze beautifully without losing their taste or nutrients. just thaw them out, and you’ve got the perfect breakfast, quick snack, or school lunchbox filler. and let’s be honest—they are so delicious, you’ll be stealing them from your kids! 😉✨ zucchini waffles recipe 🥦🧀 250g young zucchini (grated and squeezed) 40g melted butter 1 egg 1 tbsp sour cream 100g semi-hard cheese (grated) a small bunch of parsley (finely chopped) 1 tsp baking powder salt & garlic to taste 120g all-purpose flour oil (for greasing) instructions: 1. grate the zucchini, add a pinch of salt, and let it sit for a few minutes. squeeze out all the excess liquid thoroughly. 2. mix in all the remaining ingredients until combined. 3. bake in a waffle maker until golden brown (or fry them like pancakes in a skillet!).
recipes.caption:
How to get kids to eat veggies with zero drama? 🤫👇

Waffle prepping is one of my ultimate mom hacks! These zucchini waffles freeze beautifully without losing their taste or nutrients. Just thaw them out, and you’ve got the perfect breakfast, quick snack, or school lunchbox filler.
And let’s be honest—they are so delicious, you’ll be stealing them from your kids! 😉✨

Zucchini Waffles Recipe 🥦🧀
 250g young zucchini (grated and squeezed)
 40g melted butter
 1 egg
 1 tbsp sour cream
 100g semi-hard cheese (grated)
 A small bunch of parsley (finely chopped)
 1 tsp baking powder
 Salt & garlic to taste
 120g all-purpose flour
 Oil (for greasing)
Instructions:
1. Grate the zucchini, add a pinch of salt, and let it sit for a few minutes. Squeeze out all the excess liquid thoroughly.
2. Mix in all the remaining ingredients until combined.
3. Bake in a waffle maker until golden brown (or fry them like pancakes in a skillet!). #zucchiniwaffles #waffles #lunchboxidea #toddlerlunch
recipes.recipe_ingredients:
250g young zucchini (grated and squeezed)
40g melted butter
1 egg
1 tbsp sour cream
100g semi-hard cheese (grated)
A small bunch of parsley (finely chopped)
1 tsp baking powder
Salt & garlic to taste
120g all-purpose flour
Oil (for greasing)
recipes.recipe_method:
1. Grate the zucchini, add a pinch of salt, and let it sit for a few minutes. Squeeze out all the excess liquid thoroughly.
2. Mix in all the remaining ingredients until combined.
3. Bake in a waffle maker until golden brown (or fry them like pancakes in a skillet!).

recipes.caption:
🌶️ Air-Fryer Fiery Harissa Chicken

For 450–500 g boneless chicken thighs

Homemade harissa-style marinade

* 5–6 whole dried red chillies
* 3 large garlic cloves
* 1 tsp coriander seeds
* ¾ tsp cumin seeds
* ¼ tsp shah jeera (caraway seeds)
* 1 tsp smoked paprika
* ½ tsp black pepper
* ¾ tsp salt
* 1½ tbsp olive oil
* 1 tbsp fresh lemon juice
* ½ tsp lemon zest

Optional: 1 extra hot dried chilli if your other chillies are mild.

1. Prepare the chillies

Remove the stems from the dried chillies. Remove most of the seeds if you don’t want it extremely spicy.

Cover with boiling water and soak for 15–20 minutes until softened.

Drain thoroughly, but keep a little soaking water aside.

2. Toast the spices

Add the coriander seeds, cumin seeds and shah jeera to a dry pan.

Toast over low-medium heat for about 60–90 seconds, just until fragrant. Don’t let them burn.

3. Make the harissa

Blend together:

softened chillies + toasted spices + garlic + smoked paprika + black pepper + salt + olive oil + lemon juice + lemon zest.

Blend into a thick, slightly textured red paste.

If it’s too dry to blend, add 1–2 tsp of the chilli soaking water. Don’t make it runny.

Taste and adjust salt/lemon.

4. Marinate

Coat the chicken thighs thoroughly in the harissa.

Marinate for at least 30 minutes, but 1–2 hours would be better.

5. Air fry

Preheat the air fryer to 190°C for 3 minutes.

Arrange the thighs in a single layer.

Air fry at 190°C for 12–15 minutes, flipping halfway through.

Then increase to 200°C for 2–3 minutes to develop those dark, slightly charred edges.

recipes.title: Savoury Veggie Muffins
recipes.author: scrambled_eats
recipes.text: savoury > sweet 👀 no sugar… little kids, big kids and parents too will love these light, fluffy, savoury muffins. they freeze so well so you can have them ready for whenever a snack attack hits! ingredients: * 3 cups self-raising flour * 3 eggs * ½ cup butter * 1 tsp garlic powder * 1 tsp oregano * 1 and 1/2 cups chopped veg * 3 cups greek yoghurt * 2 cups grated cheese (mix 1½ cups into the batter and sprinkle ½ cup on top. method: 1. preheat oven to 180°c fan-forced. in a large bowl, combine flour, oregano and garlic powder. 2. in a separate bowl, whisk together eggs, butter and 3 cups of the yoghurt. 3. add the yoghurt mixture to the flour mixture and gently fold to combine. 4. fold through veggies and 1 1/2 cups of the cheese. 5. spoon mixture into 2 greased 12-hole muffin pan. top with the remaining ½ cup cheese. 6. bake for 20 minutes, or until golden.
recipes.caption:
Savoury > sweet 👀 
No sugar… little kids, big kids and parents too will love these light, fluffy, savoury muffins. They freeze so well so you can have them ready for whenever a snack attack hits! 

Ingredients: 
 * 3 cups self-raising flour 
* 3 eggs 
* ½ cup butter
* 1 tsp garlic powder 
* 1 tsp oregano 
* 1 and 1/2 cups chopped veg
* 3 cups Greek yoghurt
* 2 cups grated cheese (mix 1½ cups into the batter and sprinkle ½ cup on top.

Method: 

1. Preheat oven to 180°C fan-forced. In a large bowl, combine flour, oregano and garlic powder.
2. In a separate bowl, whisk together eggs, butter and 3 cups of the yoghurt.
3. Add the yoghurt mixture to the flour mixture and gently fold to combine.
4. Fold through veggies and 1 1/2 cups of the cheese.
5. Spoon mixture into 2 greased 12-hole muffin pan. Top with the remaining ½ cup cheese.
6. Bake for 20 minutes, or until golden.

recipes.caption:
Crispy Rice Paper Shrimp Bites 🍤
Air Fryer Edition

High-protein snack that takes less than 20 minutes to make! 

INGREDIENTS
Shrimp Filling:
1/2 lb shrimp, finely chopped
2 tsp cornstarch
1 tsp sesame oil
1 tsp soy sauce
2 garlic clove, grated (or 1/2 tsp garlic powder)
2 tbsp chopped green onion
Salt and black pepper, to taste

Wraps:
1-2 large rice paper sheets
Avocado oil spray

Spicy Yogurt Sauce:
2 tbsp plain Greek yogurt
1 tbsp mayonnaise
1 tsp Sriracha
1 tsp honey
1/2 tbsp lemon juice
1/4 tsp garlic powder
Salt, to taste

For Serving (Optional):
Sliced green onion
Chili crisp or chili oil
Sesame seeds

INSTRUCTIONS
Make the filling: In a bowl, combine shrimp, cornstarch, sesame oil, soy sauce, garlic, green onion, salt, and pepper.

Wrap: Dip a rice paper sheet in warm water for 3-5 seconds. Add shrimp filling and roll tightly, then cut into bite-sized pieces. 

Air Fry: Lightly spray with avocado oil. Air fry at 390°F (200°C) for 14–16 minutes, flipping halfway, until golden brown and crispy.

Make the sauce: Stir together Greek yogurt, mayonnaise, Sriracha, honey, lemon juice, garlic powder, and salt until smooth.

Serve: Top with green onion, and sesame seeds. Serve with the sauce.

*Recipe Notes
• Pat the shrimp dry before chopping so the filling isn’t watery.
• Don’t oversoak the rice paper, it should still feel slightly firm before wrapping.
• Spray generously with oil for an evenly crisp, blistered finish.

recipes.caption:
Episode 5 of my Second Servings series. I went into this one sceptical and came out impressed.👇🏻

(Over the next few weeks I'm sharing some of my favourite viral reaction reels. Because they deserve more airtime but I'm a little preoccupied in my newborn bubble.)

Lentil sheet-pan pancakes 🥞

Thank you @cookingforpeanuts for a great one!

The only tweak I’d consider is adding 1 egg to the batter for a bit more structure and lightness. Obviously that makes it no longer suitable for vegans, but it’s optional rather than essential.

The other thing to note is fat content. The base recipe is quite low, so I’d serve these with something alongside. Greek yoghurt, a spoon of nut butter helps round them out and makes them more satisfying.

Ingredients (3 servings)
1 cup split red lentils, soaked (190g)
1 cup rolled oats (90g)
1 large banana
1¼ cups unsweetened milk (300ml)
1 tbsp baking powder
1 tsp apple cider vinegar
1 tsp Ceylon cinnamon
1 tsp vanilla extract
2-3 Medjool dates, pitted
Optional toppings: berries, apple, nuts, seeds, dark chocolate
Optional tweaks: 1 egg, Greek yoghurt, nut butter or butter to serve

Method
Soak lentils in boiling water for 30 minutes, then drain and rinse
Blend all ingredients until completely smooth
Pour into a lined or greased sheet pan, about 1½ inches deep
Add toppings lightly
Bake at 180°C for 35-40 minutes until set
Cool slightly, slice, and serve

High fibre, good plant protein, steady energy. Add a fat source when serving and it becomes a far more balanced plate.

recipes.text: ep: 8 soya afghani ❤️ protein: ~35–40g calories: ~430–480 kcal approximate per generous serving, depending on the paneer, cashews, cream and oil used. ingredients * 75g dry soya chunks * 75g low-fat paneer * 3 tbsp thick curd * 4–5 cashews * 4 garlic cloves * 1-inch ginger * 1 small onion * 1 green chilli * handful of fresh coriander * ½ tsp black pepper * 1 tsp chole masala * ½ tsp garam masala * salt to taste * 1 tsp oil * hot water as required * ½ tsp kasuri methi * 1 tbsp fresh cream * ½ tsp pickle oil process 1. soak the soya chunks in hot water for 15–20 minutes. drain and squeeze out as much water as possible. 2. heat a pan and sauté garlic, ginger, onion, green chilli, cashews and fresh coriander until the onion softens. 3. let it cool slightly, then blend it with the paneer and a little water until you get a smooth, creamy paste. 4. add the soaked soya chunks to a bowl. add curd, the prepared paneer paste, salt, black pepper, chole masala and garam masala. mix until the soya is well coated. 5. heat oil in a kadai and add the marinated soya chunks. sauté briefly, then add a little hot water. 6. cover and cook on low flame for 3–4 minutes, or until the gravy reaches your preferred consistency. 7. finish with crushed kasuri methi, fresh cream and a little pickle oil. 8. serve hot with roti, paratha or rice. save and share the reel follow for more such recipes
recipes.caption:
Ep: 8 Soya Afghani ❤️

Protein: ~35–40g
Calories: ~430–480 kcal

Approximate per generous serving, depending on the paneer, cashews, cream and oil used.

Ingredients

* 75g dry soya chunks
* 75g low-fat paneer
* 3 tbsp thick curd
* 4–5 cashews
* 4 garlic cloves
* 1-inch ginger
* 1 small onion
* 1 green chilli
* Handful of fresh coriander
* ½ tsp black pepper
* 1 tsp chole masala
* ½ tsp garam masala
* Salt to taste
* 1 tsp oil
* Hot water as required
* ½ tsp kasuri methi
* 1 tbsp fresh cream
* ½ tsp pickle oil

Process

1. Soak the soya chunks in hot water for 15–20 minutes. Drain and squeeze out as much water as possible.
2. Heat a pan and sauté garlic, ginger, onion, green chilli, cashews and fresh coriander until the onion softens.
3. Let it cool slightly, then blend it with the paneer and a little water until you get a smooth, creamy paste.
4. Add the soaked soya chunks to a bowl. Add curd, the prepared paneer paste, salt, black pepper, chole masala and garam masala. Mix until the soya is well coated.
5. Heat oil in a kadai and add the marinated soya chunks. Sauté briefly, then add a little hot water.
6. Cover and cook on low flame for 3–4 minutes, or until the gravy reaches your preferred consistency.
7. Finish with crushed kasuri methi, fresh cream and a little pickle oil.
8. Serve hot with roti, paratha or rice.

recipes.caption:
You asked how I make my homemade “beauty boba”…

✨Follow @mumwithabun_nutrition and then comment PEACH I’ll send the details on how to get your peach gum extra soft/bouncy, how to find a quality one, storage, benefits, FAQs & the peach gum I’ve been using.

All I do is soak peach gum in filtered water for about 24 hours, pinch away the tiny pieces of bark, re-rinse and add the bouncy boba-like pieces to my latte, jujube tea, and desserts.

That’s it.

Peach gum is a natural resin that peach trees form to heal itself - it’s been enjoyed in Chinese cuisine for generations for beauty, skin, hydration & digestive benefits. 

Once soaked, it turns into these beautiful translucent gem-looking pieces of soft bites that don’t have much flavor other than a faint earl grey taste—which is why I love them. It’s so humble 🤭

I find it works well with milk-y desserts so yea I add a drizzle of coconut milk / ice cream sometimes ♡ 

Fun fact. 
People online sometimes call it “vegan collagen” and while it can help your skin, technically it isn’t collagen. There is no collagen in it. 
For me, it’s such a beautiful reminder that God designed so many beautiful foods in nature that are meant for our good.

Summary:
• soak 24 hours in filtered water
• remove any bark pieces
• rinse thoroughly
• keep refrigerated after soaking
• enjoy within about 3–5 days for best quality/food safety.

recipes.text: high protein dill pickle egg smash if you have your eggs pre boiled the night before this is such an easy lunch to whip up in 5 minutes or less. filling: 320 cal | 25g protein | 6g carbs | 20g fat ingredients 2 large eggs 120g cottage cheese ½ avocado 2 dill pickle spears, finely chopped 1 spring onion finely sliced 1 tbsp fresh dill or parsley, chopped 1 tsp dijon mustard salt, pepper and chili flakes toast, bagel or gf bread, to serve method 1. boil eggs 7–8 minutes for jammy yolks, then straight into iced water. 2. meanwhile, roughly mash the avocado into the cottage cheese — texture, not puree. 3. peel and roughly chop the eggs. add to the bowl with pickles, green onion, dill, dijon, onion powder and seasoning. 4. fold and mash to your preferred texture. taste — more dijon for tang, more pickles for crunch. 5. pile onto fresh bread for the most delicious high protein sandwich that will keep you full all afternoon.
recipes.caption:
High Protein Dill Pickle Egg Smash

If you have your eggs pre boiled the night before this is such an easy lunch to whip up in 5 minutes or less. 

Filling: 320 cal | 25g protein | 6g carbs | 20g fat

Ingredients
2 large eggs
120g cottage cheese
½ avocado
2 dill pickle spears, finely chopped
1 spring onion finely sliced
1 tbsp fresh dill or parsley, chopped
1 tsp dijon mustard
Salt, pepper and chili flakes
Toast, bagel or GF bread, to serve

Method
1. Boil eggs 7–8 minutes for jammy yolks, then straight into iced water.
2. Meanwhile, roughly mash the avocado into the cottage cheese — texture, not puree.
3. Peel and roughly chop the eggs. Add to the bowl with pickles, green onion, dill, dijon, onion powder
and seasoning.
4. Fold and mash to your preferred texture. Taste — more dijon for tang, more pickles for crunch.
5. Pile onto fresh bread for the most delicious high protein sandwich that will keep you full all afternoon.

recipes.title: Red Curry Chicken Bites
recipes.author: coconutandbliss
recipes.text: crispy red curry chicken bites - they’re basically little rice paper dumplings, cooked in the air fryer until crispy ingredients 500g chicken mince 2 tbsp red curry paste 1 tbsp soy sauce 1 tbsp honey 1/2 lime, juiced 1/2 tbsp grated ginger 1 garlic clove, grated 2 tbsp chives, finely chopped 8 rice paper wrappers oil spray dipping sauce 1/3 cup kewpie mayonnaise 1 tbsp red curry paste 1 tbsp lime juice 1 tsp honey 1 tsp soy sauce 1 tsp rice wine vinegar to serve chopped coriander chilli crisp 1. in a bowl, combine the chicken mince, red curry paste, soy sauce, honey, lime juice, ginger, garlic, chives until well mixed. 2. fill a shallow bowl with warm water. dip one rice paper wrapper into the water until just softened. 3. spoon a log of the chicken mixture along the bottom third of the wrapper. fold in the sides and roll tightly into a sausage shape. 4. using kitchen scissors, snip the roll into bite-sized pieces. 5. arrange the pieces in a single layer in an air fryer basket. spray generously with oil and air fry at 200°c for 12–15 minutes, turning halfway, until the chicken is cooked through and the rice paper is golden and crispy. 6. meanwhile, whisk together the kewpie mayonnaise, red curry paste, lime juice, honey, soy sauce and rice wine vinegar until smooth. 7. top the crispy chicken bites with chopped coriander and chilli crisp, then serve with the dipping sauce.
recipes.caption:
Crispy red curry chicken bites - they’re basically little rice paper dumplings, cooked in the air fryer until crispy 

Ingredients
500g chicken mince
2 tbsp red curry paste
1 tbsp soy sauce
1 tbsp honey
1/2 lime, juiced
1/2 tbsp grated ginger
1 garlic clove, grated
2 tbsp chives, finely chopped

8 rice paper wrappers
Oil spray

Dipping Sauce
1/3 cup Kewpie mayonnaise
1 tbsp red curry paste
1 tbsp lime juice
1 tsp honey
1 tsp soy sauce
1 tsp rice wine vinegar

To Serve
Chopped coriander
Chilli crisp

1. In a bowl, combine the chicken mince, red curry paste, soy sauce, honey, lime juice, ginger, garlic, chives  until well mixed.
2. Fill a shallow bowl with warm water. Dip one rice paper wrapper into the water until just softened.
3. Spoon a log of the chicken mixture along the bottom third of the wrapper. Fold in the sides and roll tightly into a sausage shape.
4. Using kitchen scissors, snip the roll into bite-sized pieces.
5. Arrange the pieces in a single layer in an air fryer basket. Spray generously with oil and air fry at 200°C for 12–15 minutes, turning halfway, until the chicken is cooked through and the rice paper is golden and crispy.
6. Meanwhile, whisk together the Kewpie mayonnaise, red curry paste, lime juice, honey, soy sauce and rice wine vinegar until smooth.
7. Top the crispy chicken bites with chopped coriander and chilli crisp, then serve with the dipping sauce.

3. Spoon a log of the chicken mixture along the bottom third of the wrapper. Fold in the sides and roll tightly into a sausage shape.
4. Using kitchen scissors, snip the roll into bite-sized pieces.
5. Arrange the pieces in a single layer in an air fryer basket. Spray generously with oil and air fry at 200°C for 12–15 minutes, turning halfway, until the chicken is cooked through and the rice paper is golden and crispy.
6. Meanwhile, whisk together the Kewpie mayonnaise, red curry paste, lime juice, honey, soy sauce and rice wine vinegar until smooth.
7. Top the crispy chicken bites with chopped coriander and chilli crisp, then serve with the dipping sauce.

recipes.title: Khatta Moong Dal
recipes.author: thechutneylife
recipes.text: perfect meal after vacay when you’re low on groceries! khatta mug is a savory and sour dal made with yogurt. comforting, hearty and simple! recipe: in an instant pot combine 1 cup of rinsed whole green moong dal, with 1 tsp salt, 2.5 cups water and 1/8 tsp turmeric powder. mix and set the ip for 10 minutes on high pressure and let it naturally release. next, in a mixing bowl whisk together 1/2 cup greek or regular yogurt, 1/2 cup water and 2 tbsp besan. heat 1.5 tbsp ghee in a large pot over medium heat and once the oil is hot, add 1 tsp mustard seeds. when they pop add 2 tsp cumin seeds, 2 finely chopped green chilis, 6 curry leaves, 1/4 tsp turmeric powder, and 1/2 tsp red chili powder. swirl that around so it doesn’t brown. add 1 tsp finely grated ginger, 1 tbsp chopped garlic, and cook for a couple minutes then add the yogurt- besan mixture and cook over a low flame for about 5 minutes while stirring. once it has slightly thickened, add the cooked moong dal, along with 1/2 tsp salt, 1/2 tsp coriander powder and 1/4 tsp garam masala. let this simmer gently for about 10-15 minutes on low heat. remove from heat and enjoy! taste and adjust salt or spice as needed. i love scooping this up with roti and having some raw onion salad on the side but it’s also great on its own or with rice, extra ghee and papad etc! instant pot recipes, lentil recipes, dal, post vacation, travel, indian food, vegetarian meals
recipes.caption:
Perfect meal after vacay when you’re low on groceries! Khatta Mug is a savory and sour dal made with yogurt. Comforting, hearty and simple!

Recipe:

In an instant pot combine 1 cup of rinsed whole green moong dal, with 1 tsp salt, 2.5 cups water and 1/8 tsp turmeric powder. Mix and set the IP for 10 minutes on High Pressure and let it naturally release.

Next, in a mixing bowl whisk together 1/2 cup greek or regular yogurt, 1/2 cup water and 2 tbsp besan.

Heat 1.5 tbsp ghee in a large pot over medium heat and once the oil is hot, add 1 tsp mustard seeds. When they pop add 2 tsp cumin seeds, 2 finely chopped green chilis, 6 curry leaves, 1/4 tsp turmeric powder, and 1/2 tsp red chili powder. Swirl that around so it doesn’t brown. Add 1 tsp finely grated ginger, 1 tbsp chopped garlic, and cook for a couple minutes then add the yogurt- besan mixture and cook over a low flame for about 5 minutes while stirring. Once it has slightly thickened, add the cooked moong dal, along with 1/2 tsp salt, 1/2 tsp coriander powder and 1/4 tsp garam masala. Let this simmer gently for about 10-15 minutes on low heat. Remove from heat and enjoy!  Taste and adjust salt or spice as needed. 

I love scooping this up with roti and having some raw onion salad on the side but it’s also great on its own or with rice, extra ghee and papad etc!

Instant pot recipes, lentil recipes, dal, post vacation, travel, Indian food, vegetarian meals
recipes.recipe_method:
In an instant pot combine 1 cup of rinsed whole green moong dal, with 1 tsp salt, 2.5 cups water and 1/8 tsp turmeric powder. Mix and set the IP for 10 minutes on High Pressure and let it naturally release.
Next, in a mixing bowl whisk together 1/2 cup greek or regular yogurt, 1/2 cup water and 2 tbsp besan.
Heat 1.5 tbsp ghee in a large pot over medium heat and once the oil is hot, add 1 tsp mustard seeds. When they pop add 2 tsp cumin seeds, 2 finely chopped green chilis, 6 curry leaves, 1/4 tsp turmeric powder, and 1/2 tsp red chili powder. Swirl that around so it doesn’t brown. Add 1 tsp finely grated ginger, 1 tbsp chopped garlic, and cook for a couple minutes then add the yogurt- besan mixture and cook over a low flame for about 5 minutes while stirring. Once it has slightly thickened, add the cooked moong dal, along with 1/2 tsp salt, 1/2 tsp coriander powder and 1/4 tsp garam masala. Let this simmer gently for about 10-15 minutes on low heat. Remove from heat and enjoy! Taste and adjust salt or spice as needed.

recipes.title: Lemon Oats with Raspberry Chia Jam
recipes.author: helenhtaylor
recipes.text: without it i don’t want it🤣 (for the lemon oats) you’ll need: - 1/2 cup oats - 1 egg ( forever) - zest of 1 lemon - 1tbsp honey - 1 cup (240ml) any milk (for the raspberry chia jam): - 1/2 cup (about 75g) fresh / frozen raspberries - juice of 1/4 of a lemon (or more if you prefer) - 2tsp chia seeds - 1tbsp honey (to serve): - any yogurt you like! - chopped pistachios method: 1. begin by placing the oats, egg, lemon zest, honey and milk in a small saucepan and place on a medium heat. 2. begin by whisking vigorously to ensure the egg is completely incorporated. 3. as soon as you start to see a little steam, lower the heat to low. 4. keep whisking continuously as the oats cook (this will take between 5-10 minutes). 5. meanwhile, you can place the raspberries, lemon juice, chia seeds and honey in a small bowl and microwave for 90 seconds. 6. stir and leave to one side. 7. keep whisking the oats until they have thickened nicely and the mixture is creamy and glossy. 8. remove from the heat and pour the oats into your serving bowl. 9. spoon over the raspberry chia jam wherever you like. 10. finish with a generous dollop of greek yogurt and a sprinkle of pistachios. 11. drizzle some extra honey / maple syrup if you like it sweeter… enjoy xxx

recipes.caption:
🍪 Clean Almond Pistachio Biscuits (No Starch!)
These melt-in-your-mouth biscuits are completely grain-free and use zero starches. They take just 15 minutes to bake and pair perfectly with your morning tea or coffee! ☕✨
Ingredients:
 Almond Flour: 2 cups (super-fine blanched)
 Pistachios: ½ cup (shelled and finely chopped)
 Ground Cardamom (Elaichi): ½ tsp
 Liquid Sweetener (Choose ONE): ⅓ cup pure maple syrup OR ⅓ cup raw honey
 Healthy Fat: 3 tbsp melted ghee (or melted butter / coconut oil)
Step-by-Step Instructions:
1. Prep the Oven: Preheat your oven to 350°F (180°C) and line a baking sheet with parchment paper.
2. Mix the Dry Ingredients: In a bowl, mix the almond flour, ground cardamom, and most of the chopped pistachios (save 1 tablespoon of the pistachios for the top).
3. Add the Wet Ingredients: Pour in your chosen liquid sweetener (maple syrup or honey) along with the melted ghee. Stir thoroughly until a soft, uniform cookie dough forms.
4. Shape Your Size: Divide the dough and roll them into balls, then shape them into your preferred size—either round discs or long bakery-style rectangles like in image.png. Use a fork to gently press lines on top for that classic bakery look.
5. Top & Bake: Press the remaining chopped pistachios firmly onto the top of each biscuit. Bake for 12–14 minutes just until the edges turn a light golden brown.
6. Cool Completely: Let them cool on the baking sheet for 10 minutes before moving them. Almond flour treats are delicate when hot but firm up into a perfect crumbly texture once fully cooled!

recipes.caption:
Kangachi Nevri (also called Kangachyo Nevryo or Ratalyachi Karanji) is a traditional Goan sweet potato dumpling typically prepared during festive occasions like Ganesh Chaturthi and Diwali. Unlike regular crispy nevris made from all-purpose flour, this version uses boiled and mashed sweet potatoes (kanang in Konkani) to create a soft, golden outer casing. The crescent-shaped pastry is packed with a classic coastal sweet filling of fresh coconut and jaggery before being shallow-fried in pure ghee.
Key Ingredients
For the Outer Cover: 1/2 cup boiled sweet potatoes , 2 tablespoon of whole wheat flour, pinch of salt.
For the Sweet Filling: 1/4 cup of freshly grated coconut, 1.5 tbsp of coconut sugar, and pinch of Cardamom powder , 1/4 tsp poppy seeds ( optional)
For Cooking: Akshayakalpa organic Cow ghee 

Method 
Prepare the Stuffing : Heat ghee in a pan over a low flame, add poppy seeds, grated coconut, jaggery, cardamom powder.
cook until the jaggery melts completely. transfer the mixture to a bowl to cool completely. 
Make the Dough: Wash, cook and peel the sweet potatoes. Mash them thoroughly to ensure there are no lumps, then knead in the wheat flour, pinch of salt to form a smooth, soft dough without adding any water. 
Shape the Nevris: Divide the dough into small, lime-sized balls. Flatten each ball on a ghee greased sheet/ banana leaf, place a spoonful of the coconut-jaggery stuffing on one half, fold it over into a crescent shape, and firmly press the edges to seal. 
Fry to Golden Perfection: Heat a flat pan or tawa, apply a generous drizzle of ghee, and shallow-fry the dumplings on low-to-medium heat. Flip them gently until both sides turn fragrant and beautifully golden brown. 

Note-
1 cup - 250 ml
Makes 5 no.

recipes.title: Chicken Mushroom Congee
recipes.author: kirstenljenkins
recipes.text: i adore this congee recipe…it feels good for the soul! chicken and mushroom congee serves 4-6 1 tbsp sesame oil 4 cloves garlic, peeled, sliced 4 spring onions, thinly sliced, extra to serve 1 cup jasmine rice 200g mixed asian mushrooms, torn and cut into pieces soy sauce, sesame seeds, chilli oil, to serve chicken stock 1 large piece of ginger 1.6kg whole chicken 4 spring onions, halved 1 bulb garlic, unpeeled, halved 2 eshallots, unpeeled, halved ⅓ cup fish sauce, extra to serve to make the chicken stock, thickly slice half of the ginger, set aside the remaining half for later. place the ginger slices in a large saucepan with the remaining “stock” ingredients and fill with water until the chicken is submerged. simmer the chicken over a low heat, covered, for 3-4 hours or until the meat is falling off the bone. remove the chicken and garlic from the pan and strain the chicken broth measuring out 9 cups of liquid. discard the other solids. when cool enough to handle, pick the chicken meat into chunks and squeeze the garlic from the skin. when ready to cook the congee, peel and finely grate the remaining ginger. heat the oil in a large saucepan over medium heat, add the ginger, cooked garlic, fresh garlic and spring onions and cook for 1-2 minutes until fragrant. add the rice and stir until coated by the oil and other ingredients. add the reserved broth to the pan and bring to the boil, reduce heat to low, cover with lid and cook slowly for 1 hour, stirring occasionally. turn
recipes.caption:
I adore this congee recipe…it feels good for the soul!

Chicken and mushroom congee 
Serves 4-6

1 tbsp sesame oil
4 cloves garlic, peeled, sliced
4 spring onions, thinly sliced, extra to serve
1 cup jasmine rice
200g mixed Asian mushrooms, torn and cut into pieces 
Soy sauce, sesame seeds, chilli oil, to serve 
Chicken stock
1 large piece of ginger
1.6kg whole chicken
4 spring onions, halved
1 bulb garlic, unpeeled, halved
2 eshallots, unpeeled, halved
⅓ cup fish sauce, extra to serve

To make the chicken stock, thickly slice half of the ginger, set aside the remaining half for later. Place the ginger slices in a large saucepan with the remaining “stock” ingredients and fill with water until the chicken is submerged. Simmer the chicken over a low heat, covered, for 3-4 hours or until the meat is falling off the bone. 

Remove the chicken and garlic from the pan and strain the chicken broth measuring out 9 cups of liquid. Discard the other solids. When cool enough to handle, pick the chicken meat into chunks and squeeze the garlic from the skin.

When ready to cook the congee, peel and finely grate the remaining ginger. Heat the oil in a large saucepan over medium heat, add the ginger, cooked garlic, fresh garlic and spring onions and cook for 1-2 minutes until fragrant. Add the rice and stir until coated by the oil and other ingredients.

Add the reserved broth to the pan and bring to the boil, reduce heat to low, cover with lid and cook slowly for 1 hour, stirring occasionally. Turn off the heat and stir through the mushrooms and chicken. Allow the pot to sit, covered for 15 minutes. Season with salt and extra fish sauce, to your liking.

Spoon into bowls and top with any or all of the following; soy sauce, sesame seeds, chilli oil, fish sauce, extra spring onions. 

#congee #congeerecipe #foodforthesoul
recipes.recipe_ingredients:
1 tbsp sesame oil
4 cloves garlic, peeled, sliced
4 spring onions, thinly sliced, extra to serve
1 cup jasmine rice
200g mixed Asian mushrooms, torn and cut into pieces
Soy sauce, sesame seeds, chilli oil, to serve
Chicken stock
1 large piece of ginger
1.6kg whole chicken
4 spring onions, halved
1 bulb garlic, unpeeled, halved
2 eshallots, unpeeled, halved
⅓ cup fish sauce, extra to serve
recipes.recipe_method:
To make the chicken stock, thickly slice half of the ginger, set aside the remaining half for later. Place the ginger slices in a large saucepan with the remaining “stock” ingredients and fill with water until the chicken is submerged. Simmer the chicken over a low heat, covered, for 3-4 hours or until the meat is falling off the bone.
Remove the chicken and garlic from the pan and strain the chicken broth measuring out 9 cups of liquid. Discard the other solids. When cool enough to handle, pick the chicken meat into chunks and squeeze the garlic from the skin.
When ready to cook the congee, peel and finely grate the remaining ginger. Heat the oil in a large saucepan over medium heat, add the ginger, cooked garlic, fresh garlic and spring onions and cook for 1-2 minutes until fragrant. Add the rice and stir until coated by the oil and other ingredients.
Add the reserved broth to the pan and bring to the boil, reduce heat to low, cover with lid and cook slowly for 1 hour, stirring occasionally. Turn off the heat and stir through the mushrooms and chicken. Allow the pot to sit, covered for 15 minutes. Season with salt and extra fish sauce, to your liking.
Spoon into bowls and top with any or all of the following; soy sauce, sesame seeds, chilli oil, fish sauce, extra spring onions.

recipes.text: 15g protein & ~245 calories per serving some flavours just taste like home. this one is creamy, fiery, and comes together in one pan — proof that comfort food can still be macro-friendly. kanthari paneer per serving (serves 3): ~245 cal | 15g protein | 10g carbs | 16g fat (approximate — verify) ingredients (serves 3): • 200g high-protein low-fat paneer, cubed • 2 tsp coconut oil • 1 tsp fennel seeds • 4–5 shallots, sliced • 1 sprig curry leaves • crushed paste: 5–6 kanthari (bird’s eye) chillies, ½-inch ginger, 3 garlic cloves • ¼ tsp turmeric powder • 1 tsp coriander powder • ½ tsp garam masala • salt, to taste • ½ cup (120 ml) coconut milk • ½ tsp sugar • coriander leaves, to finish method: 1. heat the coconut oil and splutter the mustard seeds. 2. add the sliced shallots and curry leaves; sauté for a few minutes till softened. 3. stir in the crushed chilli–ginger–garlic paste and cook till the raw smell goes. 4. add turmeric, coriander powder and garam masala; cook for a minute. 5. pour in the coconut milk, add salt and sugar, and let it come together. 6. add the paneer cubes and simmer gently till the paneer softens and soaks up the masala. 7. finish with fresh coriander leaves and serve hot. recipes.text: hyderabadi marag recipe: ingredients: * 10 cashews * 10 almonds * 1 cup milk (for soaking) * 5 tbsp ghee * 2 tbsp ginger garlic paste * 2 small cinnamon sticks * 3 cardamom pods * 1 tsp whole black peppercorns * 1 tsp kabab chini * 3 cloves * 1 tsp shahzeera * 4 green chilies, chopped * ½ onion, sliced * 650 g lamb or mutton (bone-in), medium pieces * ¼ tsp turmeric powder * salt, to taste * ½ cup plain yogurt * 6 cups water, divided * a pinch of saffron * 1½ tsp black pepper powder * 1 tsp garam masala powder * ¼ cup chopped mint * ¼ cup chopped cilantro * ½ cup heavy cream method: 1. soak the cashews and almonds in 1 cup milk for 30 minutes. blend into a smooth paste and set aside. 2. heat the ghee in a large pot. add the ginger garlic paste, cinnamon sticks, cardamom pods, whole black peppercorns, kabab chini, cloves, and shahzeera. sauté for 2–3 minutes until fragrant. 3. add the chopped green chilies and cook for another 1–2 minutes. 4. add the sliced onion and cook for about 3 minutes. add the lamb or mutton and stir well. 5. add the turmeric, salt, yogurt, and 3 cups water. cover and cook until the meat is tender. if using a pressure cooker, cook for 3–4 whistles, then simmer for 15 minutes. check the meat and cook longer if needed. 6. once the meat is tender, stir in the cashew and almond paste along with the remaining 3 cups water. bring to a gentle boil. 7. add the saffron, black pepper powder, garam masala, mint, cilantro, and heavy cream. mix well. 8. simmer on me
recipes.caption:
hyderabadi marag 

recipe:

ingredients:

* 10 cashews
* 10 almonds
* 1 cup milk (for soaking)
* 5 tbsp ghee
* 2 tbsp ginger garlic paste
* 2 small cinnamon sticks
* 3 cardamom pods
* 1 tsp whole black peppercorns
* 1 tsp kabab chini
* 3 cloves
* 1 tsp shahzeera
* 4 green chilies, chopped
* ½ onion, sliced
* 650 g lamb or mutton (bone-in), medium pieces
* ¼ tsp turmeric powder
* salt, to taste
* ½ cup plain yogurt
* 6 cups water, divided
* a pinch of saffron
* 1½ tsp black pepper powder
* 1 tsp garam masala powder
* ¼ cup chopped mint
* ¼ cup chopped cilantro
* ½ cup heavy cream

method:

1. Soak the cashews and almonds in 1 cup milk for 30 minutes. Blend into a smooth paste and set aside.
2. Heat the ghee in a large pot. Add the ginger garlic paste, cinnamon sticks, cardamom pods, whole black peppercorns, kabab chini, cloves, and shahzeera. Sauté for 2–3 minutes until fragrant.
3. Add the chopped green chilies and cook for another 1–2 minutes.
4. Add the sliced onion and cook for about 3 minutes. Add the lamb or mutton and stir well.
5. Add the turmeric, salt, yogurt, and 3 cups water. Cover and cook until the meat is tender. If using a pressure cooker, cook for 3–4 whistles, then simmer for 15 minutes. Check the meat and cook longer if needed.
6. Once the meat is tender, stir in the cashew and almond paste along with the remaining 3 cups water. Bring to a gentle boil.
7. Add the saffron, black pepper powder, garam masala, mint, cilantro, and heavy cream. Mix well.
8. Simmer on medium-low heat for 15 minutes, stirring occasionally.
9. Serve hot with soft naan.

recipes.title: Black Bean Burgers
recipes.author: liveeatlearn
recipes.text: i take these to every cookout and even the meat eaters approve! comment 👉 "recipe" and i'll send it to you! over the years, i've eaten a lot of *meh* black bean burgers, so here's what sets these apart: 🍔 holds together and has a biteable texture because the black beans are partially whole. 🥶 letting them chill isn’t required, but it makes them really look the part! comment 👉 "recipe" and i'll send it to you! https://www.liveeatlearn.com/black-bean-burgers/

recipes.recipe_ingredients:
2 15-oz cans black beans, drained and rinsed, 425 g cans
1 green bell pepper, seeds and stem removed
½ medium white onion, cut into chunks
2 cloves garlic
1 tsp each smoked paprika, cumin, chili powder
¼ tsp each salt and pepper
1 cup panko breadcrumbs, 60 g
1 large egg
recipes.recipe_method:
Dry Beans: Drain and rinse 2 15-oz cans black beans well, then spread them onto a few layers of paper towels to let them dry.
Flavor Base: Add 1 green bell pepper, ½ medium white onion, and 2 cloves garlic to a food processor. Pulse until finely chopped. Transfer mixture to a mesh sieve and use a spatula or spoon to press out as much moisture as possible.
Make Dough: Transfer dried beans, pepper mixture, 1 tsp each smoked paprika, cumin, chili powder, and ¼ tsp each salt and pepper back to the food processor. Pulse just until combined – there should still be some bigger pieces of beans.
Stir: Transfer to a large bowl and stir in 1 cup panko breadcrumbs and 1 large egg. At this point, you can move forward or refrigerate the dough for up to 24 hours. The burgers are easier to shape if the dough has been refrigerated for at least 30 minutes.
Shape: Scoop ½ cup sized portions of the burger dough, then use your hands to form them into patties.
To cook on the stove: Place patties on a greased saute pan over medium-high heat. Cook each side for 5 to 7 minutes, or until golden brown and firm.
To cook on the grill: Set patties on a greased piece of aluminum foil over medium/high heat. Cook each side for about 7 minutes, or until golden brown and firm.
To cook in the oven: Arrange patties on a greased baking sheet and bake at 400°F (204°C) for 15 to 20 minutes, flipping once during cooking.
Serve on a burger bun with your favorite burger toppings, like cheese, lettuce, tomato, and red onion!

recipes.title: Spiced Chicken Koftas
recipes.author: depinder_
recipes.text: spiced chicken koftas 🌶️🌱 serves: 4 ingredients 500g chicken mince 1 small red onion, very finely chopped or grated 3 garlic cloves, crushed 1 tbsp ginger, finely grated 1 green chilli, finely chopped (optional) ¼ cup fresh coriander, finely chopped ¼ cup fresh mint, finely chopped 1 tsp cumin powder 2 tsp coriander powder 1 tsp garam masala 1 tsp kashmiri chilli powder (for colour + mild heat) salt to taste 2 tbsp besan (gram flour) or breadcrumbs 1 egg (slightly beaten) 1 tbsp lemon juice 2 tbsp oil (for cooking) 1 tbsp soy sauce method in a large bowl, combine the chicken mince with onion, garlic, ginger, chilli, herbs, spices, besan/breadcrumbs, egg, and lemon juice. mix really well your hands are best here to help everything bind together. cover and rest the mixture in the fridge for at least 20–30 minutes. this helps the flavours deepen and makes shaping easier. with slightly damp hands, shape the mixture into small round koftas, similar to meatballs. heat oil in a pan over medium heat. cook the koftas in batches, turning gently, until golden brown on all sides and cooked through (about 8–10 minutes). you can also air-fry these at 180c for 10-12 mins. turning them over halfway. rest for a couple of minutes before serving this keeps them juicy. ps: if you skip chilli, this is superrrr kid friendly, my little ones love it ❤️✌🏼
recipes.caption:
Spiced Chicken Koftas 🌶️🌱

Serves: 4
Ingredients
500g chicken mince
1 small red onion, very finely chopped or grated
3 garlic cloves, crushed
1 tbsp ginger, finely grated
1 green chilli, finely chopped (optional)
¼ cup fresh coriander, finely chopped
¼ cup fresh mint, finely chopped

1 tsp cumin powder
2 tsp coriander powder
1 tsp garam masala
1 tsp Kashmiri chilli powder (for colour + mild heat)
Salt to taste
2 tbsp besan (gram flour) or breadcrumbs
1 egg (slightly beaten)
1 tbsp lemon juice
2 tbsp oil (for cooking)
1 tbsp soy sauce 
Method
In a large bowl, combine the chicken mince with onion, garlic, ginger, chilli, herbs, spices, besan/breadcrumbs, egg, and lemon juice. Mix really well your hands are best here to help everything bind together.
Cover and rest the mixture in the fridge for at least 20–30 minutes. This helps the flavours deepen and makes shaping easier.
With slightly damp hands, shape the mixture into small round koftas, similar to meatballs.
Heat oil in a pan over medium heat. Cook the koftas in batches, turning gently, until golden brown on all sides and cooked through (about 8–10 minutes).
You can also Air-fry these at 180C for 10-12 mins. Turning them over halfway.
Rest for a couple of minutes before serving this keeps them juicy.

PS: if you skip chilli, this is superrrr kid friendly, my little ones love it ❤️✌🏼

recipes.caption:
Episode 10 of #SweetSummerTreats ☀️✨ a series where I make easy, refreshing summer desserts right at home

Nothing beats a chilled glass of homemade Badam Milk on a warm day 💛 Loaded with almonds, saffron, pistachios, and that beautiful cardamom aroma… this recipe feels rich, nostalgic, and so satisfying

BADAM MILK
 
Ingredients
4 cups (1 litre) milk
½ cup sugar
1 cup almonds(soaked and peeled) + ¾ cup milk
1 tbsp custard powder + 2 tbsp milk
2 tsp saffron strands + 2 tbsp milk
½ tsp cardamom powder
3 tbsp pistachios, slivered
3 tbsp almonds, slivered

Instructions
Soak ¾ cup almonds in water overnight.
Peel the almonds and blend them into a thick paste along with ¾ cup milk.
Now, set a large pot on medium heat and add 1 litre milk to it.
Once it starts to simmer, add sugar, almond paste, custard powder slurry, saffron infused milk and cardamom powder.
Bring it to a boil and heat until the milk thickens a bit.
Add slivered almonds and pistachios and mix well.
Let it come to room temperature before storing in bottles. Serve chilled.

recipes.caption:
260 calories and 28g of protein per serving — done in 20 minutes, one pan, zero fuss. Plump prawns, brown onions, fiery chilli garlic paste, all tossed through cooked rice to get a desi spicy fried rice feel. 🔥❤️

Chilli Garlic Prawn Rice
📊 ~260 kcal | ~28g Protein | ~20g Carbs | ~9.5g Fat per serving (with shirataki rice)
📊 ~467 kcal | ~31g Protein | ~65g Carbs | ~9.5g Fat per serving (with regular cooked rice)
Makes 2 Servings of 350 g each

Ingredients
FOR THE PASTE
•	10–12 garlic cloves
•	1 tbsp Kashmiri chilli powder
•	2 tsp coriander powder
•	Salt to taste
•	Splash of water
FOR THE STIR FRY
•	1 tbsp oil
•	1 tsp mustard seeds
•	2 sprigs curry leaves
•	1 medium onion, sliced
•	250g prawns, diced
•	350g cooked shirataki rice (or 350g cooked white/basmati rice — approx. 130g raw)
•	Salt to taste
•	Fresh coriander leaves, chopped (to finish)
•	1.5 tbsp lemon juice (to finish)
QUICK TIP — HOW TO COOK DRY SHIRATAKI RICE (I’ve used Urban Platter)
Mix 100g dry shirataki rice with equal parts water (100ml) and microwave on high for 2 minutes.

METHOD
•	Blitz or pound the garlic, Kashmiri powder, coriander powder, salt, and a splash of water into a smooth paste.
•	Heat oil in a pan, splutter the mustard seeds, then add curry leaves and sliced onion. Sauté till the onion softens and turns translucent.
•	Add the spice paste and cook on medium for 2–3 minutes till the raw smell disappears and the oil separates.
•	Add the diced prawns, mix well, and cook for about a minute till they just turn opaque — don’t overdo it or they’ll go rubbery.
•	Add the cooked shirataki rice (or regular cooked rice), toss everything together, and let it warm through for another minute so the masala coats every grain.
•	Check salt, finish with chopped coriander leaves and a generous squeeze of lemon. Divide between 2 plates and serve hot.

FOR THE STIR FRY

recipes.recipe_method:
Mix 100g dry shirataki rice with equal parts water (100ml) and microwave on high for 2 minutes.
Blitz or pound the garlic, Kashmiri powder, coriander powder, salt, and a splash of water into a smooth paste.
Heat oil in a pan, splutter the mustard seeds, then add curry leaves and sliced onion. Sauté till the onion softens and turns translucent.
Add the spice paste and cook on medium for 2–3 minutes till the raw smell disappears and the oil separates.
Add the diced prawns, mix well, and cook for about a minute till they just turn opaque — don’t overdo it or they’ll go rubbery.
Add the cooked shirataki rice (or regular cooked rice), toss everything together, and let it warm through for another minute so the masala coats every grain.
Check salt, finish with chopped coriander leaves and a generous squeeze of lemon. Divide between 2 plates and serve hot.

recipes.caption:
🌶️🍳 Steamed Podi Eggs

These are NOT your regular eggs.
Soft steamed eggs shaped like little idlis, tossed in freshly made spicy podi and ghee — honestly, breakfast doesn’t get better than this. 🤌✨

Comes together so easily and tastes like the kind of breakfast you’ll keep thinking about all day.

✨ Ingredients for the Podi:
• 1 tbsp coconut oil
• Curry leaves
• 4–5 dry red chillies
• 2 tbsp urad dal
• 1 tbsp chana dal
• 1 tbsp sesame seeds
• A pinch of hing
• Salt to taste
• ¼ tsp turmeric

✨ For the Eggs:
• Eggs
• Ghee
• Curry leaves
• Fresh coriander
• Freshly made podi

✨ Method — Podi:
• Heat coconut oil in a pan and sauté curry leaves and dry red chillies for a minute. Set aside.

• Add sesame seeds and sauté a little more.
• Transfer everything to a mixer with hing, salt, and turmeric. Grind into a fine podi.

✨ Method — Eggs:
• Steam the eggs in an idli mould and gently demould once done.
• Heat ghee in a pan and add curry leaves along with the freshly made podi.
• Toss in the steamed eggs till beautifully coated.
• Garnish with fresh coriander and enjoy! 🌿

recipes.author: cashsofia
recipes.text: 🍯 salted honey and vanilla cookies 🐝 i’m going to start with the tips to make sure you actually follow them. please, follow them 🫶🏻 - when you incorporate the dry ingredients, do not beat them, you just want the dough to come together, you can even incorporate them by hand to avoid over mixing - weigh each cookie ball to 50g, these cookies are very sensitive to timing and heat, so you need all balls to be the same size - bake only 1 tray at a time, with only 5 balls in it. they spread quite a lot, so if you put more balls, they might become a huge pancake - bake at 180°c ❗️lower and upper heat❗️(no hot air, as they will become hard and might burn) - at minute 8 during baking you will see bubbles are forming, you want to remove them by giving the baking tray a tap. just lift it in the oven without removing it from its rail and let it fall back to the rail. you will see all bubbles become flat, exactly what you are looking for. - bake only for 14 minutes, no more. they might look too soft in the center, but they will set once out if the oven. - you will want to reshape them with a ring (as shown in the video) once they come out of the oven. do it right away, otherwise they will set and you will not be able to reshape them. - lastly, have patience, they might not come out perfect the first time, but it’s so worth it to try again and again 🫶🏻 recipe (14 cookies): - 200 g butter (cold from the fridge) - 250 g sugar - 70 g thick honey - 20 g vanilla sugar - 1 whole egg - 240 g flou
recipes.caption:
🍯 Salted honey and vanilla cookies 🐝 

I’m going to start with the tips to make sure you actually follow them. Please, follow them 🫶🏻

- When you incorporate the dry ingredients, do not beat them, you just want the dough to come together, you can even incorporate them by hand to avoid over mixing
- Weigh each cookie ball to 50g, these cookies are very sensitive to timing and heat, so you need all balls to be the same size
- Bake only 1 tray at a time, with only 5 balls in it. They spread quite a lot, so if you put more balls, they might become a huge pancake 
- Bake at 180°C ❗️lower and upper heat❗️(no hot air, as they will become hard and might burn)
- At minute 8 during baking you will see bubbles are forming, you want to remove them by giving the baking tray a tap. Just lift it in the oven without removing it from its rail and let it fall back to the rail. You will see all bubbles become flat, exactly what you are looking for.
- Bake ONLY for 14 minutes, no more. They might look too soft in the center, but they will set once out if the oven.
- You will want to reshape them with a ring (as shown in the video) once they come out of the oven. Do it right away, otherwise they will set and you will not be able to reshape them.
- Lastly, have patience, they might not come out perfect the first time, but it’s so worth it to try again and again 🫶🏻

Recipe (14 cookies):
- 200 g butter (cold from the fridge)
- 250 g sugar
- 70 g thick honey
- 20 g vanilla sugar 
- 1 whole egg
- 240 g flour
- 2 g baking powder
- 4 g baking soda
- 2 g salt

- Flake salt to taste to sprinkle 

How to:
- Beat the butter, sugar and honey until whitened and fluffy
- Add the egg and beat until completely combined 
- Add the dry ingredients just until combined, you can do this step by hand to avoid over mixing
- Make balls of 50 g each
- Place 5 balls per tray (as shown in the video)
- Bake at 180°C for a maximum of 14 minutes
- Reshape them with a ring right after baking 
- Sprinkle with salt
- Enjoy!! 🍯 

They are seriously addictive 🧚🏻‍♀️

👶 Các gia đình rất thích BLW vì bé có thể ăn cùng bữa với gia đình, học theo những gì mình thấy và xây dựng tính tự lập trong khi vẫn cảm thấy vui vẻ!
💡 Mẹo: Vào lúc 6 tháng tuổi, hãy tránh những miếng quá nhỏ (vì bé chưa có kỹ năng bốc nhón bằng ngón trỏ và ngón cái 👌). Hãy chuẩn bị đồ ăn dạng thanh hoặc miếng dài để bé có thể nắm chặt trong lòng bàn tay. Khoảng từ 10–12 tháng tuổi, những miếng nhỏ sẽ giúp bé rèn luyện kỹ năng vận động tinh.
🧂 Sử dụng dầu ăn, các loại thảo mộc và gia vị dịu nhẹ (hạn chế muối).
🍯 Tuyệt đối không dùng mật ong cho trẻ dưới 12 tháng tuổi!

recipes.caption:
248 cal & 23g protein per Serving
Sweet from ripe mango, smoky from soaked dry red chillies, salty-umami from soy, all melting into a creamy coconut sauce. The paneer is grilled till charred for that lovely smoky bite, and the crushed peanuts on top? Non-negotiable. All this goodness — and a proper restaurant-style meal — for under 250 cal a serving, with 23g of protein doing the heavy lifting.
Creamy Mango Chilli Paneer
Macros per serving: 248 cal | 23g protein | 17g carbs | 10g fat | 2g fibre
Ingredients (serves 2):
For the sauce:
	•	6 dry red chillies (soaked in hot water for 10 mins, drained)
	•	50g ripe mango
	•	5 garlic cloves
	•	1 stalk spring onion
	•	½ tsp honey
	•	1½ tbsp light soy sauce
	•	2 tsp lemon juice
	•	Salt to taste
	•	2–3 tbsp water (to blend)
To cook:
	•	200g low-fat, high-protein paneer, cubed
	•	60ml light coconut milk
	•	Salt, black pepper, and chilli flakes (for the paneer)
To finish:
	•	1 tbsp crushed roasted peanuts
	•	Fresh coriander, chopped
	•	Steamed rice, to serve
Method:
	1.	Soak the dry red chillies in hot water for 10 minutes until soft. Drain.
	2.	Blend the soaked chillies with mango, garlic, spring onion, honey, soy sauce, lemon juice, salt, and water until smooth.
	3.	Pour the sauce into a non-stick pan and cook on medium heat for 4–5 minutes, until the raw smell of garlic and onion disappears and it thickens slightly. Splash in a little water if it sticks.
	4.	Stir in the coconut milk and simmer for 2 more minutes until creamy and glossy.
	5.	Meanwhile, season the paneer cubes with salt, pepper, and chilli flakes. Dry-grill on a hot non-stick pan until charred on the edges.
	6.	Add the grilled paneer to the sauce and toss to coat.
	7.	Finish with crushed peanuts and coriander. Serve hot with steamed rice.

recipes.recipe_ingredients:
For the sauce:
6 dry red chillies (soaked in hot water for 10 mins, drained)
50g ripe mango
5 garlic cloves
1 stalk spring onion
½ tsp honey
1½ tbsp light soy sauce
2 tsp lemon juice
Salt to taste
2–3 tbsp water (to blend)
To cook:
200g low-fat, high-protein paneer, cubed
60ml light coconut milk
Salt, black pepper, and chilli flakes (for the paneer)
To finish:
1 tbsp crushed roasted peanuts
Fresh coriander, chopped
Steamed rice, to serve
recipes.recipe_method:
1. Soak the dry red chillies in hot water for 10 minutes until soft. Drain.
2. Blend the soaked chillies with mango, garlic, spring onion, honey, soy sauce, lemon juice, salt, and water until smooth.
3. Pour the sauce into a non-stick pan and cook on medium heat for 4–5 minutes, until the raw smell of garlic and onion disappears and it thickens slightly. Splash in a little water if it sticks.
4. Stir in the coconut milk and simmer for 2 more minutes until creamy and glossy.
5. Meanwhile, season the paneer cubes with salt, pepper, and chilli flakes. Dry-grill on a hot non-stick pan until charred on the edges.
6. Add the grilled paneer to the sauce and toss to coat.
7. Finish with crushed peanuts and coriander. Serve hot with steamed rice.

Recipe:

Mango Chilly Picante 🌶️🥭

Ingredients

For the Drink

* 1/2 cup mango puree
* Water
* Soda water
* 2 jalapeño slices
* 1 tsp hot honey
* Lime juice
* Ice cubes
* Mint leaf or fresh red chilli for garnish

⸻

Hot Honey Recipe

Ingredients

* 2 tbsp honey
* 1 tsp red chilli flakes
* 1 tsp apple cider vinegar

Method

1. In a small pan, simmer the honey on low heat.
2. Add the red chilli flakes and let it infuse while simmering.
3. Add the apple cider vinegar and mix well.
4. Let it infuse for about 5 minutes.
5. Remove from heat and allow it to cool slightly.

⸻

Method

1. Rim your serving glass.
2. In a shaker, muddle the jalapeño slices with lime juice and hot honey.
3. Add mango puree, a splash of water, and ice cubes.
4. Shake well until chilled.
5. Fill the prepared glass with fresh ice.
6. Strain the drink into the glass.
7. Top with soda water.
8. Garnish with a mint leaf or a fresh red chilli.

Serve chilled.

recipes.title: Muffins
recipes.author: beth_thefirstyear
recipes.text: and you can be scrolling during those 15 minutes!! in case you’re new here — hi! 👋🏻 i’m beth, and i’ve been named the internet’s muffin expert! after spending 6 months testing and perfecting my muffin recipes, i’ve created 4 tips that will level up just about any muffin recipe! 1. the rest period. let your batter rest for 15 minutes before you scoop it into your muffin pan. this allows the starch molecules in your batter to swell and absorb, creating a thicker batter, that will then bake into a tall, bakery-style dome! 2. overfill your muffin liners. if you’re anything like me, you were taught growing up to only fill your liners 3/4 of the way full. that’s not how we do things around here!! i fill my muffin liners with 6-8 heaping tablespoons of batter! this will give you that signature beth-style superdome! 3. only bake 6 muffin at a time. if you’re using a standard 12 muffin tin, fill every other well to give the muffins room to spread and dome without running into their neighbors. this gives you that beautiful round top instead of square edges! 4. jumpstart your baking with a high heat. start baking your muffins at 425°f for the first 7 minutes of your bake time, then decrease the temp to 350°f for the remaining bake time. this causes the batter to rise rapidly and set them up for superdome success! want more muffin content? follow along and comment “muffin” below! i’ll send you the link to my bakery style muffin cookbook!
recipes.caption:
And you can be scrolling during those 15 minutes!!

In case you’re new here — Hi! 👋🏻 I’m Beth, and I’ve been named the internet’s Muffin Expert! After spending 6 months testing and perfecting my muffin recipes, I’ve created 4 tips that will level up just about any muffin recipe!

1. The rest period. Let your batter rest for 15 minutes before you scoop it into your muffin pan. This allows the starch molecules in your batter to swell and absorb, creating a thicker batter, that will then bake into a tall, bakery-style dome!

2. Overfill your muffin liners. If you’re anything like me, you were taught growing up to only fill your liners 3/4 of the way full. That’s not how we do things around here!! I fill my muffin liners with 6-8 heaping tablespoons of batter! This will give you that signature Beth-style superdome!

3. Only bake 6 muffin at a time. If you’re using a standard 12 muffin tin, fill every other well to give the muffins room to spread and dome without running into their neighbors. This gives you that beautiful round top instead of square edges!

4. Jumpstart your baking with a high heat. Start baking your muffins at 425°F for the first 7 minutes of your bake time, then decrease the temp to 350°F for the remaining bake time. This causes the batter to rise rapidly and set them up for superdome success!

recipes.title: Spicy Peanut Coconut Noodles
recipes.author: salonikukreja
recipes.text: spicy peanut coconut noodles \ my dream is to open an asian café, and i’m building the menu one dish at a time – with you here! this recipe brings you the kind of noodles you make when you want something quick, satisfying, and seriously flavour-packed 😍🌶️ 100g ramen noodles 2tbsps peanut butter 1/2 cup coconut milk 1/2 cup water 2 tbsps chilli oil 6 cloves garlic - minced 1” ginger - grated 2 stalks green onion 1.5tsps sugar 2 tsps lime juice 1 stock cube 1 tbsps soy sauce 1 tsps - coriander powder sesame oil- 1tsp salt as required for garnish: sesame seeds- 2 tsps chopped peanuts green onions process for the broth: * in a pan add neutral oil. * ⁠once the oil is heated add ginger, garlic and onions and saute for about a minute. add the coriander powder and cook it. * ⁠add 1/2cup water along with soy sauce and stock cubes. let the water simmer * ⁠once the water is hot add in the peanut butter and chili oil. adjust the seasonings * ⁠add the coconut milk and let it simmer on a low flame. * ⁠stir in the lemon juice and sesame oil once off the flame. •add the noodles to the boiling water and let it cook for 4-5 mins or till they are completely cooked. * strain the noodles once done and rinse under cold water * ⁠in a bowl place the noodles and pour over the prepared broth * ⁠garnish with chopped peanuts, green onions,sesame seeds and chili oil
recipes.caption:
Spicy Peanut Coconut Noodles \ My dream is to open an Asian café, and I’m building the menu one dish at a time – with you here! This recipe brings you the kind of noodles you make when you want something quick, satisfying, and seriously flavour-packed 😍🌶️ 

100g Ramen noodles

Process
For the Broth:
* In a pan add neutral oil.
* ⁠Once the oil is heated add ginger, garlic and onions and saute for about a minute. Add the coriander powder and cook it.
* ⁠Add 1/2cup water along with soy sauce and stock cubes. Let the water simmer
* ⁠Once the water is hot add in the peanut butter and chili oil. Adjust the seasonings
* ⁠Add the coconut milk and let it simmer on a low flame.
* ⁠Stir in the lemon juice and sesame oil once off the flame.

•Add the noodles to the boiling water and let it cook for 4-5 mins or till they are completely cooked.
* strain the noodles once done and rinse under cold water
* ⁠In a bowl place the noodles and pour over the prepared broth
* ⁠Garnish with chopped peanuts, green onions,sesame seeds and chili oil

recipes.recipe_method:
In a pan add neutral oil.
Once the oil is heated add ginger, garlic and onions and saute for about a minute. Add the coriander powder and cook it.
Add 1/2cup water along with soy sauce and stock cubes. Let the water simmer
Once the water is hot add in the peanut butter and chili oil. Adjust the seasonings
Add the coconut milk and let it simmer on a low flame.
Stir in the lemon juice and sesame oil once off the flame.
Add the noodles to the boiling water and let it cook for 4-5 mins or till they are completely cooked.
strain the noodles once done and rinse under cold water
In a bowl place the noodles and pour over the prepared broth
