recipes.title: Tofu Kathi Rolls
recipes.author: myvegetarianroots
recipes.text: tofu haters are gonna hate, flavor lovers are gonna marinate! comment “roll” to get full the recipe & start the marinade 🙌🏾 https://myvegetarianroots.com/tofu-kathi-rolls/
recipes.caption:
Tofu haters are gonna hate, flavor lovers are gonna marinate! Comment “roll” to get full the recipe & start the marinade 🙌🏾

https://myvegetarianroots.com/tofu-kathi-rolls/
recipes.recipe_ingredients:
Tofu Marinade
16 oz Organic Super Firm Tofu I user Nasoya
½ cup Plain Greek Yogurt I use Fage Fat Free Plain Greek Yogurt
1 tbsp Grated Ginger
2 tbsp Minced Garlic
1 tbsp Tandoori Masala I use Shan foods tandoori masala
1 tsp Garam Masala
1½ tsp Chaat Masala
1 tsp Kashmiri Red Chili Powder ½ tsp of using regular spicy red chili powder
1½ tsp Roasted Cumin Powder
½ tsp Turmeric Powder
¼ tsp Black Pepper Powder
½ tsp Salt
½ tsp Kasuri Methi
1 tbsp Lemon Juice
2 tbsp Mustard Oil any oil of your choice will work
2 tsp Honey
1 medium Red Onion, sliced if using extra large onion, user ¾ of it
Cilantro Mint Yogurt Sauce
½ cup Fresh Cilantro washed/drained/roots removed
¼ cup Fresh Mint Leaves
½ tsp Roasted Cumin Powder
¼ tsp Black Pepper Powder
½ tsp Salt
½ Jalapeno 1 whole for more heat
1 small Garlic
1 tbsp Lemon Juice
½ cup Fage Fat Free Greek Yogurt ⅔ cup of only using greek yogurt, not sour cream
¼ cup Sour Cream skip if using ⅔ cup greek yogurt
If making kathi rolls
5 Whole Wheat Lavash Bread, or choice of paratha
1 English Cucumber, sliced
½ Red Onion, very thinly sliced
½ Green Pepper, very thinly sliced
1 cup Shredded Lettuce
1 tsp Chaat Masala
recipes.recipe_method:
Marinade the Tofu
Mix everything BUT tofu and onion listed under "Tofu Marinade" in a big wide bowl. Keep it aside.
Break tofu into small uneven pieces so that the edges are rough. Bring a pot of water to boil with 1 tsp of salt. Add in tofu pieces and boil them for 5-7 minutes. Then drain it.
Once tofu is boiled and drained, add it into marinade bowl. Add in sliced red onions too. Toss all pieces around or gently mix with rubber spatula so that each pieces are well coated with marinade, without breaking them or making them mushy. Once ready, cover it and let it marinate for anywhere from 30 minutes to over night.
Once ready to bake, pre heat oven on 375℉. Lay out marinated tofu and onions on a greased baking tray, all in single layer. Bake it for 20 minutes, tossing them half way through. Serve it with cilantro mint sauce.
Cilantro Mint Yogurt Sauce
First place everything but yogurt and sour cream in a food processor. Pulse it all until you have grainy texture.
Then add in greek yogurt and do just few pulses so that the grainy texture is mixed into yogurt. Blending too much with yogurt will make the sauce very liquidy. You want to leave the sauce thick, grainy, pasty.
Make Kathi Roll
Warm up lavash bread or choice of paratha.
Spread some cilantro mint sauce on one side of the lavash/paratha.
Top it with sliced cucumber, onion, pepper, lettuce and sprinkle of chaat masala.
Top it with baked tandoori tofu with drizzle of cilantro mint sauce. Roll it and enjoy with or without making it crispy on the skillet.

recipes.title: Tofu Theplas
recipes.author: whenmeateatsveg
recipes.text: ep 1: tofu theplas - season 2, gujarati series 🇮🇳 ingredients: 2 cups chapatti (whole wheat) flour 1½ cups tofu, grated 1 tsp homemade chilli paste 2 tbsp oil (plus extra for cooking) 2 tsp salt 1 tsp turmeric powder ¼ cup sesame seeds 1 small bunch fresh fenugreek leaves (stems removed, finely chopped) ~150 g hot water (as needed) method: 1. in a large bowl, combine the flour, salt, turmeric powder, and sesame seeds. mix well. add the oil and rub it into the flour mixture. add the grated tofu and mix thoroughly. 2. stir in the chilli paste, followed by the chopped fenugreek leaves. mix until evenly combined. 3. gradually add hot water, mixing as you go, until a soft dough forms. cover and let the dough rest for a few minutes. 4. divide the dough into small portions and roll each into a thin flatbread (thepla). 5. heat a skillet (tawa) over medium-high heat. place a rolled thepla onto the hot skillet. 6. after about 10 seconds, flip it. lightly spread oil on the cooked side, then flip again and apply oil to the other side 7. cook, flipping a few times, until both sides are golden and cooked through. 8. remove and place on a plate. enjoy warm on its own or with yogurt, pickle, or chutney.
recipes.caption:
EP 1: Tofu Theplas - SEASON 2, GUJARATI SERIES 🇮🇳 

INGREDIENTS:
2 cups chapatti (whole wheat) flour
1½ cups tofu, grated
1 Tsp homemade chilli paste
2 Tbsp oil (plus extra for cooking)
2 Tsp salt
1 Tsp Turmeric powder
¼ Cup sesame seeds
1 small bunch fresh fenugreek leaves (stems removed, finely chopped)
~150 g hot water (as needed)

METHOD:
1. In a large bowl, combine the flour, salt, turmeric powder, and sesame seeds. Mix well. Add the oil and rub it into the flour mixture. Add the grated tofu and mix thoroughly.
2. Stir in the chilli paste, followed by the chopped fenugreek leaves. Mix until evenly combined.
3. Gradually add hot water, mixing as you go, until a soft dough forms. Cover and let the dough rest for a few minutes.
4. Divide the dough into small portions and roll each into a thin flatbread (thepla).
5. Heat a skillet (tawa) over medium-high heat. Place a rolled thepla onto the hot skillet.
6. After about 10 seconds, flip it. Lightly spread oil on the cooked side, then flip again and apply oil to the other side
7. Cook, flipping a few times, until both sides are golden and cooked through.
8. Remove and place on a plate. Enjoy warm on its own or with yogurt, pickle, or chutney.

recipes.title: Gluten-Free Orange Almond Cake
recipes.author: cozycookingchris
recipes.text: gluten-free orange almond cake a moist, naturally gluten-free cake bursting with fresh orange flavor, almond flour, and almond meal. lightly sweetened with honey and enriched with olive oil, this cake is perfect for breakfast, afternoon tea, or a simple dessert. ingredients - 2 large eggs - 1/2–1 tbsp orange zest - 2 tbsp (30 g) fresh orange juice - 1/3 cup (73 g) olive oil - 1 tsp (5 g) vanilla extract - 1/4 cup (85 g) honey - 2 cups (192 g) almond flour - 1/4 cup (30 g) almond meal - 1/2 tsp (2 g) baking powder - 1/2 tsp (2.5 g) baking soda instructions 1. preheat oven to 350°f (175°c). grease 6”x3”3” loaf pan or a 8-inch round cake pan. 2. in a large bowl, whisk the eggs until lightly frothy. add the orange zest, orange juice, olive oil, vanilla, and honey. whisk until smooth and fully combined. 3. in a separate bowl, combine the almond flour, almond meal, baking powder, and baking soda. 4. gently fold the dry ingredients into the wet mixture until just incorporated. do not overmix. 5. pour the batter into the prepared pan and smooth the top with a spatula. 6. bake for 30–35 minutes, or until a toothpick inserted into the center comes out clean. 7. allow the cake to cool completely in the pan before slicing.
recipes.caption:
Gluten-Free Orange Almond Cake

A moist, naturally gluten-free cake bursting with fresh orange flavor, almond flour, and almond meal. Lightly sweetened with honey and enriched with olive oil, this cake is perfect for breakfast, afternoon tea, or a simple dessert.

Ingredients

- 2 large eggs
- 1/2–1 tbsp orange zest
- 2 tbsp (30 g) fresh orange juice
- 1/3 cup (73 g) olive oil
- 1 tsp (5 g) vanilla extract
- 1/4 cup (85 g) honey
- 2 cups (192 g) almond flour
- 1/4 cup (30 g) almond meal
- 1/2 tsp (2 g) baking powder
- 1/2 tsp (2.5 g) baking soda

Instructions

1. Preheat oven to 350°F (175°C). Grease 6”x3”3” loaf pan or a 8-inch round cake pan.
2. In a large bowl, whisk the eggs until lightly frothy. Add the orange zest, orange juice, olive oil, vanilla, and honey. Whisk until smooth and fully combined.
3. In a separate bowl, combine the almond flour, almond meal, baking powder, and baking soda.
4. Gently fold the dry ingredients into the wet mixture until just incorporated. Do not overmix.
5. Pour the batter into the prepared pan and smooth the top with a spatula.
6. Bake for 30–35 minutes, or until a toothpick inserted into the center comes out clean.
7. Allow the cake to cool completely in the pan before slicing.

1. Preheat oven to 350°F (175°C). Grease 6”x3”3” loaf pan or a 8-inch round cake pan.
2. In a large bowl, whisk the eggs until lightly frothy. Add the orange zest, orange juice, olive oil, vanilla, and honey. Whisk until smooth and fully combined.
3. In a separate bowl, combine the almond flour, almond meal, baking powder, and baking soda.
4. Gently fold the dry ingredients into the wet mixture until just incorporated. Do not overmix.
5. Pour the batter into the prepared pan and smooth the top with a spatula.
6. Bake for 30–35 minutes, or until a toothpick inserted into the center comes out clean.
7. Allow the cake to cool completely in the pan before slicing.

recipes.caption:
DAY 51/100: MISO TAHINI PEAS ON SOURDOUGH.

The 5-minute savoury reclamation of your gut health.

Most “healthy” breakfasts are sugar traps in disguise that leave you bloated + sluggish by 10:00 AM. This is the professional-grade pivot: functional fermentation + high-integrity fibre.

We’re using the umami depth of dark miso + the creamy “drizz factor” of tahini to turn humble peas into a probiotic powerhouse. This isn’t just a meal; it’s a tool for digestive recovery that actually respects your system. Dairy-free, plant-based, + zero compromise on the “YUM” factor.

INGREDIENTS 
1 heaped cup frozen peas 
1 teaspoon olive oil 
1/2 teaspoon cumin seeds
1 cup boiling water
2 tablespoons runny tahini
1 teaspoon dark organic miso paste
a good pinch of dried thyme
a good pinch of flaky sea salt + freshly ground black pepper 
1/8 teaspoon turmeric powder
a squeeze of fresh lemon
sourdough toast

METHOD 
Place a small pot over medium heat + add frozen peas. Create a small space in the centre of the peas, add olive oil + follow immediately with cumin seeds. Stir-fry amongst the peas for 1 minute until fragrant. This “blooms” the spices for maximum bioavailability + flavour depth.
Pour in boiling water, then add tahini, miso paste, thyme, salt, + turmeric. Gently fold everything together until the miso + tahini have fully integrated into the liquid.
Cook for 2 more minutes. Watch as the water reduces + evaporates, transforming into a deep, rich, + incredibly creamy golden sauce that coats every pea.
Remove from the heat + stir through a generous squeeze of fresh lemon to brighten the umami notes + support digestion.
Dollop the mixture onto hot buttered sourdough toast. Finish with a heavy grind of black pepper + an extra pinch of flaky sea salt for that essential crunch.

SAVE this for your gut-health reset + SHARE it with someone who needs help with bloating!

Are you Team Sourdough or do you prefer a gluten-free base? 👇

#guthealthreset #chefrecipe #functionalnutrition #cheflife

recipes.text: rose kulfi 🍨 - quick, no-cook recipe as per tradition, i’m sharing a quick yet absolutely stunning rose kulfi recipe that is perfect if you’re looking for a last minute eid dessert! and omg guys.. this turned out better than i expected.. it tasted like falooda! 😮‍💨 here’s what you need👇🏽 - 3 white bread slices, (slice off the ends). - 1 pack heavy whipping cream (16 oz) - 1 can evaporated milk (12 oz) - 1/2 can sweetened condensed milk (7oz) - 1 tablespoon cardamom powder (crush it yourself using a mortar pestle or spice grinder if powder is not available) - 2 tablespoons finely crushed pistachios - 2 tablespoons rose syrup (rooh afza) (you can add more if you want it to be more pink) - crushed pistachios, and dried rose petals to garnish. here’s what you do👇🏽 combine all the ingredients using a blender or food processor and pulse till well combined. pour into a freezer safe dish and freeze for at least 6-8 hours although overnight works best. i used a round dish so i could make a moon garnish but square or rectangular shape works better for serving. when the kulfi is firm approximately 2 hours later, garnish.
recipes.caption:
ROSE KULFI 🍨 - quick, no-cook recipe

As per tradition, I’m sharing a quick yet absolutely stunning rose kulfi recipe that is perfect if you’re looking for a last minute Eid dessert! And omg guys.. this turned out better than I expected.. it tasted like falooda! 😮‍💨

Here’s what you need👇🏽

- 3 white bread slices, (slice off the ends).
- 1 pack heavy whipping cream (16 oz)
- 1 can evaporated milk (12 oz)
- 1/2 can sweetened condensed milk (7oz)
- 1 tablespoon cardamom powder (crush it yourself using a mortar pestle or spice grinder if powder is not available)
- 2 tablespoons finely crushed pistachios
- 2 tablespoons rose syrup (rooh afza) (you can add more if you want it to be more pink)
- Crushed pistachios, and dried rose petals to garnish.

Here’s what you do👇🏽

Combine all the ingredients using a blender or food processor and PULSE till well combined. Pour into a freezer safe dish and freeze for at least 6-8 hours although overnight works best. I used a round dish so I could make a moon garnish but square or rectangular shape works better for serving. When the kulfi is firm approximately 2 hours later, garnish.

recipes.caption:

QUESTION: Why should you be eating more millets?

It provides a good amount of plant-based protein, and is naturally gluten-free. Plus, it’s packed with crucial vitamins and minerals that support overall health.

So unlock the power of millets with my new Jowar Masala Fulka Roti recipe! This video walks you through making perfectly puffed, spiced jowar rotis that are both tasty and incredibly beneficial to health. 

Recipe -
- Heat 1 cup Water in a deep base pan
- Add 1/2 tsp coarsely crushed Cumin Seeds 
- Add 1/2 tsp White Sesame Seeds 
- Add Salt to taste 
- Heat water up to a boil
- Now add 1 cup Sorghum Flour and turn off the heat quickly 
- Add finely chopped Coriander 
- Add crushed Black Pepper 
- Combine everything well, cover the lid and rest the dough for 5 min
- Transfer it in a bowl and start kneading a soft dough
- Apply a little Oil on it
- Start making balls from the dough prepared
- Cover the remaining dough with a wet cloth
- Take a dough ball and deep it into dry flour
- Roll the roti with the help of rolling pin
- Heat the pan and place roti on it
- Slightly cook both the sides 
- Take it directly on a flame and cook both the sides until puffed. (You can also cook it on pan by pressing with the napkin)
- Take out roti from the heat and spread Ghee on it
- Enjoy this Lucious Jowar Masala Roti with Baingan and Imli ki Chutney or your Favorite Sabji

recipes.author: christianna.nutritionist
recipes.text: high protein porridge . this is the creamiest, most gorgeous porridge i make. it’s delicious and it also happens to be high in protein, with each portion containing around 20g of. you can top it with whatever you like, today i went for peanut butter and a little chocolate which was just dreamy! . ingredients - makes one portion ▪️50g jumbo oats (1/2 heaped cup) ▪️1 egg, room temperature ▪️180ml (3/4 cup oat milk) ▪️1 teaspoon vanilla ▪️1 tablespoon honey ▪️65g greek yoghurt ▪️toppings of your choice method ▪️in a small pan off the heat, add the milk, egg, vanilla and honey. whisk well to make sure it’s fully combined. ▪️add the oats. ▪️put the pan on a low to medium heat and cook gently for about 15 minutes, stirring almost continuously till thick and creamy. ▪️take it off the heat and mix in the yoghurt till fully combined. trust me on this one, it works! ▪️spoon your porridge into a bowl and add whatever toppings you like. . . .
recipes.caption:
High protein porridge @christianna.nutritionist 
.
This is the creamiest, most gorgeous porridge I make. It’s delicious and it also happens to be high in protein, with each portion containing around 20g of. 
You can top it with whatever you like, today I went for peanut butter and a little chocolate which was just dreamy! 
.
INGREDIENTS - makes one portion 
▪️50g jumbo oats (1/2 heaped cup) 
▪️1 egg, room temperature 
▪️180ml (3/4 cup oat milk)
▪️1 teaspoon vanilla 
▪️1 tablespoon honey 
▪️65g Greek yoghurt 
▪️toppings of your choice
METHOD 
▪️In a small pan off the heat, add the milk, egg, vanilla and honey. Whisk well to make sure it’s fully combined. 
▪️Add the oats. 
▪️Put the pan on a low to medium heat and cook gently for about 15 minutes, stirring almost continuously till thick and creamy. 
▪️Take it off the heat and mix in the yoghurt till fully combined. Trust me on this one, it works! 
▪️Spoon your porridge into a bowl and add whatever toppings you like. 
.
.
.

recipes.caption:
You do not need another iron protocol or a trending list of iron rich foods.

Here is why iron shows up low on your markers even when your body is not truly deficient. The answer lives in the liver.

Ceruloplasmin is a liver protein that acts like a truck driver for iron. Without enough of it, iron cannot reach its destination. Your labs look low but the problem is not intake. It is whether your body can actually move it. This tea supports liver health primarily through its high antioxidant content: polyphenols and anthocyanins, which protect liver cells from toxins, inflammation, and damage

Why iron matters at every stage:
a. Trimester 3: Your baby is pulling iron from you to build their birth stores. Low markers here are expected but what you build now is what you draw from later.
b. Postpartum: Your bleed and tissue healing draw heavily on iron. Women who go into birth depleted recover slower with more fatigue and mood instability.
c. Breastfeeding: Iron rich milk supports your baby’s brain development and their own stores through the fourth trimester and beyond.

What actually works:
	1.	Iron must be paired with vitamin C or it will not absorb. Heme iron from liver, red meat, and sardines absorbs well on its own. Non heme iron from plants needs vitamin C as a cofactor. Without it, most passes straight through.
	2.	Trace minerals regulate and transport iron at a cellular level. Food choices become medicine.

Hibiscus/ red raspberry leaf brings iron and vitamin C together and supports liver health. Lemon amplifies absorption. Raw local honey supports liver function, gut lining, and local immunity. recipes.caption:
Gluten-Free Orange Almond Cake

A moist, naturally gluten-free cake bursting with fresh orange flavor, almond flour, and almond meal. Lightly sweetened with honey and enriched with olive oil, this cake is perfect for breakfast, afternoon tea, or a simple dessert.

Ingredients

- 2 large eggs
- 1/2–1 tbsp orange zest
- 2 tbsp (30 g) fresh orange juice
- 1/3 cup (73 g) olive oil
- 1 tsp (5 g) vanilla extract
- 1/4 cup (85 g) honey
- 2 cups (192 g) almond flour
- 1/4 cup (30 g) almond meal
- 1/2 tsp (2 g) baking powder
- 1/2 tsp (2.5 g) baking soda

Instructions

1. Preheat oven to 350°F (175°C). Grease 6”x3”3” loaf pan or a 8-inch round cake pan.
2. In a large bowl, whisk the eggs until lightly frothy. Add the orange zest, orange juice, olive oil, vanilla, and honey. Whisk until smooth and fully combined.
3. In a separate bowl, combine the almond flour, almond meal, baking powder, and baking soda.
4. Gently fold the dry ingredients into the wet mixture until just incorporated. Do not overmix.
5. Pour the batter into the prepared pan and smooth the top with a spatula.
6. Bake for 30–35 minutes, or until a toothpick inserted into the center comes out clean.
7. Allow the cake to cool completely in the pan before slicing.

recipes.title: Chocolate Banana Tofu Pudding
recipes.author: gigi_goes_vegan
recipes.text: chocolate banana tofu pudding ingredients the pudding * 1 ripe banana * 2 tbsp raw cacao powder * 80ml unsweetened soy milk * 150g silken tofu * 2-3 tbsp maple syrup, reduced sugar preferred (depending on how sweet or ripe is the banana) to serve * raw cacao powder or shaved dark chocolate * fresh strawberries or berries method add the banana, cacao powder, soy milk, silken tofu, and maple syrup to a blender. blend until completely smooth. pour the mixture into a small saucepan and cook over a low heat for around 5 minutes, stirring frequently, until the mixture is gently bubbling and has thickened slightly. before pouring into your serving jars or moulds, add a small splash of water to the base of each container — this prevents the pudding from sticking and makes it easier to turn out without breaking. pour in the pudding mixture and leave to cool to room temperature, then transfer to the fridge for at least 3 hours until fully set. to serve, run a knife gently around the edge of each mould and turn upside down onto a serving plate. dust with raw cacao powder or top with shaved dark chocolate, and serve with fresh strawberries or berries. ✨ serves 2 💪 ~8g protein per serving 🌾 ~4g fibre per serving 🌱 4 plant points original recipe by
recipes.caption:
Chocolate Banana Tofu Pudding

Ingredients
The pudding
* 1 ripe banana
* 2 tbsp raw cacao powder
* 80ml unsweetened soy milk
* 150g silken tofu
* 2-3 tbsp maple syrup, reduced sugar preferred (depending on how sweet or ripe is the banana)
To serve
* Raw cacao powder or shaved dark chocolate
* Fresh strawberries or berries

Method
Add the banana, cacao powder, soy milk, silken tofu, and maple syrup to a blender. Blend until completely smooth.
Pour the mixture into a small saucepan and cook over a low heat for around 5 minutes, stirring frequently, until the mixture is gently bubbling and has thickened slightly.
Before pouring into your serving jars or moulds, add a small splash of water to the base of each container — this prevents the pudding from sticking and makes it easier to turn out without breaking. Pour in the pudding mixture and leave to cool to room temperature, then transfer to the fridge for at least 3 hours until fully set.
To serve, run a knife gently around the edge of each mould and turn upside down onto a serving plate. Dust with raw cacao powder or top with shaved dark chocolate, and serve with fresh strawberries or berries.

✨ Serves 2 💪 ~8g protein per serving 🌾 ~4g fibre per serving 🌱 4 plant points

recipes.caption:
Forget chia pudding, have this iron-rich aleev-subja pudding instead 

Women (unless pregnant) need 18 mg of iron daily, and just a spoonful of Aleev/ halim seeds- that have 100 mg of iron per 100 gms can help meet the daily requirement. 

I’ve paired it with cooling subja seeds since aleev is known to be heating, and also add some cardamom powder while cooking it.

Here’s the recipe, try it 

Combine 
2 tsp Aleev seeds
1 tsp subja 
Soak these in 1/2 a cup of water for 2 hours 

Once they are soaked and plump up, cook them in 
1/2 cup coconut milk + 2 Tbsp of water- use thick coconut milk, else it will split once the khareek is added 

Add 1/3 cup khareek, chopped into small pieces 

You need to cook this till it reaches a pudding my consistency- about 10 mins. Cook on low heat, while constantly stirring, else the milk can split after adding Khareek. 

Add some cardamom powder and turn off the flame. 
I recently added some saffron strands, and loved the flavour- you can try that too. 

You can have this also warm, but I personally like to cool it down, pair with some pomegranate (the Vitamin C helps with iron absorption) and some pumpkin seeds for texture.
You can drizzle some honey if you want it more sweet. 

A new favorite that both tastes and does good- try it! 

Aleev can be heavy to digest, and is also heating in nature. 
So, have this in moderate qty- my husband and I shared the pudding we made with the quantity mentioned, which means each of us had just 1 tsp of Aleev seeds. 
It’s a nutrient rich food, so 1 tsp is enough.

We grew up eating Aleev, and don’t have a problem digesting it- but if it’s a new ingredient for you, start with less qty. 
And if you are pregnant/ have any medical condition pls check with a registered doctor on if/ how much you should have. 

#healthydessert #ironrich #traditionalfoods #dates #vegeterianfood

Add 1/3 cup khareek, chopped into small pieces
You need to cook this till it reaches a pudding my consistency- about 10 mins. Cook on low heat, while constantly stirring, else the milk can split after adding Khareek.
Add some cardamom powder and turn off the flame. I recently added some saffron strands, and loved the flavour- you can try that too.

recipes.author: nutriholist

recipes.caption:
You guys LOVED the black sesame paste video, so over the next few weeks I’ll be sharing plenty of delicious ways to use it. But first, let’s clear up a few common questions:

Black sesame paste is not to be used on your hair. You eat it, like any other nut/seed butter. It has a deep, toasty, nutty flavor that’s incredible in desserts, smoothies, and even savory dishes.

Black sesame seeds provide minerals like copper, iron, calcium, magnesium, and zinc. Copper is notable for its role in melanin production, the pigment involved in hair color. This is why black sesame has long been associated with hair health and, in some traditions, thought to help slow or even reverse graying. 

Black sesame won’t “dye” your hair or change its shade. So you can eat it whether your hair is black, brown, red, or blonde. It helps support normal pigment processes, not alter your natural color.

These white chocolate macadamia nut black sesame cookies are one of our favorite ways to enjoy these nutritious seeds 🤤

📌 SAVE the recipe and SHARE it with a friend who wants healthier hair 🫶🏼

White Choc Macadamia Black Sesame Cookies 
Yield: 12 cookies

1/2 cup (120 g) tahini, well stirred
2 tablespoons (30 g) black sesame paste
1/4 cup (60 ml) maple syrup
2 tablespoons (28 g) melted coconut oil, cooled to warm (not hot)
1 large egg, room temperature
1 teaspoon vanilla extract
1 1/4 cups (125 g) almond flour
1/2 teaspoon baking soda
1/3 cup (50 g) macadamia nuts, roughly chopped
1/3 cup (55 g) vegan white chocolate chips 
Pinch flaky sea salt

Preheat oven to 350°F (175°C) and line a baking sheet with parchment paper.

In a bowl, whisk tahini, black sesame paste, maple syrup, coconut oil, egg, and vanilla until smooth and glossy.

Stir in almond flour and baking soda until a dough forms. Fold in the chopped macadamia nuts and white chocolate chips.

Scoop into 12 portions, flatten slightly, and bake for 11–13 minutes until set at the edges but soft in the center.

recipes.caption:
Eat your hair care part 4: Black Sesame Truffles 🖤

These delicious truffles are quick and easy to make with just 6 simple ingredients, ready in under 15 minutes 🙌🏼

The star is black sesame paste, similar to tahini but made from ground black sesame seeds instead of white. Black sesame, tahini, and dates are rich in minerals that matter for hair and skin health, including copper (involved in melanin production), iron (supports oxygen delivery to hair follicles), zinc (important for hair growth and repair), and calcium and magnesium (key for skin and connective tissue health).

Scroll down a couple of posts to see how you can make your own black sesame paste.

👉🏼 Save the recipe, share with a friend & follow @nutriholist for more ✨

Black Sesame Truffles
Yield: about 12 truffles

1 cup (100 g) almond flour
1/2 cup (90 g) pitted dates
1/4 cup (60 g) black sesame paste (see previous post for recipe)
2 tablespoons (30 g) tahini
1 teaspoon pure vanilla extract
Pinch sea salt
Optional coating: black and/or white sesame seeds, or raw cacao nibs

Add all ingredients except for the coating to a food processor and process until smooth and sticky, scraping down the bowl as needed. If the mixture feels dry or crumbly, add 1 teaspoon of water at a time until it rolls easily. 

Use a cookie scoop or roll about 1 tablespoon of the mixture between your palms to form balls and place on a parchment paper-lined plate.

Store the truffles in an airtight container in the fridge for up to 7 days. For longer storage, freeze for up to 2 months and thaw in the fridge before serving.

#truffles #energyballs #blacksesame #haircarenaturally #hairwellness easyrecipes

1 cup (100 g) almond flour
1/2 cup (90 g) pitted dates
1/4 cup (60 g) black sesame paste (see previous post for recipe)
2 tablespoons (30 g) tahini
1 teaspoon pure vanilla extract
Pinch sea salt
Optional coating: black and/or white sesame seeds, or raw cacao nibs
recipes.recipe_method:
Add all ingredients except for the coating to a food processor and process until smooth and sticky, scraping down the bowl as needed. If the mixture feels dry or crumbly, add 1 teaspoon of water at a time until it rolls easily.
Use a cookie scoop or roll about 1 tablespoon of the mixture between your palms to form balls and place on a parchment paper-lined plate.
Store the truffles in an airtight container in the fridge for up to 7 days. For longer storage, freeze for up to 2 months and thaw in the fridge before serving.

recipes.title: Black Sesame Moringa Laddoo
recipes.author: foodly_madly_deeply
recipes.text: black sesame & moringa laddoo🖤✨ having a laddu isn’t always dessert. sometimes, it’s nutrition in the form of micronutrients. i started having one of these for my hair fall, and the results have made me very happy. ingredients • 1 cup black sesame seeds • ¾ cup pumpkin seeds • ½ cup sunflower seeds • ½ cup walnuts to sweeten & bind: • 1 cup deseeded dates (medjool or any soft variety) • 1–2 tsp ghee (as needed) add-ins: • 2–3 tsp moringa powder optional variation: • fresh moringa leaves (see method below) method 1. dry roast black sesame, pumpkin seeds, sunflower seeds and walnuts on low–medium heat for 5–7 minutes, stirring continuously. let cool completely. 2. pulse the roasted seeds and nuts in a blender till you get a coarse powder. remove half of this mixture into a bowl. 3. to the remaining half in the blender, add the deseeded dates and blend till sticky and well combined. 4. transfer this mixture to the bowl. add 2–3 tsp moringa powder and 1–2 tsp ghee (as needed) to bind. 5. mix well, shape into laddus, and store in an airtight container. optional: using fresh moringa leaves • wash the leaves thoroughly and pat dry with a cotton towel. • dry roast them separately till crisp. • cool, then blend along with the roasted seeds. storage & consumption • keeps well outside for up to 2–3 weeks in an airtight container. • i have one laddu daily.
recipes.caption:
BLACK SESAME & MORINGA LADDOO🖤✨
Having a laddu isn’t always dessert.
Sometimes, it’s nutrition in the form of micronutrients.

I started having one of these for my hair fall,
and the results have made me very happy. 

Ingredients
	•	1 cup black sesame seeds
	•	¾ cup pumpkin seeds
	•	½ cup sunflower seeds
	•	½ cup walnuts

To sweeten & bind:
	•	1 cup deseeded dates (Medjool or any soft variety)
	•	1–2 tsp ghee (as needed)

Add-ins:
	•	2–3 tsp moringa powder

Optional variation:
	•	Fresh moringa leaves (see method below)

Method
	1.	Dry roast black sesame, pumpkin seeds, sunflower seeds and walnuts on low–medium heat for
 5–7 minutes, stirring continuously. Let cool completely.
	2.	Pulse the roasted seeds and nuts in a blender till you get a coarse powder.
Remove half of this mixture into a bowl.
	3.	To the remaining half in the blender, add the deseeded dates and blend till sticky and well combined.
	4.	Transfer this mixture to the bowl.
Add 2–3 tsp moringa powder and 1–2 tsp ghee (as needed) to bind.
	5.	Mix well, shape into laddus, and store in an airtight container.

Optional: Using Fresh Moringa Leaves
	•	Wash the leaves thoroughly and pat dry with a cotton towel.
	•	Dry roast them separately till crisp.
	•	Cool, then blend along with the roasted seeds.

Storage & Consumption
	•	Keeps well outside for up to 2–3 weeks in an airtight container.
	•	I have one laddu daily.

#blacksesame #hairhealth #hairfallsolution #moringa #moringabenefits
recipes.recipe_ingredients:
1 cup black sesame seeds
¾ cup pumpkin seeds
½ cup sunflower seeds
½ cup walnuts
To sweeten & bind:
1 cup deseeded dates (Medjool or any soft variety)
1–2 tsp ghee (as needed)
Add-ins:
2–3 tsp moringa powder
Optional variation:
Fresh moringa leaves (see method below)
recipes.recipe_method:
1. Dry roast black sesame, pumpkin seeds, sunflower seeds and walnuts on low–medium heat for 5–7 minutes, stirring continuously. Let cool completely.
2. Pulse the roasted seeds and nuts in a blender till you get a coarse powder. Remove half of this mixture into a bowl.
3. To the remaining half in the blender, add the deseeded dates and blend till sticky and well combined.
4. Transfer this mixture to the bowl. Add 2–3 tsp moringa powder and 1–2 tsp ghee (as needed) to bind.
5. Mix well, shape into laddus, and store in an airtight container.
Optional: Using Fresh Moringa Leaves
Wash the leaves thoroughly and pat dry with a cotton towel.
Dry roast them separately till crisp.
Cool, then blend along with the roasted seeds.

recipes.caption:
Amaranth is used in many cultures, from Latin America to india. This is my breakfast version. 

Depending on the guideline, recommendations vary slightly. EFSA in Europe suggests about 16 milligrams of iron a day, while US guidelines are closer to 18 milligrams. 

Coffee, tea, matcha, calcium and other polyphenol-rich drinks are best about 2 hours away from iron-rich meals.

And important: if iron is a recurring issue for you, it’s not always just food. Absorption can be impaired by things like H. pylori infection or celiac disease and are worth discussing with your doctor if you have persistent symptoms or low ferritin/iron labs. 

PMID: 27411077
PMID: 29689265

🍊 Recipe

2 servings

Ingredients

Amaranth
	•	1 cup amaranth (≈ 190 g)
	•	4 dried apricots 
	•	1½ tbsp cashew butter (≈ 24 g)
	•	1¾ cups water (≈ 420 ml)
	•	pinch salt
	•	½ tsp cinnamon
	•	½ tsp vanilla
	•	pinch cardamom

Compote
	•	1 cup raspberries (≈ 125 g)
	•	zest ½ blood orange
	•	juice ½ blood orange
	•	a few blood-orange segments

Topping
	•	1–2 tbsp pumpkin seed butter
	•	1–2 tbsp pistachios, chopped

	1.	Soak the amaranth in plenty of water for 8–12 hours, then drain and rinse.
This can reduce phytates and improve mineral availability, including iron.
	2.	Blend apricots, cashew butter, water, salt and vanilla until completely smooth.
	3.	Add amaranth, cinnamon and cardamom to a saucepan.
Pour in the apricot–cashew mixture and simmer 18–20 minutes, stirring occasionally, until creamy.
	4.	Blend about ¼ of the cooked porridge briefly, then stir it back in. (Makes it extra creamy)
	5.	Simmer raspberries with the blood-orange zest  for about 2–3 minutes.
Remove from heat and stir in the blood-orange juice and segments. ( Vitamin C is heat sensitive) 
	6.	Divide the amaranth into bowls, top with the compote and finish with pumpkin seed butter and pistachios.

recipes.recipe_ingredients:
Amaranth
1 cup amaranth (≈ 190 g)
4 dried apricots
1½ tbsp cashew butter (≈ 24 g)
1¾ cups water (≈ 420 ml)
pinch salt
½ tsp cinnamon
½ tsp vanilla
pinch cardamom
Compote
1 cup raspberries (≈ 125 g)
zest ½ blood orange
juice ½ blood orange
a few blood-orange segments
Topping
1–2 tbsp pumpkin seed butter
1–2 tbsp pistachios, chopped
recipes.recipe_method:
1. Soak the amaranth in plenty of water for 8–12 hours, then drain and rinse. This can reduce phytates and improve mineral availability, including iron.
2. Blend apricots, cashew butter, water, salt and vanilla until completely smooth.
3. Add amaranth, cinnamon and cardamom to a saucepan. Pour in the apricot–cashew mixture and simmer 18–20 minutes, stirring occasionally, until creamy.
4. Blend about ¼ of the cooked porridge briefly, then stir it back in. (Makes it extra creamy)
5. Simmer raspberries with the blood-orange zest for about 2–3 minutes. Remove from heat and stir in the blood-orange juice and segments. ( Vitamin C is heat sensitive)
6. Divide the amaranth into bowls, top with the compote and finish with pumpkin seed butter and pistachios.

recipes.text: high-protein lobiya galouti kebabs 🌱🥜🍄 soft, smoky, melt-in-mouth kebabs that are packed with protein and flavour — no fancy ingredients, just pure desi comfort ✨ ingredients: • 200 gm lobiya (black-eyed peas), soaked overnight • 200 gm mushrooms 🍄 • 4 onions, sliced 🧅 • 7–8 garlic cloves 🧄 • 1 inch ginger • 4–5 green chillies 🌶️ • handful of cashews 🥜 • 2 tbsp ghee or oil 🧈 • 1 tbsp red chilli powder 🌶️ • 1 tbsp coriander powder • ½ tbsp amchoor • 2 tsp garam masala • salt to taste 🧂 • fresh coriander 🌿 • 2 tbsp besan (gram flour) steps: 1. pressure cook soaked lobiya with salt for 3 whistles. let pressure release naturally. 2. boil mushrooms in water for 5 mins, then drain. 3. heat ghee in a pan, sauté onions for 3–4 mins. 4. add garlic, ginger, green chillies, and cashews. cook till onions are soft and golden. 5. add salt, red chilli, coriander powder, amchoor, and garam masala. mix well and cook for 3–4 mins. 6. add fresh coriander, cook for 2–3 mins more. let it cool. 7. in a blender, add lobiya, mushrooms, and the cooked onion mix. blend to a coarse paste. add a splash of water only if needed. 8. transfer to a pan, add besan, and cook for 4–5 mins until thick and dough-like. cool completely. 9. shape into kebabs, brush ghee on a pan, place kebabs, brush a little ghee on top too, and cook until golden on both sides 🔥 10. serve hot with green chutney and lemony onions 🧅🍋 make-ahead tip: freeze the shaped kebabs raw — perfect for busy days or party prep 💡
recipes.caption:
High-protein lobiya galouti kebabs 🌱🥜🍄
Soft, smoky, melt-in-mouth kebabs that are packed with protein and flavour — no fancy ingredients, just pure desi comfort ✨

	6.	add fresh coriander, cook for 2–3 mins more. let it cool.

	8.	transfer to a pan, add besan, and cook for 4–5 mins until thick and dough-like. cool completely.
	9.	shape into kebabs, brush ghee on a pan, place kebabs, brush a little ghee on top too, and cook until golden on both sides 🔥
	10.	serve hot with green chutney and lemony onions 🧅🍋

recipes.recipe_method:
1. pressure cook soaked lobiya with salt for 3 whistles. let pressure release naturally.
2. boil mushrooms in water for 5 mins, then drain.
3. heat ghee in a pan, sauté onions for 3–4 mins.
4. add garlic, ginger, green chillies, and cashews. cook till onions are soft and golden.
5. add salt, red chilli, coriander powder, amchoor, and garam masala. mix well and cook for 3–4 mins.
6. add fresh coriander, cook for 2–3 mins more. let it cool.
7. in a blender, add lobiya, mushrooms, and the cooked onion mix. blend to a coarse paste. add a splash of water only if needed.
8. transfer to a pan, add besan, and cook for 4–5 mins until thick and dough-like. cool completely.
9. shape into kebabs, brush ghee on a pan, place kebabs, brush a little ghee on top too, and cook until golden on both sides 🔥
10. serve hot with green chutney and lemony onions 🧅🍋

recipes.title: Ragi Ambli
recipes.author: reverseitwithshweta
recipes.text: ragi ambli 😋 💁🏻‍♀️ ingredients - 2 tbsp ragi flour 3/4 cup water ( to make ragi paste) 2 cups water (to make butter milk) 1 cup curd 3 cups water (to make ragi slurry) salt, to taste 1 small onion, chopped (optional) 1 tbsp coriander leaves, finely chopped 💁🏻‍♀️ for tempering - 1 tsp ghee 1/2 tsp mustard seeds 1/2 tsp cumin seeds 3/4 tsp ginger, finely chopped 1-2 green chillies, finely chopped curry leaves 💁🏻‍♀️ instructions - - mix 2 tbsp ragi flour and 3/4 cup water and mix well. once done, heat 2 cups of water in a pan. when it comes to a boil, add the ragi flour slurry and keep whisking. make sure there are no lumps. - cool for 4-5 minutes and keep aside to cool down. - in a bowl, add curd, water and whisk it well. add the cooled ragi mixture, salt and whisk well. add a tadka of cumin seeds, mustard seeds, ginger, green chillies and curry leaves. mix well. - add onions, coriander and enjoy. also, do like, share, and follow on facebook & youtube for more nutritional content (link in bio 🔗)!!
recipes.caption:
Ragi Ambli 😋

💁🏻‍♀️ Ingredients -

2 tbsp ragi flour

3/4 cup water ( to make ragi paste)

2 cups water (to make butter milk)

1 cup curd

3 cups water (to make ragi slurry)

Salt, to taste

1 small onion, chopped (optional)

1 tbsp coriander leaves, finely chopped

💁🏻‍♀️ For tempering -

1 tsp ghee

1/2 tsp mustard seeds

1/2 tsp cumin seeds

3/4 tsp ginger, finely chopped

1-2 green chillies, finely chopped

Curry leaves

💁🏻‍♀️ Instructions -

- Mix 2 tbsp ragi flour and 3/4 cup water and mix well. Once done, heat 2 cups of water in a pan. When it comes to a boil, add the ragi flour slurry and keep whisking. Make sure there are no lumps.

- Cool for 4-5 minutes and keep aside to cool down.

- In a bowl, add curd, water and whisk it well. Add the cooled ragi mixture, salt and whisk well. Add a tadka of cumin seeds, mustard seeds, ginger, green chillies and curry leaves. Mix well.

- Add onions, coriander and enjoy.

recipes.title: Soya Keema Masala
recipes.author: polosjunkjournal
recipes.text: soya keema masala with crispy paratha is love❤️ note: please adjust the oil according to your dietary needs. recipe: -soak one cup of soya chunks in hot water for 10 minutes or till they double in size. - squeeze out the water and blend into a paste. -add 3 to 4 tbsp mustard oil to the pan with cardamom, cinnamon and cumin seeds. -once aromatic add in 2 big diced onions with 1 tsp sugar. -let the onion caramelise before adding 1 tbsp ginger garlic paste, cook for a few minutes and add in one chopped tomato and a pinch of salt. -once the tomato softens add in 1/2 tsp turmeric, 1 tbsp kashmiri red chilli, 1/2 tbsp red chilli powder, 1/2 tbsp coriander powder, 1 tsp garam masala. -cook the spices on medium to low heat for a few minutes then add 1/2 cup beaten curd on low flame. -when you see oil resurface add in 1/2 tbsp toasted besan for texture along with the soya paste. -mix it nicely and then add about 1 cup of water, salt to taste ano cook covered till you achieve a thick texture. -finish with a sprinkle of kasuri methi, chopped coriander, slit green chillies and julienne ginger. . . . . .
recipes.caption:
Soya Keema Masala with crispy paratha is LOVE❤️
NOTE: please adjust the oil according to your dietary needs. 

Recipe:
-Soak one cup of soya chunks in hot water for 10 minutes or till they double in size.

- Squeeze out the water and blend into a paste.

-Add 3 to 4 tbsp mustard oil to the pan with cardamom, cinnamon and cumin seeds.

-Once aromatic add in 2 big diced onions with 1 tsp sugar.

-Let the onion caramelise before adding 1 tbsp ginger garlic paste, cook for a few minutes and add in one chopped tomato and a pinch of salt.

-Once the tomato softens add in 1/2 tsp turmeric, 1 tbsp Kashmiri red chilli, 1/2 tbsp red chilli powder, 1/2 tbsp coriander powder, 1 tsp garam masala.

-Cook the spices on medium to low heat for a few minutes then add 1/2 cup beaten curd on low flame.

-When you see oil resurface add in 1/2 tbsp toasted besan for texture along with the soya paste.

-Mix it nicely and then add about 1 cup of water, salt to taste ano cook covered till you achieve a thick texture.

-Finish with a sprinkle of kasuri methi, chopped coriander, slit green chillies and julienne ginger.

recipes.recipe_method:
Soak one cup of soya chunks in hot water for 10 minutes or till they double in size.
Squeeze out the water and blend into a paste.
Add 3 to 4 tbsp mustard oil to the pan with cardamom, cinnamon and cumin seeds.
Once aromatic add in 2 big diced onions with 1 tsp sugar.
Let the onion caramelise before adding 1 tbsp ginger garlic paste, cook for a few minutes and add in one chopped tomato and a pinch of salt.
Once the tomato softens add in 1/2 tsp turmeric, 1 tbsp Kashmiri red chilli, 1/2 tbsp red chilli powder, 1/2 tbsp coriander powder, 1 tsp garam masala.
Cook the spices on medium to low heat for a few minutes then add 1/2 cup beaten curd on low flame.
When you see oil resurface add in 1/2 tbsp toasted besan for texture along with the soya paste.
Mix it nicely and then add about 1 cup of water, salt to taste ano cook covered till you achieve a thick texture.
Finish with a sprinkle of kasuri methi, chopped coriander, slit green chillies and julienne ginger.

recipes.title: Kuluki Popsicles
recipes.author: finefettlecookerys
recipes.text: anyone else keep opening the fridge in summer hoping something magically refreshing appears? 😅 so i made these electrolyte-rich kuluki popsicles and now there’s always something cold waiting in the freezer. ✨around 20 calories per popsicle and naturally hydrating. ✅save the recipe try now❤️ electrolyte-rich kuluki popsicles 1. take fresh coconut water in a bowl or shaker. 2. add 1 tsp sabja seeds (basil seeds) that have been soaked for about 15 minutes. 3. squeeze in the juice of 1 lemon. 4. add ½ tsp sugar and ½ tsp salt. 5. add 1 slit green chilli for that classic kuluki flavor. 6. shake it well (kuluki means shake). 7. pour the mixture into popsicle molds. 8. freeze for 6–7 hours or overnight. 9. unmold and enjoy these refreshing electrolyte popsicles.

recipes.caption:
Paneer Iffa 🧡
Creamy, garlicky, cheesy goodness. This Paneer Iffa is the kind of dish you mop up with extra roti without any guilt.🙌

Ingredients: 
For the Garlic Sauce:
2 Amul cheese cubes
½ cup yogurt
3–4 tbsp water
1 tsp honey
3–4 garlic cloves
Salt to taste
½ tsp black pepper
For the Gravy:
2 tbsp oil
1 medium onion, sliced
1 tsp ginger-garlic paste
1–2 green chillies, chopped
½ cup yogurt
½ tsp garam masala
1 tsp coriander powder
¼ tsp haldi (turmeric powder)
1 tsp chilli flakes
200 g paneer, cubed
Fresh coriander, chopped (for garnish)

Method:
Heat oil in a Kadhai and add sliced onions. Sauté until soft and lightly golden. Add ginger-garlic paste and chopped green chillies. Cook for a minute until fragrant. Add yogurt and mix well on low flame so it doesn’t split. Stir in garam masala, coriander powder, haldi, chilli flakes, and salt. Add paneer cubes and cook until the gravy thickens and oil starts to float on top. Meanwhile, blend the garlic sauce ingredients (cheese cubes, yogurt, water, honey, garlic, salt, and pepper) until smooth. Pour the garlic sauce over the paneer gravy, cover, and cook for 2 minutes on low heat. Garnish with chopped coriander. Serve hot with roti or naan and dig innn❤️

Cooking with dahi can be tricky, so here’s what I do: switch off the heat and let the pan cool slightly for 2 minutes before adding the dahi. Keep stirring continuously, then turn the heat back on. Don’t stop mixing until it comes to a boilthis prevents splitting. Once it boils, it’s stable and you can continue with the recipe.

recipes.title: Hair, Skin & Nails Seed Mix
recipes.author: ancientdigin
recipes.text: hair , skin and nails growth seed mix this seed-based mix provides protein, omega fats, zinc, and minerals that support hair growth, scalp health, and hair strength when used consistently as part of a balanced diet. ingredients – 1 cup flax seeds – ½ cup pumpkin seeds – ½ cup black sesame seeds – dates (as needed for binding) how to make it 1️⃣ dry roast all seeds together on low flame for 1 minute (do not burn) 2️⃣ let cool completely 3️⃣ add seeds and 7 dates to a blender 4️⃣ pulse 8–10 times, then blend until slightly sticky 5️⃣ store in an airtight glass jar how to use – take 2 tsp daily – best in the morning or between meals – use for 30 days, then take a 10-day break – repeat cycle for up to 6 months for best nutritional support ✔️ flax seeds → omega-3 fats for scalp health ✔️ pumpkin seeds → zinc + protein for hair structure ✔️ black sesame → minerals traditionally linked with hair strength ✔️ dates → natural energy + iron support together, they help nourish hair from within and support healthy growth cycles. ⚠️ note – this is a nutritional support, not a medical treatment – results vary based on diet, stress, hormones, and genetics – consult a professional if you have ongoing hair loss
recipes.caption:
Hair , Skin and Nails Growth Seed Mix

This seed-based mix provides protein, omega fats, zinc, and minerals that support hair growth, scalp health, and hair strength when used consistently as part of a balanced diet.

 Ingredients
– 1 cup flax seeds
– ½ cup pumpkin seeds
– ½ cup black sesame seeds
– Dates (as needed for binding)

 How to Make It
1️⃣ Dry roast all seeds together on low flame for 1 minute (do not burn)
2️⃣ Let cool completely
3️⃣ Add seeds and 7 dates to a blender
4️⃣ Pulse 8–10 times, then blend until slightly sticky
5️⃣ Store in an airtight glass jar

How to Use
– Take 2 tsp daily
– Best in the morning or between meals
– Use for 30 days, then take a 10-day break
– Repeat cycle for up to 6 months for best nutritional support

✔️ Flax seeds → omega-3 fats for scalp health
✔️ Pumpkin seeds → zinc + protein for hair structure
✔️ Black sesame → minerals traditionally linked with hair strength
✔️ Dates → natural energy + iron support

Together, they help nourish hair from within and support healthy growth cycles.

⚠️ Note
– This is a nutritional support, not a medical treatment
– Results vary based on diet, stress, hormones, and genetics
– Consult a professional if you have ongoing hair loss

recipes.title: Crispy Almond-Flour Choc Chip Cookies
recipes.author: sweet_n_sour08
recipes.text: ✨crispy almond-flour chocolate chip cookies 🍪🍃 — golden, crispy edges with a soft, chocolatey crunch: these almond-flour cookies are proof that indulgence can be wholesome too ✨🍫 — ingredients: 1.5 cup approx almond flour (140g) ( i used homemade almond-flour ground with the skins) ¼ tsp baking powder 2 tbsp melted salted butter 🧈 2 tbsp honey ½ tsp vanilla extract 3 tbsp chocolate chips — instructions: 1. preheat oven to 160°c (320°f) and line a baking sheet with parchment paper. 2. in a medium bowl, mix almond flour and baking powder. 3. add melted butter, honey, and vanilla to the dry mixture and combine until the dough has a crumbly texture. 4. fold in chocolate chips evenly. 5. shape the dough into small balls, press and gently flatten them, and place on the prepared baking sheet. 6. bake for 12-15 minutes, until the edges are golden (the center may still be soft). 7. let cookies cool on the sheet for 5-10 minutes, then transfer to a wire rack to crisp up completely. 8. enjoy your crispy, chocolaty, treat ✨🍃 —
recipes.caption:
✨Crispy Almond-Flour Chocolate Chip Cookies 🍪🍃
—
Golden, crispy edges with a soft, chocolatey crunch: these almond-flour cookies are proof that indulgence can be wholesome too ✨🍫
—
Ingredients:
1.5 cup approx almond flour (140g) ( I used homemade almond-flour ground with the skins)
¼ tsp baking powder
2 tbsp melted salted butter 🧈 
2 tbsp honey
½ tsp vanilla extract
3 tbsp chocolate chips
—
Instructions:
1. Preheat oven to 160°C (320°F) and line a baking sheet with parchment paper.
2. In a medium bowl, mix almond flour and baking powder.
3. Add melted butter, honey, and vanilla to the dry mixture and combine until the dough has a crumbly texture.
4. Fold in chocolate chips evenly.
5. Shape the dough into small balls, press and gently flatten them, and place on the prepared baking sheet.
6. Bake for 12-15 minutes, until the edges are golden (the center may still be soft).
7. Let cookies cool on the sheet for 5-10 minutes, then transfer to a wire rack to crisp up completely.
8. Enjoy your crispy, chocolaty, treat ✨🍃
—

recipes.recipe_method:
Preheat the oven to 350 degrees F and line a baking sheet with parchment paper.
In a bowl mix the tahini, honey, baking soda and salt until combined.
Add in the all purpose flour and ground walnuts. Stir using a spoon or a spatula until the dough comes together.
Divide the dough into 12 pieces and shape each piece into a ball.
Roll the cookie balls in sesame seeds until they are well coated on all sides. Transfer the cookie balls to the baking sheet and leave about 2 inches between them.
Using a glass with a round bottom, gently press on the cookies to flatten them so they are about 1/4 inch thick. Keep in mind that the cookies won't spread much while baking.
Bake the cookies for 12 minutes, they will be brown around the edges ever so slightly.
Let the tahini cookies cool for 10 minutes before serving.

recipes.caption:
Honey Almond Apple Cake

This light and naturally sweet cake is perfect for afternoon tea or as a simple dessert. Made with honey, almond flour, and a touch of apple for extra moisture, it’s a wholesome treat that comes together effortlessly.

Ingredients
- 4 large eggs (200g)
- 1 ½ cups (150g) almond flour
- ⅓ cup (110g) honey
-3 tbsp (50g) Almond butter
- 1 tsp (5-7g) vanilla bourbon paste (of vanilla extract)
- 2 tsp (8g) baking powder
- 1 medium apple (about 150g), diced
- 1 tbsp(10g) cinnamon
- ¼ cup sliced almonds (20g), optional, for topping

Instructions

0. Dice one apple, mi with cinnamon and set aside.
1. Preheat the oven to 350°F (175°C). Line an 8-inch (20 cm) round cake pan with parchment paper.
2. In a large mixing bowl, whisk the eggs, honey, vanilla bourbon paste, and almond butter until smooth.
3. Add the almond flour, baking powder, and diced apple. Gently mix until the batter is well combined.
4. Pour the batter into the prepared cake pan and smooth the top with a spatula.
5. Sprinkle sliced almonds evenly over the top, if desired.
6. Bake for 20–25 minutes, or until a toothpick inserted into the center comes out clean.
7. Allow the cake to cool in the pan for 10–15 minutes before removing and serving.

This is Palak Paneer like you’ve never had before. 🤓 This 2.0 version is spicy, garlicky, creamy, comforting and ALSO macro friendly.

Palak Paneer 2.0
Makes 3 Servings of 300 g each 
268 kcal | 20g protein | 14g carbs | 17g fat per Serving
Ingredients 
	•	1 tsp mustard oil (for base)
	•	1 large onion (~120g), thinly sliced
	•	1 tsp ginger garlic paste
	•	½ tsp chilli powder
	•	1 tsp coriander powder
	•	¼ tsp turmeric
	•	½ tsp garam masala
	•	120g tomato purée
	•	Salt to taste
	•	220–250g chopped palak
	•	200g soft paneer
	•	⅓ cup hot water (for blending)
	•	Fresh coriander leaves

Tadka
	•	1 tbsp mustard oil
	•	¾ tsp cumin seeds
	•	1 tsp Kashmiri chilli powder
	•	4 - 5 garlic cloves, finely chopped

Method
	1.	Heat 1 tsp mustard oil in a pan. Add sliced onions and cook until properly golden.
	2.	Add ginger garlic paste. Sauté until aromatic.
	3.	Add chilli powder, coriander powder, turmeric, and garam masala. Cook briefly.
	4.	Add tomato purée + salt. Cook until thick and glossy.
	5.	Add chopped palak. Cook 2–3 minutes until wilted. Lower flame.
	6.	Blend paneer with hot water until completely smooth and silky.

	8.	For tadka: Heat 1 tbsp mustard oil. Add cumin → garlic → lightly golden.
Switch off flame → add Kashmiri chilli powder → pour immediately over curry.

1 tsp mustard oil (for base)
1 large onion (~120g), thinly sliced
1 tsp ginger garlic paste
½ tsp chilli powder
1 tsp coriander powder
¼ tsp turmeric
½ tsp garam masala
120g tomato purée
Salt to taste
220–250g chopped palak
200g soft paneer
⅓ cup hot water (for blending)
Fresh coriander leaves
Tadka
1 tbsp mustard oil
¾ tsp cumin seeds
1 tsp Kashmiri chilli powder
4 - 5 garlic cloves, finely chopped
recipes.recipe_method:
1. Heat 1 tsp mustard oil in a pan. Add sliced onions and cook until properly golden.
2. Add ginger garlic paste. Sauté until aromatic.
3. Add chilli powder, coriander powder, turmeric, and garam masala. Cook briefly.
4. Add tomato purée + salt. Cook until thick and glossy.
5. Add chopped palak. Cook 2–3 minutes until wilted. Lower flame.
6. Blend paneer with hot water until completely smooth and silky.
7. Add paneer sauce to the spinach mixture. Simmer gently 1–2 minutes only.
8. For tadka: Heat 1 tbsp mustard oil. Add cumin → garlic → lightly golden. Switch off flame → add Kashmiri chilli powder → pour immediately over curry.
9. Finish with coriander leaves and serve hot with rice or roti.

recipes.title: Jowar Cookies
recipes.author: parhita.kitchen
recipes.text: jowar cookies ingredients • jowar flour – 1 cup • jaggery powder – ¼ cup (can be replaced with desi khand or authentic mishri) • whole cashews – 6 • cardamom – 3 • cold-pressed oil or melted ghee – ¼ cup method 1. dry roast the jowar flour on low flame for 5 minutes. set aside to cool slightly. 2. blend jaggery powder, cashews, cardamom, and oil until smooth. add the roasted jowar flour and blend again. 3. transfer the mixture to a bowl and bring it together into a hard dough (poori dough consistency). divide into small portions, shape into cookies, and place on a baking-paper-lined plate. if baking paper is unavailable, grease the plate and dust it with flour. 4. add salt or sand to a heavy pan (ensuring no air gaps) and preheat on medium flame for 10 minutes. 5. place a stand inside the pan, keep the cookies plate on it, cover, and bake on low flame for 15–20 minutes, or until the sides turn golden. (if you are using over/airfryer - bake at 160 degrees for 10 to 12 minutes) 6. the cookies will be soft when hot and will firm up completely once cooled.

recipes.recipe_ingredients:
4 cup Whole Wheat Flour Sujata whole wheat 100% chakki atta
2 scoops Truvani Plant Based Unflavored Protein Powder 2 servings, can be sub with 1/4 cup chickpea flour
½ cup Vital Wheat Gluten can be sub with 1/2 cup whole wheat flour
½ cup Chickpea Flour, Besan
6 large Garlic Cloves
3 inch Ginger
5 Thai Green Chili less for less spicy
14-16 oz Extra Firm Tofu I prefer soy free big mountain tofu, but regular tofu works exactly same way
1 cup Fat Free Greek Yogurt
3 tbsp White Sesame Seeds, till
1 tbsp Carom Seeds, ajwain
5 tsp Salt
2 tsp Garam Masala
2 tsp Kashmiri Red Chili Powder
2 tsp Turmeric Powder
2 tbsp Cumin Coriander Powder, dhana jiru powder
2 tbsp Jaggery, gud
½ cup Avocado Oil more for cooking the thepla
4 cup Fresh Fenugreek Leaves OR baby spinach washed, dried, finely chopped
½ cup Water only if needed to bind the dough
¼ cup Avocado Oil this is to cook the thepla
½ cup Rice Flour/Whole Wheat Flour/All Purpose Flour this is to roll the thepla
recipes.recipe_method:
Boiled cubed tofu in salted water for 5-7 minutes, once done drain the water out and let it sit until cool enough to handle. This step helps remove access water from tofu as well as slighly removes the tofu smell.
Blend boiled.drained tofu with fat free greek yogurt and jaggery. Once done keep it aside. This creamy mixture is needed to form the dough and to add protein.
Chopp/grind ginger, garlic, thai green chili together and keep it aside.
In a mixing bowl, add wheat flour, chickpea flout, unflavored protein powder, vital wheat gluten and all the dry spices listed above.
Mix in chopped fenugreek leaves. Be sure to remove big stems, wash thoroughly, dry completely before chopping it.
Mix in ½ cup of oil then start using tofu/yogurt/jaggery creamy mixture to start forming the dough. If the dough does not seem to come together, keep adding little more water at a time to make the dough. I ended up using ½ cup of water ot get the right consistency.
The dough consistency should be like playdoh (the one kids play with!). In other words, the dough consistency should be a little firmer than pizza dough. You should be able to roll the thepla easily with just a small amount of dry flour.
Cover the dough for 10 minutes. After 10 minutes, if the dough feels sticky, kneed the dough again with 2 tbsp of oil to smooth it out. Make 50 equal sized balls out of the dough. The bigger the dough ball, the thicker your thepla will be.
Start warming up your flat pan/tawa.
Massage one dough ball between your palms to smooth it out and press it a little to flatten it. Dust it with dry rice flour (any dry flour like rice flour, whole wheat flour, all purpose flour works just fine).
Start rolling thepla. Roll it as big/small or thin/thick you like with the help of dry flour. The less dry flour you use the better it is! Thicker thepla will stay softer for longer.
Place your rolled out thepla on the hot tawa/flat pan. Cook it on one side on low heat for 15-20 second or until you see some white and light brown spots on the side that is facing the hot tawa.
Flip the thepla so now the other side is facing the tawa. Cook it on low heat for 20-30 second and then turn the heat to medium. Cook more on medium heat for another 5-10 ish seconds or until you see the side that is facing the tawa is somewhat cooked with some brown spots on it.
Once the second side is somewhat cooked, add ¼ to ½ tsp of oil on the thepla (on the side that is facing up) and flip it.
Put some pressure on thepla and spin it with the help of Wooden Roti Chapati Presser or spatula.
Flip it after 10-15 seconds and cook the other side the same way by putting some presser on thepla and spinning with the use of tawa presser or spatula. It is cooked now, take it off the tawa!
Repeat the same process of rolling and cooking for rest of the dough balls.
Serve thepla with any pickles, tea, coffee, milk, yogurt, chutney or even peanut butter! I prefer topping each thepla with fried egg, sliced avocado and dry achar masala (sambhario masalo)
These theplas freeze well. Pack it up in a double ziplock bags and freeze them. It stays good for 3-4 months in the freezer. Take it out of freezer and warm it up in a toaster oven and eat!

recipes.caption:
This might be my smartest lazy pizza yet 👀🍕

I kept seeing this triangle pizza hack with sausages everywhere and got curious… so I tried it with the string cheese sitting in my fridge 🤭 In Korea we love cheese-stuffed crust pizza, so this felt like the perfect little shortcut to that same cheesy crust at home.

I ended up making this for breakfast the other day and went with a pesto version — egg, tomatoes, extra mozzarella, and fresh basil — and it came out SO good. Crispy outside, melty cheese crust, and that jammy yolk in the middle… honestly couldn’t stop eating it.

What I love most is how easy and flexible this is. You can switch up the sauce, toppings, or make it more breakfast / snack / late-night style depending on your mood.

Such a simple idea but so satisfying. Hope you give this one a try 🤍🍕

⚪️ Easy Tortilla Cheese-Crust Breakfast Pizza

Ingredients
 1 large flour tortilla
3 mozzarella string cheese sticks
1–2 tbsp pesto
1 egg
Shredded mozzarella
3–4 cherry tomatoes, halved
Optional: egg wash, sesame seeds, fresh basil

Instructions
1. Place 3 string cheese sticks along tortilla edges in a triangle.

2. Fold sides inward, rolling over cheese to form a stuffed crust triangle. Secure with toothpicks.

3. Spread pesto in center. Add shredded mozzarella, crack egg, add tomatoes.
Optional: brush crust with egg wash + sesame seeds.

4. Air fry at 380°F (193°C) for 10–12 min until golden and egg is cooked to your liking.

5. Remove toothpicks, finish with basil, eat warm 🤍

Full written recipe is on hubbybap.com 🤍

recipes.author: parhita.kitchen
recipes.text: no fail jowar roti ingredients (all measurements use a standard 250 ml cup) jowar flour – 1 cup (loosely packed) water – 1 cup flaxseed powder – 2 tbsp (use 2 tbsp wheat flour if flaxseed is unavailable) oil or ghee – 1 tsp (plus extra for applying on the roti) procedure 1. add the water to a saucepan, add salt and the flaxseed powder, and mix well to remove lumps. 2. bring the mixture to a boil. reduce the flame to low, add the jowar flour, and mix well using a whisk or spoon. turn off the flame and let it rest for 5–10 minutes to cool slightly. 3. add 1 tsp oil and knead with your hand to form a soft, chapati-like dough. 4. divide the dough into small portions and gently roll into rotis, applying minimal pressure. 5. cook the roti on both sides until done. transfer to a plate and apply ghee or oil on top.
recipes.caption:
No fail jowar roti 
Ingredients
(All measurements use a standard 250 ml cup)
Jowar flour – 1 cup (loosely packed)
Water – 1 cup
Flaxseed powder – 2 tbsp (use 2 tbsp wheat flour if flaxseed is unavailable)
Oil or ghee – 1 tsp (plus extra for applying on the roti)
Procedure
1.	Add the water to a saucepan, add salt and the flaxseed powder, and mix well to remove lumps.
2.	Bring the mixture to a boil. Reduce the flame to low, add the jowar flour, and mix well using a whisk or spoon. Turn off the flame and let it rest for 5–10 minutes to cool slightly.
3.	Add 1 tsp oil and knead with your hand to form a soft, chapati-like dough.
4.	Divide the dough into small portions and gently roll into rotis, applying minimal pressure.
5.	Cook the roti on both sides until done. Transfer to a plate and apply ghee or oil on top.

recipes.recipe_method:
1. Add the water to a saucepan, add salt and the flaxseed powder, and mix well to remove lumps.
2. Bring the mixture to a boil. Reduce the flame to low, add the jowar flour, and mix well using a whisk or spoon. Turn off the flame and let it rest for 5–10 minutes to cool slightly.
3. Add 1 tsp oil and knead with your hand to form a soft, chapati-like dough.
4. Divide the dough into small portions and gently roll into rotis, applying minimal pressure.
5. Cook the roti on both sides until done. Transfer to a plate and apply ghee or oil on top.

recipes.text: sweet potato kheer recipe 👇 1. 300–400 g sweet potato, grated 2. 400 ml milk 3. 2 tbsp monk fruit sweetener 4. 5 cardamom pods 5. a pinch of saffron 6. a pinch of salt 7. 1 tbsp melted ghee 8. 20 g almonds 9. 20 g pistachios 10. 20 g walnuts 11. water, as required **👨‍🍳** **preparation** 1️⃣ peel and grate the sweet potato 2️⃣ soak it in water and rinse well to remove excess starch 3️⃣ heat ghee in a kadai 4️⃣ add squeezed sweet potato and crushed cardamom 5️⃣ sauté on high flame for 3–4 minutes 6️⃣ add a little water, milk, and monk fruit sweetener 7️⃣ mix well and cook on high flame for another 3–4 minutes 8️⃣ in a mixer jar, grind almonds, pistachios, and walnuts into a coarse powder 9️⃣ add this nut powder to the kheer 🔟 add saffron and a pinch of salt 1️⃣1️⃣ cook for 5 more minutes on medium-high flame 1️⃣2️⃣ adjust sweetness if needed 1️⃣3️⃣ serve warm in small portions ✔ sweet potato → natural fiber + slow carbs ✔ nuts → healthy fats + satiety ✔ monk fruit → reduces sugar load ✔ small portion → balanced indulgence enjoy it slowly. festive doesn’t mean excessive.

recipes.title: High-Protein Tofu Balls
recipes.author: feastlyfit
recipes.text: 🍽 high protein tofu balls – a guilt-free, protein-packed delight! 💪✨ soft, chewy tofu balls in a flavorful garlic, chili, and spring onion sauce, topped with toasted sesame seeds. perfect for a wholesome meal any time! 😋 macros (total for 2 servings): • calories: 512 kcal • protein: 41 g • carbs: 41.5 g • fat: 30 g recipe: 1️⃣ in a bowl, mix 200 g mashed tofu, 3 tbsp oats flour, 2 tbsp corn flour, salt & black pepper. shape into small balls. 2️⃣ boil tofu balls in hot water for 7–8 min until they float; reserve the water for the sauce. 3️⃣ heat ½ tbsp oil in a pan, sauté 6–7 chopped garlic, ½ tsp chili flakes, and ½ cup white spring onions until soft. 4️⃣ add soy sauce-water mix (1 part soy sauce : 2 parts water) and reserved water. cook 2–3 min. 5️⃣ add tofu balls, mix gently, cook until the sauce thickens. 6️⃣ garnish with toasted sesame seeds & green part of spring onions. serve hot! 🔥 high protein, soft, and full of flavor – perfect for a nourishing meal!
recipes.caption:
🍽 High Protein Tofu Balls – a guilt-free, protein-packed delight! 💪✨

Soft, chewy tofu balls in a flavorful garlic, chili, and spring onion sauce, topped with toasted sesame seeds. Perfect for a wholesome meal any time! 😋

Macros (total for 2 servings):
	•	Calories: 512 kcal
	•	Protein: 41 g
	•	Carbs: 41.5 g
	•	Fat: 30 g

Recipe:
1️⃣ In a bowl, mix 200 g mashed tofu, 3 tbsp oats flour, 2 tbsp corn flour, salt & black pepper. Shape into small balls.
2️⃣ Boil tofu balls in hot water for 7–8 min until they float; reserve the water for the sauce.
3️⃣ Heat ½ tbsp oil in a pan, sauté 6–7 chopped garlic, ½ tsp chili flakes, and ½ cup white spring onions until soft.
4️⃣ Add soy sauce-water mix (1 part soy sauce : 2 parts water) and reserved water. Cook 2–3 min.
5️⃣ Add tofu balls, mix gently, cook until the sauce thickens.
6️⃣ Garnish with toasted sesame seeds & green part of spring onions. Serve hot!

🔥 High protein, soft, and full of flavor – perfect for a nourishing meal!
#healthy #protein #recipe #weightloss #easy
recipes.recipe_method:
In a bowl, mix 200 g mashed tofu, 3 tbsp oats flour, 2 tbsp corn flour, salt & black pepper. Shape into small balls.
Boil tofu balls in hot water for 7–8 min until they float; reserve the water for the sauce.
Heat ½ tbsp oil in a pan, sauté 6–7 chopped garlic, ½ tsp chili flakes, and ½ cup white spring onions until soft.
Add soy sauce-water mix (1 part soy sauce : 2 parts water) and reserved water. Cook 2–3 min.
Add tofu balls, mix gently, cook until the sauce thickens.
Garnish with toasted sesame seeds & green part of spring onions. Serve hot!

recipes.caption:
Amlaprash 

Ingredients 
	•	Amla (Indian Gooseberry) – 500 g, steamed & deseeded
	•	Black Pepper – 2 tbsp
	•	Cinnamon – 1 stick
	•	Cardamom – 8 pods
	•	Bay Leaf – 3
	•	Cloves – 5
	•	Mace – 2 pieces
	•	Fennel Seeds – 2 tbsp
	•	Dry Ginger Powder – ½ tsp
	•	Raisins – 1 handful
	•	Jaggery – 2tbsp (adjust to taste)
	•	Honey – 2–3 tbsp (added at the end, after cooling)
	•	Ghee – 2 tbsp (used at different stages)

Instructions

	•	Steam the Amla until soft.
	•	Remove the seeds and set aside.
	•	In a pan, dry roast all the spices: black pepper, cinnamon, cardamom, bay leaves, cloves, mace, fennel, and dry ginger.
	•	Roast for a few minutes until aromatic.
	•	Let them cool, grind into a fine powder, and set aside.
	•	Heat 1 tbsp ghee in a pan.
	•	Add raisins and roast lightly.
	•	Transfer roasted raisins and steamed Amla to a blender and blend into a smooth paste.
	•	In the same pan, add 1 tbsp ghee.
	•	Add the blended Amla paste and cook for a few minutes.
	•	Mix in jaggery and the prepared spice powder.
	•	Cook on low heat for 10–15 minutes, stirring often.
	•	Let the mixture cool completely.
	•	Add honey and mix well.
	•	Store in an airtight container in the freezer (stays good for up to 6 months).

📌 Tip: Before consuming, take out a teaspoon of Amla Prash and let it sit at room temperature, then enjoy.

Amalaprash is traditionally taken in the morning on an empty stomach or with warm milk/water, but from a nutrition point of view, the main benefits come from its antioxidants and herbs rather than vitamin C (since that’s mostly lost in cooking). So the best time really depends on your routine — many people prefer mornings for energy, or evenings with warm milk for comfort in cold weather. A small daily amount (1–2 teaspoons) is usually considered safe, but if you have medical conditions like diabetes, it’s best to check with your doctor first.

#amla #amlaprash #winterfood

recipes.recipe_method:
Steam the Amla until soft.
Remove the seeds and set aside.
In a pan, dry roast all the spices: black pepper, cinnamon, cardamom, bay leaves, cloves, mace, fennel, and dry ginger.
Roast for a few minutes until aromatic.
Let them cool, grind into a fine powder, and set aside.
Heat 1 tbsp ghee in a pan.
Add raisins and roast lightly.
Transfer roasted raisins and steamed Amla to a blender and blend into a smooth paste.
In the same pan, add 1 tbsp ghee.
Add the blended Amla paste and cook for a few minutes.
Mix in jaggery and the prepared spice powder.
Cook on low heat for 10–15 minutes, stirring often.
Let the mixture cool completely.
Add honey and mix well.
Store in an airtight container in the freezer (stays good for up to 6 months).

recipes.recipe_method: Measure 1/4 cup each of ragi, chana dal, moong dal, masoor dal, urad dal, idli rice, and dosa rice, plus a teaspoon of methi dana. recipes.text: banana bread energy bites makes about 16 bites ingredients - 1 ripe banana, mashed - 1/2 cup almond flour - 1/2 cup oat flour - ½ cup peanut butter - 3 tbsp maple syrup - ⅓ cup vanilla protein powder - 1/2 tsp cinnamon - 1/4 tsp salt chocolate coating - 1/2- 1 cup cup chocolate chips (depending on how much coating you want) - 1 tsp coconut oil - flaky sea salt, for topping instructions 1. mash banana in a bowl until smooth. 2. add almond flour, oat flour, peanut butter, maple syrup, protein powder, cinnamon, and salt. mix until a thick dough forms. 3. scoop and roll into bite-sized balls. place on a parchment-lined baking sheet. 4. freeze for 20 to 30 minutes until firm. 5. melt chocolate chips with coconut oil until smooth. 6. dip each bite into chocolate, return to parchment, and sprinkle with flaky sea salt. 7. refrigerate until chocolate is set.
recipes.caption:
Banana Bread Energy Bites 

Makes about 16 bites

Ingredients
- 1 ripe banana, mashed
- 1/2 cup almond flour
- 1/2 cup oat flour
- ½ cup peanut butter
- 3 tbsp maple syrup
- ⅓ cup vanilla protein powder
- 1/2 tsp cinnamon
- 1/4 tsp salt

Chocolate coating
- 1/2- 1 cup cup chocolate chips (depending on how much coating you want)
- 1 tsp coconut oil
- Flaky sea salt, for topping

Instructions
1. Mash banana in a bowl until smooth.
2. Add almond flour, oat flour, peanut butter, maple syrup, protein powder, cinnamon, and salt. Mix until a thick dough forms.
3. Scoop and roll into bite-sized balls. Place on a parchment-lined baking sheet.
4. Freeze for 20 to 30 minutes until firm.
5. Melt chocolate chips with coconut oil until smooth.
6. Dip each bite into chocolate, return to parchment, and sprinkle with flaky sea salt.
7. Refrigerate until chocolate is set.

Whole green moong dal, whole spices (bay leaf, cinnamon, cardamom, cloves), oil, ghee, cumin seeds, onion, green chilli, ginger-garlic paste, salt, hing, turmeric powder, kashmiri red chilli powder, coriander powder, curd, fresh cream, kasuri methi, oil for frying onions, hot water.

Method:
• Tie whole spices into a potli. Pressure cook green moong dal with water and the potli for 2–3 whistles.
• Heat oil and ghee in a pan. Add jeera, then chopped onions and sauté till golden.
• Add green chilli and ginger-garlic paste.
• Add hing, haldi, kashmiri red chilli powder and coriander powder. Mix well.
• Add a cup of hot water and let the masala cook for 5 minutes.
• Whisk curd well and add it to the pan. Cook on low heat for 10 minutes till oil separates and add salt as per taste. 
• For barista, fry thinly sliced onions on low-medium heat till golden and drain on tissue paper.
• Add cooked moong dal to the masala with some hot water and let it simmer.
• Finish with cream, crushed barista and kasuri methi.

Serve hot and enjoy this Mughlai-style comfort meal ✨

recipes.title: Vatha Kozhambu
recipes.author: _nibbly_
recipes.text: amma’s samayal: ep 4 - vatha kozhambu ✨ (stay tuned for paruppu usuli recipe!) ingredients: (serves 4-5 people) • toor dal - 1 tbsp • urad dal - 1 tbsp • peppercorns - 1/2 tsp • compound hing - 1/2 tsp • curry leaves - 10–12 • dried red chillies - 2 • manathakkali vathal - 2 tbsp (unsalted) • tamarind - big lime–sized ball, extracted with 750 ml water • sambar onion (baby onions) - 250 g • sambar powder - 3 heap tbsp • turmeric powder - 1 tsp • jaggery - 1 tbsp • rice flour slurry - 1 tbsp rice flour + 2 tbsp water • gingelly oil (sesame oil) - 1/2 cup (to add at the end) • gingelly oil (sesame oil) 2-3 tbsp (for cooking) • salt to taste method: 1. heat 2-3 tbsp gingelly oil (sesame oil) in a large kadai. 2. once the oil is hot, add the compound hing and let it foam up. 3. add the toor dal, urad dal, peppercorns, dried red chillies, curry leaves, and manathakkali, and sauté for 2 minutes on medium flame. 4. add the 250 g sambar onions, then add turmeric powder and sambar powder, and sauté well. 5. pour in the tamarind water and let it boil vigorously on a medium flame for about 10 minutes until the onions soften, the kozhambu reduces slightly, and the raw smell of the tamarind disappears. 6. add salt and jaggery, mix well. 7. add the rice-flour slurry, stirring continuously, and cook until the kozhambu thickens. 8. switch off the flame and pour in ½ cup cold-pressed gingelly oil (sesame oil). 9. cover and let it rest. mix well before serving.

9. Cover and let it rest. Mix well before serving.

recipes.title: Jowar Pudding (Jonna Junnu)
recipes.author: parhita.kitchen
recipes.text: jowar pudding (jonna junnu) ingredients jowar – ¼ cup almonds – 5 cashews – 5 water – 1 cup (½ cup + ½ cup) cardamom – 2 desi khand or jaggery – to taste procedure soak the jowar, almonds, and cashews overnight or for at least 8 hours. discard the soaking water. transfer the soaked ingredients to a blender, add ½ cup water and the cardamom, and blend well. add the remaining ½ cup water and blend again. strain the mixture through a muslin cloth to extract the jowar–nut milk. transfer the extracted milk to a pan, add the sweetener of your choice, and cook on low to medium heat, stirring continuously. cook for about 10 minutes, or until the mixture reaches the desired consistency. taste and adjust the sweetness if needed. pour the condensed jowar milk into a greased mould. refrigerate for 1–2 hours, then demould and serve.
recipes.caption:
Jowar pudding (jonna junnu)

Ingredients
Jowar – ¼ cup
Almonds – 5
Cashews – 5
Water – 1 cup (½ cup + ½ cup)
Cardamom – 2
Desi khand or jaggery – to taste
Procedure
Soak the jowar, almonds, and cashews overnight or for at least 8 hours.
Discard the soaking water. Transfer the soaked ingredients to a blender, add ½ cup water and the cardamom, and blend well.
Add the remaining ½ cup water and blend again. Strain the mixture through a muslin cloth to extract the jowar–nut milk.
Transfer the extracted milk to a pan, add the sweetener of your choice, and cook on low to medium heat, stirring continuously.
Cook for about 10 minutes, or until the mixture reaches the desired consistency.
Taste and adjust the sweetness if needed.
Pour the condensed jowar milk into a greased mould. Refrigerate for 1–2 hours, then demould and serve.

recipes.title: Creamy Coriander Soya
recipes.author: feastlyfit
recipes.text: creamy coriander soya 🌿 | high-protein comfort bowl creamy, protein-rich and made without cream 🤍 this coriander soya is comforting, filling and perfect for a balanced meal. 🥣 recipe 1. boil water with salt, add 80 g soya chunks and cook for 6–7 mins. squeeze out excess water (don’t dry completely). 2. add 1 tbsp corn flour (or rice flour), 1 tbsp coriander powder and 2–3 tsp kashmiri red chilli powder. mix well. 3. heat ½ tbsp oil, add soya chunks and cook for 6–7 mins till lightly crisp. 4. add remaining ½ tbsp oil, then add 1 chopped onion, 3–4 garlic cloves, 1 inch ginger, 2–3 green chillies & curry leaves. cook for 6–7 mins. 5. blend 50 g low-fat paneer + 7–8 soaked cashews + 250–300 ml water till smooth. add ½ cup water, blend again and pour into the pan. 6. add salt & black pepper, mix well. 7. add ½ cup chopped coriander and cook 4–5 mins till creamy. adjust consistency as needed. ✨ serve with herb rice or paratha. 🔍 macros (approx | per serving – serves 2) • calories: ~290kcal • protein: ~24g • carbs: ~20g • fats: ~9–10 g high protein ✔️ creamy without cream ✔️ comfort food done right 💚 save this recipe for your next protein-packed meal ✨
