recipes.title: Raspberry Yogurt Protein Dessert
recipes.author: tasteslovely
recipes.text: been loving this as a sweet treat lately. a lower calorie higher protein dessert that’s actually good! ingredients -2 cups nonfat plain greek yogurt (i love kirkland brand from costco) -1 scoop vanilla protein powder (i live , code nynylovely) -2 cups fresh raspberries, roughly chopped (could also use frozen!) -40g coconut sugar sweetened chocolate (i love organic milk chocolate bars) -flaky sea salt (i love ) directions 1. in a medium size bowl, combine the greek yogurt and protein powder. stir to combine. add in the raspberries, and fold into the greek yogurt. 2. line a baking sheet with parchment paper. divide the yogurt into 4 circles. spread to an even thickness. 3. melt the chocolate in a microwave safe bowl in 30 second increments, stirring in between. 4. drizzle the melted chocolate on top, then stop with flaky sea salt. 5. freeze for at least 2 hours. 6. i like to let them sit at room temperature for 3-5 minutes before eating. enjoy! macros per cluster (recipe makes 4) 197 calories 19.9g protein 18.5g carbs 5.8g fat 6g fiber
recipes.caption:
Been loving this as a sweet treat lately. A lower calorie higher protein dessert that’s actually good!

INGREDIENTS
-2 cups nonfat plain Greek yogurt (I love Kirkland brand from Costco)
-1 scoop vanilla protein powder (I live @flavcity, code NYNYLOVELY)
-2 cups fresh raspberries, roughly chopped (could also use frozen!)
-40g coconut sugar sweetened chocolate (I love @hukitchen organic milk chocolate bars)
-flaky sea salt (I love @maldonsalt)

DIRECTIONS
1. In a medium size bowl, combine the Greek yogurt and protein powder. Stir to combine. Add in the raspberries, and fold into the Greek yogurt. 
2. Line a baking sheet with parchment paper. Divide the yogurt into 4 circles. Spread to an even thickness. 
3. Melt the chocolate in a microwave safe bowl in 30 second increments, stirring in between. 
4. Drizzle the melted chocolate on top, then stop with flaky sea salt. 
5. Freeze for at least 2 hours.
6. I like to let them sit at room temperature for 3-5 minutes before eating. Enjoy!

MACROS per cluster (recipe makes 4)
197 calories
19.9g protein
18.5g carbs
5.8g fat
6g fiber

#yogurtbark #highprotein #lowcalorie #caloriedeficit #dessert

recipes.recipe_method:
1. In a medium size bowl, combine the Greek yogurt and protein powder. Stir to combine. Add in the raspberries, and fold into the Greek yogurt.
2. Line a baking sheet with parchment paper. Divide the yogurt into 4 circles. Spread to an even thickness.
3. Melt the chocolate in a microwave safe bowl in 30 second increments, stirring in between.
4. Drizzle the melted chocolate on top, then stop with flaky sea salt.

6. I like to let them sit at room temperature for 3-5 minutes before eating. Enjoy!

recipes.title: Blueberry Muffins
recipes.author: mersgoodeats
recipes.text: blueberry muffins the easiest way to sneak in a quick and healthy snack on the go! d’eats -1/2 cup unsalted melted butter -1/2 cup honey -2 eggs -1 tsp vanilla extract -2/3 cup plain greek yogurt -1/2 cup whole milk -1 & 1/2 cups all purpose flour -1 & 1/2 tsp baking soda -1/2 tsp cinnamon -1/4 tsp salt -1 cup frozen blueberries how to: start by preheating your oven to 425f in a large bowl add your butter and honey. mix until smooth before adding your eggs and vanilla extract. mix then add your greek yogurt and mix again. add your dry ingredients to your wet and mix until almost incorporated. add in your milk and mix together before you add your blueberries in. once your batter is combined add it to a lined muffin tin. top with additional blueberries. bake on 425f for 10 minutes then reduce the heat to 350f and bake for an additional 15 minutes. once cooked and cooled your muffins are ready to enjoy!
recipes.caption:
Blueberry muffins 
the easiest way to sneak in a quick and healthy snack on the go! 

d’EATS
-1/2 cup unsalted melted butter 
-1/2 cup @lineageprovisions honey 
-2 eggs
-1 tsp vanilla extract 
-2/3 cup plain greek yogurt 
-1/2 cup whole milk
-1 & 1/2 cups all purpose flour 
-1 & 1/2 tsp baking soda
-1/2 tsp cinnamon
-1/4 tsp salt
-1 cup frozen blueberries 

How to:

Start by preheating your oven to 425F 

In a large bowl add your butter and honey. Mix until smooth before adding your eggs and vanilla extract. Mix then add your greek yogurt and mix again. 

Add your dry ingredients to your wet and mix until almost incorporated. Add in your milk and mix together before you add your blueberries in. 

Once your batter is combined add it to a lined muffin tin. Top with additional blueberries. 

Bake on 425F for 10 minutes then reduce the heat to 350F and bake for an additional 15 minutes. 

Once cooked and cooled your muffins are ready to enjoy!
recipes.recipe_ingredients:
1/2 cup unsalted melted butter
1/2 cup honey
2 eggs
1 tsp vanilla extract
2/3 cup plain greek yogurt
1/2 cup whole milk
1 & 1/2 cups all purpose flour
1 & 1/2 tsp baking soda
1/2 tsp cinnamon
1/4 tsp salt
1 cup frozen blueberries
recipes.recipe_method:
Start by preheating your oven to 425F
In a large bowl add your butter and honey. Mix until smooth before adding your eggs and vanilla extract. Mix then add your greek yogurt and mix again.
Add your dry ingredients to your wet and mix until almost incorporated. Add in your milk and mix together before you add your blueberries in.
Once your batter is combined add it to a lined muffin tin. Top with additional blueberries.
Bake on 425F for 10 minutes then reduce the heat to 350F and bake for an additional 15 minutes.
Once cooked and cooled your muffins are ready to enjoy!

recipes.text: one of the most satisfying and a current new fav! cucumber idlies, also known as taushe idli or southekai idli in different parts of india i am sure many of you might have tried it and if you haven’t yet, this video is your sign to try out this amazing recipe! i am sure you will also fall in love with it at first bite. recipe details are mentioned below and also in comments for ease 👇🏼👇🏼👇🏼 ⭐️ recipe details- cucumber idli ⭐️ 👉🏼 ingredients- 1.⁠ ⁠cucumber 1 and half cup (grated) 2.⁠ ⁠coconut 3/4 cup 3.⁠ ⁠green chilli 2 4.⁠ ⁠handful of fresh coriander 5.⁠ ⁠salt to taste 6.⁠ ⁠id idly & dosa batter 500 gm 👉🏼 for tempering- 1.⁠ ⁠mustard seeds 1 tsp 2.⁠ ⁠⁠roasted chana dal 1 tbsp 3.⁠ ⁠⁠curry leaves 10-12 4.⁠ ⁠⁠oil 1 tbsp 5.⁠ ⁠⁠a pinch of heeng 👉🏼 method- 1.⁠ ⁠start by grating the cucumber into a bowl and add the finely chopped green chillis. 2.⁠ ⁠⁠next add fresh coconut, ginger and coriander to a mixer jar and pulse-blend it. 3.⁠ ⁠⁠mix this blend with the grated cucumber. 4.⁠ ⁠⁠add then add batter along with salt to taste. 5.⁠ ⁠now prepare the tempering with the ingredients given and oour it iver the batter mix. 6.⁠ ⁠⁠mix well and transfer the batter to the idly moulds for steaming. 7.⁠ ⁠⁠steam on medium flame for 8-9 minutes. 8.⁠ ⁠⁠once done, serve hot with tomato chutney and enjoy.
recipes.caption:
One of the most satisfying and a current new fav!
Cucumber Idlies, also known as taushe idli or southekai Idli in different parts of india 
I am sure many of you might have tried it and if you haven’t yet, this video is your sign to try out this amazing recipe! 
I am sure you will also fall in love with it at first bite.

Recipe details are mentioned below and also in Comments for ease 👇🏼👇🏼👇🏼

⭐️ Recipe details- Cucumber Idli ⭐️ 

👉🏼 Ingredients-
1.⁠ ⁠Cucumber 1 and half cup (grated)
2.⁠ ⁠Coconut 3/4 cup
3.⁠ ⁠Green chilli 2 
4.⁠ ⁠Handful of Fresh Coriander
5.⁠ ⁠Salt to taste
6.⁠ ⁠iD idly & dosa batter 500 gm

👉🏼 For tempering-
1.⁠ ⁠Mustard seeds 1 tsp
2.⁠ ⁠⁠Roasted Chana dal 1 tbsp
3.⁠ ⁠⁠Curry Leaves 10-12
4.⁠ ⁠⁠Oil 1 tbsp
5.⁠ ⁠⁠A pinch of heeng

👉🏼 Method-
1.⁠ ⁠Start by grating the cucumber into a bowl and add the finely chopped green chillis.
2.⁠ ⁠⁠Next add fresh coconut, ginger and coriander to a mixer jar and pulse-blend it.
3.⁠ ⁠⁠Mix this blend with the grated cucumber.
4.⁠ ⁠⁠Add then add batter along with salt to taste.
5.⁠ ⁠Now prepare the tempering with the ingredients given and oour it iver the batter mix. 
6.⁠ ⁠⁠Mix well and transfer the batter to the idly moulds for steaming.
7.⁠ ⁠⁠Steam on medium  flame for 8-9 minutes.
8.⁠ ⁠⁠Once done, serve hot with tomato chutney and enjoy.

Cucumber 1 and half cup (grated)
Coconut 3/4 cup
Green chilli 2
Handful of Fresh Coriander
Salt to taste
iD idly & dosa batter 500 gm
For tempering-
Mustard seeds 1 tsp
Roasted Chana dal 1 tbsp
Curry Leaves 10-12
Oil 1 tbsp
A pinch of heeng
recipes.recipe_method:
Start by grating the cucumber into a bowl and add the finely chopped green chillis.
Next add fresh coconut, ginger and coriander to a mixer jar and pulse-blend it.
Mix this blend with the grated cucumber.
Add then add batter along with salt to taste.
Now prepare the tempering with the ingredients given and oour it iver the batter mix.
Mix well and transfer the batter to the idly moulds for steaming.
Steam on medium  flame for 8-9 minutes.
Once done, serve hot with tomato chutney and enjoy.

recipes.title: Savory Oatmeal with Eggs
recipes.author: drfelicechan
recipes.text: recipe: ingredients (1 serving) - ½ cup rolled oats - 1½ cups water or light broth - 2 eggs - 1 small tomato, chopped - 1–2 scallions, finely chopped - ½–1 tsp soy sauce, to taste - ½ tsp sesame oil - 1 tsp neutral oil (avocado or olive) - optional: pinch of white pepper - optional: black sesame seeds, for topping - optional: chili oil, for warmth and spice instructions - bring water or broth to a gentle boil. add oats and cook until soft and porridge-like, about 5–7 minutes. lower heat. - in a separate pan, heat neutral oil. add tomato and sauté briefly until juicy and slightly broken down. - pour in beaten eggs and gently stir to create soft ribbons, cantonese-style. - spoon the egg-tomato mixture into the oatmeal and gently fold together. - finish with soy sauce, sesame oil, and scallions. - add white pepper if using. top with black sesame seeds or chili oil if desired. enjoy!!🤍
recipes.caption:
Recipe:

Ingredients (1 serving)
- ½ cup rolled oats
- 1½ cups water or light broth
- 2 eggs
- 1 small tomato, chopped
- 1–2 scallions, finely chopped
- ½–1 tsp soy sauce, to taste
- ½ tsp sesame oil
- 1 tsp neutral oil (avocado or olive)
- Optional: pinch of white pepper
- Optional: black sesame seeds, for topping
- Optional: chili oil, for warmth and spice

Instructions
- Bring water or broth to a gentle boil. Add oats and cook until soft and porridge-like, about 5–7 minutes. Lower heat.
- In a separate pan, heat neutral oil. Add tomato and sauté briefly until juicy and slightly broken down.
- Pour in beaten eggs and gently stir to create soft ribbons, Cantonese-style.
- Spoon the egg-tomato mixture into the oatmeal and gently fold together.
- Finish with soy sauce, sesame oil, and scallions.
- Add white pepper if using. Top with black sesame seeds or chili oil if desired.

Enjoy!!🤍

Finish with soy sauce, sesame oil, and scallions.
Add white pepper if using. Top with black sesame seeds or chili oil if desired.

recipes.caption:
Just 183 Kcal & 7g Carbs per serving💪🏼
Creamy, spicy, nutty ramen that feels indulgent but is actually quite low in calories and even lower in carbs. ✨
This one’s all about maximising flavour and balancing macros — shirataki noodles + a healthy cream sauce without any cream or butter or cheese + spicy chilli oil for that perfect hit 🌶️🥜
If your diet can taste and feel this good, I mean, why NOT?! 😋

Creamy Chilli Oil Noodles 
Makes 2 Servings (~210 g per serving)
Macros per Serving:
Calories: ~183 kcal | Protein: ~11 g | Carbs: ~7–8 g | Fat: ~12 g 

Ingredients
Creamy peanut paneer base
	•	Low-fat high-protein paneer or cottage cheese – 100 g (or silken tofu 120 g)
	•	Unsweetened peanut butter – 1 tbsp (16 g)
	•	Soy sauce – 1 tsp
	•	Honey – 1 tsp (7 g)
	•	Salt – a pinch
	•	Hot water – 4–6 tbsp, as needed to blend

Chili oil
	•	Grated ginger – 1 tsp
	•	Grated garlic – 1 tsp
	•	Chopped spring onion whites – 1 tbsp
	•	Chili flakes or chili crisp without the oil – 1 tsp
	•	Sesame seeds – 1 tsp
	•	Soy sauce – 1 tsp
	•	Sugar – ½ tsp
	•	Black pepper – to taste
	•	Neutral oil – 1 tbsp, hot

Noodles & garnish
	•	Shirataki noodles – 200 g, washed & drained
	•	Spring onion greens – for garnish

⸻

Method
	1.	Blend the sauce
Blend paneer, peanut butter, soy sauce, honey, salt, and hot water until completely smooth and creamy.
	2.	Make the chili oil
In a heatproof bowl, add ginger, garlic, spring onion whites, chili flakes/crisp, sesame seeds, soy sauce, sugar, pepper, and salt.
Pour hot oil over it and mix well.
	3.	Combine
Add the chili oil into the blended paneer sauce and mix thoroughly.
	4.	Assemble
Pour the sauce over the shirataki noodles, toss well, garnish with spring onion greens, and serve immediately.

⸻

recipes.title: Brined Chicken Breast
recipes.author: planes_to_plates
recipes.text: no more hating the chicken breast ✨ for brining the chicken you need 1 tbsp salt, 1 tsp sugar and 1 litre of water. dissolve salt and sugar in the water then add the chicken breast and keep it in the fridge for at-least an hour and not more than 3 hours, otherwise it will become too soft. just lightly wash it once after you remove the chicken from the brine to remove excess salt. go ahead and prepare the chicken the way you like. ingredients 2 nos chicken breasts 2-3 tbsp thick curd 6-7 minced garlic cloves 1 tsp chilli flakes 1 tsp chilli paste (optional for spice) 1 tsp chat masala handful of coriander leaves 1/3 tsp salt or as per taste 1/2 lemon squeezed let the chicken marinate for atleast 15-20 mins. then pan fry for about 4-5 minutes on one side with the lid, on low flame. then flip and cook without the lid for 4-5 minutes on a low flame.
recipes.caption:
No more hating the chicken breast ✨ 
For brining the chicken you need 1 tbsp salt, 1 tsp sugar and 1 litre of water. Dissolve salt and sugar in the water then add the chicken breast and keep it in the fridge for at-least an hour and not more than 3 hours, otherwise it will become too soft. Just lightly wash it once after you remove the chicken from the brine to remove excess salt. Go ahead and prepare the chicken the way you like. 

Ingredients
2 nos chicken breasts 
2-3 tbsp thick curd
6-7 minced garlic cloves
1 tsp chilli flakes
1 tsp chilli paste (optional for spice)
1 tsp chat masala
Handful of coriander leaves
1/3 tsp salt or as per taste 
1/2 lemon squeezed 

Let the chicken marinate for atleast 15-20 mins. Then pan fry for about 4-5 minutes on one side with the lid, on low flame. Then flip and cook without the lid for 4-5 minutes on a low flame.

recipes.recipe_method:
Dissolve salt and sugar in the water then add the chicken breast and keep it in the fridge for at-least an hour and not more than 3 hours, otherwise it will become too soft. Just lightly wash it once after you remove the chicken from the brine to remove excess salt. Go ahead and prepare the chicken the way you like.
Let the chicken marinate for atleast 15-20 mins. Then pan fry for about 4-5 minutes on one side with the lid, on low flame. Then flip and cook without the lid for 4-5 minutes on a low flame.

recipes.title: Tiramisu Overnight Oats
recipes.author: noob_runner_kris
recipes.text: high-protein tiramisu overnight oats ☕🍫 | dessert for breakfast if you love overnight oats, coffee, and chocolate — this healthy high-protein breakfast recipe is going to be your new obsession. tastes like dessert, fuels you like a meal! 🥣 ingredients (1 serving) • 25g rolled oats • 10g chia seeds • 10ml milk of choice • 1 shot espresso • 5g cocoa powder yogurt layer: • 200g greek yogurt • 10g honey • few drops vanilla essence 👩‍🍳 method 1. mix oats, chia seeds, milk, espresso & cocoa powder well. 2. in a bowl, whisk greek yogurt with honey & vanilla. 3. layer the oats mixture with the yogurt. 4. top with a light dusting of cocoa powder. 5. refrigerate overnight or for at least 4 hours. 📊 nutrition (approx.) 🔥 323 calories 💪 26g protein 🍞 36g carbs 🥑 6g fats perfect for meal prep, weight loss, and busy mornings. just multiply the ingredients and prep for the week.

recipes.title: High Protein Cottage Cheese Pancakes
recipes.author: mersgoodeats
recipes.text: high protein cottage cheese pancakes these are one of my favorite ways to up my protein game first thing in the morning! the perfect recipe to bring into the new year! try it and tag me! d’eats -1/2 cup cottage cheese -2 eggs -1 cup milk -2 cups all purpose flour -1 1/2 tsp baking powder -chocolate chips to taste how to: start by adding your cottage cheese, eggs, milk to a blender. blend on medium speed for two minutes. add your flour and baking powder and mix until combined. allow your batter to sit for 10 minutes. heat up a skillet on medium low heat and add your batter. top with chocolate chips and flip after 2 minutes serve with maple syrup and enjoy!! breakfa
recipes.caption:
High protein cottage cheese pancakes 

These are one of my favorite ways to up my protein game first thing in the morning! The perfect recipe to bring into the new year! 

Try it and tag me!

d’EATS
-1/2 cup @daisybrand cottage cheese 
-2 eggs 
-1 cup milk
-2 cups all purpose flour
-1 1/2 tsp baking powder 
-chocolate chips to taste 

How to:
Start by adding your cottage cheese, eggs, milk to a blender. Blend on medium speed for two minutes. 

add your flour and baking powder and mix until combined. allow your batter to sit for 10 minutes. 

Heat up a skillet on medium low heat and add your batter. Top with chocolate chips and flip after 2 minutes 

Serve with maple syrup and enjoy!!

recipes.title: Hot Chocolate Mug Cake
recipes.author: aathirasethumadhavan
recipes.text: just 175 calories per serving 🩷 a cosy hot chocolate mug cake you can whip up in 10 minutes — with warm milk and hot cocoa poured right into the cake. light, warm, chocolatey, and just perfect. save this for a midweek or pms pick-me-up. 🤎 🍫 hot chocolate milk mug cake (makes 2 servings) per serving: ~175 kcal • 9g protein • 14g carbs • 9g fat ingredients: for the mug cake • ¼ cup almond flour or powdered oats • ¾ tbsp cocoa powder • sweetener of choice (i used stevia, you can use monkfruit/jaggery/sugar/mashed banana/date purée etc) • ½ tsp baking soda • 2 tbsp greek yogurt or thick curd • ¾ tsp vinegar • 1½ tbsp milk • vanilla essence (optional) for the milk - hot chocolate mix • 1 cup milk (skim or regular) • 1 tsp cornflour • vanilla essence • 2 small blocks dark chocolate (9-10 g) method: 1. mug cake 1. in a mug, mix almond flour/oats, cocoa powder, sweetener, and baking soda. 2. add greek yogurt, vinegar, milk, and vanilla. 3. mix well and microwave for 60–90 seconds until set. 2. milk-hot choc 1. heat milk with cornflour and vanilla until slightly thickened. 2. remove half — this is your plain milk. 3. to the remaining half, add dark chocolate and whisk until melted — this is your chocolate milk. 3. assemble 1. pour 1 spoon plain milk + 1 spoon chocolate milk over the mug cake, alternating. 2. fill it to the top, mix gently, and enjoy warm. 🤎 . recipes.caption:
Just 175 calories per serving 🩷
A cosy hot chocolate mug cake you can whip up in 10 minutes — with warm milk and hot cocoa poured right into the cake.
Light, warm, chocolatey, and just PERFECT. 
Save this for a midweek or PMS pick-me-up. 🤎

🍫 HOT CHOCOLATE MILK MUG CAKE (Makes 2 Servings)
Per serving: ~175 kcal • 9g protein • 14g carbs • 9g fat
Ingredients:
For the Mug Cake
	•	¼ cup almond flour or powdered oats
	•	¾ tbsp cocoa powder
	•	Sweetener of choice (I used Stevia, you can use monkfruit/jaggery/sugar/mashed banana/date purée etc)
	•	½ tsp baking soda
	•	2 tbsp Greek yogurt or thick curd
	•	¾ tsp vinegar
	•	1½ tbsp milk
	•	Vanilla essence (optional)

For the Milk - Hot Chocolate Mix
	•	1 cup milk (skim or regular)
	•	1 tsp cornflour
	•	Vanilla essence
	•	2 small blocks dark chocolate (9-10 g)
 
Method:
1. Mug Cake
	1.	In a mug, mix almond flour/oats, cocoa powder, sweetener, and baking soda.
	2.	Add Greek yogurt, vinegar, milk, and vanilla.
	3.	Mix well and microwave for 60–90 seconds until set.

2. Milk-Hot Choc
	1.	Heat milk with cornflour and vanilla until slightly thickened.
	2.	Remove half — this is your plain milk.
	3.	To the remaining half, add dark chocolate and whisk until melted — this is your chocolate milk.

3. Assemble
	1.	Pour 1 spoon plain milk + 1 spoon chocolate milk over the mug cake, alternating.
	2.	Fill it to the top, mix gently, and enjoy warm. 🤎

.

recipes.recipe_method:
1. Mug Cake
1. In a mug, mix almond flour/oats, cocoa powder, sweetener, and baking soda.
2. Add Greek yogurt, vinegar, milk, and vanilla.
3. Mix well and microwave for 60–90 seconds until set.
2. Milk-Hot Choc
1. Heat milk with cornflour and vanilla until slightly thickened.
2. Remove half — this is your plain milk.
3. To the remaining half, add dark chocolate and whisk until melted — this is your chocolate milk.
3. Assemble
1. Pour 1 spoon plain milk + 1 spoon chocolate milk over the mug cake, alternating.
2. Fill it to the top, mix gently, and enjoy warm. 🤎

recipes.title: Whole-Food Berry Jam
recipes.author: kirahhealthyliving
recipes.text: 1. jams most jams are sugar bombs containing high levels of pesticide residues, high-fructose corn syrup, artificial additives and very little fruit. what i make instead— whole-food berry jam recipe ingredients: • 3 lb frozen mixed berries • ½ cup honey • juice of 1 lemon • peel of 1 lemon (organic) • 3 tbsp chia seeds instructions: simmer the berries and honey until soft. throw the lemon peel while simmering to release natural pectin. mash the fruit, remove the lemon peel, add lemon juice, then stir in chia seeds. the jam thickens as it cools. 2. nutella the original is filled with excess sugar, refined oils and very little hazelnut. what i make instead— whole-food nutella recipe ingredients: • 1½ cups raw hazelnuts • 1 cup pitted dates • ½ cup + 1 tbsp unsweetened nut milk • 3 tbsp raw unsweetened cacao powder (or cocoa) • 1 tsp vanilla extract • ¼ tsp sea salt instructions: roast hazelnuts at 350°f for 15 minutes. rub off the skins while warm and let cool. blend into a smooth nut butter. blend dates with ¼ cup nut milk until smooth, then add hazelnut butter, remaining milk, cacao, vanilla, and salt. blend until creamy. 3. biscoff spread most versions are ultra-processed with refined oils, sugar, and “natural flavors.” what i make instead— whole-food biscoff-style spread recipe ingredients: • 1 cup raw almonds • 1 cup raw cashews • 2 tbsp maple syrup • 2 tsp vanilla extract • 1 tsp ceylon cinnamon • ½ tsp ginger • ¼ tsp cloves • ¼ tsp nutmeg • ⅛ tsp salt instructions: roast
recipes.caption:
1. Jams
Most jams are sugar bombs containing high levels of pesticide residues, high-fructose corn syrup, artificial additives and very little fruit. What I make instead—

Whole-Food Berry Jam Recipe
Ingredients:
	•	3 lb frozen mixed berries 
	•	½ cup honey
	•	juice of 1 lemon
	•	Peel of 1 lemon (organic)
	•	3 tbsp chia seeds

Instructions:
Simmer the berries and honey until soft. Throw the lemon peel while simmering to release natural pectin. Mash the fruit, remove the lemon peel, add lemon juice, then stir in chia seeds. The jam thickens as it cools.

2. Nutella
The original is filled with excess sugar, refined oils and very little hazelnut. What I make instead—

Whole-Food Nutella Recipe
Ingredients:
	•	1½ cups raw hazelnuts
	•	1 cup pitted dates
	•	½ cup + 1 tbsp unsweetened nut milk
	•	3 tbsp raw unsweetened cacao powder (or cocoa)
	•	1 tsp vanilla extract
	•	¼ tsp sea salt

Instructions:
Roast hazelnuts at 350°F for 15 minutes. Rub off the skins while warm and let cool. Blend into a smooth nut butter. Blend dates with ¼ cup nut milk until smooth, then add hazelnut butter, remaining milk, cacao, vanilla, and salt. Blend until creamy.

3. Biscoff spread
Most versions are ultra-processed with refined oils, sugar, and “natural flavors.” What I make instead—

Whole-Food Biscoff-Style Spread Recipe
Ingredients:
	•	1 cup raw almonds
	•	1 cup raw cashews
	•	2 tbsp maple syrup
	•	2 tsp vanilla extract
	•	1 tsp Ceylon cinnamon
	•	½ tsp ginger
	•	¼ tsp cloves
	•	¼ tsp nutmeg
	•	⅛ tsp salt

Instructions:
Roast almonds and cashews at 350°F for 20 minutes. Let cool slightly, blend until smooth, then add remaining ingredients and blend until creamy.

4. Caramel sauce
Most caramel sauces are corn syrup and preservatives. What I make instead—

Whole-Food Caramel Sauce Recipe
Ingredients:
	•	2 cups Medjool dates
	•	½ cup cashew butter
	•	½ cup maple syrup or raw honey
	•	1 cup coconut cream
	•	2 tsp vanilla extract
	•	½ tsp sea salt
	•	¾ tsp white miso paste
	•	½ cup boiling water

Instructions:
Soak dates if needed, then blend everything until completely smooth.

recipes.title: Bulgogi-Style Tofu Rice Bowl
recipes.author: thefoodietakesflight
recipes.text: bulgogi-style tofu rice bowl 🫶🏼 comment “tofu” to get the direct link sent to your inbox 📨🌞 shredding tofu and air-frying (or baking) it to draw out excess creates this unique texture that almost resembles ground meat. the tofu is then cooked down in a bulgogi-style sauce that’s spicy, savoury, a little sweet, and really tasty making it perfect with 🍚 https://thefoodietakesflight.com/shredded-tofu-bulgogi/ . . . . .

recipes.recipe_ingredients:
TOFU
extra firm tofu (I love using pre-pressed tofu like this one!)
BULGOGI SAUCE
grated asian pear or Fuji apple
soy sauce
gochujang
sesame oil
sesame seeds
dark soy sauce
sugar
finely grated ginger
garlic, minced
TO SERVE
Chopped green onions
Sesame seeds
Steamed rice, I used short grain or Japanese sushi rice
recipes.recipe_method:
FOR THE SHREDDED TOFU
Remove the tofu from the water and drain from any excess water. Using a cheese grater, carefully grate the tofu into shreds.
Meanwhile, preheat your air-fryer or oven to 350F/180C.
On a lined baking tray or air fryer basket (I used parchment paper), place the shredded tofu and try to spread it out as thin as possible.
For air-frying, air-fry for 12-15 minutes or until lightly golden brown - do not overcook since it can easily harden and become too dry.
You can flip the tofu halfway through cooking. It’s also okay not to get even browning and even have the tofu still white, since this can add to the different textures of the overall tofu dish.
If baking, you may need to bake the tofu for 25-30 minutes.
SAUCE AND MARINATING
While the tofu is cooking, prepare the sauce by mixing everything together. Feel free to adjust to your taste.
Want it really saucy? You can double the sauce!
Once the tofu is lightly golden brown and crisp on the edges, transfer it to the sauce. Mix well to coat.
COOKING THE SHREDDED TOFU BULGOGI
In a medium wok or pan, add in the shredded tofu and sauce. Cook down over medium heat for 7-8 minutes or until the sauce has reduced and absorbed by the tofu. The sauce will also slightly thicken from the sugars in the sauce.
Taste the tofu and feel free to season more, if desired.
Turn off the heat.
SERVE AND ENJOY!
Serve this hot with rice and garnish with some chopped green onions & sesame seeds, if desired. Enjoy!

recipes.title: Paan Chia Pudding
recipes.author: salonikukreja
recipes.text: paan chia pudding | creamy, naturally sweetened, and packed with goodness, it’s the kind of no-fuss dessert (or breakfast! ) that feels indulgent yet light. i keep coming back to this recipe because quick to make and easy to prep ahead! ingredients: paan leaves - 3 fennel seeds - 1 tsp rose water- 2 tsps milk - 3/4th cup ice - 2 cubes honey-1tbsp chia seeds- 2.5tbsps process: •wash the pan leaves and remove the bottom steam. •in a blender add the pan leaves, fennel seeds, honey, rose water and half the quantity of milk along with the ice cubes. •blend it well to form a nice mixture. add the rest of them milk and blend again. •transfer it to a bowl and add the chia seeds.mix well and let it bloom for a couple of hours or overnight. •drizzle some melted dark chocolate on top if it. finish it by garnishing with rose petals and sliced/chopper pistachio and enjoy.
recipes.caption:
Paan Chia Pudding | Creamy, naturally sweetened, and packed with goodness, it’s the kind of no-fuss dessert (or breakfast! ) that feels indulgent yet light. I keep coming back to this recipe because quick to make and easy to prep ahead! 

Ingredients: 
Paan leaves - 3 
Fennel seeds - 1 tsp 
Rose water- 2 tsps 
Milk - 3/4th cup 
Ice - 2 cubes 
Honey-1tbsp

Chia seeds- 2.5tbsps

Process:
•Wash the pan leaves and remove the bottom steam. 
•In a blender add the pan leaves, fennel seeds, honey, rose water and half the quantity of milk along with the ice cubes.
•Blend it well to form a nice mixture. Add the rest of them milk and blend again.
•Transfer it to a bowl and add the chia seeds.Mix well and let it bloom for a couple of hours or overnight.
•Drizzle some melted dark chocolate on top if it. Finish it by garnishing with rose petals and sliced/chopper pistachio and enjoy. 

#chiapudding #healthybreakfast #breakfastrecipes #easyrecipes #paanchiapudding

recipes.recipe_method:
Wash the pan leaves and remove the bottom steam.
In a blender add the pan leaves, fennel seeds, honey, rose water and half the quantity of milk along with the ice cubes.
Blend it well to form a nice mixture. Add the rest of them milk and blend again.
Transfer it to a bowl and add the chia seeds.Mix well and let it bloom for a couple of hours or overnight.
Drizzle some melted dark chocolate on top if it. Finish it by garnishing with rose petals and sliced/chopper pistachio and enjoy.

recipes.title: Chocolate Hazelnut Overnight Oats
recipes.author: choosingchia
recipes.text: chocolate hazelnut overnight oats!🍫 if you love nutella or ferrero rocher chocolates this overnight oats flavour is made for you! this is a must try breakfast for day 18 of my healthy easy recipe series.🎉 full recipe is below. don’t forget to tag if you try it! choco hazelnut overnight oats ingredients: * 1 cup oats (rolled or quick oats) * 1 tbsp chia seeds * pinch of salt * 1/4 cup cocoa powder * 1 tbsp chocolate hazelnut spread * 1/3 cup greek yogurt * 1/2 tsp vanilla extract * 1 cup almond milk * 1-2 tbsp maple syrup * crushed hazelnuts and yogurt to top how to: add all the ingredients to a large mixing bowl or jar and mix together to combine. place in the fridge overnight (or for a minimum of 4 hours) remove and enjoy as is or with your favourite toppings.
recipes.caption:
Chocolate hazelnut overnight oats!🍫

Full recipe is below. Don’t forget to tag @choosingchia if you try it!

CHOCO HAZELNUT OVERNIGHT OATS

Ingredients: 

* 1 cup oats (rolled or quick oats)
* 1 tbsp chia seeds
* pinch of salt
* 1/4 cup cocoa powder
* 1 tbsp chocolate hazelnut spread
* 1/3 cup greek yogurt 
* 1/2 tsp vanilla extract
* 1 cup almond milk
* 1-2 tbsp maple syrup
* Crushed hazelnuts and yogurt to top 

How to: 

Add all the ingredients to a large mixing bowl or jar and mix together to combine. Place in the fridge overnight (or for a minimum of 4 hours) Remove and enjoy as is or with your favourite toppings.

recipes.title: Chia Oat Pudding
recipes.author: sweatysweetpotato
recipes.text: i always forget about chia pudding but every time i make it i’m hooked again 😍 love having it for breakfast or a midday snack. lots of fiber and protein! if you typically don’t like chia pudding, mixing in some oats helps with the texture imo and it’s so so satisfying!!! for one serving: 2 tbsp chia seeds 2 tbsp quick cook oats 2/3 cup milk 1 scoop chocolate protein pinch sea salt add everything to a jar and stir well. let sit for 10-15 minutes and stir again (to help the chia from clumping), then place the lid on and let sit in the fridge for at least 3 hours (ideally overnight) add your toppings! i love a scoop of yogurt, strawberries, peanut butter, and some chopped chocolate 😌

recipes.caption:
Chocolate lovers unite !!🫡

Toblerone is definitely one of my favourite chocolates, so I thought why not make it into a high protein overnight oat recipe 🥰 I love making recipes like this because it is a pretty darn healthy recipe despite looking so decadent which is all the more reason to try it!

✨recipe✨
 50g oats*
10g cocoa powder*
30g chocolate vegan protein powder* (for thickness)
5g chia seeds/flax seeds
50g of Greek yoghurt 
170 ml water (or milk) 
1 tsp honey 

For the top:
5g almond butter*
15-20g dark chocolate (I used sugar free) 
5g of soy crisps (can use honeycomb, but I couldn’t find any😅)

Ingredients with a * are from @prozis (Code FITFOODIEJULES will give you a big discount + gifts!)

Microwave the oats with the chia seeds, honey, and water for 2.30. Mix in the yoghurt, protein, and cocoa. 

Add the dollop of almond butter to the center of the oats. melt the chocolate, then mix in the soy crisps and drizzle over the top of the oats to form a shell. Refrigerate overnight and enjoy!

#overnightoats #proteinbreakfast #oats
recipes.recipe_ingredients:
50g oats
10g cocoa powder
30g chocolate vegan protein powder (for thickness)
5g chia seeds/flax seeds
50g of Greek yoghurt
170 ml water (or milk)
1 tsp honey
For the top:
5g almond butter
15-20g dark chocolate (I used sugar free)
5g of soy crisps (can use honeycomb, but I couldn’t find any😅)
recipes.recipe_method:
Microwave the oats with the chia seeds, honey, and water for 2.30. Mix in the yoghurt, protein, and cocoa.
Add the dollop of almond butter to the center of the oats. melt the chocolate, then mix in the soy crisps and drizzle over the top of the oats to form a shell. Refrigerate overnight and enjoy!

recipes.title: Purple Mulberry Smoothie
recipes.author: wethinkfusion
recipes.text: breakfast that looks like a smoothie… tastes like dessert… and has protein too! if you want a pretty + protein-rich + 2-minute breakfast… this purple mulberry smoothie is it! 💜✨ it’s thick, creamy, naturally sweet and keeps you full for hours — perfect for busy mornings, office rush, or post-workout fuel. top it with fruits, granola or seeds… and you have the easiest healthy bowl ever! save this for your next breakfast 💯🍌 1 cup oats 1 banana 1 tbsp mulberries 1 scoop whey protein (any flavor) milk (as needed) toppings: banana slices, black raisins, sunflower seeds, granola or fruits of your choice 👩🏻‍🍳 recipe: 1️⃣ blend everything add oats, banana, mulberries, whey protein and milk to a blender. blend until smooth and creamy. 2️⃣ pour & top transfer to a bowl. top with banana slices, black raisins, sunflower seeds or granola. 3️⃣ enjoy! your quick, easy, high-protein purple smoothie is ready in just 2 minutes 💜✨

recipes.title: Honey Butter Sweet Potatoes
recipes.author: hubbybap
recipes.text: honey butter sweet potatoes (air fryer) 🍠🧈🍯 sweet potatoes are seriously having a moment right now, so i had to jump in with one of my favorite ways to eat them. this honey butter version is ridiculously simple but so good it feels like a little dessert and snack all in one 🤭 i used japanese sweet potatoes here because they get extra fluffy and creamy, but honestly any kind works. just adjust the honey and butter to your taste. that korean honey-butter combo (like those iconic honey butter chips) is popular for a reason, and it pairs so perfectly with warm roasted sweet potatoes. how i made it: air fry sweet potatoes at 375°f for 30 min until soft. split open, add a chunk of salted butter, a drizzle of honey, and mozzarella, then air fry again at 400°f for 5–8 min until the cheese melts and gets lightly golden. finish with a little dried parsley and extra honey if you want. it’s cozy, a little indulgent, and so easy in the air fryer — definitely one i’ll be making again and again 😅🍠
recipes.caption:
Honey Butter Sweet Potatoes (Air Fryer) 🍠🧈🍯

Sweet potatoes are seriously having a moment right now, so I had to jump in with one of my favorite ways to eat them. This honey butter version is ridiculously simple but so good it feels like a little dessert and snack all in one 🤭

I used Japanese sweet potatoes here because they get extra fluffy and creamy, but honestly any kind works. Just adjust the honey and butter to your taste. That Korean honey-butter combo (like those iconic honey butter chips) is popular for a reason, and it pairs so perfectly with warm roasted sweet potatoes.

How I made it:

 Air fry sweet potatoes at 375°F for 30 min until soft. Split open, add a chunk of salted butter, a drizzle of honey, and mozzarella, then air fry again at 400°F for 5–8 min until the cheese melts and gets lightly golden. Finish with a little dried parsley and extra honey if you want.

It’s cozy, a little indulgent, and so easy in the air fryer — definitely one I’ll be making again and again 😅🍠

#airfryer #honeybuttersweetpotatoes
recipes.recipe_method: Air fry sweet potatoes at 375°F for 30 min until soft. Split open, add a chunk of salted butter, a drizzle of honey, and mozzarella, then air fry again at 400°F for 5–8 min until the cheese melts and gets lightly golden. Finish with a little dried parsley and extra honey if you want.

recipes.recipe_method: Heat oil and roast the peanuts until golden. Add the chana dal, green chilies, grated fresh coconut, tamarind, and mint leaves and saute briefly. Prepare a tempering with oil, mustard seeds, urad dal, cumin seeds, dried red chilies, curry leaves, and asafoetida, pour it over the chutney, and mix in.

recipes.caption:
Episode 7 of Comfort food
Kathal Yakhni Pulao : A recipe which reminds of my Childhood, the frankly speaking comfort food is underrated word for this recipe, as it’s something beyond that. Ek alag he sukoon hota tha ismay 
Also, the biryani or a pulao is incomplete without good rice and biryani masala,I have tried many and this biryani masala from @urbanplatter.in is just amazing.

Btw, I know Kathal aka Jack fruit is very common in many homes in India, But i really want to hear how you make it at your home?
And do share it with someone who loves indulging in rice in anh form 

⭐️Recipe details  are given believing ⭐️

Kathal Yakhni Pulao

Ingredients:
	1.	Kathal: 500g
	2.	Rice: 1.5 cups (soaked for 30 mins)
	3.	Yogurt: 1 cup
	4.	Water: 1.25 liters
	5.	Bay leaf: 1, Star anise: 2, Cinnamon sticks: 2, Green cardamom: 3-4, Black cardamom: 2, Cloves: 3-4
	6.	Onions: 4-5 (2 puréed, rest for frying)
	7.	Ginger-garlic paste: 2 tbsp
	8.	Red chili powder: 1 tsp, Turmeric powder: 1 tsp, Biryani masala: 2-3 tbsp
	9.	Salt: to taste
	10.	Desi ghee/Oil: for cooking
	11.	Cumin seeds: 1 tbsp
	12.	Coriander & mint leaves: a handful

Method:
	1.	Boil water with bay leaf, star anise, cinnamon (1 stick), cloves (2), and cardamoms (2). Add kathal and boil for 10-12 mins until 90% cooked. Strain the kathal and reserve the water (yakhni).
	2.	Heat ghee in a handi. Add cumin seeds and remaining spices, then sauté with ginger-garlic paste.
	3.	Add onion purée, cook till golden, then mix yogurt, chili powder, turmeric, salt, and biryani masala. Cook until oil releases.
	4.	Add boiled kathal, simmer for 5 mins, then mix in rice and strained yakhni. Cover and cook on low until rice is done.
	5.	Garnish with fried onions, coriander, and mint. Let rest for 10 mins before serving.
	6.	Serve warm with fried cashews and your favorite raita.

recipes.recipe_ingredients:
Kathal: 500g
Rice: 1.5 cups (soaked for 30 mins)
Yogurt: 1 cup
Water: 1.25 liters
Bay leaf: 1, Star anise: 2, Cinnamon sticks: 2, Green cardamom: 3-4, Black cardamom: 2, Cloves: 3-4
Onions: 4-5 (2 puréed, rest for frying)
Ginger-garlic paste: 2 tbsp
Red chili powder: 1 tsp, Turmeric powder: 1 tsp, Biryani masala: 2-3 tbsp
Salt: to taste
Desi ghee/Oil: for cooking
Cumin seeds: 1 tbsp
Coriander & mint leaves: a handful
recipes.recipe_method:
1. Boil water with bay leaf, star anise, cinnamon (1 stick), cloves (2), and cardamoms (2). Add kathal and boil for 10-12 mins until 90% cooked. Strain the kathal and reserve the water (yakhni).
2. Heat ghee in a handi. Add cumin seeds and remaining spices, then sauté with ginger-garlic paste.
3. Add onion purée, cook till golden, then mix yogurt, chili powder, turmeric, salt, and biryani masala. Cook until oil releases.
4. Add boiled kathal, simmer for 5 mins, then mix in rice and strained yakhni. Cover and cook on low until rice is done.
5. Garnish with fried onions, coriander, and mint. Let rest for 10 mins before serving.
6. Serve warm with fried cashews and your favorite raita.

recipes.recipe_ingredients:
Torai/Sponge gourd 500gm (chopped)
Potato 1 medium (chopped)
Onion 1 medium (finely chopped)
Garlic 3-4 (finely chopped)
French beans 1/4 cup (finely chopped)
Curd 100 gm
Roasted Besan/ Gram flour 2 tbsp
Salt to taste
Turmeric powder 3 tbsp
Red chilli powder 2 tsp
A pinch of heeng
Dried red chillis 2-3
Mustard seeds 1 tsp
Garam masala powder 1 tbsp
Kashmiri Lal mirch 1 tsp
Desi ghee 3 tbsp
Water 500-600 mL
recipes.recipe_method:
Heat a tbsp of ghee in a cooker.
Now pressure cook chopped Torai and potato with salt, turmeric powder and water for 3-4 whistles or until well cooked.
Once the pressure is released and the cooked Torai is on room temperature add curd, roasted gram flour and chilli powder and blend it to a smooth purée with the help of a blender to resemble kadhi.
Now let the kadhi cook on the medium low flame until thick and well cooked. This will take around 12-15 mins.
In the meanwhile prepare the tadka by heating remaing desi ghee in a pan.
Next add heeng powder, dried red chillis and mustard seeds.
Once the seeds start to splutter add the garlic and onions and let it cook on medium flame until golden brown.
Once done add the chopped beans with salt to taste , garam masala powder and Kashmiri Lal mirch.
pour this tadka over the cooked kadhi and serve warm.

recipes.recipe_ingredients:
Chickpeas 200 gm (overnight soaked)
Ginger 2 inch
Garlic cloves 3-4
Green chillis 2 (halved)
Onion 2 medium (sliced)
Tomato 2 medium (chopped)
Bay leaf 1
Badi elaichi 1
Green cardamom 3-4
Cloves 2-3
Cinnamon stick 1-2 inch
Tea bags 2
Water for boiling chickpeas
Turmeric powder 1 tsp
Red chilli powder 1 tsp
Coriander powder 1 tbsp
Garam masala 1 tsp
Chole masala 2 tbsp
Salt to taste
For tempering
Desi ghee 2 tbsp
A pinch of heeng
Kashmiri red chilli powder 1 tsp
Kasuri methi 1 tbsp
recipes.recipe_method:
In a pressure cooked add soaked chickpeas followed by ginger, garlic, green chillis, onion and tomato.
Mix well and add water enough water to cook the chickpeas. (Approx 2-3 inch level above the chickpeas in the cooker)
Then add the whole spices in a mesh cloth or a mesh ball with two tea bags and salt to taste.
Now close the lid of the cooker and pressure cook for 8-9 whistles.
Once the pressure is released remove the tea bags and whole spices mesh and then mix the chickpeas and cooked veggies.
Now add the dry spices and cook for 7-8 mins on low flame until well cooked and oil is released.
Lastly prepare the tadka with a pinch of heeng, Kashmiri red chilli powder and kasuri methi in desi ghee and pour it over the cooked chickpeas.
Serve warm with kulchas.

recipes.caption:
🍫🌰Nutella Protein Dessert

FULL RECIPE: 575 calories, 70g protein
PER SERVING (3): 190 calories, 23g protein

✅Comment “TREATS” below and I’ll send you my free mini healthy desserts ebook!

This is an easy high protein dessert that feels like a cheat. Its super rich, got the perfect balance between creamy and crunchy with the roasted hazelnuts, and is such a good way to keep on track in the new year if you’ve got weightless goals or just trying to eat healthier.

It’s very rich, so I divide the full batch into 3 servings for 23g protein each, you can do it in 4 servings if you want, too. A few spoonfuls goes a long way. For reference, I used 6 tablespoons of cacao because I like it really rich. You can use 5 if you want it slightly lighter.

INGREDIENTS
1 tub 2% cottage cheese (16 oz)
5-6 tbsp unsweetened cacao powder (I use 6)
1/2 to 3/4 cup powdered monkfruit or preferred powdered sweetener - make sure its POWDERED
Melted Lily’s milk chocolate chips (I used 2 tbsp to keep this lighter)
Crushed hazelnuts (I used 2 tbsp, too, but use however much you like)

Here is how I made it:

1.Add your cottage cheese, cacao powder, and powdered sweetener to a small food processor. Important: the sweetener must be powdered or the texture will be gritty. Blend for 30 seconds until completely smooth and creamy. Pause, mix with spoon, and go another 20-30 seconds. You’ll want to get rid of all the curds and for it to be completely smooth. Taste and adjust sweetness if needed.

2.Transfer to a container and refrigerate for 1-2 hours. You can eat it right away, but chilling thickens it and makes the texture even better.

3.Melt the chocolate chips (you may want to add 1 tsp coconut oil) in the microwave for 15 seconds, stir, then another 15 seconds until smooth.

4.Spoon your dessert into bowls, drizzle the melted chocolate on top, and sprinkle with crushed hazelnuts. Chill briefly if you want a crackable chocolate layer.

If you make this health dessert, be sure to let me know. I share other high protein recipes and lowcarb food on SHREDHAPENS!

ENJOY!!

recipes.title: Corn and Onion Cheela
recipes.author: salonikukreja
recipes.text: a plate of comfort with every bite🥰this corn and onion cheela is light, savory, and packed with fresh flavors, perfect for cozy winter mornings❤️try it once, and you’ll be making it on repeat☺️ ingredients: 3/4th cup corn - boiled 2 green onion- greens & whites - seperated 1 green chill- finely chopped 1/2 cup besan 1/4th cup rice flour 1 tsp salt 1/2 tsp pepper 1/2 tsp chilli powder 1 tsp ajwain 1/8th tsp turmeric powder 1/8th tsp baking soda 1/2cup water - as required 1tsp oil- to brush garnish - dollop of hung yogurt green onion - greens process: •wash and boil the corn kernels until cooked. .roughly chop the white onion bulbs. •blend together the boiled corn, onions and green chili with 2/3tbps of water into a coarse mixture. •transfer it to a bowl and add besan, rice flour , green onion greens along with all the dry powders including salt and pepper. •crush some ajwain into it and add rest of water to form a nice batter. •on a heated pan brush some oil and add spoonful of batter onto it. •let it cover and cook on both sides until golden and crispy. •serve it hot garnished with dollops of hung curd and green onion greens. yummy wholesome
recipes.caption:
A plate of comfort with every bite🥰This corn and onion cheela is light, savory, and packed with fresh flavors, perfect for cozy winter mornings❤️Try it once, and you’ll be making it on repeat☺️

Ingredients:
3/4th cup corn - boiled 
2 green onion- greens & whites - seperated 
1 green chill- finely chopped 
1/2 cup besan 
1/4th cup rice flour 
1 tsp salt 
1/2 tsp pepper 
1/2 tsp chilli powder 
1 tsp ajwain 
1/8th tsp turmeric powder 
1/8th tsp baking soda 
1/2cup water - as required 
1tsp oil- to brush

Garnish - dollop of hung yogurt 
Green onion - greens 

Process:
•Wash and boil the corn kernels until cooked.
.Roughly chop the white onion bulbs. 
•Blend together the boiled corn, onions and green chili with 2/3tbps of water into a coarse mixture.
•Transfer it to a bowl and add besan, rice flour , green onion greens along with all the dry powders including salt and pepper.
•Crush some ajwain into it and add rest of water to form a nice batter.
•On a heated pan brush some oil and add spoonful of batter onto it.
•let it cover and cook on both sides until golden and crispy.
•Serve it hot garnished with dollops of hung curd and green onion greens.

recipes.recipe_method:
Wash and boil the corn kernels until cooked.
Roughly chop the white onion bulbs.
Blend together the boiled corn, onions and green chili with 2/3tbps of water into a coarse mixture.
Transfer it to a bowl and add besan, rice flour , green onion greens along with all the dry powders including salt and pepper.
Crush some ajwain into it and add rest of water to form a nice batter.
On a heated pan brush some oil and add spoonful of batter onto it.
let it cover and cook on both sides until golden and crispy.
Serve it hot garnished with dollops of hung curd and green onion greens.

recipes.title: Blueberry Almond Flour Pancakes
recipes.author: sokos.kitchen
recipes.text: wild blueberry almond flour pancakes 🫐🥞🍴 perfect morning stack!! my almond flour pancakes is a recipe i’ve been perfecting for years & i hope you love it🫶 also, it’s almost wild blueberry recipe season & get ready because i have so much planned 🫐 ingredients: (makes 5–6 pancakes) 2 eggs 1 tbsp coconut sugar 1 tbsp avocado oil 1/3 cup milk 1 tsp lemon juice 1/4 tsp vanilla extract 1 cup almond flour 1/4 tsp baking soda 1/4 tsp salt frozen wild blueberries recipe: - in a mixing bowl, whisk together the eggs, coconut sugar, oil, milk, lemon juice, and vanilla extract until well combined. mix in the almond flour, baking soda, and salt until you have a smooth batter. - heat a griddle to medium heat—you want it to be pretty hot! these pancakes are best with a little bit of a crisp. add a generous amount of butter to the pan. once the butter is sizzling, pour in the batter, 1/4 cup at a time. sprinkle with frozen wild blueberries. - once the pancakes are bubbling (about 3 minutes), flip them using a spatula and cook on the other side for another 2-3 minutes. - serve topped with more butter and maple syrup.
recipes.caption:
WILD BLUEBERRY ALMOND FLOUR PANCAKES 🫐🥞🍴 perfect morning stack!! 

My almond flour pancakes is a recipe I’ve been perfecting for YEARS & I hope you love it🫶 Also, it’s almost wild blueberry recipe season & get ready because I have SO much planned 🫐

INGREDIENTS:
(makes 5–6 pancakes)
2 eggs 
1 tbsp coconut sugar 
1 tbsp avocado oil 
1/3 cup milk 
1 tsp lemon juice 
1/4 tsp vanilla extract
1 cup almond flour 
1/4 tsp baking soda 
1/4 tsp salt 
frozen wild blueberries

RECIPE:
- In a mixing bowl, whisk together the eggs, coconut sugar, oil, milk, lemon juice, and vanilla extract until well combined. 
Mix in the almond flour, baking soda, and salt until you have a smooth batter.
- Heat a griddle to medium heat—you want it to be pretty hot! These pancakes are best with a little bit of a crisp. Add a generous amount of butter to the pan. Once the butter is sizzling, pour in the batter, 1/4 cup at a time. Sprinkle with frozen wild blueberries. 
- Once the pancakes are bubbling (about 3 minutes), flip them using a spatula and cook on the other side for another 2-3 minutes. 
- Serve topped with more butter and maple syrup.

2 eggs

1/4 tsp vanilla extract

frozen wild blueberries
recipes.recipe_method:
In a mixing bowl, whisk together the eggs, coconut sugar, oil, milk, lemon juice, and vanilla extract until well combined.
Mix in the almond flour, baking soda, and salt until you have a smooth batter.
Heat a griddle to medium heat—you want it to be pretty hot! These pancakes are best with a little bit of a crisp. Add a generous amount of butter to the pan. Once the butter is sizzling, pour in the batter, 1/4 cup at a time. Sprinkle with frozen wild blueberries.
Once the pancakes are bubbling (about 3 minutes), flip them using a spatula and cook on the other side for another 2-3 minutes.
Serve topped with more butter and maple syrup.

recipes.title: White Chicken Kadai
recipes.author: _simple.kitchen11
recipes.text: this is the easiest white chicken kadai recipe.🍗 no preparations, no marination just quick cooking. save and try this recipe for your next dinner. 🍽️ ingredients: • 500 g chicken • 1 tsp cumin seeds • 3 green cardamom pods • 4 cloves • 2 medium onions, made into a paste • 1 tbsp ginger-garlic paste • salt to taste • 1 tsp coriander powder • 1/2 tsp cumin powder • 1/2 tsp black pepper powder • 1/2 tsp garam masala powder • 1/2 cup yogurt • 3-4 green chilies chopped • 1/2 cup cream • mozzarella cheese, as required • fresh coriander, green chilies, and julienned ginger for garnish method: 1. heat oil in a pan or kadai. add cumin seeds, cardamom, and cloves; sauté until fragrant. 2. add onion paste and sauté for 3–4 minutes until the raw smell disappears. 3. stir in ginger-garlic paste and cook for a minute. 4. add chicken and salt; cook on high flame for 5–6 minutes until the chicken changes color. 5. lower the flame and add cumin powder, coriander powder, garam masala, black pepper, and yogurt. mix well. 6. add a little water and green chilies, cover, and cook on low flame for 10 minutes. 7. remove the lid, add cream and mozzarella cheese, and mix well. cook on low flame until the oil separates. 8. garnish with coriander, green chilies, and julienned ginger. serve hot.

recipes.title: Paruppu Usuli
recipes.author: _nibbly_
recipes.text: amma’s samayal: ep 5 - paruppu usuli ✨ (serves 5-6 people) ingredients: daal paste • 1 cup moong dal (soaked for 30 mins) • ½ cup channa dal (soaked for 30 mins) • 1 heaped tbsp chilli powder • 1 tsp turmeric powder • a pinch of hing • 1 tbsp rock salt • 2 tbsp gingelly oil (sesame oil) vegetable • 1 kg beans, finely chopped tadka • 3–4 tbsp gingelly oil (sesame oil) • 1.5 tsp mustard seeds • 2 tsp urad dal • 3–4 dried red chillies • 8–10 curry leaves • ½ tsp hing method: 1. make the dal paste grind everything under daal paste into a smooth, fine mixture. grease a steam pan generously with gingelly oil (sesame oil), pour in the paste, and drizzle another 2 tbsp of gingelly oil (sesame oil) over the top. swirl gently so the oil spreads evenly. 2. steam the dal pressure cook for 5 whistles or steam for 30 minutes until the dal is firm and fully cooked. scoop it onto a plate and let it cool completely. once cool, grind into a fine lentil crumble. 3. as the daal cools, steam/cook the beans with a little salt steam the chopped beans with a little salt until just tender, then set aside. 4. temper and combine heat gingelly oil (sesame oil) in a pan. add mustard seeds and let them splutter. add urad dal, dried red chillies, curry leaves, and hing. once aromatic, add the lentil crumble and sauté for a minute. add the cooked beans, mix well, and adjust salt if needed. serve hot - the perfect accompaniment for vatha kozhambu.
recipes.caption:
Amma’s Samayal: Ep 5 - Paruppu Usuli ✨
(Serves 5-6 people)

Ingredients:
Daal Paste
	•	1 cup moong dal (soaked for 30 mins)
	•	½ cup channa dal (soaked for 30 mins)
	•	1 heaped tbsp chilli powder
	•	1 tsp turmeric powder
	•	A pinch of hing
	•	1 tbsp rock salt
	•	2 tbsp gingelly oil (Sesame oil)

Vegetable
	•	1 kg beans, finely chopped

Tadka
	•	3–4 tbsp gingelly oil (Sesame oil)
	•	1.5 tsp mustard seeds
	•	2 tsp urad dal
	•	3–4 dried red chillies
	•	8–10 curry leaves
	•	½ tsp hing

Method:

1. Make the dal paste
Grind everything under Daal Paste into a smooth, fine mixture. Grease a steam pan generously with gingelly oil (Sesame oil), pour in the paste, and drizzle another 2 tbsp of gingelly oil (Sesame oil) over the top. Swirl gently so the oil spreads evenly.

2. Steam the dal
Pressure cook for 5 whistles or steam for 30 minutes until the dal is firm and fully cooked. Scoop it onto a plate and let it cool completely.
Once cool, grind into a fine lentil crumble.

3. As the daal cools, steam/cook the beans with a little salt
Steam the chopped beans with a little salt until just tender, then set aside.

4. Temper and combine
Heat gingelly oil (Sesame oil) in a pan. Add mustard seeds and let them splutter. Add urad dal, dried red chillies, curry leaves, and hing.
Once aromatic, add the lentil crumble and sauté for a minute. Add the cooked beans, mix well, and adjust salt if needed.

Serve hot - the perfect accompaniment for Vatha Kozhambu.

recipes.title: Date & Walnut Cookies
recipes.author: farzanahnasser_nutrition
recipes.text: date + walnut cookies these 3 ingredient cookies are made with dates and walnuts. they are so easy to make, so delicious and i’ve dipped these in dark chocolate and added a sprinkle od sea salt. they are rich in fibre, protein and magnesium and i cannot stop eating them!!! they will be a staple in my snacking game for 2026!! each serving which is 2 cookies has 6.5 g of fibre, 7g of protein and 110gmg of magnesium recipe: 1 cup (100g) walnuts halves 40g ground almonds 6 medjool dates, pitted and chopped 50g 70% dark chocolate pinch of salt in a blender add the walnuts and pulse, then add ground almonds and the chopped dates. pulse anti it comes together. take out and will be like a dough with still some dates pieces. shape into 8 round and flatten into cookie shapes. place on some parchment paper and bake in a preheated oven (180c) for 10-12 minutes until light browned on the edges. melt some chocolate and then cover half the cookie with the chocolate as shown. place back on the parchment paper and add a pinch of salt. let set and enjoy. so so good x

DATE + WALNUT COOKIES

Recipe:
1 cup (100g) walnuts halves 
40g ground almonds 
6 medjool dates, pitted and chopped

recipes.title: Stuffed Lauki Masala
recipes.author: feastlyfit
recipes.text: stuffed lauki masala | healthy stuffed bottle gourd curry looking for a healthy indian dinner recipe that’s comforting, protein-packed, and full of flavor? try this stuffed lauki masala — soft lauki (bottle gourd) rounds stuffed with spiced paneer and simmered in a creamy tomato-cashew gravy. perfect with roti or jeera rice! 🍛💚 🥣 macros (per serving with 2 stuffed lauki): calories: ~140–150 kcal protein: ~8g carbs: ~10g fat: ~7g fiber: ~2.5g 👩‍🍳 how to make stuffed lauki curry: prep the lauki: cut lauki into thick round pieces, boil for 7–8 mins, and drain. scoop out the center. make the paneer stuffing: sauté 1 chopped onion + 2-3 green chillies in ghee. add 150g grated paneer, salt, and chopped coriander. let it cool. stuff & pan-sear: fill the lauki rings with the paneer mix. cook in a ghee-brushed pan until golden on both sides. make the gravy: sauté 1 chopped onion in ½ tbsp ghee, add 3 tomatoes, 4-5 dried red chillies, 8-10 cashews, salt. cook till soft. add 1 tbsp coriander powder, ½ tbsp red chilli powder, 1 tsp haldi, 1 tbsp kitchen king masala, 1 tsp garam masala. cook well. cool and blend with 50g paneer + 1 cup water until smooth. simmer: transfer back to the pan, adjust water, add more red chilli powder and kasoori methi. bring to a boil. assemble & serve: pour gravy into a bowl, place stuffed lauki on top. garnish with curd, chilli oil, and fresh coriander.
recipes.caption:
Stuffed Lauki Masala | Healthy Stuffed Bottle Gourd Curry

Looking for a healthy Indian dinner recipe that’s comforting, protein-packed, and full of flavor? Try this Stuffed Lauki Masala — soft lauki (bottle gourd) rounds stuffed with spiced paneer and simmered in a creamy tomato-cashew gravy. Perfect with roti or jeera rice! 🍛💚
🥣 Macros (per serving with 2 stuffed lauki):
Calories: ~140–150 kcal
Protein: ~8g
Carbs: ~10g
Fat: ~7g
Fiber: ~2.5g

👩‍🍳 How to make stuffed lauki curry:

Prep the lauki:
Cut lauki into thick round pieces, boil for 7–8 mins, and drain. Scoop out the center.

Make the paneer stuffing:
Sauté 1 chopped onion + 2-3 green chillies in ghee. Add 150g grated paneer, salt, and chopped coriander. Let it cool.

Stuff & pan-sear:
Fill the lauki rings with the paneer mix. Cook in a ghee-brushed pan until golden on both sides.

Make the gravy:
Sauté 1 chopped onion in ½ tbsp ghee, add 3 tomatoes, 4-5 dried red chillies, 8-10 cashews, salt. Cook till soft.
Add 1 tbsp coriander powder, ½ tbsp red chilli powder, 1 tsp haldi, 1 tbsp kitchen king masala, 1 tsp garam masala. Cook well.
Cool and blend with 50g paneer + 1 cup water until smooth.

Simmer:
Transfer back to the pan, adjust water, add more red chilli powder and kasoori methi. Bring to a boil.

Assemble & serve:
Pour gravy into a bowl, place stuffed lauki on top. Garnish with curd, chilli oil, and fresh coriander.

recipes.title: Gond Makhana Ladoo
recipes.author: keertidacooks
recipes.text: these gond laddus contain no jaggery/ sugar, and are sweetened instead with khareek/ chuhara and some dates. also, conventional gond ladoos contain atta, but the ones my mother-in-law- who is a ladoo-pro makes is with a base of just makhana, almonds and dried coconut. great for bone health as well as for your gut, and a must in winters, here is the recipe you’ll need 100 gms gond 350 gms khareek, cut into small pieces (you get pre-cut one online) 100 gms of de-seeded dates fry the gond, in ghee in batches. slot aside we needed ~200 gms ghee in total for this recipe. in the same residual ghee, toast 100 gms makhana till crisp- set aside. this step can also be done in the microwave/ oven toast 100 gms of khobra/ dried coconut. slot aside in the same kadhai, toast 200 gms almonds add the khareek and keep tossing till the khareek is warm now combine the makhana, almonds, khareek, gond and toasted coconut in a large paraat/ container grind it, in batches, by adding 5-6 dates each time note: you have to grind it till very fine, and till the mixture can make a ball when you press it together. taste and see if you need it to be more sweet- if you do, add more dates. once everything is ground, add raisins, chopped cashews as well as cardamom powder and shape into ladoos. if it’s difficult to shape into ladoos, simply transfer to an airtight jar and have 2-3 tbsps everyday- it was taste just as good & do you good!
recipes.caption:
These Gond laddus contain no jaggery/ sugar, and are sweetened instead with khareek/ Chuhara and some dates.

Also, conventional gond ladoos contain atta, but the ones my mother-in-law- who is a ladoo-pro makes is with a base of just Makhana, almonds and dried coconut.

Great for bone health as well as for your gut, and a must in winters, here is the recipe 

You’ll need 
100 gms gond 
350 gms Khareek, cut into small pieces (you get pre-cut one online)
100 gms of de-seeded dates 

Fry the gond, in ghee in batches. Slot aside 
We needed ~200 gms ghee in total for this recipe. 

In the same residual ghee, toast 
100 gms Makhana till crisp- set aside. This step can also be done in the microwave/ oven

Toast 100 gms of khobra/ dried coconut. Slot aside 

In the same Kadhai, toast 
200 gms almonds

Add the Khareek and keep tossing till the Khareek is warm 

Now combine the Makhana, almonds, khareek, gond and toasted coconut in a large paraat/ container 

Grind it, in batches, by adding 5-6 dates each time 

NOTE: you have to grind it till very fine, and till the mixture can make a ball when you press it together. 

Taste and see if you need it to be more sweet- if you do, add more dates.

Once everything is ground, add raisins, chopped cashews as well as cardamom powder and shape into ladoos. 

If it’s difficult to shape into ladoos, simply transfer to an airtight jar and have 2-3 Tbsps everyday- it was taste just as good & do you good!

recipes.recipe_ingredients:
100 gms gond
350 gms Khareek, cut into small pieces (you get pre-cut one online)
100 gms of de-seeded dates
recipes.recipe_method:
Fry the gond, in ghee in batches. Slot aside
We needed ~200 gms ghee in total for this recipe.
In the same residual ghee, toast
100 gms Makhana till crisp- set aside. This step can also be done in the microwave/ oven
Toast 100 gms of khobra/ dried coconut. Slot aside
In the same Kadhai, toast
200 gms almonds
Add the Khareek and keep tossing till the Khareek is warm
Now combine the Makhana, almonds, khareek, gond and toasted coconut in a large paraat/ container
Grind it, in batches, by adding 5-6 dates each time
NOTE: you have to grind it till very fine, and till the mixture can make a ball when you press it together.
Taste and see if you need it to be more sweet- if you do, add more dates.
Once everything is ground, add raisins, chopped cashews as well as cardamom powder and shape into ladoos.
If it’s difficult to shape into ladoos, simply transfer to an airtight jar and have 2-3 Tbsps everyday- it was taste just as good & do you good!

recipes.text: palak gojju🥬 that quick, spicy, tangy comfort you’ll want with rice or roti ✨ 📝ingredients: for the blended paste • 1 medium onion, chopped • 2 medium tomatoes, chopped • 6–7 garlic cloves • 1 small piece of tamarind for aromatics (tempering) • 3 tbsp oil • 1 tsp jeera (cumin seeds) • 1 tsp urad dal • a pinch of hing (asafoetida) • 1 dried red chilli, chopped masala mix • 1 tbsp red chilli powder • 1 tsp haldi (turmeric powder) • ½ tbsp coriander powder other ingredients: • 1 big cup chopped palak (spinach) • salt to taste method: 1. add onion, tomatoes, garlic, and tamarind to a blender and grind into a smooth paste. 2. heat oil in a pan, add jeera, urad dal, hing, and red chilli. let it turn lightly golden. 3. add the masala mix and sauté for a few seconds until aromatic. 4. add the blended paste, mix well, and cook for about 3 minutes until oil releases. 5. add chopped palak and salt, mix well, cook for 5 minutes, and turn off the heat. serve hot with rice and papad! enjoy! inspired by . . . . . . . . {palak gojju, easy dinner recipe, easy recipes, lunch recipe, palak, gojju, meals, quick, viral, trending, viral recipes, south indian food}

recipes.title: Creamy Chicken Soup
recipes.author: withanushkarawat
recipes.text: creamy chicken soup for the soul 🫰🏼✨ detailed recipe: - pound 1/2 inch ginger, 8-10 garlic cloves, 1 green chilli, & 1-2 lime leaves coarsely - heat 2 tsp butter & add 1 bay leaf, cardamom, a sprig of curry leaves, pounded paste & 1 small chopped onion - sauté till the onions are slightly brown - add 500 gms chicken (bone-in) - season with salt & lots of freshly cracked black pepper and roast the chicken till slightly golden brown - add 1 cup of water & 1 cup coconut milk - mix & simmer with a lid on, on low flame till the chicken is fully cooked - add a splash of fish sauce (optional) & turn off the heat - serve hot with your fav toppings (stir fried broccoli, mushrooms, noodles), a scrunch of pepper & a drizzle of lemon juice and enjoy!🥰

recipes.caption:
Creamy Mushroom Soup 🍜
Warm Bowls Ep: 3 

Soup ingredients (serves 2)
Olive oil
1 medium onion finely chopped
3 to 4 garlic cloves chopped
1 packet(200g) button mushrooms sliced
1 tbsp jowar flour
8 to 10 raw cashews soaked 15 to 20 minutes in hot water then drained
Fresh thyme plus more to finish
Chilli flakes optional
Salt and black pepper to taste
Water or veg stock as needed
Rice wine vinegar or lemon juice optional added at the end

Mushroom topping
1 tbsp olive oil
Shimeji or any mushrooms
1 small garlic clove finely chopped
1 to 2 tsp tamari or soy sauce
Fresh thyme leaves added at the end
Black pepper

Method
1 Soak cashews. Heat oil in a pot. Cook onion till soft. Add garlic 30 seconds.
2 Add mushrooms and a pinch of salt. Cook on medium high 5 to 10 minutes until they release water then turn glossy and deeper.
3 Mix in jowar flour 30 to 45 seconds. Add cashews chilli flakes thyme and pepper.
4 Add water or stock. Cover and simmer 10 to 12 minutes.
5 Cool slightly then blend silky smooth. Reheat. Adjust salt pepper and thickness with a splash of water.
6 Off heat stir in vinegar or lemon optional. Taste and adjust.

Topping
7 Heat oil. Add shimeji and cook without salting until moisture cooks off and they turn golden.
8 Add garlic 30 seconds then tamari. Toss till glossy. Add thyme leaves and pepper at the end.

Serve
Pour soup. Top with golden mushrooms thyme cracked pepper and a little extra virgin olive oil.

Notes
Use oyster shiitake or more button for the topping.
For extra umami add a small splash of tamari to the soup while simmering.

recipes.title: Green Goddess Soup
recipes.author: vaibhav_cooks
recipes.text: green goddess soup 🌿 creamy, comforting, and quietly nourishing — this one looks green but eats like pure comfort. this soup is smooth, buttery, and balanced, without tasting “healthy.” cashews and yogurt give it body, mixed greens bring depth, and a touch of lemon keeps it fresh without turning sharp. it’s the kind of bowl you make when you want warmth, not detox. how i make it: 1️⃣ heat 1 tbsp olive oil in a pot. add 1 small onion (chopped) and 2 garlic cloves (chopped). sauté till soft and translucent. 2️⃣ add ¾ cup zucchini (diced), 1 cup broccoli florets, ½ cup green peas, and 3 cups spinach along with a pinch of salt. cook 3–4 minutes till everything softens and the spinach wilts fully. 3️⃣ add 2 tbsp soaked cashews and 1½ cups vegetable stock or water. cover and simmer for 8–10 minutes till vegetables are completely tender. 4️⃣ blend till absolutely smooth and velvety with ¼ cup thick yogurt and a small splash of milk if needed for silkiness. 5️⃣ return to low heat. season with salt, ½ tsp freshly cracked black pepper, and 1–2 tsp lemon juice. finish with 1 tsp olive oil or butter. do not boil. serve hot with a yogurt swirl, olive oil drizzle, and some roasted seeds on top. soft, comforting, and deeply satisfying. wintersoups easysouprecipe hiddengreens wholesomecomfort green goddess soup, creamy green soup, healthy vegetable soup, blended vegetable soup, spinach soup recipe, comfort soup ideas, easy winter soups, creamy soup without cream, nutritious soup recipes
recipes.caption:
Green Goddess Soup 🌿
Creamy, comforting, and quietly nourishing — this one looks green but eats like pure comfort.

This soup is smooth, buttery, and balanced, without tasting “healthy.” Cashews and yogurt give it body, mixed greens bring depth, and a touch of lemon keeps it fresh without turning sharp. It’s the kind of bowl you make when you want warmth, not detox.

How I make it:

1️⃣ Heat 1 tbsp olive oil in a pot. Add 1 small onion (chopped) and 2 garlic cloves (chopped). Sauté till soft and translucent.

2️⃣ Add ¾ cup zucchini (diced), 1 cup broccoli florets, ½ cup green peas, and 3 cups spinach along with a pinch of salt. Cook 3–4 minutes till everything softens and the spinach wilts fully.

3️⃣ Add 2 tbsp soaked cashews and 1½ cups vegetable stock or water. Cover and simmer for 8–10 minutes till vegetables are completely tender.

4️⃣ Blend till absolutely smooth and velvety with ¼ cup thick yogurt and a small splash of milk if needed for silkiness.

5️⃣ Return to low heat. Season with salt, ½ tsp freshly cracked black pepper, and 1–2 tsp lemon juice. Finish with 1 tsp olive oil or butter. Do not boil.

Serve hot with a yogurt swirl, olive oil drizzle, and some roasted seeds on top.
Soft, comforting, and deeply satisfying.

Blend till absolutely smooth and velvety with ¼ cup thick yogurt and a small splash of milk if needed for silkiness.
Return to low heat. Season with salt, ½ tsp freshly cracked black pepper, and 1–2 tsp lemon juice. Finish with 1 tsp olive oil or butter. Do not boil.

recipes.title: Pumpkin Bhareet
recipes.author: keertidacooks
recipes.text: my favourite pumpkin recipe is a traditional marathi side that marries ripe sweet pumpkin with tangy thick yoghurt. mildly spiced and finished with a handlful of coconut/ crushed peanuts (or both!) for texture, this bhareet works beautifully as a dip that i’ve even served on grazing platters! sharing the recipe here: chop 250 gms / ~2 cups of ripe pumpkin, transfer to a cooker-safe container and pressure-cook till tender. don’t add any water to the container holding the pumpkin. cool, then gently press the cooked cubes with your palms to get rid of some of the water released from the pumpkin- especially important if you want a thicker consistency for the dip. you could totally leave the water in, the consistency will be thinner. now, mash the cubes with 2 green chilies, ground salt, to taste 1/2 tsp sugar/ as per taste add ~1/4 cup of thick yogurt- best if it’s tart 1/3 cup of grated coconut/ roasted peanut powder mix well. transfer to a bowl. traditionally, we top this with this tempering heat 1 tbsp ghee and add 1/2 tsp cumin seeds 1 finely chopped green chilies set aside to cool. before serving, mix in the tempered ghee, check for salt/ sugar balance. this time we forgot the tempering, and realise it isn’t really needed- making this an oil-free preparation that is still so creamy and satisfying. sneaks in a mighty lot of pumpkin without feeling too virtuous, it’s one of my favourite recipes with pumpkin + comes together in no time + versatile enough to be paired with meals
recipes.caption:
My favourite pumpkin recipe is a traditional Marathi side that marries ripe sweet pumpkin with tangy thick yoghurt. 
Mildly spiced and finished with a handlful of coconut/ crushed peanuts (or both!) for texture, this bhareet works beautifully as a dip that I’ve even served on grazing platters! 

Sharing the recipe here:

Chop 250 gms / ~2 cups of ripe pumpkin, transfer to a cooker-safe container and pressure-cook till tender. Don’t add any water to the container holding the pumpkin. 

Cool, then gently press the cooked cubes with your palms to get rid of some of the water released from the pumpkin- especially important if you want a thicker consistency for the dip. You could totally leave the water in, the consistency will be thinner. 

Now, mash the cubes with 
2 green chilies, ground 
Salt, to taste 
1/2 tsp sugar/ as per taste 

Add 
~1/4 cup of thick yogurt- best if it’s tart 
1/3 cup of grated coconut/ roasted peanut powder 

Mix well. 

Transfer to a bowl. 

traditionally, we top this with this tempering
heat 1 Tbsp ghee and add 
1/2 tsp Cumin seeds 
1 finely chopped green chilies 

Set aside to cool. 

Before serving, mix in the tempered ghee, check for salt/ sugar balance. 

This time we forgot the tempering, and realise it isn’t really needed- making this an oil-free preparation that is still so creamy and satisfying. 

Sneaks in a mighty lot of pumpkin without feeling too virtuous, it’s one of my favourite recipes with pumpkin + comes together in no time + versatile enough to be paired with meals, chillas and thalipeeth as well as crackers.

recipes.title: Tengapal Rasam (Coconut Milk Rasam)
recipes.author: vaibhav_cooks
recipes.text: tengapal rasam / coconut milk rasam 🥥 not every rasam needs to bite. some days, you want it softer — creamier, warmer, and easier on the palate. tengapal rasam is exactly that pause from the sharp tang of tamarind-heavy rasam. coconut milk rounds everything out — the spice mellows, the heat softens, and the broth turns silky instead of fiery. it’s still unmistakably rasam, just gentler and more comforting, the kind you reach for when you want something soothing but not bland. best with soft rice, a little ghee, and a quiet meal. 🎥: tengapal rasam, coconut milk rasam, mild rasam recipe, south indian rasam varieties, creamy rasam, coconut based rasam, comforting rasam, rasam without sharp tamarind, traditional tamil rasam, soothing south indian food

recipes.title: Aleevache Ladoo
recipes.author: keertidacooks
recipes.text: my favourite traditional ladoo has to be these aleevache ladoo (followed closely by dink/ gond) and yes, even more than besan/ rawa/ boondi (that i’ve never enjoyed). here are the proportions/ process for these ladoo that taste great, and turns out are good for you too. 1/2 cup aleev seeds- soaked in just enough water to submerge the seeds for 3 hours 1.25 cups of jaggery 2 cups packed freshly grated coconut 3/4 tsp cardamom powder add 1 tbsp of water to a heavy-bottomed pot, followed by the soaked aleev seeds and jaggery. mix well to combine for 2 mins- then add the grated coconut. keep mixing/ stirring for ~15 mins till the mixture comes together- this needs some patience/ arm strength. add the cardamom powder, mix well, take it off the heat and shape into ladoos while warm. store these in the fridge- since they have coconut, they spoil if left unrefrigerated for more than 3-4 days. enjoy!
recipes.caption:
My favourite traditional ladoo has to be these Aleevache ladoo (followed closely by Dink/ gond) and yes, even more than Besan/ Rawa/ Boondi (that I’ve never enjoyed).

Here are the proportions/ process for these ladoo that taste great, and turns out are good for you too. 

1/2 cup Aleev seeds- soaked in just enough  water to submerge the seeds for 3 hours 
1.25 cups of jaggery 
2 cups packed freshly grated coconut 
3/4 tsp cardamom powder 

Add 1 Tbsp of water to a heavy-bottomed pot, followed by the soaked Aleev seeds and jaggery. 

Mix well to combine for 2 mins- then add the grated coconut. 

Keep mixing/ stirring for ~15 mins till the mixture comes together- this needs some patience/ arm strength. 

Add the cardamom powder, mix well, take it off the heat and shape into ladoos while warm. 

Store these in the fridge- since they have coconut, they spoil if left unrefrigerated for more than 3-4 days. 

Enjoy!

recipes.title: Temple-Style Curd Rice
recipes.author: _nibbly_
recipes.text: amma’s samayal - ep 3: temple style curd rice ✨💛 ingredients (serves 4–5): • 4 cups cooked rice (cook it a little mushy) • 2.5 cups milk • 1/2 cup curd • 1 inch grated ginger • a handful of chopped coriander • 1 tbsp butter (unsalted or white butter) • 2 tbsp gingelly oil • 1 tsp mustard seeds • 1 tsp cumin seeds • 2–3 dried red chillies • 2–3 green chillies, slit • 7–8 curry leaves • 1 tsp hing • salt to taste method 1. in a large mixing bowl, combine the cooked rice with milk and curd. mix well, squeezing the rice lightly so it becomes soft and creamy. 2. add the butter and mix again. then add grated ginger and coriander leaves. season with salt and combine thoroughly. 3. for the tadka, heat gingelly oil and add mustard seeds and cumin seeds. once they splutter, add the red chillies, green chillies, curry leaves, and hing. 4. pour the tadka over the curd rice and mix well. 5. let it rest in a cool place/refrigerate for about an hour before serving for the best flavour and texture.
recipes.caption:
Amma’s Samayal - Ep 3: Temple Style Curd Rice ✨💛

Ingredients (serves 4–5):
	•	4 cups cooked rice (cook it a little mushy)
	•	2.5 cups milk
	•	1/2 cup curd
	•	1 inch grated ginger
	•	A handful of chopped coriander
	•	1 tbsp butter (unsalted or white butter)
	•	2 tbsp gingelly oil
	•	1 tsp mustard seeds
	•	1 tsp cumin seeds
	•	2–3 dried red chillies
	•	2–3 green chillies, slit
	•	7–8 curry leaves
	•	1 tsp hing
	•	Salt to taste

Method
	1.	In a large mixing bowl, combine the cooked rice with milk and curd. Mix well, squeezing the rice lightly so it becomes soft and creamy.
	2.	Add the butter and mix again. Then add grated ginger and coriander leaves. Season with salt and combine thoroughly.
	3.	For the tadka, heat gingelly oil and add mustard seeds and cumin seeds. Once they splutter, add the red chillies, green chillies, curry leaves, and hing.
	4.	Pour the tadka over the curd rice and mix well.
	5.	Let it rest in a cool place/refrigerate for about an hour before serving for the best flavour and texture.
