recipes.text: i have been making this ragi uppu urundai 😍 from a last few years as a healthy snack or breakfast in my home, and everyone loves it. i sometimes even pack it for my husband’s lunch box with some hot sambar and chutney. i personally love it with tomato onion chutney, but my family loves to eat it with coconut chutney. 🌱 i have used a mix of rice and ragi in this, but if you are looking for diabetic friendly recipes, you can just take it with ragi flour too. 😍 for the diabetic friendly version, you can leave a comment and i will message you the detailed recipe. recipe - add 1 cup soaked rice, 1/4 cup fresh coconut, salt to taste and 1/2 cup ragi flour in a blender and blend till it’s slightly coarse. once done, keep aside. heat 1 tbsp oil, add 1 tsp mustard seeds, 1 tsp urad dal, 1 tsp chana dal, 3-4 cashews (broken), 2 dry red chillies (crushed), 2 sprig curry leaves and 1/4 cup fresh coconut (grated). add in the prepared ragi rice batter and cook on low heat until it becomes thick. now make it small balls and steam for 8-10 minutes. serve with your favourite chutney.
recipes.caption:
I have been making this RAGI UPPU URUNDAI 😍 from a last few years as a healthy snack or breakfast in my home, and everyone loves it. I sometimes even pack it for my husband’s Lunch box with some hot sambar and chutney.

I personally love it with tomato onion chutney, but my family loves to eat it with coconut chutney. 🌱

I have used a mix of rice and ragi in this, but if you are looking for diabetic friendly recipes, you can just take it with ragi flour too. 😍

RECIPE - 
Add 1 cup soaked rice, 1/4 cup fresh coconut, salt to taste and 1/2 cup ragi flour in a blender and blend till it’s slightly coarse. Once done, keep aside. 
Heat 1 tbsp oil, add 1 tsp mustard seeds, 1 tsp urad dal, 1 tsp chana dal, 3-4 cashews (broken), 2 dry red chillies (crushed), 2 sprig curry leaves and 1/4 cup fresh coconut (grated).
Add in the prepared ragi rice batter and cook on low heat until it becomes thick. Now make it small balls and steam for 8-10 minutes. Serve with your favourite chutney.

recipes.caption:
Drumstick and Moong Dal Soup 🍲 

Share this with your parents and Save it for Dinner tomorrow  Recipe  4-5 Drumsticks - peeled and cut in 3 inch pieces  1/4 cup raw moong dal (Washed and soaked for atleast 6 hours) Salt to taste 1/2 tsp turmeric powder   Tadka  1 tbsp ghee  1 tbsp cumin seeds 5-7 garlic cloves chopped  8-10 chopped curry leaves   1/2 tsp dry ginger powder  1/2 tsp black pepper powder  Coriander leaves and lemon juice for garnish   Method  - Wash the moong dal 2-3 times of till the water is completely clean and soak for 6-8 hours  - Wash and peel the drumsticks and cut in 3 inch pices  - To a pressure cooker add the drumstick, moong dal, salt and turmeric with 750 mls of water and pressure cook on high heat till 3 whistles, then lower the heat and let it cook for 8-10 min  - Turn off the gas / induction after 10 min and let the cooker cool down
- Once the cooker is cool, open the lid and strain the dal and drumstick mixture into a kadhai
- Mash it well to extract all the pulp from the drumstick
- Pour another 750 mls of water from the strainer so that all the leftover dal and drumstick pulp is strained into the Kadhai and throw / compost the leftover fibre of the drumstick.
- Set the Kadhai on medium heat and bring it to a boil 
- In the meantime prepare the tadka - heat ghee, add cumin seeds, once they crackle add the garlic and curry leaves and cook them for a 45-60 seconds and add the tadka to the soup 
- Add dry ginger powder and black pepper powder
- Simmer the soup till the water and the dal and drumstick pulp are a cohesive blend 
- Adjust salt
- Serve with fresh coriander leaves and a dash of lime juice 
Drumsticks are a great source of potassium, calcium, phosphorous, vitamin A, C and magnesium. Mixed with moong dal this soup also has some protein and serves as a great low calorie yet filling meal when on a weight loss journey.

recipes.recipe_ingredients:

1/4 cup raw moong dal (Washed and soaked for atleast 6 hours)

Tadka

recipes.recipe_method:
Wash the moong dal 2-3 times of till the water is completely clean and soak for 6-8 hours
Wash and peel the drumsticks and cut in 3 inch pices
To a pressure cooker add the drumstick, moong dal, salt and turmeric with 750 mls of water and pressure cook on high heat till 3 whistles, then lower the heat and let it cook for 8-10 min
Turn off the gas / induction after 10 min and let the cooker cool down
Once the cooker is cool, open the lid and strain the dal and drumstick mixture into a kadhai
Mash it well to extract all the pulp from the drumstick
Pour another 750 mls of water from the strainer so that all the leftover dal and drumstick pulp is strained into the Kadhai and throw / compost the leftover fibre of the drumstick.
Set the Kadhai on medium heat and bring it to a boil
In the meantime prepare the tadka - heat ghee, add cumin seeds, once they crackle add the garlic and curry leaves and cook them for a 45-60 seconds and add the tadka to the soup
Add dry ginger powder and black pepper powder
Simmer the soup till the water and the dal and drumstick pulp are a cohesive blend
Adjust salt
Serve with fresh coriander leaves and a dash of lime juice

recipes.caption:
Pea Spinach Mint Soup 🍲
Warm Bowls · Episode 2

A calm green bowl that is light and quietly comforting. Silky from potato, sweet from peas, fresh from mint, lifted with lemon.

Ingredients:
Oil of your choice
Cumin seeds ½ tsp
1 medium onion, chopped
4 to 5 garlic cloves, sliced
1 small or medium potato, diced small
Water to just cover
1 bay leaf (I forgot to add it during the shoot. Do add it for gentle aroma.)
Shelled green peas 200 to 250 g
Baby spinach 100 g
Fresh mint leaves
Lemon zest of one lemon
Lemon juice to taste
Salt to taste
Black pepper to taste
Extra virgin olive oil for finishing

Pistachio sesame dukkah:
Pistachios about 3 tbsp
White sesame seeds about 1 tbsp
Lemon zest ½ tsp
Pinch salt
Black pepper optional

Method
	1.	Warm oil in a heavy pot. Add cumin seeds until they crackle. Add onion with a pinch of salt and cook until soft and sweet.
	2.	Add garlic and cook briefly.
	3.	Add potato and enough water to just cover. Add the bay leaf. Simmer gently until the potato is tender.
	4.	Add peas and cook 2 to 3 minutes. Stir in spinach to wilt for 30 to 60 seconds. Turn off the heat.
	5.	Strain and reserve the cooking liquid. Let things cool slightly. Add mint leaves and lemon zest and blend right away until silky and bright.
	6.	Loosen with the reserved hot liquid to a smooth pour. Season with salt, black pepper, and lemon juice to taste.
	7.	For the dukkah toast pistachios and sesame on low heat until fragrant. Cool slightly, then crush to a coarse mix with lemon zest and a pinch of salt. Add black pepper if you like.
	8.	Rewarm the soup gently. Bowl it, drizzle extra virgin olive oil, spoon over the lemony pistachio sesame dukkah, and finish with a few mint leaves.

Notes:
Blend right after mint and zest go in to keep the bright green.
Reheat gently and avoid boiling.

recipes.title: Sitaphal Payasam
recipes.author: flavoursbymounika
recipes.text: sitaphal payasam😍 rich, creamy, and bursting with the sweetness of custard apples this sitaphal payasam is the perfect fusion of tradition and freshness. the roasted nuts add a lovely crunch, while the natural flavor of sitaphal takes it to another level. ingredients • 1 cup roasted vermicelli • 4 cups full-fat milk • 1 cup condensed milk • 2 tbsp ghee • 10 cashews • 8 almonds (chopped) • 8 pistachios (chopped) • 3 medium-sized sitaphal (custard apples) • 2–3 cardamoms (crushed) preparation 1. roast the nuts: heat ghee in a pan. add cashews, almonds, and pistachios. fry until golden brown. remove and keep aside. 2. cook the vermicelli: in the same pan, add 1 cup roasted vermicelli to the remaining ghee. sauté for a minute. 3. add milk: pour 4 cups of milk and bring it to a boil. let the vermicelli cook completely in milk. 4. sweeten and flavor: add 1 cup condensed milk and crushed cardamom. mix well and simmer for 2–3 minutes. 5. cool it down: let the payasam cool until it’s warm (not hot). 6. prepare sitaphal pulp: scoop out the pulp from 3 medium-sized custard apples. lightly pulse in a manual chopper 3–4 times to loosen the seeds. remove seeds carefully and keep the pulp ready. 7. mix and serve: once the payasam is warm, add the sitaphal pulp and roasted nuts. mix gently. 8. serve: enjoy chilled or at room temperature — every spoon is a creamy, nutty, fruity delight!
recipes.caption:
Sitaphal Payasam😍

Rich, creamy, and bursting with the sweetness of custard apples this Sitaphal Payasam is the perfect fusion of tradition and freshness. The roasted nuts add a lovely crunch, while the natural flavor of sitaphal takes it to another level. 

Ingredients

	•	4 cups full-fat milk
	•	1 cup condensed milk
	•	2 tbsp ghee
	•	10 cashews
	•	8 almonds (chopped)
	•	8 pistachios (chopped)
	•	3 medium-sized sitaphal (custard apples)
	•	2–3 cardamoms (crushed)

Preparation
	1.	Roast the nuts:
Heat ghee in a pan. Add cashews, almonds, and pistachios. Fry until golden brown. Remove and keep aside.
	2.	Cook the vermicelli:
In the same pan, add 1 cup roasted vermicelli to the remaining ghee. Sauté for a minute.
	3.	Add milk:
Pour 4 cups of milk and bring it to a boil. Let the vermicelli cook completely in milk.
	4.	Sweeten and flavor:
Add 1 cup condensed milk and crushed cardamom. Mix well and simmer for 2–3 minutes.
	5.	Cool it down:
Let the payasam cool until it’s warm (not hot).
	6.	Prepare sitaphal pulp:
Scoop out the pulp from 3 medium-sized custard apples. Lightly pulse in a manual chopper 3–4 times to loosen the seeds. Remove seeds carefully and keep the pulp ready.
	7.	Mix and serve:
Once the payasam is warm, add the sitaphal pulp and roasted nuts. Mix gently.
	8.	Serve:
Enjoy chilled or at room temperature — every spoon is a creamy, nutty, fruity delight!

recipes.title: Potato Fry
recipes.author: _nibbly_
recipes.text: amma’s samayal - ep 1: potato fry 🥔🌶️ ingredients: (serves 2 people) • 3 medium sized potatoes – chopped into tiny cubes • 4–5 tbsp gingelly oil (sesame oil) • 1 tsp mustard seeds • 1 tsp jeera • 2 dried red chillies – chopped • a big handful of curry leaves – finely chopped • ¼ tsp asafoetida (hing) • 1 tsp turmeric powder • ½ tsp sambar powder • 1 heaped tsp chilli powder • salt to taste method: 1. heat 4–5 tbsp sesame oil in a wide fry pan. 2. add 1 tsp mustard seeds and let them splutter. 3. add 1 tsp jeera, 2 chopped dried red chillies, and finely chopped curry leaves. 4. once they crackle, add the cubed potatoes and sauté on high flame for 2–3 minutes. 5. add ¼ tsp asafoetida and 1 tsp turmeric powder. mix well. 6. continue cooking on high flame until the potatoes soften and start turning golden. 7. add ½ tsp sambar powder, 1 heaped tsp chilli powder, and salt to taste. 8. toss well so the masala coats the potatoes evenly. 9. cook for another minute or two till slightly crisp around the edges. serve hot! . .

recipes.recipe_method:
1. Heat 4–5 tbsp sesame oil in a wide fry pan.
2. Add 1 tsp mustard seeds and let them splutter.
3. Add 1 tsp jeera, 2 chopped dried red chillies, and finely chopped curry leaves.
4. Once they crackle, add the cubed potatoes and sauté on high flame for 2–3 minutes.
5. Add ¼ tsp asafoetida and 1 tsp turmeric powder. Mix well.
6. Continue cooking on high flame until the potatoes soften and start turning golden.
7. Add ½ tsp sambar powder, 1 heaped tsp chilli powder, and salt to taste.
8. Toss well so the masala coats the potatoes evenly.
9. Cook for another minute or two till slightly crisp around the edges. Serve hot!

recipes.title: Chana Dal Litti with Aloo Tamatar Saag
recipes.author: withanushkarawat
recipes.text: chana dal ki litti & aloo tamatar ka saag ✨ a beautiful rustic dish packed with flavours 😋 detailed recipe : - wash & soak 2 cups chana dal for 4-5 hours atleast - transfer to a blender jar along with 2 small size badi elaichi, 1/2 inch cinnamon stick, 6-7 peppercorns, 5-6 garlic cloves, 2-3 green chillies, 1/2 inch ginger, salt to taste, a pinch of haldi, a pinch of red chilli powder, a pinch of hing, 1 tsp coriander powder, 1/2 tsp roasted cumin seeds or roasted cumin powder, 1 tsp garam masala - blitz coarsely into a rustic paste; you can also add a splash of water but make sure it’s not watery at all, we need a thick consistency - transfer this mixture to a bowl & adjust the spices - add 1 finely chopped onion & mix and your litti mixture is ready - heat 2 tbsp mustard oil in a tawa till it starts smoking and then lower the flame (mustard oil gives a beautiful flavour to the litti) - dip your palm in water and roll a generous amount of the litti mixture in your palm - then gently spread a thick layer of the litti mix onto the pan/tawa with your hand - cook it on medium flame till the ends start browning; flip & cook till golden brown on both sides - once done, serve hot with the aloo tamatar saag & mint chutney!☺️ aloo tamatar saag recipe: - heat 1 tbsp ghee in a kadhai & add 1 tsp jeera, a pinch of hing and 2 slit green chillies - let the jeera pop & become toasty - add 2-3 finely chopped tomatoes & a dash of water - season with salt, haldi, coriander powder, and red chi
recipes.caption:
Chana Dal ki Litti & Aloo Tamatar ka Saag ✨
A beautiful rustic dish packed with flavours 😋

Detailed Recipe : 

- Wash & soak 2 cups chana dal for 4-5 hours atleast
- Transfer to a blender jar along with 2 small size Badi Elaichi, 1/2 inch cinnamon stick, 6-7 peppercorns, 5-6 garlic cloves, 2-3 green chillies, 1/2 inch ginger, salt to taste, a pinch of haldi, a pinch of red chilli powder, a pinch of hing, 1 tsp coriander powder, 1/2 tsp roasted cumin seeds or roasted cumin powder, 1 tsp garam masala
- Blitz coarsely into a rustic paste; you can also add a splash of water but make sure it’s not watery at all, we need a thick consistency 
- Transfer this mixture to a bowl & adjust the spices 
- Add 1 finely chopped onion & mix and your Litti mixture is ready
- Heat 2 tbsp mustard oil in a tawa till it starts smoking and then lower the flame (mustard oil gives a beautiful flavour to the Litti)
- Dip your palm in water and roll a generous amount of the Litti mixture in your palm
- Then gently spread a thick layer of the Litti mix onto the pan/tawa with your hand 
- Cook it on medium flame till the ends start browning; flip & cook till golden brown on both sides 
- Once done, serve hot with the Aloo Tamatar saag & mint chutney!☺️

Aloo Tamatar Saag recipe:
- Heat 1 tbsp ghee in a kadhai & add 1 tsp jeera, a pinch of hing and 2 slit green chillies
- Let the jeera pop & become toasty
- Add 2-3 finely chopped tomatoes & a dash of water
- Season with salt, haldi, coriander powder, and red chilli powder 
- Mix & add a splash of water
- Cover & cook for 8-10 min till the tomatoes are done
- Add 2 boiled & diced potatoes & 1/2 cup water 
- Cover & simmer for another 5-8 min
- Once done slightly mash a few potatoes & mix 
- Garnish with fresh coriander and its ready!☺️

recipes.title: Aliv Laddoo
recipes.author: aruna_vijay_masterchef
recipes.text: aliv seeds ladoo our kitchens are filled with superfoods, and halim seeds are one of the best-kept secrets! i first came across these seeds in video a few years ago, and more recently, my nutritionist recommended them. i’ve been eating halim seed ladoos for the past three months, and trust me—the difference in my skin and hair texture has been incredible. they’re so easy to make with basic ingredients. i use dry coconut for better shelf life, and yes, you’ll need to store these ladoos in the refrigerator. one batch makes about 20-24 ladoos—perfect for a month! aliv ladoo recipe - ingredients - aliv seeds - 3/4 cup coconut water - 1 cup ghee - 1/4 cup jaggery - 1.5 cup chopped almonds - 1/3 cup dessicated coconut - 1/2 cup cardamom powder - 1 tsp method - 1. start by soaking the aliv seeds in coconut water and keep it aside for half n hour 2. then, in a pan add in ghee, jaggery and stir it well until it melts 3.then add in the soaked aliv seeds and mix it all well 4. finally add in chopped almonds, grated dry coconut, cardamom and cook till it all comes together and leaves the sides of the pan 5.then transfer the mixture in a plate and start rolling them into ladoos while they are hot 6. apply ghee while on the palms while shaping them and it's ready! superfood, ladoo, aliv seeds, halim seeds, irregular periods, hairfall, iron deficiency, skin , healthy food, immunity booster
recipes.caption:
Aliv seeds ladoo 

Our kitchens are filled with superfoods, and Halim seeds are one of the best-kept secrets!

I first came across these seeds in @rujuta.diwekar video a few years ago, and more recently, my nutritionist @shinysurendran recommended them. I’ve been eating Halim seed ladoos for the past three months, and trust me—the difference in my skin and hair texture has been incredible.

They’re so easy to make with basic ingredients. I use dry coconut for better shelf life, and yes, you’ll need to store these ladoos in the refrigerator. One batch makes about 20-24 ladoos—perfect for a month!

Aliv ladoo Recipe -
Ingredients -
Aliv seeds - 3/4 cup
Coconut water - 1 cup
Ghee - 1/4 cup
Jaggery - 1.5 cup
Chopped Almonds - 1/3 cup
Dessicated coconut - 1/2 cup
Cardamom powder - 1 tsp
Method -
1. Start by soaking the aliv seeds in coconut water and keep it aside for half n hour
2. Then, in a pan add in ghee, jaggery and stir it well until it melts
3.Then add in the soaked aliv seeds and mix it all well
4. Finally add in chopped almonds, grated dry coconut, cardamom and cook till it all comes together and leaves the sides of the pan
5.Then transfer the mixture in a plate and start rolling them into ladoos while they are hot
6. Apply ghee while on the palms while shaping them and it's ready!

Welcome to Episode 1 of our Diabetic-Friendly Breakfast Series!

✅ Soak mung dal overnight or for 8 hours atleast and throw the soaked water, then grind it into a smooth paste.

✅ Finely chop veggies—capsicum, carrot, onion, and coriander. Mix these with grated paneer.

recipes.recipe_method:
Soak mung dal overnight or for 8 hours atleast and throw the soaked water, then grind it into a smooth paste.
Add the spices: turmeric, salt, and green chilli paste to the batter. Mix everything well.
Finely chop veggies—capsicum, carrot, onion, and coriander. Mix these with grated paneer.
Season the veggie-paneer mixture with salt and chilli flakes.
In a heated pan, pour the mung dal batter and spread evenly. Add the veggie and paneer mixture on top.
Drizzle some ghee around the edges, flip the chilla, and cook until golden and crisp.

RECIPES 👇 (with approximate measurements because I suck and never measure lol)

1. SEED CRACKERS 🌰

Take about 3 tbsp of ground flax seeds. Add water till you get a thick mixture. Add a pinch of salt, a handful or more of pumpkin seeds, sesame seeds, and other seeds of choice. It should be very thick and you should be able to form a shape without it breaking apart.
Shape into crackers on wax paper, and then bake at really low temperature (around 70-80 degrees celcius) for a realllly long time (around 30, 45 minutes). Check so that it doesn't burn.

2. CHOC GRANOLA 🍫

Add around 1.5 cups of rolled oats to a bowl. Add a quarter cup of pumpkin seeds, quarter cup of chopped almonds, pinch of salt.
In a separate bowl, add 3-4 tbsp maple syrup, 1 tbsp tahini, 1 tbsp coconut oil, and 1-2 tbsp cocoa powder. Mix. Pour into the oat mixture and make sure everything is coated well. 
Transfer to a greased baking tray and bake at 150 celsius for about 25 minutes. Let cool and add chopped chocolate. 

3. MAKHANA 🧈

Roast 2 cups makahana in the oven until crunchy. In a bowl, mix 3 tbsp ghee, 1 tsp turmeric, 1 tsp salt, and a pinch of black pepper. Drizzle onto the makhana and mix together.

4. DATE LADDOOS 🥥

Soak 3 medjool dates for a few hours. Add to a food processor with a handful of walnuts, 2-3 tbsp shredded coconut, 1 tbsp peanut butter. Blitz until you get a dough. Shape into ladoos.

recipes.title: Roasted Vegetable Soup
recipes.author: lucysallysommer
recipes.text: a very comforting and nourishing soup that was one of my most popular recipes from 2024! ingredients | serves 4 roasted vegetables: 3 onions, peeled, halved and sliced into thirds 1 small butternut squash, peeled and sliced into cubes 1-2 tsp chilli powder 4 cloves garlic 2 sprigs fresh thyme leaves soup: 2 tbsp olive oil 4 garlic cloves, sliced 2 sprigs each - rosemary, sage, thyme 1 parmesan rind 1.4l vegetable or chicken stock 2 tbsp sherry vinegar 1 lemon zest ½ lemon juice 200g short pasta 6 leaves cavolo nero, stems removed and sliced 100 ml double cream ⅓ cup parmesan salt and pepper method set the oven to 190c. place butternut squash, onion and garlic into a roasting tin and season with thyme, chilli powder, salt, pepper and drizzle with olive oil. mix everything together and place in the middle (not top) of the oven until golden (approx 18 mins) place a dutch oven/ deep saucepan on a medium heat and drizzle the base with olive oil. add the sliced garlic followed by salt, rosemary, thyme, sage leaves and parmesan rind. let this all infuse for a couple of minutes but don’t let the garlic burn. pour in the stock, add the lemon zest, lemon juice, sherry vinegar and season with salt and pepper. return the lid and let this simmer gently for a couple of minutes. add the pasta. you can remove the sprig of thyme and rosemary at this point but keep the sage leaves they are delicious! when the pasta is al dente add the cavolo nero and let this cook for a couple of minutes. remo
recipes.caption:
A very comforting and nourishing soup that was one of my most popular recipes from 2024! 

Ingredients | serves 4 

Roasted vegetables:

3 onions, peeled, halved and sliced into thirds 

1 small butternut squash, peeled and sliced into cubes

1-2 tsp chilli powder 

4 cloves garlic

2 sprigs fresh thyme leaves 

Soup:

2 tbsp olive oil

4 garlic cloves, sliced

2 sprigs each - rosemary, sage, thyme 

1 parmesan rind

1.4L vegetable or chicken stock 

2 tbsp sherry vinegar 

1 lemon zest 

½ lemon juice

200g short pasta

6 leaves cavolo nero, stems removed and sliced

100 ml double cream

⅓ cup parmesan 

Salt and pepper 

Method

Set the oven to 190C. Place butternut squash, onion and garlic into a roasting tin and season with thyme, chilli powder, salt, pepper and drizzle with olive oil. Mix everything together and place in the middle (not top) of the oven until golden (approx 18 mins) 

Place a dutch oven/ deep saucepan on a medium heat and drizzle the base with olive oil. Add the sliced garlic followed by salt, rosemary, thyme, sage leaves and parmesan rind. Let this all infuse for a couple of minutes but don’t let the garlic burn. 

Pour in the stock, add the lemon zest, lemon juice, sherry vinegar and season with salt and pepper. Return the lid and let this simmer gently for a couple of minutes. 

Add the pasta. You can remove the sprig of thyme and rosemary at this point but keep the sage leaves they are delicious! 

When the pasta is al dente add the cavolo nero and let this cook for a couple of minutes. 

Remove from the heat and add  the roasted veggies to the soup. Squeeze in the roasted garlic don’t waste it! You need to season again at this point and you can add more lemon juice if needed.

Stir in the cream and parmesan.

Serve instantly in bowls with a grating of parmesan, some black pepper and a drizzle of extra virgin olive oil.

Eggless Nankhatai🥳
Follow @savourydesserts for more!🥰

Let me know which festive special recipe you want next✨

This traditional Indian Biscuits are flavourful, nostalgic and hits the right spot with that cardamom goodness 😍
A perfect balance of sweetness and crunchy nankhatais can make anyone’s day!😁

🤍Ingredients🤍
100g Ghee (clarified butter)
100g Powdered Sugar
10-12 Kesar Strands
1tsp Cardamom powder
120g All purpose flour (Maida)
30g Semolina (Sooji)
27g Besan (Gran flour)
1/2+1/8tsp Baking Powder
1/4tsp Baking Soda
Pistachios and Kesar strands to Garnish
💛Process💛
1. Take ghee and chill it for 15 mins in refrigerator it should not be too stiff but not melted also.
2. Take it out of the refrigerator, and add powdered sugar and kesar, elaichi and whisk it for atleast 5 mins. It shiuld be light and fluffy.
3. Then add all the other ingredients and make a soft dough using spatula or your hands.
4. If required add 1-2tsp of Milk and make the dough.
5. Now very important, chill the dough in the freezer (not fridge) for 15-20 mins and then shape into Balls.
6. I made 10 balls of 37g Each! But I would suggest to make small Nankhatai if serving to your guests or including in your hampers.
7. ⁠Make sure to flatten it out a lil and then make cut marks and garnish with pistachio and kesar.
8. Bake this in preheated oven at 170° with both rods on for 25-28 mins.
9. Let then cool down on a wire rack, and don’t try to remove from the baking sheet as they will set once they cool completely or else they would crumble.
 10. Once cooled, store them in airtight container and enjoy!😉

recipes.text: lets make *ekdum spicy nepali style gilo chatpate*🔥🔥 you’ll need for dry masala -dry roast 1 tbsp cumin, 1 tbsp coriander seeds & 3-4 red chillies -let these cool down completely -then blend to a fine powder for chatpate chutney -boil 1 tomato, 1 onion & 4-5 kashmiri red chillies -peel skin from tomato -then transfer in blender along with 7-8 garlic cloves, salt to taste & 2 tbsp kashmiri red chillies powder, blend for smooth puree -add 2 tbsp oil in pan -add prepared puree(just pass through strainer for a smooth texture) -cook well -add maida slurry(mix 1 tbsp maida in 1/2 cup water) -mix well and cook -make sure the sauce has no lumps -turn off the flame and let it cool down completely preparation for the chatpate -add puffed rice in a bowl -add mixture namkeen, matar, wai wai(you can add namkeen of your choices) -add chopped onion, tomato, cucumber, boiled potato, green chilli & coriander leaves -prepared masala -add prepared chatpate sauce -mix well & your spicy nepali style chatpate is ready 😍 [ nepali style gilo chatpate recipe nepali chatpate recipe wai wai bhel nepali chow chow nepali food snacks time evening snacks recipes puffed rice chaat recipe ]
recipes.caption:
Lets Make *Ekdum Spicy Nepali Style Gilo Chatpate*🔥🔥

You’ll Need

For Dry Masala
-Dry roast 1 tbsp cumin, 1 tbsp coriander seeds & 3-4 red chillies 
-let these cool down completely 
-then blend to a fine powder 

For Chatpate Chutney 
-Boil 1 tomato, 1 onion & 4-5 kashmiri red chillies 
-peel skin from tomato
-then transfer in blender along with 7-8 garlic cloves, salt to taste & 2 tbsp kashmiri red chillies powder, blend for smooth puree
-add 2 tbsp oil in pan
-add prepared puree(just pass through strainer for a smooth texture)
-cook well
-add maida slurry(mix 1 tbsp maida in 1/2 cup water)

-make sure the sauce has no lumps
-turn off the flame and let it cool down completely 

Preparation for the Chatpate
-Add Puffed Rice in a bowl
-Add Mixture Namkeen, Matar, Wai Wai(you can add namkeen of your choices)
-Add chopped onion, tomato, cucumber, boiled potato, green chilli & Coriander leaves
-Prepared masala
-Add Prepared chatpate sauce
-Mix Well
& Your Spicy Nepali Style Chatpate is Ready 😍

recipes.caption:
5-Minute Peanut Chili Noodles 🔥

Comment “Recipe” and I’ll send you the full recipe card for free!!

As simple as it gets, as flavorful as it gets: sweet, savory, and just the right spice.

Protein tip: Best served with chicken, shrimp, or tofu 🫡

Ingredients:
-9 oz (250 g) hand-cut thick noodles (or any noodles you like)
-1.5 tbsp peanut butter
-1 tsp chili flakes (optional)
-1/3 cup fresh green onion, sliced
-2 tsp sesame seeds
-5 garlic cloves, minced
-1 tbsp white sugar (optional, but balances the heat)
-1 tbsp chili crisp (+ 2 more tbsp extra for garnish) 
-1 tbsp rice vinegar
-2 tbsp dark soy sauce
-1/3 cup neutral oil (I use avocado)
-3 tbsp reserved pasta water (optional)
-More sliced green onion, for garnish
-Fresh lime wedges, for garnish

I recommend “Lao Gan Ma Spicy Chili Crisp”

Instructions:
1. Bring a  pot of salted water to a boil and cook your noodles according to package instructions. Undercook them by about 30 seconds because they’ll finish in the sauce. Save some pasta water (!!), then drain and rinse the noodles under cold water so they don’t stick together like clingy exes.
2. In a cold pan (no heat yet), add: peanut butter, chili flakes, green onion, sesame seeds, garlic, sugar, 1 tbsp chili crisp, rice vinegar, and dark soy sauce.
3. Heat 1/3 cup neutral oil until it’s really hot (like “sizzle your eyebrows off” hot), then carefully pour it over the cold ingredients in the pan. Watch the magic happen. Stir it all together.
4. Toss in your noodles and coat them in the sauce. If you want them extra silky, turn on the heat to medium-low, splash in 2–3 tbsp of the reserved noodle water and thoroughly mix together.
5. Turn off the heat, top with more green onion, extra chili crisp, and lime wedges if you’re fancy.

recipes.title: Instant Benne Dosa
recipes.author: meltin_mouth
recipes.text: instant benne dosa ~ an iconic dosa recipe from karnataka ***sorry if i hurted you through my pronunciation..as in north india we pronounce like this *** detailed recipe for instant benne dosa - ingredients - ( made around 7-8 dosa) 1. rice flour - 1 cup 2. besan (gram flour) - 1/4 cup 3. curd - 1/2 cup 4. potato - 1 medium/small 5. kashmiri whole red chilli - 2 (soaked) 6. salt - 1 tsp 7. garlic - 2 pcs 8. water - 3/4 cup - 1 cup 9. baking soda - 1/2 tsp 10. butter - 2 tbsp (or as required) method - 1. in a grinder take rice flour, besan, curd, soaked kashmiri red chilli, chopped potatoes, garlic, salt & some water. grind it into smooth batter. 2. now add more water to make dosa like consistency & adjust salt as per taste. 3. add baking soda & mix well. 4. grease hot dosa tawa & wipe it. 5. now spread the batter & spread some butter on top. 6. if you want you can flip & cook the dosa from other side too.. 7. cook the dosa till they turn golden & crisp & serve hot with coconut chutney or onion tomato chutney and enjoy 😊 ❤️❤️ ❤️ ❤️
recipes.caption:
Instant Benne Dosa ~ an iconic Dosa recipe from Karnataka 

***sorry if I hurted you through my pronunciation..as in North India we pronounce like this ***

Detailed recipe for instant Benne Dosa -
Ingredients - ( made around 7-8 dosa)
1. Rice flour - 1 cup
2. Besan (gram flour) - 1/4 cup
3. Curd - 1/2 cup
4. Potato - 1 medium/small
5. Kashmiri whole red chilli - 2 (soaked)
6. Salt - 1 tsp
7. Garlic - 2 pcs
8. Water - 3/4 cup - 1 cup
9. Baking soda - 1/2 tsp
10. Butter - 2 tbsp (or as required) 

Method -
1. In a grinder take rice flour, besan, curd, soaked Kashmiri red chilli, chopped potatoes, garlic, salt & some water. Grind it into smooth batter.
2. Now add more water to make dosa like consistency & adjust salt as per taste.
3. Add baking soda & mix well.
4. Grease hot dosa tawa & wipe it. 
5. Now spread the batter & spread some butter on top.
6. If you want you can flip & cook the dosa from other side too..
7. Cook the dosa till they turn golden & crisp & serve hot with coconut chutney or onion tomato chutney and enjoy 😊

recipes.title: Tomato Garlic Tokku
recipes.author: suman.ranganath.gowda
recipes.text: tomato garlic tokku 🍅🧄 perfect combo with hot rice – stays fresh in the fridge for 3–4 months if stored properly. ⸻ 🛒 ingredients • ½ kg tomatoes (roughly chopped) • 2 small pieces tamarind • 1 tsp fenugreek seeds (menthye) • 1 tsp mustard seeds (sasive) – for roasting • 1 tsp salt (adjust to taste) • 2 tsp red chilli powder (karad pudi) • 5 tbsp oil (enne) • 1–2 tsp mustard seeds (sasive) – for tempering • 1–2 tbsp garlic (belulli), finely chopped ⸻ 🔥 method 1. roast & grind • dry roast 1 tsp fenugreek + 1 tsp mustard seeds until aromatic. • grind to a fine powder. 2. tomato base • in a pan, add tomatoes + tamarind and sauté well. • cook until tomatoes release water and soften. • add salt + red chilli powder, roast until masala blends. • cool slightly, then blend tomatoes + roasted fenugreek–mustard into a smooth paste (no water). 3. final fry • heat 5 tbsp oil in a pan. • add mustard seeds and let them splutter. • add chopped garlic, fry till golden and fragrant. • add the prepared tomato paste, roast until oil separates. 4. serve & store • tastes heavenly with steaming hot rice. • store in a clean, airtight container in the fridge – stays good for 3–4 months 🇩🇪 [ amma samyal, mother’s cooking, amma, quick recipes, easy recipes, mom’s recipes, kannada, karnataka, tomato garlic tokku, tomato garlic chutney, tomato, garlic recipes , recipes, quick recipes, easy recipes ]

recipes.caption:
🌿Kothimbir Vadi🌿

Crisp, golden slices of coriander goodness! 🥰
I can never stop at just one—this is that snack you keep coming back to, whether it’s tea time, a rainy evening, or a last-minute dinner side.
Perfectly crunchy outside, herby inside, and so Maharashtrian at heart. 💛

⸻

Ingredients
	•	2 large bunches fresh coriander leaves, washed & finely chopped
	•	Salt, to taste
	•	1 tsp red chilli powder
	•	½ tsp turmeric
	•	1 tsp jeera (cumin) powder
	•	A pinch of hing
	•	½ tsp ajwain
	•	1 tbsp sesame seeds (plus extra for garnish)
	•	1 tbsp tamarind pulp
	•	1 tbsp ginger-garlic-green chilli paste
	•	About 1 cup besan (gram flour), or a little more as needed
	•	1–2 tsp oil for mixing + oil for shallow-frying

⸻

Step-by-Step
	1.	Mix the chopped coriander with salt, red chilli powder, turmeric, jeera powder, hing, ajwain, and sesame seeds.
	2.	Add tamarind pulp and ginger-garlic-green chilli paste; mix well.
	3.	Add a little besan, give it a mix, and keep adding more as needed—no extra water required—until the mixture binds.
	4.	Drizzle in a teaspoon of oil and shape into a firm thick log.
	5.	Place the log on a greased steamer plate, cover, and steam for about 20 minutes until set.
	6.	Let it cool completely, then slice into golden oval pieces.
	7.	Shallow-fry the slices until crisp and finish with extra sesame seeds. Serve hot.

⸻

Tips & Tricks
	•	Use a salad spinner to wash and spin-dry the coriander so there’s no excess water. Or air-dry it or gently press with a damp cloth after washing.
	•	Skip the water! The salted coriander releases enough moisture for the batter.

recipes.text: tried out a different version of this south indian spiced yogurt curry today, using tomatoes and murungakkai (moringa drumsticks). mooru curry - coconut oil mustard seeds: 1 tsp funegreek seeds: 1 tsp onion: 1 garlic: 1 whole tomatoes: 2 turmeric powder: 1 tsp cumin powder: 1 tsp salt: 1 tsp murungakkai: 2 (drumsticks) water: 250ml red chili: 1 curry leaves yogurt: 450g (blend with 250ml water) make sure to nicely brown the onions etc. just be patient ok, where are you rushing to? also make sure to wait until the tomatoes are nice and mushy to get a nice consistency. i always use the same amount of yogurt and water... i find this is just the right consistency and how we like it. coz it’ll thicken as soon as you switch off the fire. i usually just use the same yogurt tub to measure the same amount of water. but this time i used half the water measurement first to cook the murungakkai drumsticks. and the balance half was used to blend the yogurt. i cooked the moringa drumsticks covered over low flame for 30 minutes so that it’s cooked through but the water doesn’t fully evaporate. stir occasionally. after 30 minutes, the tomatoes would be nice and mushy which gives a lovely thick texture to the mooru curry. whatever you do in life, once you add the yogurt mixture in… don’t let it boil. turn it down to super low flame before adding the yogurt mix. stir gentle to incorporate and switch it off before it boils. alsooooo... make sure to blend/whisk the yogurt before adding it in so

Make sure to nicely brown the onions etc. Just be patient ok, where are you rushing to? Also make sure to wait until the tomatoes are nice and mushy to get a nice consistency.

I always use the same amount of yogurt and water... I find this is just the right consistency and how we like it. Coz it’ll thicken as soon as you switch off the fire. 

I usually just use the same yogurt tub to measure the same amount of water. But this time I used half the water measurement first to cook the murungakkai drumsticks. And the balance half was used to blend the yogurt. 

I cooked the moringa drumsticks covered over low flame for 30 minutes so that it’s cooked through but the water doesn’t fully evaporate. Stir occasionally. After 30 minutes, the tomatoes would be nice and mushy which gives a lovely thick texture to the mooru curry. 

Whatever you do in life, once you add the yogurt mixture in… DON’T LET IT BOIL. Turn it down to super low flame before adding the yogurt mix. Stir gentle to incorporate and switch it off before it boils.

Alsooooo... make sure to blend/whisk the yogurt before adding it in so that it doesn’t separate and curdle! I’ve previously added a whole tub of yogurt straight into the pot from the fridge... And almost woke my grandmother up from her grave!

I usually make sure my mooru curry is not spicy so that little man can have some too. If you prefer it spicy… Add the chillies and some dry chillies in the beginning with the onions and garlic etc. I usually just add the chili at the end for decoration and photography purposes 🙈🙈

recipes.caption:
The Paati Protocol - Ep 6 : Lime Rasam 🍋🍋‍🟩🌼

Ingredients ( serves 5-6 people )
	•	3–4 green chillies, slit
	•	1 inch ginger, grated or finely chopped
	•	1 tsp turmeric powder
	•	2 tbsp rasam powder (any variety of your choice)
	•	1 cup boiled tuvar dal (pressure cook with a pinch of turmeric)
	•	¼ tsp asafoetida (hing) – if using compound hing, dissolve in 2–3 tbsp water
	•	2-3 cups water (extra, for rasam base)
	•	1–1½ tomatoes, roughly chopped
	•	Salt to taste (about 1 tbsp rock salt used here)
	•	A handful of coriander leaves, finely chopped
	•	3–4 tbsp fresh lime juice

For dal mixture
	•	Blend 1 large cup of boiled tuvar dal with 1 cup water into a smooth dal-water mixture.

For tempering (tadka)
	•	2 tsp groundnut oil (or ghee, if  you like)
	•	1 tsp mustard seeds
	•  1 tsp cumin (jeera) seeds
	•	2–3 dried red chillies
	•	A few curry leaves
	•	A pinch of asafoetida (hing)

Method:
	
1. Prepare rasam base
	•	In a vessel, add 2 cups water along with slit green chillies, ginger, turmeric, salt, asafoetida, and rasam powder.
	•	Bring to a boil.
	
2.	Cook tomatoes
	•	Add chopped tomatoes to the boiling mixture.
	•	Let them cook until very soft (about 5 minutes).
	
3.	Add dal mixture
	•	Stir in the blended dal-water mixture and 1–2 cups of extra water to adjust consistency.
	•	Allow the rasam to froth. (do not let it boil hard).
	
4.	Finish with coriander
	•	Once it starts frothing lightly, add in the chopped coriander leaves.
	
5.	Prepare tempering (tadka)
	•	Heat groundnut oil or ghee in a small pan.
	•	Add mustard seeds, let them splutter.
	•	Add cumin, dried red chillies, curry leaves, and hing.
	•	Pour the tadka over the rasam.
	
6.	Add lime juice

recipes.recipe_ingredients:
3–4 green chillies, slit
1 inch ginger, grated or finely chopped
1 tsp turmeric powder
2 tbsp rasam powder (any variety of your choice)
1 cup boiled tuvar dal (pressure cook with a pinch of turmeric)
¼ tsp asafoetida (hing) – if using compound hing, dissolve in 2–3 tbsp water
2-3 cups water (extra, for rasam base)
1–1½ tomatoes, roughly chopped
Salt to taste (about 1 tbsp rock salt used here)
A handful of coriander leaves, finely chopped
3–4 tbsp fresh lime juice
For dal mixture
Blend 1 large cup of boiled tuvar dal with 1 cup water into a smooth dal-water mixture.
For tempering (tadka)
2 tsp groundnut oil (or ghee, if  you like)
1 tsp mustard seeds
1 tsp cumin (jeera) seeds
2–3 dried red chillies
A few curry leaves
A pinch of asafoetida (hing)
recipes.recipe_method:
1. Prepare rasam base
In a vessel, add 2 cups water along with slit green chillies, ginger, turmeric, salt, asafoetida, and rasam powder.
Bring to a boil.

2. Cook tomatoes
Add chopped tomatoes to the boiling mixture.
Let them cook until very soft (about 5 minutes).

3. Add dal mixture
Stir in the blended dal-water mixture and 1–2 cups of extra water to adjust consistency.
Allow the rasam to froth. (do not let it boil hard).

4. Finish with coriander
Once it starts frothing lightly, add in the chopped coriander leaves.

5. Prepare tempering (tadka)
Heat groundnut oil or ghee in a small pan.
Add mustard seeds, let them splutter.
Add cumin, dried red chillies, curry leaves, and hing.
Pour the tadka over the rasam.

6. Add lime juice
Switch off the flame (rasam should just be frothing, not boiling).
Stir in lime juice.

7. Adjust seasoning
Taste and adjust salt or lime juice if needed.

recipes.title: Ghee Rice
recipes.author: _nibbly_
recipes.text: ghee rice✨ ingredients : • 1 cup jeeraga samba rice (preferred) or basmati rice – soaked for minimum 30-40 mins, drained • 5–6 tbsp good quality ghee • 3 tbsp grated ginger (or ginger paste) • 4–5 slit green chillies (large, mild ones) • 2 onions, finely sliced whole spices: • 2 bay leaves • 1 star anise • 4–5 cardamom pods • 2 cloves • 2-inch piece cinnamon stick liquid & seasoning: • 1-1¼ cups coconut milk ( use the same cup used for measuring rice ) • salt – about 1 tbsp (or to taste) for garnish: • fresh coriander, finely chopped • lots of fried onions method: 1. heat ghee in a pressure cooker on the lowest flame possible. 2. add the whole spices and let them slowly roast in the ghee for 2 minutes. 3. next, add the slit green chillies and let them blister. 4. add sliced onions and sauté till they turn translucent (about 5 minutes). 5. stir in the ginger and sauté for just 1 minute. 6. add the soaked & drained rice. keep stirring and sautéing for 10 minutes on low flame, till the grains turn slightly nutty and aromatic. 7. pour in 1-1¼ cups coconut milk, add salt, and give everything a gentle mix. 8. cover the cooker, keep the flame at its absolute lowest, and let it cook for 30-40 minutes. allow the pressure to release naturally. 9. once done, open, fluff the rice gently with a fork, then garnish with coriander and fried onions. serve warm-honestly, it’s divine on its own, but pairs beautifully with any curry or side dish.
recipes.caption:
Ghee Rice✨

Ingredients :
	•	1 cup Jeeraga Samba Rice (preferred) or Basmati Rice – soaked for minimum 30-40 mins, drained
	•	5–6 tbsp good quality ghee
	•	3 tbsp grated ginger (or ginger paste)
	•	4–5 slit green chillies (large, mild ones)
	•	2 onions, finely sliced

Whole spices:
	•	2 bay leaves
	•	1 star anise
	•	4–5 cardamom pods
	•	2 cloves
	•	2-inch piece cinnamon stick

Liquid & seasoning:
	•	1-1¼ cups coconut milk ( use the same cup used for measuring rice )
	•	Salt – about 1 tbsp (or to taste)

For garnish:
	•	Fresh coriander, finely chopped
	•	Lots of fried onions

Method:
	1.	Heat ghee in a pressure cooker on the lowest flame possible.
	2.	Add the whole spices and let them slowly roast in the ghee for 2 minutes.
	3.	Next, add the slit green chillies and let them blister.
	4.	Add sliced onions and sauté till they turn translucent (about 5 minutes).
	5.	Stir in the ginger and sauté for just 1 minute.
	6.	Add the soaked & drained rice. Keep stirring and sautéing for 10 minutes on low flame, till the grains turn slightly nutty and aromatic.
	7.	Pour in 1-1¼ cups coconut milk, add salt, and give everything a gentle mix.
	8.	Cover the cooker, keep the flame at its absolute lowest, and let it cook for 30-40 minutes. Allow the pressure to release naturally.
	9.	Once done, open, fluff the rice gently with a fork, then garnish with coriander and fried onions.

Serve warm-honestly, it’s divine on its own, but pairs beautifully with any curry or side dish.

recipes.caption:
Pancakes you can eat all day?

As a nursing mom I snacked on these all week long to satisfy those sugar/carb cravings while still filling up on protein. 

Comment PANCAKE and I’ll send you a recipe card or you can save this post to come back to for later. 

✨ PROTEIN PANCAKES ✨ 

1 1/2 cups flour 
2 tsp baking powder
2 tsp baking soda
1/4 tsp salt 
2 tbsp pure maple syrup
1 egg 
1 cup cottage cheese
1/2 cup plain or vanilla yogurt 
1/2 cup milk 
1 tsp vanilla

Butter for cooking 

🥞 🥞 🥞 

-In a large bowl mix dry ingredients. 

-Blend cottage cheese and yogurt until smooth.

- Make a well in the dry ingredients and pour in all the wet. Whisk gently to combine. 

-Heat large pan or griddle to medium heat and rub down with butter. Use a small cookie scoop to scoop batter and cook until golden brown. 

-Serve with whipped cream and fresh berries. 

Enjoy, friend!

recipes.text: pav bataka (gujarati-style) this gujarati breakfast dish is so simple, hearty and delicious. let’s make this. ingredients: potatoes (boiled & mashed) – 3–4 medium coriander leaves – ½ cup green chillies – 2–3 (adjust to spice level) ginger – 1-inch piece garlic – 4–5 cloves cumin seeds – 1 tsp coriander seeds – 1 tsp oil – 2 tbsp mustard seeds – ½ tsp hing (asafoetida) – a pinch curry leaves – 8–10 turmeric powder – ½ tsp red chilli powder – ½ tsp garam masala – ½ tsp salt – to taste water – ½ to 1 cup (as needed for consistency) lemon juice – 1 tbsp (or more to taste) pav – 6–8, toasted in butter method: in a mortar-pestle, pound together: coriander leaves, green chillies, ginger, garlic, cumin seeds, and coriander seeds. make it into a coarse paste. heat oil in a pan. add mustard seeds and let them splutter. add hing, cumin seeds, coriander seeds, curry leaves. sauté till aromatic. add the prepared green paste and fry on medium flame till raw smell goes away. add turmeric powder, a little red chilli powder, salt, and garam masala. stir well. add a splash of water and bring to a boil. add the mashed potatoes and mix well into the masala. cook on medium flame till everything blends and the oil starts separating. squeeze lemon juice and adjust seasoning. garnish with fresh coriander. toast pav in butter, pav bhaji masala and red chilli powder on a tawa. recipes.caption:
Pav Bataka (Gujarati-Style)
This Gujarati breakfast dish is so simple, hearty and delicious. 
Let’s make this. 

Ingredients: 
Potatoes (boiled & mashed) – 3–4 medium
Coriander leaves – ½ cup
Green chillies – 2–3 (adjust to spice level)
Ginger – 1-inch piece
Garlic – 4–5 cloves
Cumin seeds – 1 tsp
Coriander seeds – 1 tsp
Oil – 2 tbsp
Mustard seeds – ½ tsp
Hing (asafoetida) – a pinch
Curry leaves – 8–10
Turmeric powder – ½ tsp
Red chilli powder – ½ tsp
Garam masala – ½ tsp
Salt – to taste
Water – ½ to 1 cup (as needed for consistency)
Lemon juice – 1 tbsp (or more to taste)
Pav – 6–8, toasted in butter

Method: 
In a mortar-pestle, pound together: coriander leaves, green chillies, ginger, garlic, cumin seeds, and coriander seeds. Make it into a coarse paste. Heat oil in a pan. Add mustard seeds and let them splutter. Add hing, cumin seeds, coriander seeds, curry leaves. Sauté till aromatic. Add the prepared green paste and fry on medium flame till raw smell goes away. Cook on medium flame till everything blends and the oil starts separating. Squeeze lemon juice and adjust seasoning. Garnish with fresh coriander. Toast pav in butter, pav bhaji masala and red chilli powder on a tawa.

recipes.author: sarahtodd
recipes.text: street foods of india – episode 13: indori poha with jalebi 🇮🇳🍋🍬 ㅤ soft, fluffy, steamed poha… topped with crunchy sev… and served with jalebi for breakfast. only in indore. 🔥 ㅤ indore, tucked right in the heart of madhya pradesh, is often called india’s street food capital, and for good reason. the city lives and breathes food. but no dish represents it better than this iconic breakfast combo. ㅤ unlike regular poha, indori poha is gently rinsed, never soaked, and then lightly steamed after tempering to give it that signature soft texture. the real magic comes from jeeravan masala, a spicy-tangy blend of cumin, dry mango, black salt, fennel, clove, cinnamon, and chilli that hits all the right notes. topped with ratlami sev for crunch, pomegranate for sweetness, and always served with piping hot jalebis, because indore doesn’t believe in skipping dessert, even at breakfast. ㅤ type poha if you want the full recipe sent straight to your inbox! ㅤ

recipes.caption:
When comfort meets indulgence — but guilt never shows up! 💚
This Guilt-Free Afghani Paneer is creamy, aromatic, and loaded with flavor… all without the heavy cream. A wholesome twist on a restaurant favorite, made with turai, hung curd, and paneer itself for that rich, velvety base. Perfect with hot chapatis or parathas. 🍽️

🥣 Recipe: Guilt-Free Afghani Paneer

Ingredients:
	•	200 g paneer (cut into cubes)
	•	½ tsp black pepper
	•	Salt to taste
	•	1 tsp ginger-garlic paste
	•	1 tsp oil
	•	1 tsp ghee
	•	1 tej patta
	•	1 cinnamon stick
	•	2 onions (chopped)
	•	2 turai (chopped)
	•	6–7 garlic cloves
	•	1-inch ginger
	•	4–5 green chilies
	•	1 tbsp coriander powder
	•	1 tsp garam masala
	•	Handful fresh coriander leaves
	•	50 g paneer
	•	2 tbsp hung curd
	•	1 tsp kasoori methi
	•	Chilli oil + curd (for garnish, optional)

Method:
	1.	In a bowl, mix paneer cubes with black pepper, salt, and ginger-garlic paste. Set aside for 15 mins.
	2.	Heat oil in a pan and cook the paneer until golden on both sides. Keep aside.
	3.	In another pan, heat ghee, add tej patta and cinnamon. Sauté onions, turai, garlic, ginger, and green chilies with salt until water evaporates.
	4.	Add coriander powder + garam masala. Cook for 2–3 mins. Toss in fresh coriander and cook again for 2–3 mins. Let cool.
	5.	Remove tej patta & cinnamon, then blend with 50 g paneer, hung curd, and little water into a smooth paste.
	6.	Transfer back to the pan, add kasoori methi, and bring to a boil.
	7.	Add cooked paneer, mix well. Garnish with chili oil & curd (optional).
	8.	Serve hot with chapati or paratha.

recipes.title: Smoky Garlic Squash Bhorta
recipes.author: smalltowngirl_isha
recipes.text: ✨ smoky garlic & squash bhorta ✨ a comforting, earthy chutney-style side dish that pairs like magic with hot, steaming rice 🍚. the smokiness of charred red chillies, the sweetness of squash, and the zing of lemon make this one an unforgettable rustic flavor bomb! 🌶️🧄🎃 🛒 ingredients 8–10 dried red chillies 🌶️ 12 garlic cloves 🧄 ½ medium butternut squash or pumpkin 🎃 1 small red onion 🧅 1 tbsp mustard oil (for sautéing) salt 🧂 (to taste) handful of fresh coriander leaves 🌿 juice of 1 lemon 🍋 👩‍🍳 process heat mustard oil in a pan. sauté garlic until golden, then remove. in the same oil, sauté red chillies until fragrant. take them out. next, sauté onion until slightly charred, remove and set aside. add chopped squash to the pan with a drizzle of oil and a splash of water. cook until soft and slightly caramelized. once all are charred and cooled, mash everything together by hand (or a stone mortar for extra rustic vibes). add salt, lemon juice, and lots of fresh coriander leaves. mix well. serve with hot, piping rice and enjoy that smoky, tangy, garlicky magic! 🔥🍚
recipes.caption:
✨ Smoky Garlic & Squash Bhorta ✨
A comforting, earthy chutney-style side dish that pairs like magic with hot, steaming rice 🍚. The smokiness of charred red chillies, the sweetness of squash, and the zing of lemon make this one an unforgettable rustic flavor bomb! 🌶️🧄🎃
🛒 Ingredients
8–10 dried red chillies 🌶️
12 garlic cloves 🧄
½ medium butternut squash or pumpkin 🎃
1 small red onion 🧅
1 tbsp mustard oil (for sautéing)
Salt 🧂 (to taste)
Handful of fresh coriander leaves 🌿
Juice of 1 lemon 🍋
👩‍🍳 Process
Heat mustard oil in a pan. Sauté garlic until golden, then remove.
In the same oil, sauté red chillies until fragrant. Take them out.
Next, sauté onion until slightly charred, remove and set aside.
Add chopped squash to the pan with a drizzle of oil and a splash of water. Cook until soft and slightly caramelized.
Once all are charred and cooled, mash everything together by hand (or a stone mortar for extra rustic vibes).
Add salt, lemon juice, and lots of fresh coriander leaves. Mix well.
Serve with hot, piping rice and enjoy that smoky, tangy, garlicky magic! 🔥🍚

recipes.title: Ammini Kozhukattai
recipes.author: _nibbly_
recipes.text: the paati protocol - ep 2 : ammini kozhukattai. . . here’s what you’ll need: for dough: • 1 cup kozhukattai flour ( i’ve used anil ) • 2 cups water ( use the same cup ) • 1 tbsp sesame oil (plus extra for kneading) • salt to taste • 1 tsp kashmiri chili powder • 1/4 tsp hing for tempering: • 1 ½ tsp mustard seeds • 1 tsp urad dal • 2–3 dried red chilies • 1 sprig curry leaves • 2–3 tsp sesame oil • ¼–½ cup grated coconut • 1 heaping tbsp idli/dosa molaga podi • a pinch of hing • 1/2 tsp kashmiri red chilli powder method: 1. roast & dough – dry roast flour until aromatic. boil water with salt + sesame oil. add flour, stir vigorously until it forms a soft, non-sticky dough with no lumps. 2. knead – cool slightly, knead with 1 tsp of sesame oil, chili powder & hing. 3. shape – roll into tiny balls (amminis) with oiled hands. 4. steam – place on a greased steam tray and steam for 7–8 mins until glossy. 5. temper – heat sesame oil, splutter mustard, urad dal, dried red chilies & curry leaves. add coconut, hing and red chilli powder. sauté 30 secs. then add molaga podi and mix. 6. finish – toss steamed balls in tempering, check salt, and serve. . .
recipes.caption:
The Paati Protocol - Ep 2 : Ammini Kozhukattai.
.
.
Here’s what you’ll need:

For Dough:
	•	1 cup kozhukattai flour ( I’ve used Anil )
	•	2 cups water ( use the same cup )
	•	1 tbsp sesame oil (plus extra for kneading)
	•	Salt to taste
	•	1 tsp Kashmiri chili powder
	•	1/4 tsp hing

For Tempering:
	•	1 ½ tsp mustard seeds
	•	1 tsp urad dal
	•	2–3 dried red chilies
	•	1 sprig curry leaves
	•	2–3 tsp sesame oil
	•	¼–½ cup grated coconut
	•	1 heaping tbsp idli/dosa molaga podi
 •  a pinch of Hing

recipes.author: the_fusion_of_flavours
recipes.text: pala thalikalu detailed recipe 👇 ingredients: rice flour 1 cup jaggery 1 cup milk 2 cups water 1 cup saggubiyyam 2 tbsp cardamom powder 1 tsp cashews 10-15 ghee as required procedure: step 1 – rice flour preparation • take 1 glass rice and soak it overnight. • next morning, wash the soaked rice well. • strain the water completely and spread the rice on a cloth for about 5 minutes. • grind the rice into a smooth powder in a mixer. • sieve the ground rice – soft rice flour is ready. • soak sago in water for 1 hour and keep aside. step 2 – dough & jaggery syrup • heat a kadai, add 2 tbsp jaggery and 2 tbsp water. • once jaggery melts, switch off the stove. • add rice flour to this and mix well to make dough. • if the dough is too loose, add some more rice flour. • if it is too tight, sprinkle little water and adjust. • for syrup: take 1 cup jaggery + ½ glass water, melt it completely, switch off the stove and keep aside. step 3 – cooking pala thalikalu • in a kadai, add 1 cup water + 2 cups milk. • allow it to boil well. • add the soaked sago and cook for 2 minutes. • now take the prepared rice dough, press it through a sev/janthikalu maker directly into the boiling milk to form “thalikalu”. • cook for 10 minutes until the thalikalu become soft. • from the flour kept aside earlier, add little water and make a smooth paste without lumps. • slowly pour this paste into the milk – it helps to thicken the consistency. • add cardamom powder for flavor. • switch off the stove and pour
recipes.caption:
Pala thalikalu detailed recipe 👇 

Ingredients: 
Rice flour 1 cup
Jaggery 1 cup
Milk 2 cups 
Water 1 cup
Saggubiyyam 2 tbsp
Cardamom powder 1 tsp
Cashews 10-15
Ghee as required 

Procedure:
Step 1 – Rice Flour Preparation
• Take 1 glass rice and soak it overnight.
• Next morning, wash the soaked rice well.
• Strain the water completely and spread the rice on a cloth for about 5 minutes.
• Grind the rice into a smooth powder in a mixer.
• Sieve the ground rice – soft rice flour is ready.
• Soak sago in water for 1 hour and keep aside.

Step 2 – Dough & Jaggery Syrup
• Heat a kadai, add 2 tbsp jaggery and 2 tbsp water.
• Once jaggery melts, switch off the stove.
• Add rice flour to this and mix well to make dough.
• If the dough is too loose, add some more rice flour.
• If it is too tight, sprinkle little water and adjust.
• For syrup: take 1 cup jaggery + ½ glass water, melt it completely, switch off the stove and keep aside.

Step 3 – Cooking Pala Thalikalu
• In a kadai, add 1 cup water + 2 cups milk.
• Allow it to boil well.
• Add the soaked sago and cook for 2 minutes.
• Now take the prepared rice dough, press it through a sev/Janthikalu maker directly into the boiling milk to form “thalikalu”.
• Cook for 10 minutes until the thalikalu become soft.
• From the flour kept aside earlier, add little water and make a smooth paste without lumps.
• Slowly pour this paste into the milk – it helps to thicken the consistency.
• Add cardamom powder for flavor.
• Switch off the stove and pour the melted jaggery syrup.
• Fry cashews in ghee and add them on top.

✨ Traditional Pala Thalikalu is ready to serve!

Water 1 cup
Saggubiyyam 2 tbsp
Cardamom powder 1 tsp
Cashews 10-15
Ghee as required
recipes.recipe_method:
Step 1 – Rice Flour Preparation
Take 1 glass rice and soak it overnight.
Next morning, wash the soaked rice well.
Strain the water completely and spread the rice on a cloth for about 5 minutes.
Grind the rice into a smooth powder in a mixer.
Sieve the ground rice – soft rice flour is ready.
Soak sago in water for 1 hour and keep aside.

Step 2 – Dough & Jaggery Syrup
Heat a kadai, add 2 tbsp jaggery and 2 tbsp water.
Once jaggery melts, switch off the stove.
Add rice flour to this and mix well to make dough.
If the dough is too loose, add some more rice flour.
If it is too tight, sprinkle little water and adjust.
For syrup: take 1 cup jaggery + ½ glass water, melt it completely, switch off the stove and keep aside.

Step 3 – Cooking Pala Thalikalu
In a kadai, add 1 cup water + 2 cups milk.
Allow it to boil well.
Add the soaked sago and cook for 2 minutes.
Now take the prepared rice dough, press it through a sev/Janthikalu maker directly into the boiling milk to form “thalikalu”.
Cook for 10 minutes until the thalikalu become soft.
From the flour kept aside earlier, add little water and make a smooth paste without lumps.
Slowly pour this paste into the milk – it helps to thicken the consistency.
Add cardamom powder for flavor.
Switch off the stove and pour the melted jaggery syrup.
Fry cashews in ghee and add them on top.

recipes.title: Sikil P'ak
recipes.author: goatboyintl
recipes.text: sikil p’ak is one of the oldest salsas in mexico: pre-hispanic, yucatecan, and still slept on by most people outside the region. it’s made from roasted pumpkin seeds, chile, and tomato - a thick, earthy, nutty spread that predates colonization and is rooted in ancient maya food traditions. think of it as salsa from a different time and place: not liquid-y, not red or green, but bold in its own way. today, versions like mine often add citrus (originally naranja agria), garlic, and herbs. these post-colonial ingredients bring brightness and balance. it’s evolved like most indigenous foods have, layered with centuries of change, but still grounded in its original spirit. the heat comes from habanero, but it’s gentle and always adjustable because like i always say, make it your own. serve it with duras, chips, crudité, grilled meats, tacos, whatever’s around. it adds richness and depth without trying too hard. if you’ve never had it, this is your sign. and if someone tells you it’s “not salsa”… that just means they haven’t tasted it yet. comment below for my recipe 👇🏼👇🏼👇🏼
recipes.caption:
Sikil P’ak is one of the oldest salsas in Mexico: pre-Hispanic, Yucatecan, and still slept on by most people outside the region.

It’s made from roasted pumpkin seeds, chile, and tomato - a thick, earthy, nutty spread that predates colonization and is rooted in ancient Maya food traditions. Think of it as salsa from a different time and place: not liquid-y, not red or green, but bold in its own way.

Today, versions like mine often add citrus (originally naranja agria), garlic, and herbs. These post-colonial ingredients bring brightness and balance. It’s evolved like most Indigenous foods have, layered with centuries of change, but still grounded in its original spirit.

The heat comes from habanero, but it’s gentle and always adjustable because like I always say, make it your own. Serve it with duras, chips, crudité, grilled meats, tacos, whatever’s around. It adds richness and depth without trying too hard.

If you’ve never had it, this is your sign.
And if someone tells you it’s “not salsa”… that just means they haven’t tasted it yet.

recipes.text: suji corn cheela i packed suji corn cheela , milk powder peda ( i made it for rakhi ) , blueberries and homemade yoghurt . suji corn palak cheela suji/semolina/rava – 1 cup water as needed ( i used more than 1 cup ) palak and onion leaves some water so you can add later ) besan – ¼ cup -1/3 cup salt - 1 tsp red chili powder/flakes – ¾ tsp (adjust spice level according to your taste) turmeric powder – 3/4 tsp chat masala as per taste boiled corn -1/2 cup chopped spinach - 1 cup spring onion 1/3 cup baking soda -pinch add suji , corn , spinach , spices , besan and onion and water . keep it aside for 10-15 mins . suji soaks the water so you can add water if batter is really thick . add a pinch of baking soda . baking soda helps in making cheela softer for longer time . you can skip it if you are eating fresh and not packing . put it in heated pan and cook it on both sides
recipes.caption:
Suji corn cheela 

I packed Suji corn cheela , milk powder peda ( I made it for Rakhi ) , blueberries and homemade yoghurt .

Suji corn palak cheela 

Suji/Semolina/Rava – 1 cup
Water as needed ( I used more than 1 cup ) palak and onion leaves some water so you can add later ) 
Besan – ¼ cup -1/3 cup 
Salt - 1 tsp
Red chili powder/flakes – ¾ tsp (adjust spice level according to your taste)
Turmeric powder – 3/4 tsp
Chat masala  as per taste 
Boiled corn -1/2 cup 
Chopped spinach - 1 cup 
Spring onion 1/3 cup 
Baking soda -pinch 

Add Suji , corn , spinach , spices , besan and onion and water . Keep it aside for 10-15 mins . Suji soaks the water so you can add water if batter is really thick . 

Add a pinch of baking soda . Baking soda helps in making cheela softer for longer time . You can skip it if you are eating fresh and not packing . 

Put it in heated pan and cook it on both sides

#lunch #healthyrecipe #indianrecipe #quickrecipes #easyrecipeideas
recipes.recipe_ingredients:
Suji/Semolina/Rava – 1 cup
Water as needed ( I used more than 1 cup ) palak and onion leaves some water so you can add later )
Besan – ¼ cup -1/3 cup
Salt - 1 tsp
Red chili powder/flakes – ¾ tsp (adjust spice level according to your taste)
Turmeric powder – 3/4 tsp
Chat masala  as per taste
Boiled corn -1/2 cup
Chopped spinach - 1 cup
Spring onion 1/3 cup
Baking soda -pinch
recipes.recipe_method:
Add Suji , corn , spinach , spices , besan and onion and water . Keep it aside for 10-15 mins . Suji soaks the water so you can add water if batter is really thick .
Add a pinch of baking soda . Baking soda helps in making cheela softer for longer time . You can skip it if you are eating fresh and not packing .
Put it in heated pan and cook it on both sides

recipes.title: Homemade Bagels
recipes.author: cookinlyds
recipes.text: baking powder** i love this one~ hope you enjoy it as much as i do~ plain dough ingredients: - 2 cups all purpose flour - 1.5 cups of greek yogurt - 1 tsp salt - 1 tsp baking powder - egg wash i realize this is 5 ingredients… but i didn’t count salt 🕺🏻 chocolate bagels - 1 tbsp cocoa powder - chocolate chips cheddar cheese bagels - 1/3 cup shredded cheese mix instructions: 1. set your oven to 350 degrees f to cut time. 2. combine plain bagel ingredients together and knead your dough for a couple of minutes until everything is well combined. the dough will be a little sticky, so you may dust your hands in flour to work with dough. 3. divide dough into 5 equal portions. 4. if you would like to make chocolate bagels, mix one half of your dough with cocoa powder. then flatten the other half of the dough and add chocolate to the center of the bagel. roll out these two pieces of dough and stick them together to create a dough shape. feel free to use cocoa powder to work with sticky dough. 5. if you would like to make cheese bagels, flatten your dough and add cheese to the center. seal your dough and shape into bagel shapes. make sure to brush egg wash on your bagels before sprinkling on more cheese on top. 6. for plain bagels, shape your dough into bagel shapes. 7. place your bagels spaced out on a baking tray with parchment paper. brush egg wash on each bagel. 8. bake in the oven for 25 minutes at 350 f. after it’s done, enjoy! plain bagel macros per bagel (divided by 5) calories:
recipes.caption:
Baking POWDER** I love this one~ hope you enjoy it as much as I do~

Plain Dough ingredients:
- 2 cups all purpose flour
- 1.5 cups of Greek yogurt
- 1 tsp salt
- 1 tsp baking powder
- Egg wash
I realize this is 5 ingredients… but I didn’t count salt 🕺🏻

Chocolate bagels
- 1 tbsp cocoa powder
- Chocolate chips 

Cheddar cheese bagels
- 1/3 cup Shredded cheese mix

Instructions:
1. Set your oven to 350 degrees F to cut time.
2. Combine plain bagel ingredients together and knead your dough for a couple of minutes until everything is well combined. The dough will be a little sticky, so you may dust your hands in flour to work with dough.
3. Divide dough into 5 equal portions.
4. If you would like to make chocolate bagels, mix one half of your dough with cocoa powder. Then flatten the other half of the dough and add chocolate to the center of the bagel. Roll out these two pieces of dough and stick them together to create a dough shape. Feel free to use cocoa powder to work with sticky dough.
5. If you would like to make cheese bagels, flatten your dough and add cheese to the center. Seal your dough and shape into bagel shapes. Make sure to brush egg wash on your bagels before sprinkling on more cheese on top.
6. For plain bagels, shape your dough into bagel shapes. 
7. Place your bagels spaced out on a baking tray with parchment paper. Brush egg wash on each bagel.
8. Bake in the oven for 25 minutes at 350 F. After it’s done, enjoy!

Plain Bagel Macros Per Bagel (Divided by 5)
Calories: ~253 kcal
Protein: ~15g
Carbs: ~42g
Fat: ~2.6g

2 cups all purpose flour
1.5 cups of Greek yogurt
1 tsp salt
1 tsp baking powder
Egg wash
1 tbsp cocoa powder
Chocolate chips
1/3 cup Shredded cheese mix
recipes.recipe_method:
Set your oven to 350 degrees F to cut time.
2. Combine plain bagel ingredients together and knead your dough for a couple of minutes until everything is well combined. The dough will be a little sticky, so you may dust your hands in flour to work with dough.
3. Divide dough into 5 equal portions.
4. If you would like to make chocolate bagels, mix one half of your dough with cocoa powder. Then flatten the other half of the dough and add chocolate to the center of the bagel. Roll out these two pieces of dough and stick them together to create a dough shape. Feel free to use cocoa powder to work with sticky dough.
5. If you would like to make cheese bagels, flatten your dough and add cheese to the center. Seal your dough and shape into bagel shapes. Make sure to brush egg wash on your bagels before sprinkling on more cheese on top.
6. For plain bagels, shape your dough into bagel shapes.
7. Place your bagels spaced out on a baking tray with parchment paper. Brush egg wash on each bagel.
8. Bake in the oven for 25 minutes at 350 F. After it’s done, enjoy!

recipes.author: nourishedbynutrition
recipes.text: high protein egg biscuits // a garlic & herb version of my viral make-ahead breakfast that’s supports balanced hormones and blood sugar. by supporting blood sugar balance you’re supporting insulin and glucagon which in turn supports cortisol and every sex hormone 🤓 when blood sugar is unstable (spikes and crashes), cortisol is released to help stabilize it. chronically elevated cortisol levels can disrupt the hypothalamic-pituitary-gonadal (hpg) axis, suppressing the production of sex hormones like estrogen, progesterone, and testosterone. garlic & herb high-protein egg biscuits ingredients: 6 large eggs 1/2 cup diced yellow onion 1 tbsp minced garlic 2 cups chopped kale 1/2 cup mixed herbs (dills, chives, parsley, etc) 1/2 cup collagen peptides ( i use ) 1/2 cup cottage cheese 3/4 cup almond flour 1/4 cup coconut flour (can sub 3/4 more almond flour) ½ tsp baking powder ½ cup shredded cheese (like gruyere or mild cheddar) salt and pepper to taste preheat oven to 375°f and line a baking sheet with parchment paper. heat a skillet over medium high heat. add 1/2 tablespoon avocado oil, onions, garlic and kale . let cook until onions are softened and kale has wilted. stir occasionally. whisk eggs until smooth and season with salt and pepper. add in the cottage cheese and kale mixture, almond flour, coconut flour and baking powder. stir until a thick batter forms. let sit for about 5 minutes. scoop the batter onto the baking sheet (about 1/4 cup per biscuit). top with a sprinkle o
recipes.caption:
HIGH PROTEIN EGG BISCUITS // a Garlic & Herb version of my viral make-ahead breakfast that’s supports balanced hormones and blood sugar. @nourishedbynutrition 

By supporting blood sugar balance you’re supporting insulin and glucagon which in turn supports cortisol and every sex hormone 🤓 when blood sugar is unstable (spikes and crashes), cortisol is released to help stabilize it. Chronically elevated cortisol levels can disrupt the hypothalamic-pituitary-gonadal (HPG) axis, suppressing the production of sex hormones like estrogen, progesterone, and testosterone.

Garlic & Herb High-Protein Egg Biscuits

Ingredients:
6 large eggs
1/2 cup diced yellow onion
1 tbsp minced garlic
2 cups chopped kale
1/2 cup mixed herbs (dills, chives, parsley, etc)
1/2 cup collagen peptides ( I use @greatlakeswellness)
1/2 cup cottage cheese
3/4 cup almond flour
1/4 cup coconut flour (can sub 3/4 more almond flour)
½ tsp baking powder
½ cup shredded cheese (like gruyere or mild cheddar) 
Salt and pepper to taste

Preheat oven to 375°F and line a baking sheet with parchment paper.

Heat a skillet over medium high heat. Add 1/2 tablespoon avocado oil, onions, garlic and kale . Let cook until onions are softened and kale has wilted. Stir occasionally.

Whisk eggs until smooth and season with salt and pepper.
Add in the cottage cheese and kale mixture, almond flour, coconut flour and baking powder. Stir until a thick batter forms. Let sit for about 5 minutes.

Scoop the batter onto the baking sheet (about 1/4 cup per biscuit). Top with a sprinkle of shredded cheese.

Bake for 18-25 minutes, until golden and firm to the touch. Storage in the fridge for 4-5 days. Reheat of desired.

recipes.title: Ramen Eggs
recipes.author: michaeltchao
recipes.text: ramen eggs [👇🏼2x recipe] one of my favourite ways to prepare eggs! marinade: -1 part tamari -1 part mirin -3 parts water method: -pierce eggs -boil eggs for 6:30 min -once eggs are cooked, add to ice/cold water bath -peel eggs, and add to marinade and refrigerate **** gyudon (beef bowl) ingredients: - 2 small onions sliced (north to south) - 300g sliced beef - 3 tbsp mirin - 3 tbsp sake - 3 tbsp low sodium - 1.5 tsp honey - 3/4 cup dashi (i used hondashi - instant dashi) - 0.5 tsp grated ginger garnish with: - scallions - benishoga (pickled ginger) - pickled onions - furikake - togarashi - sesame seeds 1. slice onions, prep scallions 2. mix sauce ingredients and whisk well, mirin, sake, tamari, honey, dashi 3. add onions to a pot, add sauce mixture, and bring to a simmer - around medium heat 4. simmer onions for about 3-4 minutes, or until onions start to go translucent 5. add sliced beef, simmer until cooked through (~1 min) 6. serve over rice, garnish with optional toppings.
recipes.caption:
RAMEN EGGS [👇🏼2x RECIPE]

One of my favourite ways to prepare eggs! 

Marinade:
-1 part @sanjtamari tamari 
-1 part mirin
-3 parts water

Method:
-pierce eggs
-boil eggs for 6:30 min
-once eggs are cooked, add to ice/cold water bath
-peel eggs, and add to marinade and refrigerate 

****

GYUDON (BEEF BOWL)

Ingredients:
- 2 small onions sliced (north to south)
- 300g sliced beef
- 3 tbsp mirin
- 3 tbsp sake
- 3 tbsp low sodium @sanjtamari
- 1.5 tsp honey
- 3/4 cup dashi (I used hondashi - instant dashi)
- 0.5 tsp grated ginger

Garnish with:
- Scallions
- Benishoga (pickled ginger)
- Pickled Onions
- furikake
- togarashi
- sesame seeds

1. Slice onions, prep scallions
2. Mix sauce ingredients and whisk well, mirin, sake, tamari, honey, dashi
3. Add onions to a pot, add sauce mixture, and bring to a simmer - around medium heat
4. simmer onions for about 3-4 minutes, or until onions start to go translucent
5. Add sliced beef, simmer until cooked through (~1 min)
6. Serve over rice, garnish with optional toppings.

recipes.text: healthy & nutritious weightloss snack - almond chocolate bars . ingredients 1 cup almonds 2 cups foxnuts 2 tbsp unsweetened cocoa powder 10 pitted mejdool dates 20 gm 100% dark chocolate chips for mixture 40 gm 70% dark chocolate chips for top layer 1 tsp coconut oil 3 finely chopped almonds for garnishing method: 1. in a bowl, add pitted dates & soak them in hot water for 30 min. after that, add them to blender & make a paste of dates. 2. in a pan, roast almonds for 6-8 min & then add foxnuts to it. roast until foxnuts turn crispy. 3. let them cool down & and transfer into a blender jar and blend till it makes a fine powder. 4. added it in a mixing bowl along with cocoa powder, chocolate chips, and date paste. mix everything together to make dough, it should make firm bites. 5. either you can roll them into balls or you can take a silicone mould like i am using to make the bars or you can transfer the entire material on a parchment paper on a baking sheet and press it down to make a smooth texture from the top layer. 6. freeze it for 45 minutes to an hour and let it set. then, take 40 g of chocolate chips in a bowl along with coconut oil and microwave it for one minute with 30 second interval. it should be silky, smooth, melted chocolate. 7. now take out the bites from the freezer and dipping into the melted chocolate and keep it to let it set, garnish it with some chopped almonds on the top. note: if you want to make these bites high protein & want to use it as post workout
recipes.caption:
Healthy & Nutritious Weightloss Snack - Almond Chocolate Bars 
.
Ingredients 
1 cup almonds 
2 cups foxnuts 
2 tbsp unsweetened cocoa powder 
10 pitted Mejdool dates 
20 gm 100% dark chocolate chips for mixture
40 gm 70% dark chocolate chips for top layer
1 tsp coconut oil 
3 finely chopped Almonds for garnishing 

Method: 
1. In a bowl, add pitted dates & soak them in hot water for 30 min. After that, add them to blender & make a paste of dates.
2. In a pan, roast almonds for 6-8 min & then add foxnuts to it. Roast until foxnuts turn crispy. 
3. Let them cool down & and transfer into a blender jar and blend till it makes a fine powder.
4. Added it in a mixing bowl along with cocoa powder, chocolate chips, and date paste. Mix everything together to make dough, It should make firm bites.
5. Either you can roll them into balls or you can take a silicone mould like I am using to make the bars or you can transfer the entire material on a parchment paper on a baking sheet and press it down to make a smooth texture from the top layer. 
6. Freeze it for 45 minutes to an hour and let it set. Then, take 40 g of chocolate chips in a bowl along with coconut oil and microwave it for one minute with 30 second interval. It should be silky, smooth, melted chocolate.
7. Now take out the bites from the freezer and dipping into the melted chocolate and keep it to let it set, garnish it with some chopped almonds on the top. 
Note: if you want to make these bites high protein & want to use it as post workout fuel then add two scoops of vanilla protein in this material

recipes.title: Piri Piri Masala
recipes.author: we_nourish
recipes.text: ✨ homemade piri piri masala ✨ my neighbour recently asked for some piri piri masala last-minute for her chicken popcorns. i sent her this recipe, and she messaged me back saying it tasted just like the real thing! that’s when i knew i had to share it with you too 🧂❤️ also i made it for myself the same day to serve it with the potato wedges i had made for my guests🥰 🌿no store-bought packet can beat this fiery, flavour-packed seasoning made straight from your kitchen staples. 🌿i made this for guests and tossed it over air-fried red potato wedges – which, by the way, i always pre-boil (2 whistles), cut, and store in the fridge. once they cool and dry a bit, they crisp up beautifully in the air fryer. bonus: cooling starches like potatoes or rice before eating helps manage blood glucose spikes too – a smart little hack that your gut (and glucose levels) will thank you for. 💡 🌿if you want a collection of all my healthy snacks and seasonings, comment “snacks” and you’ll get a pdf✨ here’s what i used: 🌿2 tsp spicy red chilli powder 🌿2 tsp garlic powder 🌿2 tsp onion powder 🌿2 tsp amchur 🌿1 tsp black pepper (whole or powdered) 🌿2 tsp oregano (or mixed italian herbs) 🌿2 tsp desi khaand (or any sugar) 🌿2 tsp salt 🌿2 tbsp kashmiri red chilli powder just grind everything together and store in an airtight jar. your homemade piri piri masala is ready! 🔥 this seasoning is super versatile – sprinkle it on popcorn, fries, wedges, tofu, makhana, or literally anything that needs a kick💥 🥰
recipes.caption:
✨ Homemade Piri Piri Masala ✨ My neighbour recently asked for some piri piri masala last-minute for her chicken popcorns. I sent her this recipe, and she messaged me back saying it tasted just like the real thing! That’s when I knew I had to share it with you too 🧂❤️ Also I made it for myself the same day to serve it with the potato wedges I had made for my guests🥰

🌿No store-bought packet can beat this fiery, flavour-packed seasoning made straight from your kitchen staples. 

🌿I made this for guests and tossed it over air-fried red potato wedges – which, by the way, I always pre-boil (2 whistles), cut, and store in the fridge. Once they cool and dry a bit, they crisp up beautifully in the air fryer. Bonus: cooling starches like potatoes or rice before eating helps manage blood glucose spikes too – a smart little hack that your gut (and glucose levels) will thank you for. 💡

🌿if you want a collection of all my healthy snacks and seasonings, comment “snacks” and you’ll get a pdf✨

Here’s what I used:
🌿2 tsp spicy red chilli powder
🌿2 tsp garlic powder
🌿2 tsp onion powder
🌿2 tsp amchur
🌿1 tsp black pepper (whole or powdered)
🌿2 tsp oregano (or mixed Italian herbs)
🌿2 tsp desi khaand (or any sugar)
🌿2 tsp salt
🌿2 tbsp Kashmiri red chilli powder

Just grind everything together and store in an airtight jar. Your homemade piri piri masala is ready! 🔥

This seasoning is super versatile – sprinkle it on popcorn, fries, wedges, tofu, makhana, or literally anything that needs a kick💥

Recipe ⬇️ (~150 Cals per slice)

🌸Ingredients
200g ripe banana (about 2 medium, mashed)
120–130g blended paste (from ~8–10 dates + 4–5 anjeer soaked in hot water and blended)
50g ghee, melted
100ml buttermilk (75g curd + 25ml water)
1 tsp lemon juice

65g whole wheat flour

½ tsp cinnamon powder
