✨ Pour into tin, smooth the top.
✨ Bake at 180°C for 35–40 mins. Check at 35 with a toothpick.
✨ Cool fully before slicing — makes 12 slices.

recipes.recipe_method: Pulse the sweet corn kernels, garlic cloves, green chilies, and coriander leaves in a grinder into a coarse mixture. recipes.text: palak besan ki sabzi 🥬 spinach but make it fun! 🌿✨ palak besan ki sabzi – 10 minutes ⏳, zero fuss 🙌, full desi comfort 🥰! its an easy recipe that makes every bite wholesome and cozy 🤗. pair it with hot rotis 🫓, and it’s basically home on a plate! 🍽️ recipe: - start by chopping 100g spinach finely - then heat 1 tbsp oil in a pan, with 1 tsp jeera, 3 garlic finely chopped, 2 green chillies finely chopped, 1 medium onion & cook - then add 2 kashmiri red chillies, & cook. then add 1 tbsp besan & cook well now add in the spinach let it wilt & cook once done add 1 tsp salt, 1 tsp red chilli powder, 1/2 tsp amchoor, 1/4 tsp haldi & mix well - serve hot & enjoy! recipes.title: Orange Pani Puri
recipes.author: aruna_vijay_masterchef
recipes.text: orange pani puri i don’t know anyone who can say no to pani puri. i’ve tried many varieties, but i think my new favorite is the orange pani puri. it’s sweet, spicy, and has a perfect balance of flavors. the burst of citrus is truly unmissable! you should definitely give it a try. orange pani puri recipe - ingredients: - orange juice - 2 cup - chilled water - 1 cup - black salt - 1 tsp - salt - to taste - cumin powder - 1 tsp - jaljeera powder - 1 tsp - chaat masala - 1 tsp - lemon juice - 1/2 lemon - green chilli paste - 1 tsp - tamarind chutney - 1 tsp - mint leaves - handful - boondi - 2 tbsp - soda water / 7 up - 1 cup method: 1. *extract orange juice*: wash and extract the juice from the oranges. 2. *mix the pani*: add all the ingredients, one by one, to the orange juice and mix well. 3. *serve*: serve the orange pani puri chilled, along with crispy puris and spicy aloo filling. tips: 1. *adjust seasoning*: adjust the seasoning according to your taste preferences. 2. *orange juice*: add orange juice according to your desired level of sweetness and flavor. 3. *chill before serving*: serve the orange pani puri chilled to enhance the flavors and refreshment. enjoy your refreshing orange pani puri! recipes.caption:
Orange pani puri 

I don’t know anyone who can say no to pani puri. I’ve tried many varieties, but I think my new favorite is the orange pani puri. It’s sweet, spicy, and has a perfect balance of flavors. The burst of citrus is truly unmissable! You should definitely give it a try.

Orange Pani Puri Recipe -

Ingredients:
- Orange juice - 2 cup
- Chilled Water - 1 cup
- Black salt - 1 tsp
- Salt - to taste
- Cumin powder - 1 tsp
- Jaljeera powder - 1 tsp
- Chaat masala - 1 tsp
- Lemon juice - 1/2 lemon
- Green chilli paste - 1 tsp
- Tamarind chutney - 1 tsp
- Mint leaves - handful
- Boondi - 2 tbsp
- Soda water / 7 up - 1 cup

Method:
1. *Extract Orange Juice*: Wash and extract the juice from the oranges.
2. *Mix the Pani*: Add all the ingredients, one by one, to the orange juice and mix well.
3. *Serve*: Serve the Orange Pani Puri chilled, along with crispy puris and spicy aloo filling.

Tips:
1. *Adjust Seasoning*: Adjust the seasoning according to your taste preferences.
2. *Orange Juice*: Add orange juice according to your desired level of sweetness and flavor.
3. *Chill Before Serving*: Serve the Orange Pani Puri chilled to enhance the flavors and refreshment.

Enjoy your refreshing Orange Pani Puri!

recipes.recipe_method: Cook the garlic cloves with the lemon rinds and olive oil in a small pot until golden brown and tender. recipes.title: Pumpkin Halwa
recipes.author: rumanahaaris
recipes.text: if you can scroll instagram, you can make this. it's that easy. recipe🎃 ingredients: – 400g pumpkin – 200g cottage cheese or paneer – 1 cup milk of choice – 1 tbsp ghee – cardamom & kesar (optional but highly recommended) – sweetener of choice (i used erythritol/monkfruit/stevia) instructions: scoop out the inside of the pumpkin. save the shell cus that’s your cute edible bowl 😌 blend pumpkin, paneer, sweetener and milk until smooth. heat ghee in a pan. add the blended mix. add cardamom, kesar, and extra sweetener if needed. keep stirring till it thickens into halwa texture. once cooled, pour it back into the pumpkin shell and chill in the fridge for 2+ hours. serve cold. resist the urge to eat it hot and burn your mouth 😂
recipes.caption:
If you can scroll Instagram, you can make this. It's that easy.

RECIPE🎃

Ingredients:
– 400g pumpkin 
– 200g cottage cheese or paneer
– 1 cup milk of choice
– 1 tbsp ghee
– Cardamom & kesar (optional but highly recommended)
– Sweetener of choice (I used Erythritol/Monkfruit/stevia)

Instructions:

Scoop out the inside of the pumpkin. Save the shell cus that’s your cute edible bowl 😌

Blend pumpkin, paneer, sweetener and milk until smooth.

Heat ghee in a pan. Add the blended mix.

Add cardamom, kesar, and extra sweetener if needed. Keep stirring till it thickens into halwa texture.

Once cooled, pour it back into the pumpkin shell and chill in the fridge for 2+ hours.

Serve cold. Resist the urge to eat it hot and burn your mouth 😂

recipes.title: Chilli Oil Rice Paper Noodles
recipes.author: chefchinuvaze
recipes.text: 2 min chilli oil rice paper noodles have you ever been to ? not only do they have the best dimsum in the world, their hand pulled noodles are stuff of legend! so how about a copycat version that took me literally one second, ok fine, 5 minutes to make. who knew that if you cut rice paper into strips and soaked them very briefly in hot water and make a super fast chilli oil (with added good fat cashew butter), it becomes the silkiest, most delicious, easiest noodle dish! and if you haven’t been to dintaifung , it’s all over asia & dubai, please go eat there! 2 min chilli oil rice paper noodles 4-8 rice paper hot water chilli oil 1 tbsp chopped garlic 1 tsp gochujang / chilli flakes 1 tbsp sesame 1 tbsp cashew butter/ peanut butter/ tahini/ coconut milk 1 tbsp sugar (optional) 1 tbsp light soya sauce 4 tbsp hot vegetable oil method 1. soak- cut rice paper into strips and soaked in warm water for 2 min 2. chilli oil- put all chilli oil ingredients in a heatproof bowl, heat oil to smoking point, pour on top of ingredients and mix. 3. mix- add soaked noodles into the chilli oil mix. top with spring onions & sesame & yenjoy!
recipes.caption:
2 MIN CHILLI OIL RICE PAPER NOODLES 

Have you ever been to @dintaifungsg ? Not only do they have the BEST DIMSUM in the world, their hand pulled noodles are stuff of LEGEND!
So how about a copycat version that took me literally one second, ok fine, 5 minutes to make.
Who knew that if you cut rice paper into strips and soaked them very briefly in hot water and make a super fast chilli oil (with added good fat cashew butter), it becomes the silkiest, most delicious, easiest noodle dish!

And if you haven’t been to dintaifung , it’s all over Asia & Dubai, please go eat there!

2 MIN CHILLI OIL RICE PAPER NOODLES 

4-8 rice paper 
Hot water

Chilli Oil
1 tbsp chopped garlic
1 tsp gochujang / chilli flakes
1 tbsp sesame 
1 tbsp cashew butter/ peanut butter/ tahini/ coconut milk
1 tbsp sugar (optional)
1 tbsp light soya sauce
4 tbsp hot vegetable oil

METHOD
1. SOAK- cut rice paper into strips and soaked in warm water for 2 min
2. CHILLI OIL- Put all chilli oil ingredients in a heatproof bowl, heat oil to smoking point, pour on top of ingredients and mix.
3. MIX- add soaked noodles into the chilli oil mix. Top with spring onions & sesame & YENJOY!

recipes.title: Beetroot Dumplings
recipes.author: aruna_vijay_masterchef
recipes.text: beetroot dumpling when you hear ‘dumplings,’ i bet you’re thinking about momos, dim sums—those steamy delights. imagine a dumpling that’s flat, cold, and made of… beetroot. yup, beetroot! the first time i tried it, i couldn’t believe i was eating a simple slice of beetroot stuffed with something magical. and it tasted so, so good. seriously, it’s one of those ‘i can’t believe this is beetroot’ moments. it’s light, refreshing, and definitely worth a try!” beetroot dumplings recipe - ingredients - beetroot - 1 big water - 1.5 cup sugar - 2.5 tbsp for assembling - basil pesto orange segments crumbled paneer seasoned with salt and pepper chopped walnuts method - 1. make sure your buy some large beets, peel and slice them into thin roundels using a mandolin. 2. in a saucepan add water and sugar and let it come to a boil then add in the sliced beetroot into the saucepan for few minutes, until they get soft and then strain it out 3. once done , dry them using a kitchen towel for assembling - take a beetroot , spread pesto , orange , paneer , chopped walnuts and seal it and it’s ready [ serve these cold ] garnish it with basil leaves, chopped walnuts and enjoy ! recipes.caption:
Beetroot dumpling 

When you hear ‘dumplings,’ I bet you’re thinking about momos, dim sums—those steamy delights. 

Imagine a dumpling that’s flat, cold, and made of… beetroot. Yup, beetroot! The first time I tried it, I couldn’t believe I was eating a simple slice of beetroot stuffed with something magical. And it tasted so, so good. Seriously, it’s one of those ‘I can’t believe this is beetroot’ moments. It’s light, refreshing, and definitely worth a try!”

Beetroot Dumplings Recipe - 

Ingredients - 
Beetroot - 1 big 
Water - 1.5 cup
Sugar - 2.5 tbsp

For assembling - 
Basil Pesto 
Orange segments 
Crumbled paneer seasoned with salt and pepper 
Chopped walnuts 

Method - 
1. Make sure your buy some large beets, peel and slice them into thin roundels using a mandolin. 
2. In a saucepan add water and sugar and let it come to a boil 
Then add in the sliced beetroot into the saucepan for few minutes, until they get soft and then strain it out 
3. Once done , dry them using a kitchen towel 

For assembling - 
Take a beetroot , spread  pesto , orange , paneer , chopped walnuts and seal it and it’s ready [ SERVE THESE COLD ]
Garnish it with basil leaves, chopped walnuts and enjoy !

recipes.title: Pesto Sauce
recipes.author: chefmarcoit
recipes.text: pesto sauce 🌿 from scratch this is one of the most common pasta sauces in italy. unfortunately convenience is conquering italy too, even there most of the people are buying premade pesto. making it from scratch is gonna give benefits to your health (every single ingredient is nutrients-packed) but mostly a way better flavor. for the best pesto you ever had is essential using a mortar and pestle. using a food processor works just fine, i have a video doing it on my profile, back in 2024. serving 2: 300g pasta ~1 garlic clove ~100g basil leaves ~70g parmigiano (or half and half with pecorino sardo) ~40g nuts ~salt to taste ~a bunch of evoo all the quantities are very imprecise. use your taste while doing it to find the perfect balance. the perfect balance means what you like the best. ❗️careful with the garlic,you can easily end up with a very garlicky sauce. start by putting less than you expect. ❗️wash basil leaves very well. remove all the stems and make sure they’re well dried before using them. ❗️never ever heat up pesto on a pan. how to store: add olive oil to fully cover the sauce. store it in the fridge up to 4 days and in the freezer for months. as always check appearance and smell before eating. about the nuts 🌰 🥜 pine nuts are considered more traditional. pretty much every type of nut work, use your favorite or the most convenient. 🍝 every pasta shape works with pesto. the most traditional are “trofie” and “trenette”.
recipes.caption:
Pesto sauce 🌿 from scratch 

This is one of the most common pasta sauces in Italy. Unfortunately convenience is conquering Italy too, even there most of the people are buying premade pesto. 

Making it from scratch is gonna give  benefits to your health (every single ingredient is nutrients-packed) but mostly a WAY better flavor. 

For the best pesto you ever had is essential using a mortar and pestle.
Using a food processor works just fine, I have a video doing it on my profile, back in 2024.

Serving 2: 
300g Pasta 
~1 garlic clove 
~100g Basil leaves 
~70g parmigiano (or half and half with Pecorino Sardo)
~40g nuts 
~Salt to taste 
~A bunch of EVOO
All the quantities are very imprecise. 
Use your taste while doing it to find the perfect balance. 
The perfect balance means what you like the best.

❗️Careful with the garlic,you can easily end up with a very garlicky sauce. Start by putting less than you expect.
❗️Wash basil leaves very well. Remove all the stems and make sure they’re well dried before using them.
❗️Never ever heat up pesto on a pan. 

How to store:

Add olive oil to fully cover the sauce.
Store it in the fridge up to 4 days and in the freezer for months. 
As always check appearance and smell before eating. 

About the nuts 🌰 🥜
Pine nuts are CONSIDERED more traditional.
Pretty much every type of nut work, use your favorite or the most convenient. 

🍝 Every pasta shape works with pesto. 
The most traditional are “Trofie” and “Trenette”.

recipes.caption:
Lately, I’ve been on a little journey to revive and share some of the childhood recipes I grew up eating — dishes filled with love, simplicity, and comfort. One such recipe is Ukad, a humble yet delicious dish my mom and aaji used to make for us when we were little.

This recipe is super quick (under 10 minutes!) and needs only basic pantry ingredients. But don’t let its simplicity fool you — the flavor is just chef’s kiss 💛

📝 Here’s how my mom and aaji made it:

🌿 Ingredients:

Rice flour
Garlic & green chilies
Curd (optional)
Mustard seeds
Jeera (cumin)
Curry leaves
Turmeric & hing
Salt to taste
Oil

– Start by mincing garlic and green chilies with some salt.
– In a bowl, add 1 cup rice flour, a pinch of salt, and a spoon of curd (optional, but gives a lovely tang). Mix this into a watery slurry.
– Heat oil in a kadhai and add mustard seeds, jeera, the garlic-chili paste, curry leaves, turmeric, and hing. Let it all sizzle and come together.
– Now add the slurry to the pan. Keep stirring constantly on medium flame — don’t stop, or it will curdle quickly.
– Adjust the salt if needed.
– Finally, make a simple tadka with mustard seeds and green chili in mustard oil and pour it over the Ukad just before serving.

That’s it! So simple, but sooo, sooo delicious. It brings back so many memories every time I make it.

If you’re looking for a quick, wholesome, and nostalgic dish to warm your heart (and belly), give Ukad a try.

🍲 Happy cooking and lots of love from my kitchen to yours!

(not a bhaaji/ subzi/ kofta) peel of 1 large dudhi, grated- about 1.25 cups. try to get just the thick peel and not the soft inner part. once grated, sprinkle some salt, and set it aside for 2-3 mins. this will draw out the water, which we then squeeze out. reducing the water makes for crisper chutney. save the water to use in dals/ while make roti- it does tend to darken really quickly though now, in a heavy-duty kadhai, heat 3 tbsp oil (groundnut) and temper it with 1/4 tsp mustard seeds scant 1/4 tsp cumin seeds heeng 1/8 tsp turmeric powder 1 green chili, finely chopped add 1/3 cup sesame seeds let these toast in the tempering for 2 mins, till they just about start to sputter. tip in the grated peels and combine everything well.
recipes.caption:
Dudhi peels make the crispiest chutney that adds SO much texture and flavour to everyday meals. 
Save this recipe, so that the next time you get dudhi, instead of discarding the peel, grate it and try the chutney.

This is the first recipe in the ‘1 dudhi, 3 recipes’ mini series that came about when Tai Atte was home, saw a large dudhi and rattled off everything that could be made with my favourite vegetable. 

This chutney needs just a few ingredients, and while it does need some time to make crispy wisps of the moist peel, Atte mentioned how if you set this to cook first, in a heavy-bottomed pan/ Kadhai, and let it slowly toast to crispy perfection while you cook other things. 

Here’s the recipe, try it!  And, can you guess what the second recipe is? (Not a bhaaji/ subzi/ kofta)

Peel of 1 large dudhi, grated- about 1.25 cups. Try to get just the thick peel and not the soft inner part. 
Once grated, sprinkle some salt, and set it aside for 2-3 mins. This will draw out the water, which we then squeeze out. Reducing the water makes for crisper chutney. Save the water to use in dals/ while make roti- it does tend to darken really quickly though

Now, in a heavy-duty Kadhai, heat 
3 Tbsp oil (groundnut) and temper it with 
1/4 tsp mustard seeds
Scant 1/4 tsp cumin seeds
Heeng
1/8 tsp turmeric powder
1 green chili, finely chopped

Add 1/3 cup sesame seeds
Let these toast in the tempering for 2 mins, till they just about start to sputter. 

Tip in the grated peels and combine everything well.

Let this patiently cook for 10-12 mins, stirring occasionally. 

Once the lauki peels dry out and turn crispy, add 
1/2 tsp red chili powder/ to taste
Scant 1/4 tsp sugar 
1/4 tsp amchoor powder 

Mix everything well, taste- see if you need more salt/ sugar/ red chili powder/ amchoor. 

Once cool, transfer to an airtight container. Easily stays for at least a week, without refrigeration- if it lasts that long!

recipes.text: my us visa was first rejected in june, 2011. why? because i was unmarried or jobless, i guess. my dream was to travel to la with the last batch of my savings to try my luck at the food network to pursue my dream of being a chef in the food content industry! i wanted to merge my passion for cooking and acting, together. i was shattered when this last attempt to live my dream was rejected (after having already faced multiple rejections in mumbai in 2010). after a month out of nowhere i got a call from 'foodfood' tv channel to come for a life changing audition, later i was told it was through an email i had dropped back in the year 2010 when i was struggling to be in mumbai. after my audition i was shortlisted to be on mahachallenge. life took a turn on that show, i went on to win it and i also met my idol chef sanjeev kapoor. then 9 months later - march, 2012 - i was invited to the us to represent indian cuisine and a young interviewer at the visa consulate asked "why was your visa rejected, i can't understand, also with a polite smile he told me that i didn't have to carry amy newspaper clippings to prove a point. please teach me more about indian food" he said. i wish i could explain to him that life had happened to me. if i had gone earlier to the us, who knows i might have struggled all my life. my rejection made me who i am today. this is arbhi tuk canape that i made for a demo in new york to showcase how beautiful indian cuisine is. i would not change a single thing about
recipes.caption:
My US visa was first rejected in June, 2011. Why? Because I was unmarried or jobless, I guess. My dream was to travel to LA with the last batch of my savings to try my luck at the food network to pursue my dream of being a chef in the food content industry! I wanted to merge my passion for cooking and acting, together. I was shattered when this last attempt to live my dream was rejected (after having already faced multiple rejections in Mumbai in 2010).

After a month out of nowhere I got a call from 'FoodFood' tv channel to come for a life changing audition, later I was told it was through an email I had dropped back in the year 2010 when I was struggling to be in Mumbai. After my audition I was shortlisted to be on Mahachallenge. Life took a turn on that show, I went on to win it and I also met my idol Chef Sanjeev Kapoor.

Then 9 months later - March, 2012 - I was invited to the US to represent Indian cuisine and a young interviewer at the Visa consulate asked "Why was your Visa rejected, I can't understand, also with a polite smile he told me that I didn't have to carry amy newspaper clippings to prove a point. Please teach me more about Indian food" he said. I wish I could explain to him that life had happened to me. If I had gone earlier to the US, who knows I might have struggled all my life. My rejection made me who I am today. This is Arbhi tuk canape that I made for a demo in New York to showcase how beautiful Indian cuisine is. I would not change a single thing about this journey because if you dare to dream, life will happen to you.
.
.

Boil 250g Arbi 
for 10 minutes 

Strain & set aside 

Fry them for 10 mins in low medium hot oil

Look at that 
Cool them down 
& smash them 
Fry in super hot oil 
Till GBC 

Tuk Masala
1tbsp Chili powder
1 tbsp Coriander powder
1/4tsp Haldi powder

Toss tuk and masala together 

Slice 1 onion 
1 inch Ginger, julienne 
Lemon juice to taste 
Kala namak to taste 
Mix well 

Grate 1 Cucumber 
Squeeze out the excess water 

200g Thick yogurt 
Add the cucumber 
2 Garlic cloves, grated
Coriander and Mint 
Salt, mix well.

Assemble!

recipes.text: ingredients: • 1 cup rice (soaked in buttermilk for 30 minutes or more) • salt to taste • ½ tsp jeera (cumin) powder for tempering: • 1–2 tsp ghee • ½ tsp cumin seeds • a pinch of hing (asafoetida) • 8–10 curry leaves • 1 dried red chilli • 1 green chilli (slit or chopped, as per preference) • fresh coriander leaves for garnish ⸻ method: 1. soak the rice soak rice in buttermilk for about 30 minutes. this adds a tangy, creamy flavor. 2. cook the rice cook the soaked rice with a little salt and jeera powder. you can either boil it or pressure cook for 2 whistles. 3. prepare the tempering in a small tadka pan, heat ghee. add cumin seeds, hing, curry leaves, red chilli, and green chilli. sauté until aromatic. 4. combine and serve pour the tempering over the cooked rice and mix gently. garnish with fresh coriander leaves and serve warm.

recipes.caption:
Eggless Pistachio Rose Muffins with Pistachio Crumble🌹💚

Ingredients

60g shelled pistachios (kernels)
100g caster sugar
120ml buttermilk (milk mixed with juice of half lemon)
60ml cooking oil
40g yogurt or curd
1/2tsp Pista Flavour by @ossoroflavours 
1/4tsp Moroccan Rose Flavour by @ossoroflavours 
120g all-purpose flour 
1 and 1/2tsp baking powder 
1/4tsp baking soda 
1/4tsp salt

Method:
1. Mix the lemon juice and milk, set it aside to curdle.
2. In a bowl, mix together the ground pistachios with the sugar. Mix well before adding the oil, curd and buttermilk. Mix mix mix. 
3. Add in the Moroccan Rose as well as the Pista flavour, both by @ossoroflavours . This is the actual game changer. The rose and the pistachio go so well as a flavour combination and plus, the Pista flavour really brings out the, well, Pista flavour of the cake. 10/10 recommend.
3. Now add in the flour, baking soda, baking powder and salt. Using a spatula, fold gently. 
4. Let it rest in the refrigerator while we prepare the pistachio crumble. 

Pistachio Crumble
20g shelled pistachios, chopped
1.5tbsp all purpose flour
1tbsp caster
1/2tbsp melted butter/oil

Mix them all well and you have the crumble ready. 

Assembly time
-  In a muffin tray, add the muffin liners and only fill half of them as shown in the video and add the crumble on top. This helps the muffins rise taller with that perfect muffin top. 
-  In a preheated oven, bake at 180C for about 28 minutes. 

This is definitely my new favourite muffin. Well, until I bake a new recipe😌

recipes.caption:
Chai Time Masti -2 | Jowar Jeera Biscuits 

Since many of you have been asking for tea-time snack recipes, I’m excited to continue this series! 

I recently developed this recipe, and it turned out amazing! In our family, we usually don’t have biscuits with tea, but someone recently tried jeera cookies and shared the experience. That got me thinking—why not give them a millet twist? And that’s how these Millet Jeera Biscuits came to life🫶

☕ These unsweetened, diabetic-friendly cookies are a great way to add millets to your diet. Enjoy them with tea or coffee, and the best part? They stay crispy for up to a month in an airtight container. Try them out and let me know how you like them! 🫶

Ingredients:
	•	1 cup Jowar (sorghum) flour
	•	1-2 tsp cumin seeds (jeera)
	•	¼ tsp baking soda
	•	½ tsp salt
	•	2 cardamoms, crushed
	•	4 tbsp ghee ( approx 56 ml)
	•	2 tbsp milk (approx - kneading)

Method:
In a mixing bowl, add Jowar flour, cumin seeds, baking soda, salt, and crushed cardamom. Mix well.
Add ghee and mix it into the flour until the mixture resembles a crumbly texture. When pressed together, it should hold its shape.
Gradually add milk and knead into a soft dough.
Roll the dough on a parchment paper or a clean board. Cut into desired shapes using a cookie cutter or knife.
Preheat the oven to 180°C (356°F). Place the cookies on a baking tray and bake for 12-14 minutes until golden brown.
Allow the cookies to cool completely before storing them in an airtight container. They stay fresh for up to one month.

recipes.recipe_ingredients:
1 cup (210 g) cottage cheese
1 cup + 2 tbs (125 g) flour
3 tsp baking powder
1/2 tsp salt
1 tbs olive oil
2 oz (56.7 g) baby spinach, micro chopped
1/2 cup (56 g) shredded mozzarella cheese
Egg Wash: 1 egg, lightly beaten
recipes.recipe_method:
Preheat oven to 375℉. Line a large rimmed baking sheet with parchment paper.
In a mini food processor, add in your cottage cheese and pulse until smooth.
To a large bowl, add the cottage cheese, flour, baking powder, salt, olive oil, spinach, mozzarella and mix together until combined. Use your hands to form the dough into a thick log (6 inches long). Divide the dough into 6 equal pieces. Shape the pieces into flatter circles and poke a hole in the middle with your finger. Place onto pan and brush them with egg wash. Bake for 22-25 minutes or until golden brown on top. Transfer to wire rack to let cool completely.

recipes.caption:

https://reallifenutritionist.com/blueberry-cottage-cheese-pancakes/

BLUEBERRY COTTAGE CHEESE PANCAKES: the perfect, easy, high-protein breakfast for sweet breakfast lovers. NO fancy ingredients, protein powders, or specialty flours required.

Here’s how to make them!

Serves 2

INGREDIENTS
Dry Ingredients
▢½ cup all purpose flour, spooned and leveled
▢1 tsp baking powder
▢½ tsp salt, reduce by half if your cottage cheese is particularly salty
Wet Ingredients
▢¾ cup low fat cottage cheese, I use 2%
▢2 large egg
▢½ Tbsp olive oil, or melted butter
▢½ Tbsp vanilla extract
▢1 ½ Tbsp maple syrup
▢⅔ cup blueberries, washed and thoroughly dried
For cooking
▢salted butter

INSTRUCTIONS
-To a large mixing bowl, add flour, baking powder, and salt. Whisk until combined and set aside.
-To a small blender, add all wet ingredients except blueberries. Blend until completely smooth, about 20-seconds.
-Pour wet ingredients into dry ingredients. Use a wooden spoon or spatula to gently stir until a batter forms. Then, gently stir in your blueberries. Let your batter sit for 5-minutes while your pan heats (it needs this time to thicken), but no longer than 10-minutes.
-Heat a non-stick pan to slightly below medium. Coat with a thin layer of butter. If the pan is too hot, the outsides will burn and the insides won’t cook through.
-Pour batter on to the pan, about ¼ cup per pancake, making sure they don’t touch. Cook for 3-4 minutes untouched, or until the tops have lots of bubbles and the bottoms are golden brown. Flip, and cook for a few more minutes or until cooked through. -Repeat until all batter has been used, adding more butter to the pan as needed.
-Serve immediately with maple syrup, berries, and other toppings as desired. Enjoy!

Would you try?!!

recipes.text: malai kesar pista kulfi celebrate holi with the rich and creamy goodness of malai kesar pista kulfi made in my artisan kadhai ! infused with saffron, pistachios, and festive flavors, this homemade delight is pure indulgence in every bite. a perfect treat to make your celebrations even sweeter! ✨🎨🍦 wearing serves 6 1lt milk 1/2 cup jaggery 15 cashews; boil and bring to smooth paste 1/2tsp elaichi powder 15-20 strands of kesar few drops of kesari colour 2-3tbsp chopped pista cook the milk until it reduces to almost half and forms a lot of malai. then, add all the other ingredients and cook until everything is well combined. allow this mixture to cool completely before transferring it into small glasses or kulfi molds. freeze it overnight. when ready to serve, heat a knife and insert it into the center. place the ice cream stick and press down to ensure it is tight and secure. rub the glass between your palms to slightly loosen the sides and demold. serve immediately as is or with falooda and dig innn!

recipes.caption:
I thought nothing to worry about LEAN PCOS until 
the symptoms of fatigue , mood swings , excessive body hair, hair loss became severe,  I was worried about how it’s going to affect my fertility . The doctors prescribing me birth control pills for getting periods was making me feel more sick 🤢

It’s shocking Lean PCOS is difficult to be diagnosed and is associated with : 

1. Insulin resistance
2. Higher levels of androgens or male hormones ( facial hair 😭)
3. Fatigue , Depression and anxiety 
4. Poor cholesterol levels 
5. Type 2 diabetes later in life 
6. Fertility challenge 

Now how do I manage this Lean PCOS when there is no weight to loose in the first place ? 

✅ I decided to do fitness atleast 3 days a week or more. Overweight or not movement meant more than loosing kilos and improving overall health . 

❌ strictly cut down on processed and packaged foods . That means no restaurants, no sausages, no sugary biscuits

✅ I switched to carbs like red rice which kept my blood sugar in control 

❌ no more cocoa just cacao with mild jaggery .I did binge on healthy brownies, nice desserts now and then

✅ eating lots of berries , apples, fatty fish , avocado, extra virgin olive oil , cinnamon , turmeric , spearmint in my food and having it as tea 

❌ Ignoring gut health : as much as it sounds weird , it all starts in the gut - our second brain. Eating fibre rich food and making sure my plate was always filled with half veggies . 

✅it was always clear to me when I kept myself happy with self care like going for a good body spa, doing things I love , music my hormones loved it .

It’s important to check fasting insulin level test first for lean PCOS ( not the fasting blood sugar test )

recipes.text: 🍚 plain white rice ain’t it… add some protein, fiber, texture, and taste to it💅👏😌 which one are you most interested in trying ( and are my personal favs rn)! ingredients & instructions (for both rice cooker & stovetop cooking) below!!!⬇️ 🧡bone broth rice ingredients (3-4 servings): 1.5 cups white rice 1.75 cups bone broth 💚lentil rice ingredients (3-4 servings): 1.5 cups white rice ~½ cup lentils 2 cups water 💜purple rice (with peas) ingredients (3-4 servings): 1.5 cups white rice (short-grain or medium-grain) 2 tablespoons black rice (short-grain black glutinous rice) handful of fresh/frozen green peas 1.75 cups water 🍚cooking the rice (rice cooker vs. stovetop) rice cooker: rinse & transfer the rice and water/bone broth to your rice cooker and cook on the white rice/glutinous rice setting. stovetop: add the rice and water/bone broth to a pot. bring it to a boil over medium-high heat, then reduce the heat to low, cover, and simmer for 15 minutes. once cooked, let the rice sit with the lid on (heat turned off) for 10 minutes to finish steaming. • • • • • •
recipes.caption:
🍚 Plain white rice ain’t it… add some protein, fiber, texture, and taste to it💅👏😌

Which one are you most interested in trying (#1 and #3 are my personal favs rn)! Ingredients & instructions (for both rice cooker & stovetop cooking) below!!!⬇️ 

🧡Bone Broth Rice
Ingredients (3-4 servings):
1.5 cups white rice
1.75 cups bone broth

💚Lentil Rice
Ingredients (3-4 servings):
1.5 cups white rice
~½ cup lentils
2 cups water

💜Purple Rice (with peas)
Ingredients (3-4 servings):
1.5 cups white rice (short-grain or medium-grain)
2 tablespoons black rice (short-grain black glutinous rice)
Handful of fresh/frozen green peas
1.75 cups water

🍚Cooking the Rice (rice cooker vs. stovetop)

Rice Cooker: Rinse & transfer the rice and water/bone broth to your rice cooker and cook on the white rice/glutinous rice setting.

Stovetop: Add the rice and water/bone broth to a pot. Bring it to a boil over medium-high heat, then reduce the heat to low, cover, and simmer for 15 minutes. Once cooked, let the rice sit with the lid on (heat turned off) for 10 minutes to finish steaming.

recipes.title: Date Nut Almond Cake
recipes.author: dainty_bite
recipes.text: this is one of my favorite healthy cakes. dates, nuts and almond flour, it’s satisfying, moist and very good for you. you will need: 2 cups almond flour 2 tsp baking powder 3/4 cup date paste/ almost 2 cupswhole dates 3 extra large eggs 65 g each 1/2 cup butter 3/4 tsp cinnamon 1 tsp vanilla extract 3/4 cup chopped walnuts plus more for decoration. preparation: soak 2 cups of dates in hot water for and hour. peel, remove the pits. save 1 tbsp of the soaking water and add to the food processor. process finely and set aside. in a clean bowl and using a hand whisk mix the eggs and dates, flavor with the cinnamon and vanilla extract, add the very soft butter, mix well then add the flour and baking powder. bake inside a well greased 8 or 9 inch pan. bake 30 minutes at 350 degrees f or until a toothpick inserted comes out clean, enjoy this warm satisfying, healthy cake. . .
recipes.caption:
This is one of my favorite healthy cakes. 
Dates, nuts and almond flour, it’s satisfying, moist and very good for you.
You will need:
2 cups almond flour 
2 tsp baking powder 
3/4 cup date paste/ almost 2 cupswhole dates
3 extra large eggs 65 g each 
1/2 cup butter 
3/4 tsp cinnamon 
1 tsp vanilla extract 
3/4 cup chopped walnuts plus more for decoration.

Preparation:
Soak 2 cups of dates in hot water for and hour. Peel, remove the pits.
Save 1 tbsp of the soaking water and add to the food processor. Process finely and set aside.
In a clean bowl and using a hand whisk mix the eggs and dates, flavor with the cinnamon and vanilla extract, add the very soft butter, mix well then add the flour and baking powder. Bake inside a well greased 8 or 9 inch pan. Bake 30 minutes at 350 degrees F or until a toothpick inserted comes out clean, enjoy this warm satisfying, healthy cake.

recipes.recipe_method:

recipes.title: Lentil Coconut Curry
recipes.author: minaelleskitchen.ca
recipes.text: 20-min lentil coconut curry this cozy lentil coconut curry, that i love serving with a batch of homemade naan, comes together in about 20 mins and makes a perfect weeknight meal 🧡 also great for meal prep, get the recipe below! ingredients (serves 2) 1 small-medium onion 1 tbsp olive oil for frying 3 cloves of garlic 1 red bell pepper 1 can lentils (19 fl oz) 1 can coconut milk (light or full-fat, 13.5 fl oz) 1 tbsp tomato paste 1 tsp curry powder 1/2 tsp cumin powder 1/2 tsp garlic powder 1/2 tsp turmeric powder pinch of salt and pepper 1-2 cups kale or spinach 1/4 cup chopped cilantro rice or naan method 1. if serving with rice, cook rice according to package directions. 2. dice an onion and fry over medium heat with olive oil, stirring occasionally. 3. peel and mince the garlic and add it to the pot, then dice the pepper and add it to the garlic and onions, continuing to stir. 4. drain and rinse the can of lentils. 5. add lentils, spices (curry, cumin, turmeric, garlic powder, salt and pepper), tomato paste, and coconut milk. mix well then reduce the heat to medium-low and let simmer for about 10-15 minutes until the curry thickens. 6. wash your greens. if using kale, tear off the stem then chop into small pieces, or if using spinach, roughly chop into smaller pieces. mix into the curry along with half of the cilantro, then remove the pot from heat after 2 minutes. 7. serve over rice or with homemade naan, garnish with the remaining cilantro, and enjoy!
recipes.caption:
20-min lentil coconut curry

This cozy lentil coconut curry, that I love serving with a batch of homemade naan, comes together in about 20 mins and makes a perfect weeknight meal 🧡 also great for meal prep, get the recipe below!

INGREDIENTS (serves 2)
1 small-medium onion
1 tbsp olive oil for frying
3 cloves of garlic
1 red bell pepper
1 can lentils (19 fl oz)
1 can coconut milk (light or full-fat, 13.5 fl oz)
1 tbsp tomato paste
1 tsp curry powder
1/2 tsp cumin powder
1/2 tsp garlic powder
1/2 tsp turmeric powder
Pinch of salt and pepper
1-2 cups kale or spinach
1/4 cup chopped cilantro
Rice or naan

METHOD
1. If serving with rice, cook rice according to package directions.
2. Dice an onion and fry over medium heat with olive oil, stirring occasionally.
3. Peel and mince the garlic and add it to the pot, then dice the pepper and add it to the garlic and onions, continuing to stir.
4. Drain and rinse the can of lentils.
5. Add lentils, spices (curry, cumin, turmeric, garlic powder, salt and pepper), tomato paste, and coconut milk. Mix well then reduce the heat to medium-low and let simmer for about 10-15 minutes until the curry thickens.
6. Wash your greens. If using kale, tear off the stem then chop into small pieces, or if using spinach, roughly chop into smaller pieces. Mix into the curry along with half of the cilantro, then remove the pot from heat after 2 minutes.
7. Serve over rice or with homemade naan, garnish with the remaining cilantro, and enjoy!

recipes.title: Spicy Egg Roast
recipes.author: anjalee.menon
recipes.text: eggs but make it spicy 😮‍💨 here’s how i made it: heat a generous pool of coconut oil (because flavour, my friend), toss in roughy crushed ginger (half an inch), garlic (6-8 cloves or more!), a tsp of fennel seeds, 2 slit green chillies, and a tsp of peppercorns. let them sizzle. next, onions—four big ones, sliced thin. patience is key here. you want them brown, caramelized, almost weeping with joy. add salt, curry leaves, and give it a good stir. kashmiri chilli powder 1 tablespoon, turmeric 1 tspn, coriander powder 1 tablespoon, and half a tspn garam masala. feeling extra? throw in tablespoon of eastern chicken masala—yes, even though it’s egg roast. trust me. in goes a chopped tomato. let it melt into the masala. splash in some hot water and let it all simmer into a thick gravy. finally, your boiled eggs. slice them slightly so they soak up the masala, then let them roast till they get that glorious coat of spice. taste, adjust salt, maybe a sneaky pinch of sugar, and boom—you’ve cracked the code to the perfect kerala egg roast. serve with appam, parotta, or rice ♥️ until next time i make something delicious, xx . .

finally, your boiled eggs. slice them slightly so they soak up the masala, then let them roast till they get that glorious coat of spice.

taste, adjust salt, maybe a sneaky pinch of sugar, and boom—you’ve cracked the code to the perfect kerala egg roast.

recipes.caption:
What’s on your  menu today ?!

I needed something comforting like this Sabudana ni Khichdi after a holiday weekend !

Ingredients:

1.5 cups Dry Sabudana 
2 Thai green chilis, finely diced
4 tbsp oil
6 Curry Leaves
1 tsp cumin seeds
1 potato, diced small (leave the diced potato in a bowl of water until ready to use to prevent browning- and then drain when ready)
1 tsp chili powder
2 tsp sugar
2 tsp salt
1/2 lemon juiced
2 tbsp finely chopped cilantro
1/4 tsp turmeric powder

DIRECTIONS:

Rinse the sabudana until water runs clear. Then soak in water in a large bowl and let sit over night covered or upto 4 hours. If you’re short on time, you can submerge the Sabudana in boiling hot water for about 30 minutes until they are soft when squeeze between your finger tips. Drain all the water. 

In a wide skillet over medium heat the oil and add the cumin seeds and green chilis and let splutter for a few seconds. Add the curry leaves followed by the diced (and drained if you soaked them) potatoes.  Reduce the heat, Add 1 tsp of salt, stir and cover the potatoes for about 8 minutes until potatoes are fork tender. 

Next add the drained sabudana, chili powder, sugar, lemon juice and remaining salt. Stir well and continue to heat through and cook for an additional 4-5 minutes while stirring occasionally. You can cook longer at this step if you feel your sabudana are too firm or remove from heat if the sabudana are too soft. Cooking longer will give you a chewy texture. 

Add the cilantro for garnish, mix well and remove from heat. Serve hot with a big dollop of yogurt if you like !

Recipe: 
 

Pav Bataka: 
 

Ingredients: 
 

-For the Green Paste: 
 

- 1 Cup Coriander 
- ⁠1 TSP Cumin Seeds 
- ⁠1 TSP Coriander Seeds 
- ⁠4-5 Garlic Cloves 
- ⁠1 Inch Ginger 
- ⁠5 Chopped Green Chillies 
- ⁠Salt to taste 
- ⁠1 TSP Lemon Juice 
 

For Pav Bataka: 
 

- 2 TBSP Oil 
- ⁠1 TSP Mustard Seeds
- ⁠1 TSP Cumin Seeds 
- ⁠Pinch Hing 
- ⁠1 TSP Coriander Seeds 
- ⁠5-8 Curry Leaves 
- ⁠1/4 TSP Turmeric 
- ⁠Green Paste 
- ⁠1 Cup Water 
- ⁠2 Boiled Potatoes 
- ⁠Salt to taste 
- ⁠1 TSP Garam Masala 
- ⁠Coriander for garnish 
 

For Masala Pav: 
 

- 1 TBSP Butter 
- ⁠1/2 TSP Garam Masala 
- ⁠1 TSP Red Chilli Powder 
- ⁠A slice of Bread / Pav 
 

Step by step recipe: 
 

-In a mortal pestle, grind all the ingredients mentioned under green paste. 

In a pan, heat oil, add mustard seeds and cumin. Let it splatter. Add hing, coriander seeds, curry leaves and turmeric. Cook for 1-2 minutes on medium flame 
 

-Add the prepared green paste and mix it well, cook for 2-4 minutes and keep stirring the pan 
 

-Add water and mashed potatoes, cook and gently mix well until it’s all well combined. Add salt, a little sugar (optional), garam masala and mix well. Top with fresh coriander and add a dash of lemon juice. 
 

-Serve with warm and toasted masala butter bread slices.

recipes.title: Coconut Dill Poached Cod
recipes.author: bluezone.recipes
recipes.text: coconut dill poached cod 🐟🥥 recipe: * 2 cod fillets (about 6 oz each) * 1 can (14 oz) coconut milk * 1 lemon, thinly sliced * 3 tablespoons fresh dill, chopped * 4 cloves garlic, smashed * 1 teaspoon ginger, grated * salt and pepper to taste * 1-2 tablespoons olive oil * garlic chili oil for garnish * cooked jasmine rice or orzo for serving directions: * pat the cod fillets dry with a paper towel and season both sides with salt and pepper. * in a large skillet or shallow pan, heat olive oil over medium heat. add smashed garlic and grated ginger, sautéing until fragrant and slightly browned. * add about 4 slices of lemon to the base of the pan, then place the cod filets on top of the lemons. * pour in the coconut milk, add the dill, and gently stir to combine the flavors. bring the coconut milk to a gentle simmer. * let the cod simmer in the coconut milk for 8-10 minutes or until the fish is opaque and easily flakes with a fork. baste the fish with the coconut milk occasionally/as needed. * adjust the seasoning if needed. squeeze a bit of fresh lemon juice over the poached cod just before serving. * serve the poached cod over a bed of rice or orzo, spooning some of the coconut milk sauce on top. garnish with additional fresh dill and chili oil. recipe by @ legallyhealthyblonde follow for more daily creative and healthy recipes!
recipes.caption:
coconut dill poached cod 🐟🥥

RECIPE:
* 2 cod fillets (about 6 oz each)
* 1 can (14 oz) coconut milk
* 1 lemon, thinly sliced
* 3 tablespoons fresh dill, chopped
* 4 cloves garlic, smashed
* 1 teaspoon ginger, grated
* Salt and pepper to taste
* 1-2 tablespoons olive oil
* Garlic chili oil for garnish
* Cooked jasmine rice or orzo for serving

directions:

* Pat the cod fillets dry with a paper towel and season both sides with salt and pepper.
* In a large skillet or shallow pan, heat olive oil over medium heat. Add smashed garlic and grated ginger, sautéing until fragrant and slightly browned.
* Add about 4 slices of lemon to the base of the pan, then place the cod filets on top of the lemons.
* Pour in the coconut milk, add the dill, and gently stir to combine the flavors. Bring the coconut milk to a gentle simmer.
* Let the cod simmer in the coconut milk for 8-10 minutes or until the fish is opaque and easily flakes with a fork. Baste the fish with the coconut milk occasionally/as needed.
* Adjust the seasoning if needed. Squeeze a bit of fresh lemon juice over the poached cod just before serving.
* Serve the poached cod over a bed of rice or orzo, spooning some of the coconut milk sauce on top. Garnish with additional fresh dill and chili oil.

recipes.title: Chaal'er Ruti
recipes.author: bongeats
recipes.text: ✨ new video on youtube ✨ chaal'er ruti is a type of flatbread made from rice instead of wheat flour. in the fourth episode of 'pasher barir ranna' with , salma casually displays her absolute mastery of rice flour. rice flour is hard—both literally and figuratively. to turn raw rice flour into thin, translucent, pristine-white bread that remains soft even the next day is a mind-bogglingly hard task, as anyone who has worked with rice flour will attest. these breads made from rice flour are staples in bengali muslim homes. salma learnt this from her mother while growing up in west midnapore. in this episode she generously shares everything that she has learnt over the years making chaal'er ruti. chaal'er ruti can be eaten with anything that you would normally eat with rooti but it goes best with meat curries. especially in winter these rice rotis are served with a spicy duck curry. as salma mentioned, chaal'er ruti and chhola'r dal'er halwa are staples in bengali muslim households on shab-e-barat. interestingly, we found that rice roti is also common in coorg where it is called otti or akki roti. we remember having otti with their delicious coorgi pandi curry many years back!
recipes.caption:
✨ New video on YouTube ✨ Chaal'er ruti is a type of flatbread made from rice instead of wheat flour. In the fourth episode of 'Pasher Barir Ranna' with @salmathechef, Salma casually displays her absolute mastery of rice flour. Rice flour is hard—both literally and figuratively. To turn raw rice flour into thin, translucent, pristine-white bread that remains soft even the next day is a mind-bogglingly hard task, as anyone who has worked with rice flour will attest.

These breads made from rice flour are staples in Bengali Muslim homes. Salma learnt this from her mother while growing up in West Midnapore. In this episode she generously shares everything that she has learnt over the years making chaal'er ruti.

Chaal'er ruti can be eaten with anything that you would normally eat with rooti but it goes best with meat curries. Especially in winter these rice rotis are served with a spicy duck curry. As Salma mentioned, chaal'er ruti and chhola'r dal'er halwa are staples in Bengali Muslim households on Shab-e-Barat.

Interestingly, we found that rice roti is also common in Coorg where it is called otti or akki roti. We remember having otti with their delicious Coorgi pandi curry many years back!

recipes.author: salonikukreja
recipes.text: 100/10 recommend making this 15-minute focaccia sandwich! made with burrata, basil chutney, and marinated tomatoes, it’s my new go-to for a busy workday! ingredients: 1 small focaccia bread burrata basil chutney (recipe below) tomatoes marinated in salt, pepper, olive oil and balsamic vinegar chutney: 1/4th cup basil 2 cloves garlic 1/4th cup coriander 3-4 cashews- soaked in hot water 1 tbsp lime juice 2 spicy green chillies salt & pepper to taste process: - soak the cashews in hot water for 10-15 minutes - add everything to a blender - basil, coriander, garlic, cashews, lime juice, salt & pepper and blend till slightly coarse - pre heat the oven to 200 c - slice the focaccia in half , drizzle with olive oil and toast in the oven for 6-7 minutes - toss the sliced tomato in salt, pepper, extra virgin olive oil and balsamic vinegar - to assemble, start with the bread, spread the chutney, add the tomatoes & burrata - serve and enjoy!
recipes.caption:
100/10 recommend making this 15-Minute Focaccia Sandwich!  Made with burrata, basil chutney, and  marinated tomatoes, it’s my new go-to for a busy workday! 

Ingredients: 
1 small Focaccia bread 
Burrata 
Basil chutney (recipe below) 
Tomatoes marinated in salt, pepper, olive oil and balsamic vinegar 

Chutney: 
1/4th cup Basil 
2 cloves garlic 
1/4th cup coriander
3-4 cashews- soaked in hot water
1 tbsp lime juice
2 spicy green chillies 
Salt & Pepper to taste 

Process: 
- Soak the cashews in hot water for 10-15 minutes 
- Add everything to a blender - basil, coriander, garlic, cashews, lime juice, salt & pepper and blend till slightly coarse

recipes.text: recipe ⬇️ (33g p, 572 cals) ingredients : 25g soya chunks 1/2 cup peas handful of methi masalas - salt, red chilli powder, aamchur, pepper, pinch of haldi 2 tbsp onion 2 green chillies chopped 2-3 cloves of garlic crushed 1 small cup wheat flour 2 tbsp kalaunji and sesame seeds 1 tsp ghee pair with 90g greek yogurt 🌸 grind boiled soya chunks, boiled peas, methi, onion, garlic, chillies and masala in a mixer jar. 🌸in a bowl, add wheat flour and this mixture along with 1 tsp ghee 🌸you don’t need water as this mixture is already moist. if needed you may add a little more flour to knead it properly. let this dough rest for 10 mins in the fridge 🌸imp - apply oil on the rolling board and pin and also dust your roti dough with a little flour so it does not stick to the bottom. 🌸make mini theplas, garnish with the sesame and kalaunji mix and cook it on a tava 🌸once the theplas cook on both sides then apply very little ghee and its ready! ✅just like this i also reinvented our normal wheat rotis packed with 25g of protein!! comment “roti” and i will send you that recipe💝 protein theplas, healthy thepla, healthy recipe, quick recipe, easy recipes, high protein, vegetarian, vegan recipes, fat loss diet, weight loss, nutrition tips, wholesome meals

Ingredients :
25g Soya Chunks

Handful of Methi
Masalas - Salt, Red Chilli Powder, Aamchur, Pepper, Pinch of Haldi

🌸Once the theplas cook on both sides then apply very little ghee and its ready!

recipes.caption:
Can you believe this soup has 75 grams of protein?

You can easily divide this into 3-4 generous servings. For 4 super filling servings, it has 200 calories + 19g protein per serving.

*Comment COOKBOOK below and I’ll message you the link the preorder my upcoming ShredHappens cookbook!

I used cottage cheese to pack in that creamy texture and a protein boost, and added bone broth for another 20g protein. Besides protein, you can sneak in a ton of veggies.

Here is how I made it:

1️⃣ Preheat your oven to 410°F. 2️⃣ Cut 1 large butternut squash (or 2 honey nut squash like I did) in half and scoop out the seeds. Carefully score the flesh with a knife to help it cook evenly and soak up all those spices. Place it on a large baking tray. 3️⃣ Add 1 large red onion, cut into eighths, to the tray. 4️⃣ Grab 12-14 mini red peppers (or 2 red bell peppers), slice in half, remove seeds, and add to the tray. 5️⃣ Drizzle or spray 1 tbsp oil, 1 tbsp onion powder, 1 tbsp thyme, and 1 tbsp smoked paprika over the veggies. 6️⃣ Slice the top off a garlic bulb, drizzle with 1 tbsp olive oil, wrap in foil or parchment, and add to the tray. Roast everything at 410°F for 45-50 minutes. 7️⃣ Once roasted, scoop the squash away from the skin, then toss it in a blender with the roasted onion and peppers. Squeeze out the garlic from the bulb and add that in too. 8️⃣ Pour in 17 oz bone broth (chicken, veggie, or beef—your choice) and 3.5 servings of cottage cheese (around 3/4 of a tub). 9️⃣ Blend until it’s super creamy and smooth. 🔟 Serve it up hot or save for later!

For that extra touch, I topped it with 1/2 tbsp cream, a drizzle of chipotle hot sauce, red pepper flakes, and some fresh herbs like cilantro or parsley. 🌿

ENJOY!!

recipes.caption:
LOWCARB AIRFRIED SPICY STICKY CHICKEN TENDERS

I’ve lost 100+lbs eating healthier versions of my favorite foods with more protein and fewer carbs, and its things like these lowcarb, high protein chicken tenders that keep me on track. If you love chicken tenders, these are an AMAZING healthier option and taste incredible.

To keep them lowcarb, I coated these in lowcarb almond flour bread crumbs (you can use cereal, crushed pork rinds, or regular crumbs, too) and used a low sugar honey instead of honey, but regular honey works, too!

If you haven’t preordered my cookbook yet, you can always comment COOKBOOK below and I’ll send you a DM with the link!

Chicken Ingredients:
1 pound chicken tenders or cut of choice, cut into thin strips
1 cup low-carb breadcrumbs (or crushed pork rinds)
2 large eggs
1 tsp smoked paprika
Pinch of salt & pepper

Sauce Ingredients:
1/4 cup low sugar or regular honey
2 to 3 tbsp sriracha
1 tbsp rice vinegar 
1 tbsp soy sauce
1/2 tsp garlic powder 

Directions:

1.In a bowl, whisk 2 eggs. In another bowl, combine the lowcarb breadcrumbs (or crumbs) with smoked paprika, a touch of salt & black pepper.

2. Dip each chicken tender into the whisked egg, allowing any excess to drip off, then coat it with the seasoned breadcrumbs.

3. Place the breaded tenders in a single layer in the air fryer basket. Spray them lightly with avocado oil for a crispy finish. Air-fry or bake for 12 mins, flip, and airfry for another 3-5 mins until golden brown and cooked through (internal temp should reach 165F - time varies by airfryer + thickness, so it may be longer for you.

4.While the tenders are going, bring a pan to LOW heat, add 1/4 cup low sugar honey or regular honey, 2 to 3 tbsp sriracha, 1 tbsp rice vinegar, 1 tbsp soy sauce, and 1/2 tsp garlic powder. Mix well.

5. Add the sauce into a bowl and carefully dip both sides of the tenders, or you can spoon it over. Top with sesame seeds. Serve with your favorite dipping sauce. I dipped them in my homemade ranch and they were spectacular.

ENJOY!

If you make it, be sure to let me know on SHREDHAPPENS

recipes.title: Udadacha Ghuta
recipes.author: keertidacooks
recipes.text: a dal a day/ episode 4 udadacha ghuta, featuring a dal i had never used as the primary ingredient ever except for making vadas. this is a recipe from satara, where udid dal is first dry roasted, and then cooked in a spicy, herby, garlicy style that’s been an altogether new discovery for me. here’s the recipe, try it! serves 3 dry roast 1/2 cup split urad dal (with skin), and then pressure cook it with 1.5 cups of water while the dal is cooking, grind together 2-3 green chilies 6-7 cloves of garlic 7-8 curry leaves 1.5 cups of coriander leaves 1 heaping tbsp khobra grind without water/ just a tbs or so if needed now, once the dal cooks, muddle it till uniformly mashed and then, in a kadhai, temper 2 tbsp oil (groundnut) with 1/4 tsp mustard seeds heeng tip in the spiced herb paste, and sauté for 2-3 mins now add scant 1/4 tsp turmeric powder followed by the cooked mashed udid dal add water as needed- urad dal is dense, so i like the ghuta to have a looser, flow consistency also add salt let it simmer for 5-7 mins to let the flavours combine, and then serve over crushed bhakri/ hot rice.
recipes.caption:
A Dal a day/ Episode 4

Udadacha Ghuta, featuring a dal I had never used as the primary ingredient ever except for making vadas. 

This is a recipe from Satara, where udid dal is first dry roasted, and then cooked in a spicy, herby, garlicy style that’s been an altogether new discovery for me.

Here’s the recipe, try it!

Serves 3

Dry roast 1/2 cup split urad dal (with skin), and then pressure cook it with 1.5 cups of water 

While the dal is cooking, grind together
2-3 green chilies
6-7 cloves of garlic 
7-8 curry leaves
1.5 cups of coriander leaves
1 heaping Tbsp Khobra

Grind without water/ just a Tbs or so if needed

Now, once the dal cooks, muddle it till uniformly mashed and then, 
in a kadhai, temper 

2 Tbsp oil (groundnut) with 
1/4 tsp mustard seeds
Heeng

Tip in the spiced herb paste, and sauté for 2-3 mins

Now add 
Scant 1/4 tsp turmeric powder

Followed by the cooked mashed udid dal

Add water as needed- Urad dal is dense, so I like the Ghuta to have a looser, flow consistency

Also add Salt 

Let it simmer for 5-7 mins to let the flavours combine, and then serve over crushed bhakri/ hot rice.

recipes.title: Sweet Potato Brownies
recipes.author: aathirasethumadhavan
recipes.text: 115 kcal per serving 🤤 fudgy double chocolate sweet potato brownies (makes 9 large piece of roughly 100 g each - 115 kcal per piece) ingredients 1 cup cooked sweet potato (i pressure cooked mine - you can steam/bake) 3/4 cup oats (i used multigrain) 1/3 cup cocoa powder 1/3 cup chocolate chips + more for sprinkling on top (optional) 2 bananas - roughly 3/4 cup sliced 1 tsp baking soda 1 tbsp olive oil 1/2 cup skim milk 1 tsp vanilla 1 tbsp peanut butter method 1. simply blend everything together and pour into a brownie tin. 2. top off with more chocolate chips if you’d like and bake in the oven at 180 c for about 35 -40 minutes. 3. divide into 9 equal portions and enjoy it as a fudge immediately or let it cool down in the fridge for a few hours and enjoy it as a brownie. ❤️ .

recipes.title: Zucchini Poriyal
recipes.author: madrasigoingplaces
recipes.text: zucchini poriyal a simple, flavorful south indian stir-fry!! ingredients • sesame oil (good quality) • 1 tsp mustard seeds • 1 tsp gram dal • 1 small onion, finely chopped • 4-5 curry leaves • 3 green chilies, slit • 2-3 zucchinis, chopped • 1/2 tsp turmeric powder • 1 tsp chili powder or sambhar powder • 1/4 cup grated coconut • 3 tbsp cilantro, chopped steps 1. heat sesame oil in a pan. 2. add mustard seeds and gram dal; let them splutter. 3. add onion, curry leaves, chilies, and salt. sauté until onion turns translucent. 4. mix in turmeric and chili powder. cook on low flame for 2 minutes, ensuring the spices don’t burn. 5. add zucchini and sprinkle a little water (avoid excess to prevent sogginess). 6. cover and cook for 7 minutes on medium-low flame. 7. uncover, add grated coconut, and cook for 2 more minutes until moisture is absorbed. 8. garnish with cilantro and serve. enjoy it with rice, quinoa, roti, or dosa—or on its own!💕 ps - highly recommend for good quality, wood crushed oils ♥️

recipes.title: Carrot Cake Pancakes
recipes.author: momnutritionist
recipes.text: easy high protein carrot cake pancakes this easy high protein breakfast idea is so simple to make. you can meal prep the batter ahead of time and bake when ready! 3 eggs 1 cup cottage cheese 1/2 cup milk of choice 1 teaspoon vanilla extract 1/4 cup grated carrot 1 tbsp cinnamon 1/4 tsp nutmeg zest of 1 orange 1 1/4 cup all-purpose flour 1 tablespoon baking powder cooking spray or butter for greasing the pan add all the ingredients in a bowl (or blender). heat a large nonstick pan over medium heat and spray with nonstick cooking spray. using a measuring cup, pour batter into the pan. cook until the pancakes are puffed on top and golden brown on the bottom. flip the pancakes and cook on the other side until risen and cooked through. serve with greek yogurt, nut butter and maple syrup if you like a little sweetness!
recipes.caption:
Easy High Protein Carrot Cake Pancakes 

This easy high protein breakfast idea is so simple to make. You can meal prep the batter ahead of time and bake when ready!

3 eggs
1 cup cottage cheese
1/2 cup milk of choice
1 teaspoon vanilla extract
1/4 cup grated carrot
1 tbsp cinnamon 
1/4 tsp nutmeg
zest of 1 orange 
1 1/4 cup all-purpose flour
1 tablespoon baking powder
Cooking spray or butter for greasing the pan

Add all the ingredients in a bowl (or blender). Heat a large nonstick pan over medium heat and spray with nonstick cooking spray. Using a measuring cup, pour batter into the pan. Cook until the pancakes are puffed on top and golden brown on the bottom. Flip the pancakes and cook on the other side until risen and cooked through. Serve with Greek yogurt, nut butter and maple syrup if you like a little sweetness!

recipes.author: aathirasethumadhavan
recipes.text: full recipe ⬇️ been seeing this recipe everywhere so wanted to try out a modified version. thought of calling it crispy smashed pototoes with garlicky honey mustard tzatziki but my husband humbled me saying it’s a modified aloo papdi chaat. 😀 either way, tastes amazing! recipe (makes 2 servings - 249 kcal, 8g p, 6 g f, 43g c per serving) ingredients for the potatoes 2 cups large diced potatoes, boiled until soft with salt and optionally a low sodium stock cube (i used knorr) 1 tsp each of chilli flakes, italian seasoning, pepper powder and peri peri seasoning few sprays oil for the sauce 130 g (about 4-5 tbsp) of greek yoghurt 1 tbsp mayo (optional) 1 tsp mustard sauce 1 tsp honey/sugar 1/2 cup grated cucumber, water squeezed out 2 tbsp chopped spring onion chopped coriander and mint leaves to garnish (optional) drizzle of chilli oil crushed cashew/peanuts pomegranate seeds method 1. smash the cooked potatoes, spray with oil and season run a little salt and air fry/bake at 180 c for 10-12 mins (mix a few times in between) until brown and crispy. 2. toss with spice mixes and set aside. 3. mix everything together for yoghurt sauce. 4. serve the potatoes on the sauce and garnish as required. .
recipes.caption:
Full recipe ⬇️
Been seeing this recipe everywhere so wanted to try out a modified version. 
Thought of calling it Crispy Smashed Pototoes with Garlicky Honey Mustard Tzatziki but my husband humbled me saying it’s a modified aloo papdi chaat. 😀 either way, tastes Amazing!
Recipe (makes 2 servings - 249 Kcal, 8g P, 6 g F, 43g C per serving)
Ingredients 
For the potatoes 
2 cups large diced potatoes, boiled until soft with salt and optionally a low sodium stock cube (I used Knorr)
1 tsp each of chilli flakes, Italian seasoning, pepper powder and peri peri seasoning 
Few sprays oil 

For the sauce 
130 g (about 4-5 tbsp) of Greek yoghurt 
1 tbsp mayo (optional)
1 tsp mustard sauce
1 tsp honey/sugar
1/2 cup grated cucumber, water squeezed out 
2 tbsp chopped spring onion 
Chopped coriander and mint leaves

To garnish (optional) 
Drizzle of chilli oil
Crushed cashew/peanuts 
Pomegranate seeds 

Method
1. Smash the cooked potatoes, spray with oil and season run a little salt and air fry/bake at 180 C for 10-12 mins (mix a few times in between) until brown and crispy. 
2. Toss with spice mixes and set aside. 
3. Mix everything together for yoghurt sauce. 
4. Serve the potatoes on the sauce and garnish as required.

recipes.title: Ragi Seed Crackers
recipes.author: salonikukreja
recipes.text: ragi seed crackers ✨ such an easy snack to make that is crunchy, healthy, and packed with the goodness of seeds and ragi flour. pair them with your favourite dip or enjoy them on their own. i promise you’ll want to make a second batch once you try it! ingredients: 1/2 cup flax seeds 2 tbsp chia seeds 1 cup hot water 1/2 cup pumpkin seeds 1/2 cup sunflower seeds 2 tbsp white sesame 2 tbsp black sesame 3 tbsps ragi flour 1 tbsp ghee 1/2 tsp salt 1 tsp cumin 1 tsp chilli flakes 1/2 tsp pepper ghee to grease the tray to sprinkle on top: ajwain seeds, cumin powder and chaat masala process: - preheat the oven to 150 c - combine the flax seeds, chia seeds and hot water - let the mixture sit for 15-20 minutes until it thickens and gels up - in a separate bowl combine the ragi flour, ghee, cumin, chilli flakes, salt and pepper - after resting the chia and flax, add the pumpkin seeds, sesame seeds, sunflower seeds and ragi mix to the bowl and combine well until everything is mixed in - grease baking paper with ghee and place it on the tray - spread the seed mix as thin as possible with the help of a spatula and sprinkle ajwain, cumin and chaat masala on top - bake at 150 c for 50-60 minutes until the crackers are nice and crispy - let it cool down completely - enjoy with your favourite dip! store it in an airtight container so it stays crispy

recipes.recipe_ingredients:
parmesan roasted chickpeas
1 15 oz can chickpeas
1 tbsp olive oil
1/2 tsp salt
1/2 tsp garlic powder
1/2 tsp onion powder
1/2 tsp herbs de province or Italian seasoning
2 tbsp parmesan cheese
roasted sweet potatoes
1 large sweet potato
1 tbsp olive oil
1/2 tsp salt
1/2 tsp cinnamon
1/4 tsp cumin
chicken meatballs
1 lb ground chicken
1 cup ricotta cheese
1 egg
1/2 cup panko breadcrumbs
1 shallot finely chopped
2 green onions finely chopped
1/2 cup cilantro finely chopped
1/4 cup dill finely chopped
zest of a lemon
1/2 tsp salt
1/2 tsp pepper
2 tbsp olive oil
yogurt jalapeño dressing
1 cup greek yogurt
1 cup fresh basil
1/2 cup fresh dill
juice of a lemon
1 tbsp olive oil
1 tbsp honey
1 jalapeño seeds removed and washed
2 cloves of garlic
salt and pepper to taste
other
4 cups kale
recipes.recipe_method:
Preheat the oven to 400F. Begin by making the parmesan roasted chickpeas. Drain the chickpeas and pat them dry with paper towels. Transfer the beans to a baking sheet.
Add the olive oil, salt, garlic powder, onion powder, herbs de province, and parmesan cheese. Toss until everything is well coated. Transfer to the oven and bake for 15 minutes.
While the chickpeas roast, start on the sweet potatoes. Cut the sweet potato into bite-sized pieces. Transfer to a baking sheet and add the olive oil, salt, cinnamon, and cumin. Toss until everything is well coated. Transfer to the oven and bake for 15-20 minutes, until sweet potatoes are cooked through and starting to brown.
While the sweet potatoes and chickpeas cook, make the chicken meatballs. Add all the ingredients (except the olive oil) to a bowl. Mix until well combined. Scoop out about 2 tbsp of the chicken mixture. Use your hands to form the chicken into a cylinder shape (you can also just roll them into balls, but I like having more surface area to brown).
Add the olive oil (2 tbsp) to a large pan over medium-high heat. Add half of the meatballs and cook for 3-4 minutes on each side, until golden brown and until the internal temperature reaches 165 F. Repeat with the remaining chicken.
While the chicken meatballs cook, make the dressing. Add all the ingredients (greek yogurt, fresh basil, fresh dill, juice of a lemon, olive oil, honey, jalapeño, garlic, salt, and pepper) to a food processor or blender. Blend until smooth.
To assemble, divide the kale, sweet potatoes, roasted chickpeas, and chicken meatballs between bowls. Top with plenty of yogurt jalapeño dressing and enjoy!

recipes.title: Rikdok (Nepali Potato Soup)
recipes.author: amilo.piro.stories
recipes.text: nepali potato soup - rikdok 🇳🇵 eyeball everything, no measurements required. channel your inner cook and roll with it. recipe: boil red potatoes till fork tender. peel and let them cool completely. while the potatoes cool, make a garlic paste by mixing garlic, red chillies and timur or szechuan peppercorns. set aside. mash the potatoes and transfer them to a mortar and pastel. use a wooden mortar and pastel if you have one to pound the potatoes. the potatoes need to have a cheese pull-like consistency or they will dissolve in your soup. set aside. in a pot, heat oil over medium-high heat. add the onion and garlic mixture and cook for 2-3 minutes. add tomatoes and green onions. cook till wilted. add salt. (i also added turmeric, but idk whats the rule on it) add water and let it simmer for 3-4 minutes. wet your hands in water and carefully form small balls from the mashed potatoes. drop the potato balls into the soup. transfer to a serving bowl immediately and garnish with green onions, chilies, and butter, preferably yak butter. enjoy! . vegetarian potato soup sherpa himalaya everest history culture story recipe cooking soup season
recipes.caption:
Nepali Potato Soup - Rikdok 🇳🇵 

eyeball everything, no measurements required. channel your inner cook and roll with it. 

Recipe: 

Boil red potatoes till fork tender. Peel and let them cool completely. 

While the potatoes cool, make a garlic paste by mixing garlic, red chillies and timur or szechuan peppercorns. Set aside. 

Mash the potatoes and transfer them to a mortar and pastel. Use a wooden mortar and pastel if you have one to pound the potatoes. The potatoes need to have a cheese pull-like consistency or they WILL dissolve in your soup. Set aside.

In a pot, heat oil over medium-high heat. Add the onion and garlic mixture and cook for 2-3 minutes.

Add tomatoes and green onions. Cook till wilted. Add salt. (i also added turmeric, but idk whats the rule on it) 

Add water and let it simmer for 3-4 minutes. 

Wet your hands in water and carefully form small balls from the mashed potatoes. Drop the potato balls into the soup. 

Transfer to a serving bowl immediately and garnish with green onions, chilies, and butter, preferably yak butter. Enjoy!

.
#nepal #nepalifood #soup #soupseason #potatoes

recipes.recipe_method:
Boil red potatoes till fork tender. Peel and let them cool completely.

While the potatoes cool, make a garlic paste by mixing garlic, red chillies and timur or szechuan peppercorns. Set aside.

Mash the potatoes and transfer them to a mortar and pastel. Use a wooden mortar and pastel if you have one to pound the potatoes. The potatoes need to have a cheese pull-like consistency or they WILL dissolve in your soup. Set aside.

In a pot, heat oil over medium-high heat. Add the onion and garlic mixture and cook for 2-3 minutes.

Add tomatoes and green onions. Cook till wilted. Add salt. (i also added turmeric, but idk whats the rule on it)

Add water and let it simmer for 3-4 minutes.

Wet your hands in water and carefully form small balls from the mashed potatoes. Drop the potato balls into the soup.

Transfer to a serving bowl immediately and garnish with green onions, chilies, and butter, preferably yak butter. Enjoy!

recipes.text: secret to the creamiest mushroom soup !! ingredients:- * 3 tbsp olive oil * 3 tbsp butter * 1 large onion, chopped * 8-10 cloves garlic, minced * 1 packet of mushrooms, cleaned + sliced 1/2 inch thick * 1/4 cup chopped walnuts * salt and pepper to taste * 1 tsp red chili flakes optional * 2 tbsp all purpose flour * 2.5 cups of water * 1 maggi stock cube * 1 tbs fresh thyme optional * 1 tsp oregano * 1/4- 1/3 cup fresh cream as preference 🍄add your olive oil and butter and melt on medium heat, add in the onion and saute for 5 minutes. stir in the garlic for 30 seconds. add in the mushrooms stir it all to saute for 2-3 minutes. 🍄 next add in chopped walnuts and cook for about 10 minutes until it all caramelises 🍄next, sprinkle on the flour and stir to coat all. cook for 2 minutes pour in veg stock or water + veg stock cube. mix well and let it boil 🍄add in salt pepper and herbs and bring to a boil.lower the heat to simmer covered for 10 minutes, stirring occasionally. add cream and mix 🍄transfer about half of the soup to a mini food processor or blender to puree. add it back into the pot and mix

recipes.caption:
📌Capsicum fry📌

I love veggies that require very little prep and cook time. Capsicum checks all these boxes including flavor. 😍
This is how Amma makes it! Perfect with plain rice or as a side to any South Indian meal. Also works well with rotis. 😊

🌿Ingredients: 
Capsicum/ Green bell peppers: 3, cubed

-For tempering: 
Oil: 1 Tbsp
Mustard seeds: 1 tsp
Channa dal: 2 tsp
Urad dal: 1 tsp
Cumin seeds/jeera: 1/2 tsp
Dried red chillies: 1 or 2
Curry leaves: 1 sprig
Hing: one pinch

-Spices:
Turmeric powder: 1 tsp
Kashmiri red chilly powder: 2 tsp
Coriander powder: 1 tsp
Dry mango/aamchur powder: 1 tsp 
Salt: to taste 
Chickpea flour/ Besan: 2 Tbsp
Chopped Coriander leaves: for garnish

🌿 Method
-To a cast iron skillet, add oil and mustard seeds. Once they start to splutter, add channa dal, urad dal, cumin seeds, dry red chillies and curry leaves with a pinch of asofoetida. Wait until the dals turn light brown and then add the cubed capsicum. 
-Saute it for about two minutes and start to add the spices one by one. Now we just keep stirring occasionally and allow the peppers to cook down. It takes around 6 minutes. You can cover and cook if you want it to get done quicker. 
-Add a Tbsp or two of water to deglaze the pan and mix in the spices that may be stuck to the bottom. 
-After the peppers cook down and the oil separates, add two Tbsp of besan/chickpea flour. Keep stirring until the besan gets cooked and coats the peppers (for about 3 minutes). 
-Turn off the stove and garnish with coriander leaves 😊 

Absolutely delicious capsicum fry is ready! 🌿

I’ve made vendakkai this way too by adding besan to it. Gives it a unique taste. 😍

📌Save this simple recipe and tag me when you try! 🙌🏽

recipes.recipe_method:
To a cast iron skillet, add oil and mustard seeds. Once they start to splutter, add channa dal, urad dal, cumin seeds, dry red chillies and curry leaves with a pinch of asofoetida. Wait until the dals turn light brown and then add the cubed capsicum.
Saute it for about two minutes and start to add the spices one by one. Now we just keep stirring occasionally and allow the peppers to cook down. It takes around 6 minutes. You can cover and cook if you want it to get done quicker.
Add a Tbsp or two of water to deglaze the pan and mix in the spices that may be stuck to the bottom.
After the peppers cook down and the oil separates, add two Tbsp of besan/chickpea flour. Keep stirring until the besan gets cooked and coats the peppers (for about 3 minutes).
Turn off the stove and garnish with coriander leaves 😊

recipes.text: let’s chai for 100 years of living 🫖✨ here’s to a century of joy, wisdom, and a perfect cup of chai! follow along and make this timeless recipe—spiced to perfection and steeped in tradition. 🌿 ingredients • 3 cups water • 1 tablespoon fresh ginger (grated or crushed) • 1 tablespoon coriander seeds (slightly powdered) • 10 black peppercorns (crushed) • 1 small cinnamon stick • ½ teaspoon fennel seeds (crushed) • 4 cardamom pods (cracked open) • 1 tablespoon assam black tea leaves (organic preferred) • 1 cup milk (dairy or plant-based) • a pinch of saffron • sweetener to taste (jaggery or sugar) 🫖 method 1. bring 3 cups of water to a rolling boil in a saucepan. 2. add: • ginger for its warming, zesty kick. • coriander seeds for earthy depth. • crushed black pepper for a spicy spark. • cinnamon stick for a sweet aroma. • crushed fennel seeds for a subtle sweetness. • cardamom pods for that unmistakable chai magic. 3. let the spices simmer for 3 minutes, releasing their rich flavors. 4. add assam black tea leaves, and let the blend steep for 8–10 minutes. 5. pour in 1 cup of milk and bring to a gentle boil. 6. add a pinch of saffron for a luxurious touch. 7. sweeten with jaggery or sugar to your liking, and stir well. 8. strain the chai into your favorite cup and savor every silky-smooth sip. ✨ notes • adjust the spice levels to suit your dosha or mood! • enjoy chai mindfully—its warmth is best shared with loved ones. let’s chai to life, love, and 100 years of living. cheers!
recipes.caption:
Let’s Chai for 100 Years of Living 🫖✨

Here’s to a century of joy, wisdom, and a perfect cup of chai! Follow along and make this timeless recipe—spiced to perfection and steeped in tradition.

🌿 Ingredients
	•	3 cups water
	•	1 tablespoon fresh ginger (grated or crushed)
	•	1 tablespoon coriander seeds (slightly powdered)
	•	10 black peppercorns (crushed)
	•	1 small cinnamon stick
	•	½ teaspoon fennel seeds (crushed)
	•	4 cardamom pods (cracked open)
	•	1 tablespoon Assam black tea leaves (organic preferred)
	•	1 cup milk (dairy or plant-based)
	•	A pinch of saffron
	•	Sweetener to taste (jaggery or sugar)

🫖 Method
	1.	Bring 3 cups of water to a rolling boil in a saucepan.
	2.	Add:
	•	Ginger for its warming, zesty kick.
	•	Coriander seeds for earthy depth.
	•	Crushed black pepper for a spicy spark.
	•	Cinnamon stick for a sweet aroma.
	•	Crushed fennel seeds for a subtle sweetness.
	•	Cardamom pods for that unmistakable chai magic.
	3.	Let the spices simmer for 3 minutes, releasing their rich flavors.
	4.	Add Assam black tea leaves, and let the blend steep for 8–10 minutes.
	5.	Pour in 1 cup of milk and bring to a gentle boil.
	6.	Add a pinch of saffron for a luxurious touch.
	7.	Sweeten with jaggery or sugar to your liking, and stir well.
	8.	Strain the chai into your favorite cup and savor every silky-smooth sip.

✨ Notes
	•	Adjust the spice levels to suit your dosha or mood!
	•	Enjoy chai mindfully—its warmth is best shared with loved ones.

Let’s chai to life, love, and 100 years of living. Cheers! #100YearsJay #ChaiTime #TimelessTradition

recipes.title: Methi Matar Paneer
recipes.author: fit.khurana
recipes.text: recipe⬇️ (cals -370, p- 27g) 100g low fat paneer 2 cups of methi 1/2 cup matar (peas) - (boiled) 1 tsp jeera ✅in a pan, add 1.5 tsp ghee and saute some jeera. ✅then add matar and cook for 2-3 mins. then add methi and let it cook for 6-7 mins on low flame. spices - salt, 1/2 tsp coriander powder, 1/2 tsp haldi, 1/2 tsp red chilli powder, 1/2 tsp garam masala ✅add the above spices in the cooked methi, matar and saute for 3-4 mins. turn off the flame. for the creamy base: 2 big chopped onions 4-5 garlic cloves 2-3 cashews 1 cinnamon stick 1 bayleaf 2-3 peppercorns 1 clove 2-3 elaichi ✅boil the above ingredients for 12-15 mins (water should be just enough to soak all the above well) until everything is soft and the water has turned slightly pink (onion will leave its color) ✅let it cool down and remove the bayleaf and cinnamon stick before blending ✅blend this all along with its water (this is the magical ingredient as it contains all the flavor of the spices post boiling) with 100g low fat paneer. ✅add this creamy mixture to the methi matar mixture and cook for another 7-8 mins on low flame (add more water while cooking to adjust consistency if needed) ✅add 1 tsp sugar and mix well. ✅let it thicken a little and its ready! 🟢do you make low fat paneer at home? if not, then try making the softest low fat paneer at home with my recipe. comment “paneer” and i will dm you✨ methi matar malai, healthy sabzi, healthy meals, vegetarian, protein, high protein, paneer sabzi, methi sabzi, fa
recipes.caption:
Recipe⬇️ (Cals -370, P- 27g)

100g low fat paneer
2 cups of methi
1/2 cup Matar (peas) - (Boiled)
1 tsp jeera

✅In a pan, add 1.5 tsp ghee and saute some jeera. 
✅Then add Matar and cook for 2-3 mins. Then add methi and let it cook for 6-7 mins on low flame. 

Spices - Salt, 1/2 tsp coriander powder, 1/2 tsp haldi, 1/2 tsp red chilli powder, 1/2 tsp garam masala

✅Add the above spices in the cooked methi, matar and saute for 3-4 mins. Turn off the flame.

For the creamy base:
2 big chopped onions
4-5 garlic cloves
2-3 cashews 
1 cinnamon stick
1 bayleaf
2-3 peppercorns
1 clove
2-3 elaichi

✅Boil the above ingredients for 12-15 mins (water should be just enough to soak all the above well) until everything is soft and the water has turned slightly pink (onion will leave its color)
✅Let it cool down and remove the bayleaf and cinnamon stick before blending
✅Blend this all along with its water (this is the magical ingredient as it contains all the flavor of the spices post boiling) with 100g low fat paneer. 
✅Add this creamy mixture to the methi matar mixture and cook for another 7-8 mins on low flame (Add more water while cooking to adjust consistency if needed)
✅Add 1 tsp sugar and mix well.
✅Let it thicken a little and its ready!

🟢Do you make low fat paneer at home? If not, then try making the softest low fat paneer at home with my recipe. Comment “Paneer” and i will dm you✨
