recipes.recipe_ingredients:
100g low fat paneer
2 cups of methi
1/2 cup Matar (peas) - (Boiled)
1 tsp jeera
Spices - Salt, 1/2 tsp coriander powder, 1/2 tsp haldi, 1/2 tsp red chilli powder, 1/2 tsp garam masala
For the creamy base:
2 big chopped onions
4-5 garlic cloves
2-3 cashews
1 cinnamon stick
1 bayleaf
2-3 peppercorns
1 clove
2-3 elaichi
recipes.recipe_method:
In a pan, add 1.5 tsp ghee and saute some jeera.
Then add Matar and cook for 2-3 mins. Then add methi and let it cook for 6-7 mins on low flame.
Add the above spices in the cooked methi, matar and saute for 3-4 mins. Turn off the flame.
Boil the above ingredients for 12-15 mins (water should be just enough to soak all the above well) until everything is soft and the water has turned slightly pink (onion will leave its color)
Let it cool down and remove the bayleaf and cinnamon stick before blending
Blend this all along with its water (this is the magical ingredient as it contains all the flavor of the spices post boiling) with 100g low fat paneer.
Add this creamy mixture to the methi matar mixture and cook for another 7-8 mins on low flame (Add more water while cooking to adjust consistency if needed)
Add 1 tsp sugar and mix well.
Let it thicken a little and its ready!

recipes.title: High-Protein Matar Toast
recipes.author: we_nourish
recipes.text: reposting coz it got a lot of love last winters and i think it’s worth all the space in my feed: high protein desi 🥑 toast- matar🫛 toast 🌿 🌿do you know 1 cup hari matar as 8.6gm protein. we have added paneer to add creaminess and so the texture gets just like avocado. honestly it tasted better than avocado toast, my husband loved it to the point that i’m making it every other day now♥️ ingredients: 🌿2 cups peas 🌿150gm paneer 🌿2 onions 🌿4 garlic cloves 🌿2 tbsp olive oil 🌿salt 🌿pepper 🌿thinly sliced tomatoes 🌿juice from one lemon 🌿chilli flakes, oregano, mixed herbs, crunchy garlic for garnish take some thinly sliced tomatoes. sprinkle salt and mixed herbs and keep in oven on convection mode for 15mins til then cook peas in water for 10mins and then rinse and drain the water. take a pan, add 1 tbsp oil, add onions and garlic, salt, let onions caramelise- get brown and then keep aside. take a mixer jar, add peas, add paneer, fried garlic, salt, pepper, lemon and blend- your spread is ready. airfry sourdough slices for 7-10mins so you get the crunchiest bread. apply the spread. top it with the tomatoes and caramelised onions. garnish with herbs mentioned above and enjoyy! . . . . . . . .
recipes.caption:
Reposting coz it got a lot of love last winters and I think it’s worth all the space in my feed: High Protein Desi 🥑 toast- matar🫛 toast 🌿

🌿Do you know 1 cup Hari matar as 8.6gm protein. We have added paneer to add creaminess and so the texture gets just like avocado. Honestly it tasted better than avocado toast, my husband loved it to the point that I’m making it every other day now♥️

INGREDIENTS:
🌿2 cups peas
🌿150gm paneer
🌿2 onions
🌿4 garlic cloves
🌿2 tbsp olive oil
🌿salt
🌿pepper
🌿thinly sliced tomatoes
🌿juice from one lemon
🌿chilli flakes, oregano, mixed herbs, crunchy garlic for garnish

Take some thinly sliced tomatoes. Sprinkle salt and mixed herbs and keep in oven on convection mode for 15mins @180C. Til then cook peas in water for 10mins and then rinse and drain the water. Take a pan, add 1 tbsp oil, add onions and garlic, salt, let onions caramelise- get brown and then keep aside. Take a mixer jar, add peas, add paneer, fried garlic, salt, pepper, lemon and blend- your spread is ready. Airfry sourdough slices @180C for 7-10mins so you get the crunchiest bread. Apply the spread. Top it with the tomatoes and caramelised onions. Garnish with herbs mentioned above and enjoyy!

recipes.title: Healthy Momos
recipes.author: visha.khandelwal
recipes.text: momos, who?🥟 i recently had to make some dietary changes and honestly, i am not someone who can entirely give up on ‘taste’. so, while being on a mission to make healthy+tasty recipes, this one is truly my favourite!! gets ready in 15 mins and is unbelievably good🤤 recipe: for the filing: - heat some oil (i use olive oil) in a pan and put garlic. - once it’s a bit brown, add vegetables of your choice (i like to add onion, cabbage, mushroom) - you can also add tofu/paneer for protein and also to add some texture. - add just a little bit of soy sauce, vinegar if you want (this is optional), salt as per taste. you are 90%done here! - take the rice paper, dip it into water for 3-5 seconds, take it out and allow it to settle and become soft (don’t start wrapping right away or else it might break). - put the filing, and wrap it in the shape you desire. - pan fry it using very little oil and enjoyyyy (you can either make the dip yourself or use chilly oil)🤤 this was ep2: letting go before 29 follow for more🥰

recipes.title: Curry Leaves Potato
recipes.author: _daddycooks
recipes.text: i am back with a banger recipe, curry leaves potato, i know it sounds sussy but you won’t be disappointed, trust me on it 🫶 start by peeling 2 medium sized ooty potatoes and wash them well. cube them into the preferred size and soak it in some cold water for 15 mins. after soaking, dry it with a cloth. wash and rinse your curry leaves (60g with the sprig), remove the leaves, wash well, and dry using a paper towel. to you cast iron pan, roast your curry leaves on the lowest flame, for around 15-20 mins, and let it cool down well. add in 1 tbsp sesame oil to the same pan, add in 8-10 cloves of smashed garlic, roast it on the lowest flame until crispy and let it cool as well. to the same pan, add in another 2 tsp sesame oil, add in your dried potatoes and toss it well. salt it and let it cook slowly, don’t close the pan. roast it till it’s golden brown and crispy. now to a mixy, add in your curry leaves, roasted garlic, 1/2 tsp garlic granules, salt and pulse into a coarse mixture. once the potatoes are crispy and bootiful, add in 1/4 tsp turmeric powder, 1/3 tsp red chilli powder, 1/3 tsp cumin powder, hing and toss it well. add in 2 tbsp of the curry leaves mixture, toss it well, cook for 3-4 mins for it to crisp up again, and serve it with a squeeze of lime. trust me, you have to try this recipe and there’s no going back, i promise 🫶
recipes.caption:
I am back with a banger recipe, curry leaves potato, I know it sounds sussy but you won’t be disappointed, trust me on it 🫶

Start by peeling 2 medium sized ooty potatoes and wash them well. Cube them into the preferred size and soak it in some cold water for 15 mins. After soaking, dry it with a cloth. 

Wash and rinse your curry leaves (60g with the sprig), remove the leaves, wash well, and dry using a paper towel. 

To you cast iron pan, roast your curry leaves on the lowest flame, for around 15-20 mins, and let it cool down well. 

Add in 1 tbsp sesame oil to the same pan, add in 8-10 cloves of smashed garlic, roast it on the lowest flame until crispy and let it cool as well. 

To the same pan, add in another 2 tsp sesame oil, add in your dried potatoes and toss it well. Salt it and let it cook slowly, don’t close the pan. Roast it till it’s golden brown and crispy. 

Now to a mixy, add in your curry leaves, roasted garlic, 1/2 tsp garlic granules, salt and pulse into a coarse mixture. 

Once the potatoes are crispy and bootiful, add in 1/4 tsp turmeric powder, 1/3 tsp red chilli powder, 1/3 tsp cumin powder, hing and toss it well. Add in 2 tbsp of the curry leaves mixture, toss it well, cook for 3-4 mins for it to crisp up again, and serve it with a squeeze of lime.

recipes.title: Honeynut Squash Brownies
recipes.author: glowwithella
recipes.text: honeynut squash brownies 🍫 ingredients: - 2 cups pureed honeynut squash (about two medium sized honey nut squashs) - 4 large eggs - 1/2 cup melted butter - 2/3 cup maple syrup - 1/2 cup cacao powder - 1/2 cup ap or einkorn flour - 1 tbsp vanilla extract - 1 tsp baking soda - salt - 2 bars dark chocolate - flakey sea salt instructions: 1. preheat your oven to 350°f (175°c). 2. cut your honey nuts in half, remove seeds, add a little olive oil and roast it in the oven until soft (about 40 minutes but varies depending on size) 3. once cool, scoop out the flesh and mash or blend until smooth 4. melt butter and allow to cool 5. in a large mixing bowl, whisk together the mashed squash, eggs, melted butter, maple syrup, and vanilla extract until smooth 6. sift the cocoa powder, flour, baking soda, and salt together in a separate bowl, then add the wet ingredients 7. stir until just combined but do not overmix (batter should be thick but pourable) 8. chop up chocolate and fold in dark chocolate chunks 9. grease an 9x9-inch baking dish or line it with parchment paper. pour the batter into the pan, spreading it evenly 10. bake in the oven for 25-30 minutes or until a toothpick inserted into the center comes out mostly clean (a little moistness is good because this helps make it fudgy) 11. let the brownies cool for at least 10 minutes if not more in the pan before cutting into squares 12. top with flakey sea salt and enjoy!!!!
recipes.caption:
Honeynut Squash Brownies 🍫

Ingredients:
- 2 cups pureed honeynut squash (about two medium sized honey nut squashs)
- 4 large eggs
- 1/2 cup melted butter
- 2/3 cup maple syrup 
- 1/2 cup cacao powder
- 1/2 cup AP or einkorn flour
- 1 tbsp vanilla extract
- 1 tsp baking soda
- Salt 
- 2 bars dark chocolate 
- Flakey sea salt 

Instructions:
1. Preheat your oven to 350°F (175°C).
2. Cut your honey nuts in half, remove seeds, add a little olive oil and roast it in the oven until soft (about 40 minutes but varies depending on size)
3. Once cool, scoop out the flesh and mash or blend until smooth
4. Melt butter and allow to cool
5. In a large mixing bowl, whisk together the mashed squash, eggs, melted butter, maple syrup, and vanilla extract until smooth
6. Sift the cocoa powder, flour, baking soda, and salt together in a separate bowl, then add the wet ingredients
7. Stir until just combined but do not overmix (batter should be thick but pourable)
8. Chop up chocolate and fold in dark chocolate chunks
9. Grease an 9x9-inch baking dish or line it with parchment paper. Pour the batter into the pan, spreading it evenly
10. Bake in the oven for 25-30 minutes or until a toothpick inserted into the center comes out mostly clean (a little moistness is good because this helps make it fudgy) 
11. Let the brownies cool for at least 10 minutes if not more in the pan before cutting into squares
12. Top with flakey sea salt and enjoy!!!!

recipes.caption:
Fudgy Cheesecake Brownie Recipe

Ingredients

Cream Cheese Layer

- 8 oz cream cheese, softened
- 1 large egg, room temperature
- 1/4 cup granulated sugar
- 1 tsp vanilla extract

Brownie Layer

- 1 cup unsalted butter
- 1/2 cup natural cocoa powder
- 1 tsp vanilla extract
- 1/2 cup light brown sugar
- 1 3/4 cups powdered sugar
- 3/4 cup semi-sweet chocolate chips
- 1/3 cup semi-sweet chocolate, chopped
- 3 large eggs, room temperature
- 1/2 cup all-purpose flour
- Pinch of salt
- 3 tbsp olive oil

Method

Preheat oven to 175°C / 350°F, Grease and line an 8x8 inch pan with parchment paper.

Prepare cream cheese layer: 

Whisk cream cheese, egg, vanilla, and sugar until smooth.

Prepare brownie layer:

Brown butter in a saucepan over medium-low heat, stirring every 10 seconds. Once milk solids from butter sink and turn golden brown, transfer to heatproof bowl.Add cocoa powder, oil, vanilla, and chopped chocolate; mix until dissolved. Let the mixture cool at room temperature for 15-20 mins 
Whisk eggs and light brown sugar ( for 4-6 min ) until dissolved and mixture turns into light pale in color.
Add powdered sugar; mix until combined. (1-2 min )
Combine with browned butter mixture,mix until combined. Add flour, and chocolate chips. Mix until just combined don’t over the batter.
Transfer half of brownie mixture to prepared pan. Reserve 30g / 2-3 tbsp cream cheese mixture; add remaining on brownie mixture.
Top with remaining brownie batter; add reserved cream cheese mixture. Make swirls. Bake for 40-45 minutes or until the edges are golden and center is a little fudgy. Let cool completely before cutting.

Tips:

Dissolve sugar in eggs for crackly top.
Avoid overmixing.
Adjust baking time.

recipes.author: aathirasethumadhavan
recipes.text: 178 kcal per serving and a very happy teej ❤️ healthy did not disappoint. trust me - this is too good to miss. healthier shahi toast/tukda (makes 4 servings - 178 kcal per serving- 2 pieces per serving) ingredients 4 slices of bread, crust removed and sliced into two 1.5 tsp ghee 1 tsp sugar 3/4 cup milk 1.5 tbsp milk powder 5 pitted dates blended with 1/4 cup warm milk into a fine paste a few saffron strands (optional) pinch of cardamom powder (optional) slivered almonds to garnish method 1. brush the bread slices with ghee, sprinkle with sugar and toast in the oven until golden brown (roughly for 5 mins at 200 c on top heat). 2. whisk milk powder, milk and optionally saffron/cardamom and start to simmer on a low flame. 3. keep stirring to make sure it doesn’t stick to the base of the pan. make sure to scrape down the pan to get the tastiest milky bits. 4. once it reduces by 1/3rd, add in the puréed dates and keep stirring well. 5. let it cook until it begins to thicken to the desired consistency. 6. you can either wait for it to cool down or serve it warm - drizzle the rabdi all over the toast slices, garnish with slivered almonds and enjoy! 😋 .
recipes.caption:
178 Kcal per Serving and a very Happy Teej ❤️
Healthy did not disappoint. Trust me - this is too good to miss. 
Healthier Shahi Toast/Tukda (makes 4 servings - 178 Kcal per Serving- 2 pieces per serving)
Ingredients 
4 slices of bread, crust removed and sliced into two 
1.5 tsp ghee 
1 tsp sugar 

3/4 cup milk 
1.5 tbsp milk powder 
5 pitted dates blended with 1/4 cup warm milk into a fine paste 
A few saffron strands (optional) 
Pinch of cardamom powder (optional) 

Slivered almonds to garnish 

Method
1. Brush the bread slices with ghee, sprinkle with sugar and toast in the oven until golden brown (roughly for 5 mins at 200 c on top heat).
2. Whisk milk powder, milk and optionally saffron/cardamom and start to simmer on a low flame. 
3. Keep stirring to make sure it doesn’t stick to the base of the pan. Make sure to scrape down the pan to get the tastiest milky bits.
4. Once it reduces by 1/3rd, add in the puréed dates and keep stirring well. 
5. Let it cook until it begins to thicken to the desired consistency.
6. You can either wait for it to cool down or serve it warm - drizzle the rabdi all over the toast slices, garnish with slivered almonds and enjoy! 😋

recipes.title: Yakhni Pulao
recipes.author: mrinalmarwaha
recipes.text: one pot yakhni pulao for mom! 🤍 making her through each fragrant step, from the simmering broth to that final, fluffy bite. nothing beats a homemade classic with a touch of love. in my opinion, this recipe is a much quicker version of the original dish that is flavourful and super easy to make! 🥘 ingredients: -chicken 750g -lehsan (garlic) sliced 8-10 cloves -adrak (ginger) sliced 1 inch piece -pyaz (onion) 1 medium -saunf (fennel seeds) 1 tbs -zeera (cumin seeds) ½ tbs -sabut dhania (coriander seeds) 1 tbs -hari elaichi (green cardamom) 3-4 -javitri (mace) 2 pieces -darchini (cinnamon sticks) 2-3 -laung (cloves) 5-6 -bari elaichi (black cardamom) 2 -namak (salt) ½ tbs or to taste -sabut kali mirch (black peppercorns) ½ tsp -degi lal mirch 2 tsp -green chilli paste 2 tsp -olive oil 2 tsp -water 1 & ½ litre -basmati rice 750g (4 cups) -more water as required toss the chicken in the masalas for a few minutes until the chicken browns and add water to slowly cook the chicken and prepare the broth (yakhni). add soaked rice and let the broth evaporate on high heat. "
recipes.caption:
One Pot Yakhni Pulao for Mom! 🤍

Making her through each fragrant step, from the simmering broth to that final, fluffy bite. Nothing beats a homemade classic with a touch of love. In my opinion, this recipe is a much quicker version of the original dish that is flavourful and super easy to make! 🥘
@soultosoul_diaries

Ingredients:

-Chicken 750g
-Lehsan (Garlic) sliced 8-10 cloves 
-Adrak (Ginger) sliced 1 inch piece
-Pyaz (Onion) 1 medium
-Saunf (Fennel seeds) 1 tbs
-Zeera (Cumin seeds) ½ tbs
-Sabut dhania (Coriander seeds) 1 tbs
-Hari elaichi (Green cardamom) 3-4
-Javitri (Mace) 2 pieces
-Darchini (Cinnamon sticks) 2-3
-Laung (Cloves) 5-6
-Bari elaichi (Black cardamom) 2
-Namak (Salt) ½ tbs or to taste
-Sabut kali mirch (Black peppercorns) ½ tsp
-Degi Lal mirch 2 tsp
-Green Chilli Paste 2 tsp
-Olive Oil 2 tsp
-Water 1 & ½ litre
-Basmati Rice 750g (4 Cups)
-More water as required 

Toss the chicken in the masalas for a few minutes until the chicken browns and add water to slowly cook the chicken and prepare the broth (Yakhni). Add Soaked Rice and let the broth evaporate on high heat.

recipes.comment_recipe:
Ingredients for eggless vanilla cake 🍰 

1.5 cups maida (all-purpose flour)
1 cup milk
1/2 cup melted butter
3/4 cup sugar 
1 tsp baking powder
1/2 tsp baking soda
1 tsp vanilla extract

Instructions:

 1. Sieve together the maida, baking soda, and baking powder. Set them aside.
 2. Use a mixer grinder to powder the sugar.
 3. In a mixing bowl, take the powdered sugar and add the melted butter along with the vanilla extract. Whisk well until the mixture turns creamy.
 4. Gradually add the flour and milk, a little at a time, and mix gently to make a smooth batter.
 5. Once the batter is ready, transfer it to a greased baking pan. Bake at 180°C for 40 minutes in a preheated oven, or until a toothpick inserted in the center comes out clean. 
 6. Take the pan out of the oven, let the cake cool slightly before slicing, and enjoy the best-ever eggless vanilla cake at home 🫶

Notes:

 - You can use 1/2 cup of sugar if you prefer. Adjust the quantity of sugar to your taste.
 - Line the baking tray with parchment paper for easier removal.
 - Ensure all ingredients are at room temperature before starting.
 - Baking time and temperature may vary slightly, as every oven is different.

Super Easy and super Healthy 🤗

(Revisiting my old recipe) #save this #recipe 

“The Coconut Milk Rasam / Thengai Paal Rasam”. 
Very healthy, delicious and easy to make❣️

🥥 Recipe

Cumin seeds - 1 tsp
Pepper corns - 1 tsp
Pound coarsely 
Garlic - 4 cloves 
Shallot - 2 nos (small onion)
Pound it together 
Transfer the ingredients to a pot 
Add tamarind extract (lemon sized tamarind soaked in 1 cup water and extracted)
Water - 1-2 cup
Coriander leaves
Turmeric powder - 1/2 tsp
Salt to taste
Bring it boil, when it starts foaming on the sides 
Add 1/2 cup thick or 1 cup diluted coconut milk 
Reduce the heat to low for 1 to 2 minutes 
Do not let it to boil 
Add the tempering, mix well and serve or enjoy

🥥 For tempering 

Coconut oil - 1 tbsp
Mustard seeds -1/2 tsp
Fenugreek seeds - 1-4 tsp
Dried red chilies - 2 nos
Hing - 1/4 tsp
Curry leaves 

Try this Rasam once and I bet you’ll like it. Very subtle with big flavors. Gut friendly 🙌

recipes.caption:
Diwali is incomplete without this crunchy-crisp chiwda that my mother-in-law makes. 

Diwali food prep somehow always begins with this chiwda that has a beautiful khamang flavour. 

If there’s just one Pharaal item you make this season, let it be this! 

Here’s the recipe

The primary ingredients are:

250 gms of Patal Pohe- the thin variety of Pohe 
1/2 cup peanuts 
1/2 cup Dalya/ popped chana dal
1/3 cup Khobra 

In a heavy-bottomed Kadhai, first dry-roast the pohe till they are uniformly warm- about 5-8 mins for this qty, depending on your Kadhai/ heat source. You want to stop before the pohe start curling.

Transfer the roasted pohe to a dry vessel, clean out the Kadhai and temper 

1/3 cup groundnut oil with 
1/2 tsp mustard seeds
A generous pinch of heeng 
6-8 green chilies, chopped 
1 Tbsp khas-khas
1/2 cup peanuts 

Stir everything well for 2-3 mins 

Now add 
1/2 cup loosely packed kadipatta 
1.5 tsp grated ginger

Stir everything well once again, and add 
1/3 cup Khobra followed by
1 Tbsp sesame seeds 
1/2 cup Dalya/ popped chana dal

Stir well for about 2-3 minutes till the Khobra turns light brown 

Add 
1/2 tsp turmeric powder 
1/2 tsp red chili powder 

The roasted pohe and gently toss to combine the pohe with the tempering 

Then add
1.5 tsp coriander powder 
1/4 tsp jeera powder 
1 tsp amchoor powder 
2 Tbsp powdered sugar- we like chiwda that has a distinct sweet undertone. If you don’t start with 1 Tbsp, taste and add more as needed 
Salt, to taste

Gently fold these spices into the pohe- be very gentle- you don’t want a poha crumble.

Taste to check if you need to add salt/ sugar/ amchoor/ red chili powder - adjust if needed, let it cool, then store in an air-tight container.

recipes.title: Ragi Kozhukottai Payasam
recipes.author: auraartofhealthyliving
recipes.text: ragi kozhukottai payasam ✨ who i am today, especially in the kitchen, is all thanks to my amma—my forever inspiration. we shot this video together before navratri, but due to my travels, i couldn’t share it earlier. when i asked her for a healthy payasam recipe, she came up with this unique ragi kozhukottai payasam. traditionally, “kozhukottai” in tamil refers to steamed rice balls, usually stuffed or plain. but in this version, amma replaced the rice with wholesome ragi (finger millet) and used creamy coconut milk instead of cow’s milk. the result? a rich, flavorful payasam that’s not only delicious but also nutritious. if you’re looking for a guilt-free dessert that feels indulgent, you have to try this recipe! 😍 let me know if you’d like any other tweaks!
recipes.caption:
Ragi Kozhukottai Payasam ✨

Who I am today, especially in the kitchen, is all thanks to my Amma—my forever inspiration. We shot this video together before Navratri, but due to my travels, I couldn’t share it earlier.

When I asked her for a healthy payasam recipe, she came up with this unique Ragi Kozhukottai Payasam. Traditionally, “Kozhukottai” in Tamil refers to steamed rice balls, usually stuffed or plain. But in this version, Amma replaced the rice with wholesome ragi (finger millet) and used creamy coconut milk instead of cow’s milk. The result? A rich, flavorful payasam that’s not only delicious but also nutritious.

If you’re looking for a guilt-free dessert that feels indulgent, you have to try this recipe! 😍

Let me know if you’d like any other tweaks!
recipes.recipe_ingredients:
ragi flour
water
jaggery
fresh coconut
oil
crushed cardamom
ghee
recipes.recipe_method: Boil water in a pan, add the ragi flour, and stir it into a thick dough; cover and let it cook. Dissolve the jaggery in water to make a syrup. Grate the fresh coconut and squeeze it through a strainer to extract coconut milk. Knead the cooked ragi dough with a little oil and roll it by hand into many small marble-sized balls. Pour the coconut milk into a pot, strain it, mix in the jaggery syrup, and heat it, seasoning with crushed cardamom and ghee. Add the ragi balls to the simmering payasam and cook until soft.

recipes.caption:
Instant onion pickle 🌿🌿

I am obsessed with easy breezy recipes these days. And, I am a complete chutney and pickle fan. So today we are making another super easy and delicious pickle recipe that comes together in no time. 
Store in a sterilized jar in the fridge (for up to 2 weeks) and enjoy with dal chawal and parathas. 

Let’s see the recipe.

Ingredients 

3-4 onions, sliced
4-5 green chillies, slit
2 inches ginger, julienned 
Handful of coriander leaves with stems, chopped
1 tsp white sesame seeds
1 tsp fennel seeds
1 tsp mustard seeds
1/4 tsp fenugreek seeds
1 tsp Kashmiri red chilli powder
Salt to taste 
2 tsp vinegar

For the tempering 
2-3 tsp mustard oil
1/4 tsp hing
1 tsp kalonji seeds
1/4 tsp turmeric powder 
 Method
1. Dry roast sesame seeds, fennel seeds, mustard seeds, fenugreek seeds. Once it cools down, coarsely grind them. 
2. Now in a bowl add onion, green chillies, ginger, coriander, roasted masala, chilli powder, salt, and vinegar. Mix well.
3. Make a tempering and pour over the onions and enjoy :)

2. Water 2 cup
3. Milk 400 ml
4. Mixed dry fruit (chopped)
5. Cardamom/Elaichi Powder 1 tsp
6. Jaggery powder 3-4 tbsp
7. Grated/Dessicated Coconut
8. Mixed Fruits of your choice
9. Pumpkin/Musk melon seeds for toppings
10. Desi ghee 1 tbsp

Recipe-
1. Wash the amaranth seeds 2-3 times in enough water and drain the water.
2. Now a tbsp of desi ghee in a pressure cooker and saute the washed rajgira seeds for 1-2 mins.
3. Then add 2 cups of water and pressure cook for 2 whistles.
4. Once the seeds are cooked and pressure released add the milk, cardamom powder and chopped dry fruits. (I have added cashews, almomds and raisins).
5. Stir well and cook on medium low heat until the milk has thickened.
6. Then switch of the flame and add the  jaggery powder and mix well.
7. Refrigerate this pudding for 2-3 hours or you can also prepare it a night before and refrigerate it overnight.
8. Once the pudding is ready, plate in glasses or bowls with a layer of rajgira pudding, topped with a layer of dessicated coconut, banana slices and mixed fresh fruits of your choice.
9. Top it with more fresh seeds and serve. Trust me this recipe is fingerlicking good.

recipes.caption:
These dudhi/ lauki muthiya made with jowar flour are naturally gluten-free, don’t need any rava or soda and make for both the perfect breakfast, snack and tiffin item.

Also, I use a much higher ratio of dudhi: jowar & besan (1 cup for 1/4 cup each of jowar, besan) and unlike many recipes that ask for the water to be squeezed out, we keep all the water and nutrient intact.

I love dudhi and will find ways to eat it regularly in many ways, but, if you’re worried about whether you’ll enjoy a recipe with so much of this gourd- friends who can’t stand this vegetable love these muthia, making this a great non-sabzi way to have this vegetable.

Here’s the recipe, try it!

In a bowl, combine the dry ingredients:
1/4 cup jowar flour from @twobrothersorganicfarmsindia 
1/4 cup coarse besan 
1 Tbsp sesame seeds from @twobrothersorganicfarmsindia 
1/4 tsp coriander powder
1/4 tsp turmeric powder
1/2 tsp Himalyan pink salt (two brothers)
A generous pinch of Heeng 

Drizzle in 
1 tsp groundnut oil (two brothers), mix well 

Then add
1 cup doodhi, grated 
Paste of 1-2 green chilies + 1/2 inch ginger 

Mix well, then shape into logs and steam for 12-14 mins.

Once cool, slice and stir fry in a tempering of 
1 Tbsp Groundnut oil 
1/4 tsp mustard seeds
1 tsp sesame seeds
1 green chilies
7-8 curry leaves

Serve as is, or with a green chutney, for breakfast or as a snack.

Also is perfect to pack for tiffin (without the green chutney)- I’ve carried this in a dabba for two recent travels and it made for the perfect on-road snack. 

Also, the steamed muthiya also freeze perfectly. So if you expect busy times ahead, make a large batch, thaw as many as you need and simply toss in the tempering- the texture doesn’t get dense even after freezing.

Try it!

recipes.text: 🪔diwali special - paan falooda shots💚 this diwali, give a spin to your paan shots and up your game by serving paan falooda shots, that are super easy to make.😍 how to? ✨ start by removing the veins of fresh paan leaves. this step is important to ensure the paan is clean and good to use. ✨ add 9-10 chopped paan leaves, 1/4 cup gulkand and 1 tbsp variyali in a mixer jar to make paste. ✨ in a shake maker/ bigger jar, add 3 cups of milk, 1/2 cup of condensed milk and all the prepared paan paste into it and blend to make paan flavoured milk. 👉🏼 in shot glasses, add 1 tsp of soaked chia seeds, 1 tsp of sevaiyan, and fill the glass with paan milk leaving enough space for a small scoop of vanilla ice-cream. garnish with dried and crushed rose and paan leaves. serve chilled and enjoy!😋 it is a must try. share this with your friends and family. save it for future reference.💯 follow for more follow for more follow for more (paan, paan shots, diwali food, diwali recipes, easy recipes, falooda, paan falooda shots, diwali 2024, indian recipes, party drinks, mumbai street food, )
recipes.caption:
🪔Diwali special - Paan Falooda Shots💚

This Diwali, give a spin to your paan shots and up your game by serving PAAN FALOODA SHOTS, that are super easy to make.😍

How to?
✨ Start by removing the veins of fresh paan leaves. 
This step is important to ensure the paan is clean and good to use.
✨ Add 9-10 chopped paan leaves, 1/4 cup gulkand and 1 tbsp variyali in a mixer jar to make paste. 
✨ In a shake maker/ bigger jar, add 3 cups of milk, 1/2 cup of condensed milk and all the prepared paan paste into it and blend to make paan flavoured milk. 

👉🏼 In shot glasses, add 1 tsp of soaked chia seeds, 1 tsp of sevaiyan, and fill the glass with paan milk leaving enough space for a small scoop of vanilla ice-cream. 
Garnish with dried and crushed rose and paan leaves.

Serve chilled and enjoy!😋
It is a MUST TRY.

Share this with your friends and family. Save it for future reference.💯

recipes.recipe_method:
Start by removing the veins of fresh paan leaves.
This step is important to ensure the paan is clean and good to use.
Add 9-10 chopped paan leaves, 1/4 cup gulkand and 1 tbsp variyali in a mixer jar to make paste.
In a shake maker/ bigger jar, add 3 cups of milk, 1/2 cup of condensed milk and all the prepared paan paste into it and blend to make paan flavoured milk.
In shot glasses, add 1 tsp of soaked chia seeds, 1 tsp of sevaiyan, and fill the glass with paan milk leaving enough space for a small scoop of vanilla ice-cream.
Garnish with dried and crushed rose and paan leaves.

This gluten free pudding is a super hit at my home! It’s so delicious and healthy! Try it and let me know what you think! 

☀️Amaranth is extremely nutritious, it’s high protein and serves as a great breakfast option with some fruits and nuts! Your gut & taste buds will thank you for this amazing recipe! It will also  help you with your fat loss when you replace your oily, processed breakfast with this.

INGREDIENTS: makes 3 jars
🌿2 cups water
🌿1 cup amaranth/rajgira/chaulai ( I’m using @organictattva  one (not sponsored- it’s clean & good quality unlike most brands available) 
🌿1.5 cup yoghurt/curd
🌿1 scoop unflavoured protein powder
🌿2-3 tbsp honey or you can use monk fruit 
🌿1/2 cup pomegranate
🌿1/4 cup banana
🌿1/4 cup mango cubes 
🌿crushed makhana 1/4 cup 
🌿crushed dry fruits like almonds, cashews, walnuts and pistachios ( optional) 

Wash amaranth and then boil in water. I’m using slightly dry roasted amaranth(you can do the same). Cover for 5mins on low flame. Boil until water completely disappears. Once it cools down. Add curd or yoghurt. Add protein powder. Add honey for sweetness or you can use monk fruit. The fruits also render perfect sweetness to the pudding. Just layer with fruits, makhanas, pudding and some seeds and nuts in the end. Refrigerate overnight and in the morning, your hella delicious, high protein breakfast is ready♥️

recipes.title: Ragi Milk
recipes.author: kriti_kaur_dhiman
recipes.text: have you ever heard of ragi milk ? ragi milk and regular milk have different nutritional profiles and health benefits: nutrition ragi milk is high in protein and fiber, and may help with weight loss, skin damage, and anemia. ragi is also rich in calcium, which is important for bone health. regular milk is a good source of protein, calcium, phosphorus, b vitamins, potassium, and vitamin d. fat content regular milk has an average fat content of 3.5%, while reduced-fat milk has at least 25% less fat, low-fat milk has less than 1.5% fat, and skim milk has no more than 0.15% fat. other considerations ragi alone can't replace milk or other dairy products in your diet, as milk provides other essential nutrients. you should also consider your unique nutritional demands and preferences, and speak with a medical practitioner or a certified dietitian if you have any special health issues or dietary limitations. people with thyroid should also avoid this
recipes.caption:
Have you ever heard of ragi milk ?

Ragi milk and regular milk have different nutritional profiles and health benefits:

Nutrition
Ragi milk is high in protein and fiber, and may help with weight loss, skin damage, and anemia. Ragi is also rich in calcium, which is important for bone health. Regular milk is a good source of protein, calcium, phosphorus, B vitamins, potassium, and vitamin D.

Fat content
Regular milk has an average fat content of 3.5%, while reduced-fat milk has at least 25% less fat, low-fat milk has less than 1.5% fat, and skim milk has no more than 0.15% fat.

Other considerations
Ragi alone can't replace milk or other dairy products in your diet, as milk provides other essential nutrients. You should also consider your unique nutritional demands and preferences, and speak with a medical practitioner or a certified dietitian if you have any special health issues or dietary limitations.
People with thyroid should also avoid  this

recipes.caption:
This is my viral breakfast with 32g protein and 11g fibre per bowl. It’s made with natural ingredients and I didn’t want to cheat by using powders to artificially boost the nutrient content.

This breakfast has:
🎯No protein powders
🎯No added fibre powders
🎯No collagen powder

It does however contain, natural ingredients;

❤️ Well strained Greek yogurt with 10g protein / 100g. Some brands don’t strain it properly to give more volume (cheaper to make) but therefore lower and protein so do read the label. 200g

❤️ Milled flaxseeds (30g), I normally grind my own in a bullet style blender, however I was given a bag of pre-milled flaxseeds at a conference from @linwoodshealthfoods which I’m using here. 

❤️ Milk to loosen, I used a soy milk here which is slightly higher and protein and many other plants based milks. 

❤️ 1 fig and  20g pomegranates on top, but you can use whatever fruits you have available.

❤️ I also use a drizzle of squeezy 100% pure peanut butter on top. It’s easy to use a little bit less when it comes in a squeezy bottle, I use 10 g approximately. 

This is one of my favourite breakfasts. It really is a massive bowl that keeps you full up all morning.

The advantage of this breakfast is that you don’t think about food between breakfast and lunch and your focus is better because you have the energy being delivered slowly throughout the morning. 

This means your appetite is stable as well as your blood sugars, from both yoghurt and the flaxseeds. 

The fibre and the protein slow down the release of any sugars in the figs and pomegranates meaning that you can have a slightly sweet breakfast and still not upset blood sugar control. It doesn’t always have to be savoury! We just need to eat smarter.

Stable blood sugars have a knock on effect on our mood which often also feels more stable as we avoid the dips in our blood sugars that can make us feel tired, lacking concentration, or even a little anxious.

So if you get hungry mid morning,  give us breakfast a try, it might just change the way you do breakfast. Xx
recipes.recipe_ingredients:
Well strained Greek yogurt 200g
Milled flaxseeds (30g)
Milk to loosen
1 fig and 20g pomegranates
drizzle of squeezy 100% pure peanut butter

recipes.title: Healthy Air-Fried Moong Dal
recipes.author: auraartofhealthyliving
recipes.text: healthy air-fried moong dal ✨ if you enjoy haldiram's fried moong dal, here's a healthier version of it. step 1: soak moong dal for 1 hour. step 2: drain the water completely and add the dal to the air-fryer. step 3: spray some oil, mix it well, and spread it into a uniform layer. step 4: air-fry for 4 minutes at 160°c. step 5: take it out, mix it well, and air-fry for another 4 minutes. step 6: repeat this process 2 more times. step 7: transfer the dal to a bowl, season it with salt and your choice of spices. step 8: put it into a container, shake it well, and enjoy!
recipes.caption:
Healthy Air-Fried Moong Dal ✨

If you enjoy Haldiram's fried moong dal, here's a healthier version of it.

Step 2: Drain the water completely and add the dal to the air-fryer.

Step 4: Air-fry for 4 minutes at 160°C.
Step 5: Take it out, mix it well, and air-fry for another 4 minutes.
Step 6: Repeat this process 2 more times.
Step 7: Transfer the dal to a bowl, season it with salt and your choice of spices.
Step 8: Put it into a container, shake it well, and enjoy!

recipes.title: Tapioca Pudding (Sago)
recipes.author: hellolisalin
recipes.text: it is so, so hot in sacramento right now 🥵 i’ve been stocking our house with ice cream and making many batches of tapioca pudding/sago to stay cool. the pudding is so refreshing. you can always adjust the sweetness to your taste and use whatever fruit is in the house. the recipes for the mango and purple sweet potato versions are on my site! tap the link in my profile and then the tapioca pudding photos. in the past, i’ve suggested boiling the milk and coconut milk first to preserve the vibrancy of the dessert. i’ll be honest, i’m usually too lazy to do that and just blend the milk with chilled coconut milk. as long as you serve the dessert immediately, you’ll be fine. let me know if you make this!! 💜💛

recipes.author: katlinandsourabh

recipes.caption:
Been a while since we made this 💓💫

Bhindi Do Pyaza Recipe

*Ingredients:*
- 1/2 pound okra (bhindi), cut into 1-inch pieces
- 2 medium red onions, 1 cubed and 1 minced
- 1 teaspoon cumin seeds
- 5 cloves garlic, chopped
- 1 teaspoon red chili powder
- 1 teaspoon coriander powder
- 1/2 teaspoon turmeric powder
- A few splashes of hing (asafoetida)
- 2 tablespoons heavy whipping cream
- Olive oil for frying
- Fresh cilantro, chopped (for garnish)
- Salt to taste

*Instructions:*

1. **Prepare the Okra:** Cut the okra into 1-inch pieces. Fry them in a generous amount of olive oil on high heat until they are slightly crispy. Add the cubed red onions towards the end and sauté until the onions soften. Set aside.

2. **Make the Masala Base:** In the same pan, with the leftover oil, add 1 teaspoon of cumin seeds and 5 cloves of chopped garlic. Cook until the garlic is almost golden brown. Add the minced red onion and sauté on high heat for 5-10 minutes until the onions are caramelized.

3. **Add the Spices:** Add 1 teaspoon each of red chili powder and coriander powder, 1/2 teaspoon of turmeric powder, and a few splashes of hing. Pour in a little water to cover the spices and sauté until the oil starts to separate from the masala.

4. **Finish the Masala:** Stir in 2 tablespoons of heavy whipping cream and mix well.

5. **Combine and Serve:** Add the fried okra and onion mixture to the masala, gently combining everything. Garnish with fresh cilantro and serve hot with crispy roti.

Enjoy this flavorful and delicious Bhindi Do Pyaza with a side of crispy roti!

recipes.author: fit.khurana
recipes.text: recipe⬇️ makes 16 medium laddus ingredients: 1/2 cup dalia 2 cups water 1 tablespoon rice flour 1.5 tbsp ghee cardamom powder 8-10 stands of saffron 4-5 tbsp sweetner (monkfruit extract - zero calorie sweetner/ coconut sugar) - try avoiding jaggery 10-12 small raisins 3-4 drops orange food color recipe: (use non-stick pan only) 1. roast dailya for 4-5 mins in 1 tsp ghee 2. add water and cover the pan. let it cook on low flame until its soft and mushy. takes 5-10 mins. don’t let it become too dry, it should be wet and mushy. 3. add rice flour, cardamom powder, saffron infused water, sweetner, food color and raisins. also add 1 tbsp ghee at this stage. 4. sauté for 2 minutes. turn off the flame and let it cool down. the mixture should be sticky and have a starchy texture. 5. apply ghee on your palms and starting rolling into laddus. garnish with pistachios/ cashews and dig in❤️ thank you for this amazing recipe its a game changer❤️ commeny your favourite dessert and i will try to make a healthy alternative for it❤️ healthy motichoor laddus, motichoor laddu, healthy mithais, healthy desserts, indian mithai, ganesh chaturthi, ganpati
recipes.caption:
Recipe⬇️

Makes 16 Medium Laddus

Ingredients:
1/2 Cup Dalia
2 Cups Water
1 tablespoon rice flour
1.5 tbsp ghee
Cardamom powder 
8-10 stands of saffron
4-5 tbsp sweetner (Monkfruit extract - zero calorie sweetner/ Coconut Sugar) - Try avoiding jaggery
10-12 Small raisins
3-4 drops orange food color

Recipe: (Use non-stick pan only)
1. Roast dailya for 4-5 mins in 1 tsp ghee
2. Add water and cover the pan. Let it cook on low flame until its soft and mushy. Takes 5-10 mins. Don’t let it become too dry, it should be wet and mushy.
3. Add Rice flour, cardamom powder, saffron infused water, sweetner, food color and raisins. Also add 1 tbsp ghee at this stage.
4. Sauté for 2 minutes. Turn off the flame and let it cool down. The mixture should be sticky and have a starchy texture.
5. Apply ghee on your palms and starting rolling into laddus. Garnish with pistachios/ cashews and dig in❤️

Thank you for this amazing recipe @guiltfree.cookbook. Its a game changer❤️

recipes.title: Air Fryer Yogurt Toast
recipes.author: lordlucy
recipes.text: air fryer yogurt toast. ready in less than 10 minutes with 15g protein per serve. a sweet, custard like filling baked until caramelised on a golden, crunchy brioche base topped with fresh berries. your new favourite sweet breakfast: serves 1 ingredients: 2 slices brioche bread 60g greek yogurt 1 egg 1 tbsp honey 1/2 tsp vanilla extract sliced strawberries and blueberries method: 1. mix the greek yogurt, egg, honey and vanilla in a bowl until smooth. 2. use the back of a spoon to press into each brioche slice to create a ‘well’. 3. spoon your custard mixture into the well and top with berries. 4. air fry at 200°c for 6 minutes until the edges are golden and crisp. 5. finish with icing sugar and a drizzle of honey.
recipes.caption:
Air fryer yogurt toast. Ready in less than 10 minutes with 15g protein per serve. 

A sweet, custard like filling baked until caramelised on a golden, crunchy brioche base topped with fresh berries. Your new favourite sweet breakfast:

Serves 1

Ingredients:
2 slices brioche bread
60g Greek yogurt
1 egg
1 tbsp honey
1/2 tsp vanilla extract
Sliced strawberries and blueberries

Method:
1. Mix the Greek yogurt, egg, honey and vanilla in a bowl until smooth.
2. Use the back of a spoon to press into each brioche slice to create a ‘well’.
3. Spoon your custard mixture into the well and top with berries.
4. Air fry at 200°C for 6 minutes until the edges are golden and crisp.
5. Finish with icing sugar and a drizzle of honey.

Masala Chai is more than just a cup of tea. It’s an emotion and an age-old Indian tradition. It’s a soothing and rejuvenating drink made to bring utter joy. We Indians are way too attached to chai and nothing can beat a hot cup of tea, especially during the monsoon season. Tea in monsoon in Mountains with a plate of pakoras is like a therapy that everyone desires to relish. 

Chai tea offers a major boost to physical and mental health. Not only does chai tea provide many of the benefits, but it also has a bold flavor and tempting aroma that only a few people can resist.

I call this Chai, Pahadi Chai simply because of its taste and aroma that takes me back to the first time I had this Chai on my trip to Uttarkashi, in Uttarakhand. 

The lady prepared the Masala on a stone grinder, with Ginger, Tulsi, Mint Leaves (yes, they taste amazing in Chai), cardamom and cloves. That hand pounded Masala had added an earthy flavour to this Chai, and kept me mesmerised and feeling close to Nature. 

This Chai boosts immunity and gives your body the extra kick from within! Do give this a try and share it with a Chai Lover you know! 

Ingredients: (serves 3)
Water, 1.5 Cup 
Ginger, 1 inch
Tulsi, 5-6 leaves
Mint Leaves, 12-15 leaves
Cloves, 3-4
Cardamom, 2-3
Black Tea Leaves, 2-3 Tsp
Jaggery Block to taste

Instructions:
1. Hand pound ginger, tulsi, mint, cloves and cardamom on a stone grinder.
2. Add water to a vessel, to this add the hand pounded masala. Bring to boil on simmer. 
3. Add Black Tea Leaves, simmer for 2 minutes.
4. Add Milk, let boil for 2 minutes on low heat. 
5. Add Jaggery block to taste, turn off the heat and mix to dissolve. 
6. Serve hot.

recipes.recipe_method: Split a red onion and roast it directly over a gas flame until charred black. Grind the burnt onion with garlic cloves, ginger, fresh cilantro, and coriander seeds into a coarse green paste. Mix the besan with salt, turmeric, and water to form a smooth yellow dough and rest it with oil. Roll the dough flat, spread it with the green paste, sprinkle with sesame seeds and chopped cilantro, cut it into strips, and roll the strips into small cylinders (patodi). In a pan, sauté the remaining green paste with oil, season with red chili powder, turmeric, and salt, then add water to create a gravy. Gently drop the patodi into the simmering gravy and cook until tender. Garnish with fresh cilantro.

recipes.title: Chocolate Banana Bread
recipes.author: _ongsquad
recipes.text: my how the tables have turned. something happened when my daughter turned 8. along with the normal cognitive and language improvements, she also developed an attitude. my sweet, compliant baby was suddenly questioning my authority and arguing back. is this a glimpse into her teenage future? her sass can be exasperating but i’m also mindful that in her thought process, she is showing signs of leadership and intelligence. she thinks critically, isn’t afraid to express her feelings and doesn’t take no until she underhands the why. i can already tell she will be my most challenging child, but she also has the greatest potential. watch out world! brown butter banana bread cookie recipe (makes 24 cookies) ingredients 1.5 cups flour 1.5 cups oats 1 teaspoon cinnamon 1/2 teaspoon baking soda 1/2 teaspoons baking powder 1/2 teaspoon salt 1 cup butter 1 cup sugar 2 bananas 1.5 tbsp yogurt 1.5 teaspoons vanilla 1 cup chocolate chips directions 1. combine flour, oats, cinnamon, baking powder, baking soda, and salt. 2 in a separate bowl, combine browned butter, sugar, bananas, yogurt, and vanilla. 3. combine the wet and dry ingredients and add chocolate chips. 4. cover and refrigerate for at least 30 minutes. 5. scoop onto cookie sheet and bake at 375° for 14 minutes. 6. allow cookies to cool for 5 minutes and transfer to cooling rack. enjoy!
recipes.caption:
My how the tables have turned. Something happened when my daughter turned 8. Along with the normal cognitive and language improvements, she also developed an attitude. My sweet, compliant baby was suddenly questioning my authority and arguing back. Is this a glimpse into her teenage future? 

Her sass can be exasperating but I’m also mindful that in her thought process, she is showing signs of leadership and intelligence. She thinks critically, isn’t afraid to express her feelings and doesn’t take no until she underhands the why. I can already tell she will be my most challenging child, but she also has the greatest potential. Watch out world! 

Brown Butter Banana Bread Cookie Recipe (makes 24 cookies)

Ingredients
1.5 cups flour
1.5 cups oats
1 teaspoon cinnamon
1/2 teaspoon baking soda
1/2 teaspoons baking powder
1/2 teaspoon salt

1 cup butter
1 cup sugar
2 bananas 
1.5 TBSP yogurt
1.5 teaspoons vanilla
1 cup chocolate chips 

Directions
1. Combine flour, oats, cinnamon, baking powder, baking soda, and salt. 
2 in a separate bowl, combine browned butter, sugar, bananas, yogurt, and vanilla.
3. Combine the wet and dry ingredients and add chocolate chips.
4. Cover and refrigerate for at least 30 minutes. 
5. Scoop onto cookie sheet and bake at 375° for 14 minutes. 
6. Allow cookies to cool for 5 minutes and transfer to cooling rack. Enjoy!

recipes.author: eatmoreplants.no
recipes.text: creamyyyy lemon garlic soup🍋 reposting this one because it’s my most saved recipe this year and we can not forget. healthy comfort food at its finest. how come lemon makes everything great? ingredients (4-6 servings) 1 tbsp olive oil 4 garlic cloves 1 red onion 0.5 tsp paprika 1 tsp dried rosemary 1 tsp dried thyme 0.5 tsp garlic powder ¼ tsp chili flakes 1.2 l (5 cups) cooked butter beans 1 l (4 cups) vegetable broth salt & black pepper, to taste juice from 1 lemon + zest instructions 1. heat the olive oil in a pot over medium heat, add the onion sauté for about 1 minute, add the garlic and sauté for another minute. 2. add the spices, butter beans and broth. 3. use an immersion blender and blend until smooth. 4. let it simmer for 10 minutes, stirring occasionally. 5. add lemon juice and zest. 6. add more salt and pepper to taste. enjoy!
recipes.caption:
Creamyyyy Lemon Garlic Soup🍋 reposting this one because it’s my most saved recipe this year and we can not forget. Healthy comfort food at its finest. How come lemon makes everything great? 

Ingredients (4-6 servings)
1 Tbsp olive oil
4 garlic cloves
1 red onion
0.5 tsp paprika
1 tsp dried rosemary
1 tsp dried thyme
0.5 tsp garlic powder
¼ tsp chili flakes
1.2 L (5 cups) cooked butter beans
1 L (4 cups) vegetable broth 
salt & black pepper, to taste
Juice from 1 lemon + zest

Instructions
1. Heat the olive oil in a pot over medium heat, add the onion sauté for about 1 minute, add the garlic and sauté for another minute.
2. Add the spices, butter beans and broth.
3. Use an immersion blender and blend until smooth.
4.  Let it simmer for 10 minutes, stirring occasionally.
5. Add lemon juice and zest.
6. Add more salt and pepper to taste. Enjoy!

recipes.recipe_method: Place the cooked leftover rice on a large plate and add the red chili powder, salt, cumin seeds, and sesame seeds. Comment “kebab” & I’ll DM you the recipe for the chicken seekh kebab!! It’s also linked in my bio or google “eatsbyramya chicken kebab” :) 

If you comment for the recipe, plsss make sure you’re following BEFORE your comment cause the links don’t send otherwise.

——

Can I make seekh kebabs without skewers?
I wrote out step by step directions to shape the seekh kebabs without skewers above. I honestly never used skewers cause it’s not something I have on hand.

My mixture is falling apart. What do I do?
It sounds like you might be using ground chicken with higher fat content. This recipe calls for LEAN ground chicken to avoid any extra fat or moisture while forming and cooking the kebabs. You have a few options now. You can either form them into flat patties (kind of like mini burger patties) or add some breadcrumbs to soak up any extra moisture.

Can I add extra veggies to this?
Yes you can BUT make sure to grate the veggies and then squeeze out any water. Any sort of excess moisture will make the moisture really hard to work with and keep from falling apart.

How many calories are in the Chicken Seekh Kebab?
This recipe makes 10 Seekh kebabs and each one has 60 calories.

How much protein is in each Seekh Kebab?
Each seekh kebab has 10g of protein! I usually have 2-3 as a part of my meal which adds an easy 20-30 grams of protein per meal.

How do I store seekh kebabs?
Let the kebabs cool completely and place them in an airtight Tupperware container. Then, you can store them in the fridge for up to a week!

Can I freeze seekh kebabs?
Yep! You should shape the kebabs & freeze them individually first. Just place them on a tray without touching each other and freeze for 1 hour. Then, pout them all into a container or bag and freeze for up to 2 months. When you’re ready to use, let it sit in the refrigerator for 5-6 hours and then bake until completely cooked.

 I have included my favorite @californiawalnutsindia for their gold-standard taste, exceptional quality, and satisfying crunch; just a handful transform this recipe into something extraordinary.

recipes.caption:
Comment if you carry tiffin with you or not 👇
.
Ingredients
For the Batter:
- 1 cup quinoa, soaked for 4-5 hours
- 1/2 cup moong dal, soaked for 4-5 hours
- 1/2 cup urad dal , soaked for 4-5 hours
- 1 tsp methi (fenugreek) seeds, soaked for 4-5 hours
- Salt to taste
- 100 ml water

For the Filling:
- 1 medium onion, finely chopped
- 1 small capsicum, finely chopped
- 1 small carrot, finely chopped
- 1 tbsp coriander, finely chopped
- 1/4 cup paneer, crumbled
- Salt to taste
- Red chili flakes to taste
- Oil for cooking

Instructions

1. Drain the soaked quinoa, moong dal, urad dal, and methi seeds. Combine them in a blender with 100 ml of water and blend until smooth. Add salt to taste.

Ensure the batter is of a pourable consistency. If it is too thick, add a little more water.

2. In a bowl, combine the chopped onion, capsicum, carrot, coriander, and crumbled paneer. Add salt and red chili flakes to taste. Mix well.

3. Heat the old school sandwich maker or griddle over medium heat and lightly grease it with oil.

4. Pour a ladleful of batter onto the pan and spread it out evenly then put the veggies mixture and again the batter to make a sandwich.

5. Cook until the underside is golden brown and crisp. Flip and cook the other side until golden and cooked through.

6. Serve the no bread sandwiches hot with your favorite chutney.

Enjoy your healthy and delicious no bread sandwich!

✨ Date & Walnut Cake ✨

Hi, I am Tarneet 🙋🏻‍♀️
And this is my most viral recipe of 2023 with over 2,000 recreations. 
You need to give this one a try because it has no Maida, no added sugar and is made with whole wheat flour & tastes absolutely divine🥰

25 Dates (pitted) (197g) 
(1 + 1/2 cups) Hot Milk (375g) 
1/2 cup Melted Butter/Vegetable Oil(95g)
1 cup Whole wheat Flour (120g) 
1/2 tsp Baking Powder 
1 tsp Baking Soda 
1/2 cup Walnuts (chopped)  50gm 

Method:
* Soak the pitted dates in Hot milk for 1 hour so that they become super soft.

* Add in your dry ingredients and whisk. 
* Transfer the batter to a 6’inch lined tin, top it up with walnuts and bake at 180 degrees Celsius for about 50 mins or until a skewer inserted in comes out clean!

recipes.caption:
Dhokla Idli Recipe

- 1 cup besan (gram flour)
- 1/2 cup semolina (rava)
- 1/2 cup yogurt (dahi)
- 1/2 cup water (adjust as needed)
- 1 tbsp lemon juice
- 1 tsp Eno fruit salt or baking soda
- 1 tsp ginger-green chili paste
- 1 tsp sugar
- Salt to taste

For Tempering:
- 1 tbsp oil
- 1 tsp mustard seeds
- 1 tsp sesame seeds
- 1-2 green chilies, slit
- A few curry leaves
- A pinch of asafoetida (hing)
- 1/4 cup water
- 1 tsp sugar

1. Prepare the Batter: In a mixing bowl, combine besan, semolina, yogurt, water, lemon juice, ginger-green chili paste, sugar, and salt. Mix well to form a smooth batter. Adjust the consistency with more water if needed. The batter should be thick but pourable. Let the batter rest for 15-20 minutes.

2. Steam the Idlis :Grease idli moulds with a little oil. Just before steaming, add Eno fruit salt or baking soda to the batter. Mix gently and immediately pour the batter into the idli moulds. Steam the idlis in an idli steamer or pressure cooker (without the whistle) for about 10-12 minutes or until a toothpick inserted comes out clean.

3. Prepare the Tempering: In a small pan, heat oil. Add mustard seeds and let them splutter. Add sesame seeds, slit green chilies, curry leaves, and asafoetida. Sauté for a few seconds. Add 1/4 cup of water and 1 tsp of sugar. Bring it to a boil and then turn off the heat.

4. Once the idlis are done, remove them from the moulds and place them on a serving plate. Pour the prepared tempering over the idlis, ensuring they are well-coated.

5. Garnish and Enjoy: Garnish with freshly chopped coriander leaves and freshly grated coconut, serve hot with green chutney or tamarind chutney.

2. Steam the Idlis :Grease idli moulds with a little oil. Just before steaming, add Eno fruit salt or baking soda to the batter. Mix gently and immediately pour the batter into the idli moulds. recipes.caption:
My US visa was first rejected in June, 2011. Why? Because I was unmarried or jobless, I guess. My dream was to travel to LA with the last batch of my savings to try my luck at the food network to pursue my dream of being a chef in the food content industry! I wanted to merge my passion for cooking and acting, together. I was shattered when this last attempt to live my dream was rejected (after having already faced multiple rejections in Mumbai in 2010).

After a month out of nowhere I got a call from 'FoodFood' tv channel to come for a life changing audition, later I was told it was through an email I had dropped back in the year 2010 when I was struggling to be in Mumbai. After my audition I was shortlisted to be on Mahachallenge. Life took a turn on that show, I went on to win it and I also met my idol Chef Sanjeev Kapoor.

Then 9 months later - March, 2012 - I was invited to the US to represent Indian cuisine and a young interviewer at the Visa consulate asked "Why was your Visa rejected, I can't understand, also with a polite smile he told me that I didn't have to carry amy newspaper clippings to prove a point. Please teach me more about Indian food" he said. I wish I could explain to him that life had happened to me. If I had gone earlier to the US, who knows I might have struggled all my life. My rejection made me who I am today. This is Arbhi tuk canape that I made for a demo in New York to showcase how beautiful Indian cuisine is. I would not change a single thing about this journey because if you dare to dream, life will happen to you.

recipes.comment_recipe:
Mughlai Anda Masala Recipe

Ingredients:- 
For the Eggs:
 - 5-6 boiled eggs
 - 1 tbsp oil
 - 1/2 tsp chili powder
 - 1/4 tsp turmeric powder
For the Onion Paste:
 - 2 medium onions, roughly chopped
 - 10-12 soaked cashews
 - 1 big piece of chopped ginger
 - 10-12 garlic cloves
 - 4-5 green chilies
 - 1/4 cup water
For the Masala:
 - 4-5 tbsp oil
 - Whole spices: 2 cloves, 2 green cardamom, 1 bay leaf, 1 small cinnamon stick, 3-4 black peppercorns, 1 small piece of javatri, 1 black cardamom
 - 1 tbsp kitchen king masala
 - 1 1/2 tsp garam masala
 - 1 tsp black pepper powder
 - 1/2 cup whisked dahi (yogurt)
 - 1/2 cup water
 - Salt to taste
 - 2 tbsp kasuri methi (dried fenugreek leaves)
 - 3-4 tbsp fresh cream
 - 1/4 cup milk
 - Pinch of garam masala
 - 1 tsp chaat masala
To Finish:
 - Chopped coriander
Method:

1.Heat 1 tbsp oil in a pan over medium heat.
 -Add the boiled eggs, chili powder, and turmeric powder. Fry until golden and slightly crispy, about 5-7 minutes. Remove and set aside.

2. In a blender, combine onions, soaked cashews, ginger, garlic, green chilies, and 1/4 cup water. Blend until smooth.

3. **Cook the Masala:**
 - In a kadai, heat 4-5 tbsp oil over medium heat.
 - Add the whole spices (cloves, green cardamom, bay leaf, cinnamon stick, black peppercorns, javatri, and black cardamom). Sauté until fragrant, about 2-3 minutes.
 - Add the onion paste and cook until golden brown and dry, stirring occasionally, about 7-8 minutes.
 - Add the kitchen king masala, garam masala, and black pepper powder. Sauté for a few minutes.
 - Lower the heat and add the whisked dahi and 1/2 cup water. Cook slowly on low heat for about 7-8 minutes until the oil separates from the masala, stirring occasionally.

4. **Finish the Dish:**
 - Add kasuri methi, fresh cream, milk, pinch of garam masala, and chaat masala. Stir well.
 - Add the fried eggs and cook on low heat for about 5 minutes until the oil separates. Adjust the consistency with more water if needed.
 - Add chopped coriander leaves and mix well.

5. **Garnish and Serve:**
 - Garnish with chopped coriander.
 - Serve hot with rice or naan.

recipes.text: dates and walnut cake - we tried this amazing cake at home with zero sugar and maida and it’s turned out mighty impressive. ingredients: dates 200 g milk 1 ½ cup desi ghee ½ cup wheat flour atta 1 cup baking soda 1 teaspoon baking powder 1/2 teaspoon salt 1/4 teaspoon cacao nibs 1 ½ tablespoon chopped walnuts recipe: soak dates in hot milk for about an hour until they become soft. then blend it and make a fine mixture. now add desi ghee to this puree, you can also add refined oil or extra light olive oil and mix it properly. now sieve all the dry ingredients and add it in the dates and oil mixture until it is lump free. take a greased cake mould and pour the batter in the mould. to this, add cacao nibs and mix them well and garnish with chopped walnuts. bake in a preheated oven at 180°c for 50 minutes and voila, something magical is ready

recipes.caption:

Ingredients:

1 cup Ragi flour 
Salt to taste 
1 tsp oil to coat the bowl in which we will make dough

1/2 cup grated paneer
1 tbsp ginger garlic paste 
1/2 tsp turmeric

Water IF needed 
Dry whole wheat flour or Ragi flour 
Ghee for cooking parathas 

Method: Start by heating 1 cup of water in a pan. Let it come to a full boil then add salt and 1 cup of Ragi flour. Turn stove off and using a spatula/spoon mix the flour. 
Once mixed together cover with a lid & let it sit in the steam for 10 minutes. 
In the meanwhile, coat the bowl (in which you will make the paratha atta in) with oil 
Add the mixed Ragi flour, along with chopped spinach, grated paneer, ginger garlic paste, salt, turmeric and coriander powder.

recipes.caption:
Thai basil chicken✨

For the Sauce:▪️1 Tbsp Soy Sauce▪️1 Tbsp Dark Soy Sauce (or sub regular soy sauce)▪️3 Tbsp Oyster Sauce▪️1 Tbsp Fish Sauce▪️2 tsp Sugar▪️1/4 Cup Water▪️

For the Stir Fry:▪️2 Tbsp Avocado Oil (or other neutral oil)▪️2 Large Shallots, sliced thin▪️4 Cloves Garlic, minced▪️1 Fresno Chili (not very spicy), sliced in thin strips▪️1 Thai Chili (spicy), sliced in thin rounds▪️1 lb. 96/4 Ground Chicken▪️2 Scallions, sliced▪️2 Cups Fresh Basil or Thai Basil Leaves▪️4 Cups Cooked White Rice, for serving▪️

For the Eggs:▪️1 Tbsp Avocado Oil (or other oil)▪️4 Eggs▪️

🌱Vegan Modification: Sub in firm tofu for chicken (crumble it up with your fingers), vegan oyster sauce for oyster sauce, and leave out the fish sauce and eggs

1️⃣ Mix together the ingredients for the sauce and set aside.
2️⃣ In a large wok or pan preheated over medium-high heat, add the avocado oil and shallots. Stir fry for 2-3 mins until tender, then add the garlic, fresno chili, and Thai chili. Stir fry for 1 more min.
3️⃣ Add the ground chicken and stir fry for 3-4 mins until cooked through, breaking it up into small irregularly sized pieces. 
4️⃣ Pour on the sauce and add the scallions. Stir fry 2-3 mins until the sauce coats the chicken and gets heated through, then turn off the heat and stir in the basil. Cover to keep warm while you fry the eggs.
5️⃣ In a separate pan preheated over medium heat, add oil to coat the pan then add the eggs. Fry eggs sunny side up with a sprinkle of salt until the white is set but the yolk is still runny. Tilt the pan, scoop up the hot oil with a spoon, and baste the top of the egg white to help it cook through.
6️⃣ Serve the basil chicken over warm rice with fried eggs on top and enjoy!

⏲15 minute prep time + 15 minute cook time

Recipe serves 4 people
recipes.recipe_ingredients:
For the Sauce:
1 Tbsp Soy Sauce
1 Tbsp Dark Soy Sauce (or sub regular soy sauce)
3 Tbsp Oyster Sauce
1 Tbsp Fish Sauce
2 tsp Sugar
1/4 Cup Water
For the Stir Fry:
2 Tbsp Avocado Oil (or other neutral oil)
2 Large Shallots, sliced thin
4 Cloves Garlic, minced
1 Fresno Chili (not very spicy), sliced in thin strips
1 Thai Chili (spicy), sliced in thin rounds
1 lb. 96/4 Ground Chicken
2 Scallions, sliced
2 Cups Fresh Basil or Thai Basil Leaves
4 Cups Cooked White Rice, for serving
For the Eggs:
1 Tbsp Avocado Oil (or other oil)
4 Eggs
recipes.recipe_method:
Mix together the ingredients for the sauce and set aside.
In a large wok or pan preheated over medium-high heat, add the avocado oil and shallots. Stir fry for 2-3 mins until tender, then add the garlic, fresno chili, and Thai chili. Stir fry for 1 more min.
Add the ground chicken and stir fry for 3-4 mins until cooked through, breaking it up into small irregularly sized pieces.
Pour on the sauce and add the scallions. Stir fry 2-3 mins until the sauce coats the chicken and gets heated through, then turn off the heat and stir in the basil. Cover to keep warm while you fry the eggs.
In a separate pan preheated over medium heat, add oil to coat the pan then add the eggs. Fry eggs sunny side up with a sprinkle of salt until the white is set but the yolk is still runny. Tilt the pan, scoop up the hot oil with a spoon, and baste the top of the egg white to help it cook through.
Serve the basil chicken over warm rice with fried eggs on top and enjoy!

recipes.caption:
Why is no one talking about how the way we’re cooking is making us sicker?

Maybe it just hasn’t been on anyone’s radar because it’s not what people want to hear.

Maybe it’s because food companies don’t want us to hear it.

Either way, we’re not talking about it enough.

If you’ve been following me, you’ll know that I’m always talking about why we should cook with water based cooking methods to lower our risks of chronic diseases and premature aging. 

I get a lot of messages from people who never knew water based cooking, like I am here with steam, could actually produce delicious, time-saving dishes. 

Wish I could say I invented all this but water based cooking is as old as it gets and many of my recipes are pulled from older cuisines and generational dishes from my own family.

If you’ve never tried water eggs or steamed eggs before, you’re going to love this one. 

I said two ingredients in the video, but honestly water doesn’t even count!

There are so many versions of water eggs. This is the Chinese version and I’ll actually be sharing the Japanese  version (Chawanmushi) next!

Ingredients:
2 Eggs
Warm water (double the volume of eggs)
Pinch of salt 
Optional toppings: sesame oil, soy sauce, sliced green onions 

Directions:
1. Measure the volume of the eggs you are using. Beat the eggs until smooth.
2. Add double the volume of warm water (2:1 water to eggs ratio). Add sprinkle of salt. Mix.
3. Pour mixture through a sieve into a heat-safe bowl that will fit into your steamer. Cover bowl with a heat safe plate. This recipe will make 2 bowls and you can cook them individually or together depending on the size of your steamer.
4. Steam for 10-12 minutes on low heat.
5. Remove and cut into squares, then add toppings.

Enjoy!

recipes.caption:
Mexican Burrito Bowl !! 

Is this your fav too ??

Serves 3 

Saute veggies :
1 tbsp olive oil
1/2 cup yellow & red bell pepper, sliced
1/2 cup zucchini 
1 onion, sliced
Salt to taste
1 tsp oregano
Heat oil in a pan. Add in the bell peppers & onions. Add in the salt & oregano & saute till the onions brown a little. Remove from heat & keep aside. Can use veggies of choice 

Corn salad
1 tsp olive oil
3/4 cup corn
1/4 cup coriander leaves
Salt to taste & chilli powder 
Squeeze lemon juice 
Heat oil in the same pan. Add in the corn, cook add salt, chili powder & coriander. Saute till it slightly browns. Take it off heat & keep aside.

Herbed rice : 
1 cup rice cooked 
1 tsp chopped garlic 
2 tsp butter or oil 
1/4 cup coriander
Salt to taste
Chilli flakes 
Squeeze lemon juice 
Add the rice, coriander & salt to the same pan. Mix it well & take it off heat. Keep aside.

Rajma : 
1 tbsp oil
1 bay leaf
1 onion, finely chopped
1 tomato, finely chopped
2 tsp ketchup
Salt to taste
1 cup kidney beans, boiled
1/2 cup water
2 tsp Kashmiri red chili powder 
2 tsp cumin powder 
Water 1/2 cup 

Heat oil in a pan. Add in the bay leaf & onions & saute for 2 minutes. Add in the tomatoes & salt & cook till the tomatoes soften. Add in the kidney beans & & smash the kidney beans little. Add all spices & cook for 2-3 minutes. Add water and let it cook for a while

Salsa
1/2 onion, finely chopped
2 tomato, finely chopped
2 green chilli, finely chopped
3 tbsp coriander, finely chopped
1 tbsp lemon juice
Salt to taste
1/4 tsp pepper powder
2 tsp ketchup or sriracha sauce 
Mix all the ingredients together.
You can also add all the ingredients to a chopper and chop it up finely. Then add lemon juice and salt.

Healthy sour cream-
1/2 cup hung curd
1tbsp Fresh Cream optional 
1tsp lemon juice or more
Salt pinch 

Assembly
In a large bowl, add in the rice, sauteed veggies, kidney beans, sour cream, corn & salsa. Top it with some lettuce optional, cheese, Nachos if you have & tobasco & enjoy :)

recipes.text: ultimate homemade cheese 👇😍 must try ✅ 1️⃣ take 2 l of milk in a pan slightly heat it to the point that your fingers can bear it. turn the flame off. 2️⃣ add 1tbsp vinegar and stir, repeat this step until the milk is completely curdled. it will take approximately 5tbsp vinegar to completely curdle milk. 3️⃣ cover it with a lid and let it rest for 5 to 10 minutes. 4️⃣ meanwhile we will prepare a solution of 1tbsp water , 1tsp citric acid , 1tsp baking soda. this acts as an emulsifiers that helps to blend cheese into a smooth paste. 5️⃣ now add curdled cheese, above solution, 5 to 10 g of butter, 1/3 cup of milk into a blender ( reduce the quantity of milk, if you want to have a solid cheese block ) and blend together 6️⃣ if you’re not adding the flavours do it then add salt in the above step . 7️⃣ now at flavours like chopped jalapeños, olives, sun-dried tomatoes, crispy garlic. 8️⃣ mix it well store it in a greased container overnight. 9️⃣ enjoy with your sandwiches, pasta or any other dish.

recipes.caption:

My new digital cookbook will be out June 27th save the date 😍🙌🏽

Macros (x2 servings): 609 calories |57g P | 16g C | 37g F

1.5 lb chicken thigh, bonelesss skinless 
4 tbsp soy sauce
black pepper, to taste
2 tbsp oyster sauce, 
1 tbsp honey
2 tsp cornstarch 
1/2 red onion
5 cloves garlic
1 lemon
1 Cilantro bunch, roughly chopped 🌿 

Instructions:
1. Preheat your pan on high for 2-3 mins then add 1 tbsp avocado oil and sauté the chicken for 6-7 minutes
2. Next add in the onion and garlic and sauté together for another 2-3 minutes. 
3. Finally, finish off with the lemon and lots of cilantro. Sauté on high heat for 1 more minute. Then turn heat off and let rest for 3-4 minutes.
4. Serve over rice and enjoy you lil chunky monkey 😍

recipes.caption:
COOKIE DOUGH COTTAGE CHEESE ICE CREAM ✨ // SAVE + FOLLOW @jar.of.lemons! // So many of you asked for this one. I could not be more obsessed! Made with cookie dough protein bites (that are optional), chocolate chips, oat flour, and almond butter. This healthy ice cream recipe is next-level! 🙌🏻 Here’s the recipe:
⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀
- 3 cups cottage cheese
- 1/3 cup maple syrup
- 1 teaspoon vanilla
- 2 Tablespoons oat flour
- 1/4 cup mini chocolate chips (add more for topping)
- 2 Tablespoons creamy almond butter (add more for topping)
⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀
Cookie Dough Bites
- 1/4 cup almond flour
- 1/4 cup vanilla protein powder
- 1/4 teaspoon salt
- 1/4 cup maple syrup
- 1/2 cup creamy almond butter
- 1/2 teaspoon vanilla
- 1/4 cup mini chocolate chips
⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀
1. Blend cottage cheese, maple syrup, vanilla, oat flour, and almond butter until smooth.
2. Pour into an ice cream container.
3. Mix the cookie dough bites ingredients together, roll into bites, then add into the ice cream (you can save some for extra toppings).
4. Cover and freeze for 4-6 hours.
5. Be sure to thaw the ice cream on the countertop for at least 15-20 minutes, then break it up a bit and mix before scooping!
6. Add any extra toppings and enjoy! :)
⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀
>> Be sure to follow @jar.of.lemons for more healthy ice cream recipes!! What do you want to see next?
⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀
TIPS:
- Be sure to thaw the ice cream a bit before scooping. 
- If you have a Ninja Creami (link in my highlights), this recipe works great in that!
- Use high quality cottage cheese for best results.
⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀
⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀

recipes.recipe_ingredients:
3 cups cottage cheese
1/3 cup maple syrup
1 teaspoon vanilla
2 Tablespoons oat flour
1/4 cup mini chocolate chips (add more for topping)
2 Tablespoons creamy almond butter (add more for topping)
Cookie Dough Bites
1/4 cup almond flour
1/4 cup vanilla protein powder
1/4 teaspoon salt
1/4 cup maple syrup
1/2 cup creamy almond butter
1/2 teaspoon vanilla
1/4 cup mini chocolate chips
recipes.recipe_method:
1. Blend cottage cheese, maple syrup, vanilla, oat flour, and almond butter until smooth.
2. Pour into an ice cream container.
3. Mix the cookie dough bites ingredients together, roll into bites, then add into the ice cream (you can save some for extra toppings).
4. Cover and freeze for 4-6 hours.
5. Be sure to thaw the ice cream on the countertop for at least 15-20 minutes, then break it up a bit and mix before scooping!
6. Add any extra toppings and enjoy! :)

recipes.recipe_ingredients:
8 chicken thighs, bone-in, skin-on
2 tablespoons olive oil
¼ cup plain yogurt, I used Balkan-Style but any works
½ tablespoon salt, to taste
¼ tablespoon pepper, to taste
1 ½ tablespoons dried oregano
2 lemons, juiced
6 cloves garlic, unpeeled
recipes.recipe_method:
Add the chicken to a baking dish with the olive oil and yogurt. Season with salt, pepper, and oregano. Add the juice of 2 lemons and add the squeezed lemon pieces to the dish as well. Add the garlic. With clean hands, massage the mixture well to evenly distribute the spices. Let the chicken marinate in the fridge for at least 1 hour or up to overnight. (If you don't let it marinate for 1 hour it will still be delicious but not as tender.)
Preheat the oven to 400F (200C)
Bake, uncovered, for 45 minutes to 1 hour depending on the size of the thighs. The chicken is done when a meat thermometer inserted in the thickest part of a piece of chicken registers 165F (74C).
If you want to crisp up the skin you can put it under the broiler for the last few minutes of cooking, but keep a close eye on it as it can burn quickly.
Enjoy the chicken on salad, mashed potatoes, in wraps, with rice, or with any side you like.

recipes.recipe_ingredients:

150g medjool Dates
30g shredded coconut
40g Dark chocolate, melted (I used 70%)
Pinch of Salt
recipes.recipe_method:
In a food processor add cashews, dates and shredded coconut and salt.
Blitz for a few minutes until the ingredients are well incorporated. It’s ready when the dough is not crumbling anymore and it compact itself when you squish it with your finger.
Divide into 18 cookie shapes and make a hole in the middle with your thumb (to make space for the chocolate).
Place the cookie balls on a tray with baking paper on top.
Leave in the freezer for 20-30 minutes until the dough is firm.
Take out of the freezer and add the melted chocolate on top.
Put back in the freezer for 5-10 minutes so the chocolate hardens up.

recipes.recipe_ingredients:
3 tablespoon unsalted butter
8 oz kataifi
3 tbsp tahini
¼ teaspoon salt
16 oz milk chocolate bars roughly chopped
10½ oz pistachio cream
any color candy melts for decoration, melted optional
recipes.recipe_method:
Remove kataifi from freezer to defrost for 1-2 hours. This will make chopping it easier, or shred in a food processor. Melt butter in large pan on medium heat and add kataifi, toasting it for 8-10 mins or until golden brown. Transfer to large mixing bowl and allow to cool completely.
Add pistachio cream, tahini, and salt to cooled kataifi. Mix until well combined and set saide.
Optional: melt any decorating candy melts in small bowls using the microwave. Drizzle desired decorations in chocolate mold, and chill in fridge for 10 mins.
Melt the milk chocolate in a large bowl also using the microwave, or alternatively over a double boiler. If you wish to temper your chocolate, reserve a small handful of chocolate and melt the rest until it reaches 113℉ (45℃). Remove bowl from the heat and stir in the reserved pieces until it melts in. Cool chocolate until it reaches 84-86℉ (28-30℉).
Pour milk chocolate into mold. Tilt mold sideways or upside-down to allow excess chocolate to drip off back into chocolate bowl. We're trying to layer a thin even coating. You can also use an offset spatula to scrape off all extra chocolate. We will be re-melting the chocolate bowl, so avoid wasting any! Once you finish the first layer, tap mold on the counter a few times to allow chocolate to settle and to get rid of any air bubbles. Transfer back to fridge for another 10 mins to set.
Spoon filling into chocolate mold and spread evenly. Be sure to leave room for the final chocolate layer - do not overfill. Chill mold in fridge for 10 more mins.
Re-melt (or temper) milk chocolate. Then, pour over filling and spread evenly to seal in the filling. Tap mold again gently a few times on counter to create a smooth finish. Chill mold in fridge for 1-2 hours minimum before enjoying. Carefully detach finished bars from mold. Keep refrigerated.

Ingredients:

Turmeric (a pinch)
Chopped onions (to taste)
Chopped tomato (to taste)

Instructions:
Blend the Base:
In a blender, add the block of soft tofu, 30g of chickpea flour or sattu, a little water, salt, and a pinch of turmeric.
Blend the mixture until it is completely smooth.

Prepare the Mixture:
Pour the blended tofu and chickpea flour mixture into a bowl.
Add the chopped onions, tomato, capsicum, and green chilies to the bowl.
Stir well to combine all the ingredients.

Cook the Omelette:
Heat a pan over medium heat and spray it with a little oil.
Pour the tofu and chickpea flour mixture into the pan and spread it evenly.
Cook the omelette until it is fully set and golden brown on both sides, flipping carefully as needed.

recipes.caption:
Handvo Bites 

Here’s a fun twist on the classic Gujarati handvo, perfect for breakfast! These bite-sized delights are crispy, wholesome & a breeze to whip up. Just the fuel you need to kickstart your day, so let’s get cooking! #EasyMorningEats

Ingredients:
1 cup Rice
½ cup Chana Dal
¼ cup Tuar Dal
2 tbsp Urad Dal
½ cup Dahi
1 tbsp Ginger Green Chilli paste
Pinch of Hing
¼ tsp Haldi
¼ tsp Red Chilli Powder
½ tsp Lemon Juice
½ cup Corn Kernels steamed
¾ cup Doodhi grated
½ cup Carrot grated
¼ cup Coriander leaves chopped
1 tsp Eno

Tempering:
Oil
Mustard Seeds
White Sesame
Curry Leaves 

Method:
- Transfer rice and dals into a bowl and rinse well using water
- Soak in water for 4 hours 
- Drain out the water and transfer into a blender with dahi and grind it into a thick batter (make sure it is thick)
- Whisk the batter for 7-10 mins to make it light and fluffy to avoid using eno 
- Add in all the other ingredients and lastly add eno, if you’re not whisking the batter
- Prepare your paniyaram pan by heating it 
- Add some oil, mustard seeds, sesame & curry leaves in each cavity
- Followed by a spoonful of the batter and cook it on low flame till golden brown from both sides
- Serve hot with green chutney and enjoy!
