recipes.title: Ranginak Date Bark
recipes.author: linajabbari
recipes.text: ranginak date bark is the best date bark you’ll ever have. as a person who has made much date bark, you can trust me. ranginak is an existing persian date dessert, i just flattened it into bark form. the process of cooking the flour in hot butter makes your house smell incredible. just keep an eye on it because it goes from toasted to burnt real quick. 16 pitted medjool dates 1 c walnuts 1/2 c (112g) unsalted butter, melted 1 c oat/ wholewheat flour 1 tsp cinnamon 1/2 tsp cardamom pinch of salt 1 c pistachio slivers/ desiccated coconut/ nut of choice ground up in a frying pan, toast the walnuts on medium-high heat, stirring every so often until fragrant (5-8 minutes) and set aside. in the same pan, switch heat to low and melt the butter while the butter melts, pit and flatten the dates. arrange walnuts on top and press (slightly crush) i used a rolling pin to help flatten the walnuts. go back to the butter, turn the heat to medium-high and combine the flour with a rubber spatula. keep stirring, making sure to scrape the base so it doesn’t burn until it thickens up slightly. take off heat when it smells toasty and fragrant - kinda like popcorn. mix in the cinnamon, cardamom and salt. pour the mixture on top of the dates. let it cool for about 5 mins. sprinkle the ground pistachio on top and press down gently but firmly. allow it to cool and set in the fridge for a couple hours before slicing. enjoy!!!!

recipes.title: Patra Dhokla
recipes.author: sanjana.feasts
recipes.text: patra dhokla. a 2-in-1 indian snack experience like no other! if you like spicy, savoury indian food, you’ll adore this love child of two tea-time snack heroes. the batter for the fluffy part (khaman/dhokla) is made from gram flour which is first soaked and then aerated to create all those spongy bubbles. the squish gives me life! the top is made from a mosaic of patra, another snack prepared with colocasia leaves (elephant ears) spread with tamarind-spiked batter. it’s sharper than grandma’s wit. roll them up and steam until they’re bouncy. i pull them together as if i’m making an upside-down cake and then steam until they look like they’re in a committed relationship. tadka of mustard seeds, sesame, curry leaves, asafoetida and chillies on top. full recipe link is in my bio, or google ‘sanjana patra dhokla’ for the full video, ingredients and method🤘🏽
recipes.caption:
Patra Dhokla. A 2-in-1 Indian snack experience like no other! If you like spicy, savoury Indian food, you’ll adore this love child of two tea-time snack heroes.

The batter for the fluffy part (Khaman/dhokla) is made from gram flour which is first soaked and then aerated to create all those spongy bubbles. The squish gives me LIFE!

The top is made from a mosaic of Patra, another snack prepared with colocasia leaves (elephant ears) spread with tamarind-spiked batter. It’s sharper than grandma’s wit. Roll them up and steam until they’re bouncy.

I pull them together as if I’m making an upside-down cake and then steam until they look like they’re in a committed relationship.

Tadka of mustard seeds, sesame, curry leaves, asafoetida and chillies on top.

recipes.caption:
Pine Cone Brownies 🎄 (gluten-free, vegan, paleo friendly)

These brownies are seriously the cutest and make such a fun dessert to share around the holidays 🥰 They are pretty easy to make, and you can use a boxed brownie mix to save some time! I made mine gluten, dairy, egg, and refined sugar-free because I have food sensitivities 🤗 

*Go to the link in my profile where you can find the full printable recipe and details!!*

Save and follow for more fun, healthier holiday recipes ❤️

Ingredients:
• GF Fudgey Brownie mix of choice(@simplemills works best)
• Sliced almonds(If you can't do almonds, use cereal flakes instead)
• 9 oz chocolate chips(@hukitchen Hu Gems works best)
• 1-2 tsp coconut oil(use more if your chocolate is very thick)
• Powdered sugar or powdered monk fruit

Directions:
1) Make your brownie mix accordingly to the instructions(make sure to not over bake them so they will be somewhat gooey in the middle and easy to work with) Bake your brownie mix and then let it cool down for a few minutes.
2) Take the baked brownie mixture and remove any really crispy parts then form into about 12 cone shapes.(kinda like you would a cake pop)
3) Place the almond slices in and around the brownie cones(carefully because they are fragile), making the pine cone look full with "scales."
4) Place the pine cones on a parchment paper lined sheet pan, and stick in the freezer for 30 minutes.
5) Melt the chocolate chips with the coconut oil by heating in a bowl in the microwave in 30-second increments.(Or use a double boiler).
6) Take the pine cones out of the freezer and carefully coat each one with the melted chocolate. Place the pine cone brownies back on the parchment paper to set.
7) Sprinkle some powdered sugar on top for a frosted look and enjoy!

Note: If your brownies didn't turn out as soft, try crumbling them and mixing with a little bit of frosting like you would a cake pop 👌 You can also try making chocolate cake instead of brownies for this recipe!

recipes.author: two_plaid_aprons
recipes.text: let’s make honey walnut shrimp just like your chinese takeout! it’s pretty expensive to buy to here’s how to make it at home! full recipe is on our blog, llnk is in our bl0! just type “honey” in the search!❤️
recipes.caption:
Let’s make Honey Walnut Shrimp just like your Chinese Takeout! It’s pretty expensive to buy to here’s how to make it at home! 

Full Recipe is on our Blog, LlNK is in our Bl0! Just type “Honey” in the search!❤️ 

#shrimp #honeywalnutshrimp #chinesetakeout #easyrecipes #reel #recipes
recipes.recipe_ingredients:
Shrimp marinade:
1 pound jumbo shrimps peeled and deveined (we used 26/30 shrimps)
1 teaspoon Shaoxing rice wine (optional)
¾ teaspoon salt
1 TBSP cornstarch or potato starch
Shrimp batter:
1 large egg
½ cup potato starch packed
4 tablespoons oil any neutral oil
For the sauce:
4 tablespoons Kewpie mayo or regular mayo
3 tablespoon sweetened condensed milk
1 tablespoon honey
1 teaspoon lemon juice (optional)
For the candied walnuts:
½ cup walnut (halves or pieces)
3 tablespoons granulated sugar
1 tablespoon water
recipes.recipe_method:
Marinade the shrimps:
In a bowl, season shrimps with Shaoxing rice wine and salt. Mix until well combined.
Add the cornstarch and mix until the shrimps are evenly coated. Set aside to marinade while you prepare the other ingredients.
Make the candied walnuts:
In a medium size pan over medium heat, combine the granulated sugar and water. Bring to a simmer and let the sugar cook until it becomes an amber color. Stir occasionally if necessary. Be very careful as the sugar will be super hot! Also, keep a close eye on the sugar once it becomes golden in color. It can go from amber to burnt in seconds.
Once the sugar caramelized to an amber color, add the walnut and mix until all the nuts are well coated.
Immediately transfer the candied walnuts to a parchment paper and separate the nuts as best as possible. Set the candied walnuts aside and let them cool until needed.
Prepare the sauce:
Into a large pan, combine the mayo, condensed milk, honey, and optionally, lemon juice. Mix until well combined. Set the sauce aside until needed.
Batter the shrimps:
In a mixing bowl, combine the potato starch, egg, and oil. Mix thoroughly until smooth and well combined.
Add the marinated shrimps and mix until all the shrimps are evenly coated with batter.
Make the honey walnut shrimps:
Heat 1 to 2 inches of oil in a wok or pan to 375°F. Also prepare a plate lined with paper towels.
Once the oil is hot, carefully place the shrimps into the oil, one at a time. Fry in batches if needed. Let the shrimps fry for about 3 to 5 minutes, until the shrimps are just cooked and looks golden. Remove the shrimps from the oil and let it drain on the prepared plate with paper towels.
When all of the shrimps are fried, heat the prepared sauce over medium heat until warm. Turn off the heat and add the shrimps along with the candied walnuts. Toss until everything is evenly coated.
Serve the honey walnut shrimps immediately and enjoy with some steamed broccoli and/or rice!

recipes.caption:
Creamy Mushroom Soup 

Mushroom lovers this Mushroom soup is a must try this winters 

It’s like a hug in a bowl, warm and comforting and makes for a perfect dinner which is light as well as keeps you full. 

The soup has my favourite ingredient - California walnuts - that adds mild sweetness and nutty aroma. It also adds rich and creamy taste as we blend it to puree as well as a nutty texture to our soup. California walnuts are versatile and adds delightful burst of flavour to the dishes we add it in along with enhancing nutrition. 

Ingredients:- 
* 3 tbsp olive oil
* 3 tbsp butter
* 1 large onion, chopped
* 8-10 cloves garlic, minced
* 1 packet mushrooms, cleaned + sliced 1/2 inch thick
* 1/4 cup chopped California walnuts 
* salt and pepper to taste
* 1 tsp red chili flakes optional
*  2 tbsp  all purpose flour
*  2.5 cups water
* 1 Maggi stock cube
* 1 tbs fresh thyme optional 
* 1 tsp oregano 
* 1/4- 1/3 cup fresh cream as preference 

🍄Add your olive oil and butter and melt
on medium heat, add in the onion and saute for 5 minutes. Stir in the garlic for 30 seconds. Add in the mushrooms 
Stir it all to saute for 2-3 minutes. 
🍄 Next add in chopped walnuts and cook for about 10 minutes until it all caramelises 
🍄Next, sprinkle on the flour and stir to coat all. Cook for 2 minutes Pour in veg stock or water + veg stock cube. Mix well and let it boil 
🍄Add In salt pepper and  herbs  and bring to a boil.Lower the heat to simmer COVERED, for 10 minutes, stirring occasionally. Add cream and mix 
🍄Transfer about half of the soup to a mini food processor or blender to puree. Add it back into the pot and mix

1 large onion, chopped
8-10 cloves garlic, minced
1 packet mushrooms, cleaned + sliced 1/2 inch thick
1/4 cup chopped California walnuts
salt and pepper to taste
1 tsp red chili flakes optional
2 tbsp  all purpose flour
2.5 cups water
1 Maggi stock cube
1 tbs fresh thyme optional
1 tsp oregano
1/4- 1/3 cup fresh cream as preference
recipes.recipe_method:
Add your olive oil and butter and melt
on medium heat, add in the onion and saute for 5 minutes. Stir in the garlic for 30 seconds. Add in the mushrooms
Stir it all to saute for 2-3 minutes.
Next add in chopped walnuts and cook for about 10 minutes until it all caramelises
Next, sprinkle on the flour and stir to coat all. Cook for 2 minutes Pour in veg stock or water + veg stock cube. Mix well and let it boil
Add In salt pepper and  herbs  and bring to a boil.Lower the heat to simmer COVERED, for 10 minutes, stirring occasionally. Add cream and mix
Transfer about half of the soup to a mini food processor or blender to puree. Add it back into the pot and mix

recipes.title: One-Pot Tandoori Chicken Rice
recipes.author: sadias_haq
recipes.text: ✨one pot tandoori chicken and rice✨ chicken: 6 boneless skinless chicken thighs 2 tbsp tandoori masala (i’ve used shaan) 1 tbsp coriander powder 1 tbsp cumin powder 1 tbsp paprika powder 1 tsp chilli powder 2 tsp salt 2 tsp black pepper powder 1 lemon worth of lemon juice 2 tbsp ginger and garlic paste 3 tbsp greek yoghurt rice: 2 cups basmati rice (washed and soaked for 30 mins) 4 tbsp olive oil 1 large diced 1 green pepper diced 2 tbsp tomato purée 1 tsp coriander powder 1 tsp cumin powder 2 tsp red chilli flakes (or more for more spicy) 1/2 tsp turmeric powder 1 tsp salt or according to taste 3 cups boiling water dissolved with 1 chicken stock cube 1. marinate chicken in all the spices listed 2. heat a large pan with olive oil and fry the chicken for 4 mins on each side. doesn’t need to be fully cooked at this point 3. set aside and in the same pan, fry onions and add a splash of water to prevent the pot from burning 4. add green peppers and garlic. cook till onions have soften 5. add the rice spices and tomato paste. cook for 2 mins 6. add the soaked and drained basmati rice. toast the rice with the masala for 5 mins continuously mixing the rice to prevent burning (be gentle don’t break the grains) 7. add 3 cups of chicken stock and bring to a boil. let the liquid evaporate. 8. when the water has dried, re add the chicken thighs and cover the pot. put flame on lowest setting and let the rice cook for 30 mins in the steam 9. garnish with fresh coriander and chillies. enjoy

recipes.caption:
Winter pickle♥️✨🥰 Nani’s recipe - Making achar is an ancient food preservation technique and in India, we have so much variety of achar. Pickles are not salt and oil, you eat a very small amount and that has so many benefits esp for our gut health. It’s high time we learn achar making from our dadi nani and pass on this generational wealth to our kids too. 

INGREDIENTS:
🌿1/2 cauliflower(washed & blanched head) cut into small pieces 
🌿1 carrot cut into 1 inch pieces with medium thickness
🌿1/2 radish cut into 1 inch pieces with medium thickness
🌿10-12 green chillies slit 
🌿10-12 garlic cloves 
🌿1 inch ginger
🌿1 tsp turmeric 
Crush ginger and garlic cloves using mortar & pestle. Add to the veggies. Add some turmeric and let it dry in the sun for 4 hours on a clean cotton cloth. If you don’t get sun light then you can dry them under fan. I’m making it the traditional way so sun drying is imp

Make spice mix -
🌿1/4 tsp fenugreek ( methi)
🌿1 tsp black peppercorns
🌿1 tbsp fennel seeds
🌿1 tbsp black mustard
🌿1 tbsp yellow mustard
🌿1 tsp cumin 
🌿1/4 tsp heeng (asafoetida)
🌿 1/4 tsp ajwain(caron seeds)
🌿1 tsp kalonji 
 Roast all these spices on low flame until a bit fragrant. You want slight roasting and not overdo this step
Grind them and add to the sun dried veggies

Heat 
🌿1/2 cup kacchi ghani oil until a light smoke emerges, switch the flame off and let it cool down for 2 mins and then add the hot oil to the veggies

Add
🌿2 tbsp salt ( I’m using pink salt so it’s lighter, be careful & add less if using white)
🌿1 tsp amchur
🌿1 tbsp Kashmiri red chilli
🌿1 tbsp apple cider vinegar (increases shelf life) 

Store in a sterilised glass container. Cover using a cotton/muslin cloth and let it sit in the sun for 2-4 days depending on the amount of sunlight. Shake it a bit everyday. Make sure to not let any moisture get in so use dry spoon while serving this. 

Ps: I like this achar less oily that’s why I have added less oil. You can skip vinegar and add more oil but we prefer it this way!

recipes.text: strawberry sago with nata de coco jellies ingredients: 3 cups strawberries 3/4 cup sago (tapioca pearls) 1 jar of nata de coco (coconut jellies) 2 cups of half and half (this is half milk, half cream mixture) 1/2 cup condensed milk cut the strawberries into cubes. in a bowl, add strawberries and the syrup from the nata de coco jellies. this will help to sweeten the strawberries. set it aside. boil the sago/tapioca pearls on medium low heat for about 10 minutes then remove from heat and cover with lid for 10-15 minutes until it is translucent in color. don’t worry if there if there are tiny specks of white, it’s fine. drain and rinse the in cold water. to your bowl of strawberries, add sago, condensed milk, nata de coco jellies, and half and half. taste and adjust for your sweetness level. refrigerate for at least hours before serving. serve chilled or with crushed ice.

recipes.caption:
PEA + MINT SOUP - SOUP SEASON 🫛

Welcome back to SOUP SEASON, my new series, where I show you how to make 10 of the best soups in town. 

For EPISODE 4, we’re making my PEA + MINT SOUP with a crispy onion topping, which is ready in just 30 minutes 🔥

You can find the full written recipe down below - so let me know if you give it a go in the comments below!

And remember, if you like what you see, make sure to follow for more soup season with me 🤩

INGREDIENTS (serves 4)

900g frozen peas
1 potato
1 onion
4 garlic cloves
1 litre vegetable stock
1tbsp miso paste (optional)
Large bunch of mint
1 lemon
2tbsp olive oil
2tbsp (vegan) butter
Salt
Pepper
Sugar

TO SERVE 

Crispy onions / shallots
(Vegan) cream
Smoked paprika
Toasted sourdough

METHOD

1. Add the oil + butter to a large saucepan over a medium heat. 
2. Finely dice the onion, then add to the saucepan once the butter has melted with a large pinch of salt. 
3. Peel the potato, chop into small cubes, then add to onions + cook until soft (10-15 minutes) 
4. Mince the garlic, add to the pot + fry until fragrant (1 minute). 
5. Add 750g peas, the vegetable stock + miso paste.
6. Simmer for 5/10 minutes, or until potatoes are cooked through. Add a large handful of mint leaves & cover with a lid.
7. Reserve the rest of the peas for garnish - place in a bowl of boiling water for 3 minutes, then into cold water + set aside. 
8. Blend the soup until smooth, then place back in the pot + bring to a simmer. Season to taste with a squeeze of lemon juice, then salt, pepper + sugar if needed.
9. To serve, ladle into bowls, top with a swirl of cream, olive oil, a spoonful of peas, crispy shallots + a sprinkle of smoked paprika. 
10. Toast + butter your sourdough, then dive on in.

recipes.caption:
Comment if you want 30+ Easy Snack Ideas you can try this season, I’ll send them to you!

Today, we have Smashed Broccoli! 
A delicious way to enjoy broccoli. You’ll never be bored of broccoli again once you try this smashed creamy & cheesy broccoli. 

It’s so delicious and you can change it around with different flavours and toppings. 

Smashing your vegetables and roasting them just seems to make them 10x more tasty!

Share this easy recipe, and save it for later!

Before i get asked, you can make it an air fryer too.

Preparation Time: 30 Minutes 
Serves: 2-3

Nutrition Info: (per floret)
Calories: 35 kcal
Protein: 2 grams
Fats: 2 grams
Carbs: 2 grams
Fiber: 1 gram

Ingredients:
* 1 medium broccoli cut into florets.
* 4 Tbsp curd
* 1 Tsp Mustard oil
* 1 Tsp Ginger Garlic Paste
* A few fenugreek leaves/kasuri methi
* Salt & Pepper to taste
* Mozzarella Cheese, 1 Tsp on each floret.

Instructions:
1. In a pot, bring water to a boil.
2. Add in the broccoli florets along with 1/2 Tsp of sugar.
3. On the second boil/after 2-3 Minutes, strain the broccoli.
4. In a bowl, add curd, mustard oil, ginger garlic paste, salt, pepper and fenugreek leaves.
5. Whisk to a smooth and creamy texture.
6. On a baking tray, lined with parchment paper, smash the broccoli florets using a flat surface.
7. Pour in 1 Tbsp of the creamy dip on each broccoli.
8. Top it up with 1 Tsp of Mozzarella on each broccoli.
9. Bake it for 10-15 Minutes at 180 degrees until that cheese is perfectly broiled!
10. Enjoy, serve with dips of choice.

recipes.text: spicy heavy cream eggs 🥹 something freaking magical happens when you fry eggs in heavy cream…it caramelizes and the results are sublime, especially with a bit of salsa macha or chili crisp! i learned this while working in restaurants and it was a game changer! ingredients: •4-5 eggs. •1/4 cup heavy cream. •1 tbsp salsa macha + more for topping. •chives to taste. •salsa macha. directions: 1. preheat a pan for 2 min on high. add in heavy cream and chili crisp. lower heat to medium and simmer for 1 min. 2. add in eggs and cover. cook like this for 2-3 min until the whites set. 3. top with chives, seasoned eggs and chili crisp.

Ingredients:
•4-5 eggs.
•1/4 cup heavy cream.

recipes.caption:
💥GREEN GODDESS CHICKEN & RICE BOWL
.
This is an incredible meal that will have you HOOKED.

I made this HIGH PROTEIN and LOWCARB with my @kaizenfoodco lowcarb rice. Just 6 net carbs and 20g protein! Use code SHREDHAPPENS to save 20% on my kaizen lowcarb pasta or rice.
.
You can bake, airfare, grill, or pan fry the chicken.
.
Here is how to make it:
.
1. Add 2lbs chicken thighs to a bowl. Drizzle with 1-2 tbsp olive oil, the juice of a lemon, a couple generous pinches of salt, pepper, 1 tbsp onion powder & 1/2 to 1 tbsp garlic powder. Mix well, then ideally let this marinate for 2 hours to overnight, but if you want to make it right away you can.
.
2.Bring a pan to medium heat, add 1 tbsp avocado oil, add chicken, and cook it on medium heat. This takes 12-15mins depending on thickness of chicken. I usually cook first side down for 5 mins, flip for 5, flip for 2, then flip for another 1 min.
.
3. Make the green goddess sauce by processing or blending: 1 large handful EACH cilantro, parsley, basil, and chives; a small handful of mint and dill, 1 small shallot, 2 garlic cloves, 1/2 cup creme fraiche, sour cream, or thick yogurt, the zest & juice of 1 lemon, 2 tbsp olive oil, and a generous pinch of salt + pepper. Process well, taste and adjust.
.
4.Make the sumac pickled red onions by thinly slicing a red onion. Add to a bowl, sprinkle with 2-3 pinches salt, 1 to 2 tbsp of sumac, and juice of 1 large lemon. Mix well, then let it sit for about 10-15 mins, stirring a couple of times.
.
5.Finally, the base. I used my Kaizen lowcarb rice, but you can use rice, cauli rice, quinoa, or whatever you like. I boiled my rice for 5 mins in a mixture of salted water & chicken broth.
.
6.When rice is done, add a serving to the bowl, with a heaping handful of greens, some chicken, & pile high with pickled red onions, red radish, fresh herbs, green goddess sauce, & white sesame seeds.
.
Remember you can get my Kaizen lowcarb rice or pasta on my profile and use code SHREDHAPPENS to save 20%, or you can find it on Amazon.
.

.
.

recipes.caption:
Lasooni Methi Malai Paneer and Lemon Jeera Rice!
A great way to spruce up your Diwali dinner for a restaurant style meal at home. Creamy garlic and fenugreek paneer served with some zesty cumin rice. A guaranteed crowd pleaser using ingredients JUST from Asda. #ad

You can honestly get everything you need for a super special Diwali meal under one roof – super handy!

500g paneer
3 onions, sliced
50g cashews
7 cloves garlic
3tbsp ghee
250ml water
1tsp cumin seeds
3 green cardamom
1 bay leaf
1 cinnamon stick
2 green chillies, sliced
75g fresh methi, roughly chopped
1tsp salt
2tsp garam masala
2tsp black pepper
1tsp cumin powder
100ml double cream
1/2tbsp kasuri methi
Handful fresh coriander

Tempering:
1tbsp ghee
2 cloves garlic, sliced
2 green chillies, sliced
1/2tsp chilli powder

Start by chopping the paneer into bite-sized pieces, then soak in boiling water for 30 mins
Heat tbsp of ghee in a pan and sauté the onions, 3 cloves of garlic, and cashews for 10 mins on low heat
Then transfer to a blender jug with 250ml of water and blend till smooth
Heat another 2tbsp of ghee and toast the cumin seeds, cardamom, cinnamon, and bay leaf for 1 minute
Mince the remaining 4 cloves of garlic and add to the pan along with the green chillies. Continue to cook until the garlic has turned golden
Next add the fresh methi and sauté until it has started to wilt
Pour in the onion sauce along with the salt, black pepper, cumin powder, garam masala, and paneer. Mix to combine, then cover the pan and let it simmer on a low heat for 5 minutes
Finish with cream, kasuri methi, and fresh coriander
For the tempering, heat ghee in a pan and sauté the garlic and green chillies until the garlic becomes crispy. Mix in chilli powder and spoon over the paneer before serving

750g cooked Basmati rice (made from 300g raw rice)
1tbsp ghee
2tsp cumin seeds
1 bay leaf
1/2tsp turmeric
2tbsp water
1tsp salt
Juice of 1 lemon

Heat the ghee in a pan + toast the cumin seeds and bay leaf for 30s
Add in the turmeric and splash of water
Then add in the cooked rice and salt, and mix to combine
Finish with lemon juice

recipes.caption:
Caramelized lemon with miso cod 🍋🐟 | recipe

Miso cod is one of my favorite recipes for busy weeknights because it’s both make-ahead and fast-cooking. Cod should taste fresh, mild, and flaky, and this beautiful Wild-Caught Icelandic Cod from @bluecirclefoods is it. Plus it’s @mscecolabel certified, important for preserving our oceans.

Ingredients: (3 serving) 
-  3 Wild-Caught Icelandic Cod (@bluecirclefoods)
- 1 lemon 
Marinade for the cod:
- 1/4 cup mirin
- 1/4 cup sake
- 3 tbsp miso paste
- 1 tbsp sugar

Instruction:
- For caramelized lemon, cut 1 lemon into thin slices and sear it in a pan on medium low heat until it browns
- In a pot, on medium heat, boil the marinade ingredients until well combined. Then let it cool.
- Put the fish in a container then pour it all over the fish
- Keep in fridge for 24-48 hours
- Broil the fish in the oven for 7-10 mins (depending on your oven heat)

recipes.title: Lemon Rosemary Roast Potatoes
recipes.author: harrisonwebb97
recipes.text: how many times do i say potatoes? save this roast potato recipe for christmas🥔 2kg maris piper or king edward potatoes 5 tbsp goose fat 2 rosemary sprigs 2 garlic cloves, crushed lemon rosemary salt 1 tbsp rosemary, freshly chopped 1 tbsp maldon salt zest of ½ a lemon • preheat the oven to 180ºc/350ºf. • peel and quarter the potatoes (or halve smaller ones). wash them under running water to remove the starchy residue until the water is clear. •salt the cold water, add rosemary sprigs and crushed garlic, and simmer for 15-20 minutes until soft. •pour goose fat into a roasting tray. drain and roughen the potatoes in a colander. let them cool for 5 minutes, then coat them evenly in the hot fat using a large spoon. • roast for 1hr 30 minutes, turning every 30 minutes. • make rosemary-lemon salt by combining rosemary and salt in a mortar and pestle, adding lemon zest at the end. • remove the potatoes from the oven, drain on kitchen towels, and generously sprinkle with rosemary-lemon salt. note: any recipe that says they only need to be in for 40-50 minutes are never going to be crispy enough. i keep them in for a minimum of 1/1hr30mins
recipes.caption:
How many times do I say potatoes? Save this roast potato recipe for christmas🥔

2kg Maris Piper or King Edward potatoes
5 Tbsp Goose fat
2 Rosemary sprigs
2 Garlic cloves, crushed

Lemon Rosemary Salt
1 Tbsp Rosemary, freshly chopped
1 Tbsp Maldon salt
Zest of ½ a Lemon

• Preheat the oven to 180ºC/350ºF.

• Peel and quarter the potatoes (or halve smaller ones). Wash them under running water to remove the starchy residue until the water is clear. 

•Salt the cold water, add rosemary sprigs and crushed garlic, and simmer for 15-20 minutes until soft.

•Pour goose fat into a roasting tray. Drain and roughen the potatoes in a colander. Let them cool for 5 minutes, then coat them evenly in the hot fat using a large spoon. 

• Roast for 1hr 30 minutes, turning every 30 minutes.

• Make rosemary-lemon salt by combining rosemary and salt in a mortar and pestle, adding lemon zest at the end.

• Remove the potatoes from the oven, drain on kitchen towels, and generously sprinkle with rosemary-lemon salt.

recipes.recipe_ingredients:
2kg Maris Piper or King Edward potatoes
5 Tbsp Goose fat
2 Rosemary sprigs
2 Garlic cloves, crushed
Lemon Rosemary Salt
1 Tbsp Rosemary, freshly chopped
1 Tbsp Maldon salt
Zest of ½ a Lemon
recipes.recipe_method:
Preheat the oven to 180ºC/350ºF.
Peel and quarter the potatoes (or halve smaller ones). Wash them under running water to remove the starchy residue until the water is clear.
Salt the cold water, add rosemary sprigs and crushed garlic, and simmer for 15-20 minutes until soft.
Pour goose fat into a roasting tray. Drain and roughen the potatoes in a colander. Let them cool for 5 minutes, then coat them evenly in the hot fat using a large spoon.
Roast for 1hr 30 minutes, turning every 30 minutes.
Make rosemary-lemon salt by combining rosemary and salt in a mortar and pestle, adding lemon zest at the end.
Remove the potatoes from the oven, drain on kitchen towels, and generously sprinkle with rosemary-lemon salt.

recipes.recipe_ingredients:
Fish — 250 grams
Turmeric Powder — ½ tsp
Ginger Garlic Paste — 1 tsp
Red Chilli Powder — 1 tsp
Kashmiri Red Chilli Powder — 1½ tsp
Salt — 1 tsp
Tamarind — 1 tbsp
Small Onion (Shallots) — 20
Dry Red Chilli — 7
Water — 3 tbsp
Coconut Oil — ¼ cup
Coconut Oil — 2 tbsp
Small Onion (Shallots), Chopped — 5
Garlic, Chopped — 4
Ginger, Chopped — ½ inch
Curry leaves — 1 sprigs
Coriander Leaves — 1 tbsp
recipes.recipe_method:
Marinate the fish with turmeric powder, ginger garlic paste, red chili powder, Kashmiri chili powder, and salt as required. Mix well and set it aside for 15-20 minutes.
Take a tablespoon of tamarind and soak it until it becomes soft. Roast 15-20 shallots until they turn slightly brown. Add 6 to 7 dried red chilies and roast them for 2 minutes on low flame. Grind the roasted shallots and chilies into a fine paste along with the tamarind water.
In a pan, add coconut oil and fry the marinated fish to a golden brown colour on all sides and keep it aside.
In another pan, heat 1 ½ tbsp of coconut oil. Add 5 chopped shallots, ½ tsp of finely chopped garlic, ½ inch of finely chopped ginger, and a sprig of curry leaves. Stir for about a minute. Add the ground paste and mix it over low flame. Add the fried fish to the mixture and mix till it is coated well with the masala. Give it one final toss, garnish it with coriander leaves and serve it hot with rice.

recipes.title: Eggless Date and Walnut Cake
recipes.author: iamtarneet
recipes.text: ✨ date & walnut cake ✨ your search for the best eggless date cake ends here. you need to give this one a try because it has no maida, no added sugar and is made with whole wheat flour & tastes absolutely divine🥰 25 dates (pitted) (197g) (1 + 1/2 cups) hot milk (375g) 1/2 cup vegetable oil (95g) 1 cup whole wheat flour (120g) 1/2 tsp baking powder 1 tsp baking soda 1/2 cup walnuts (chopped) 50gm method: * soak the pitted dates in hot milk for 1 hour so that they become super soft. * then in a bowl, add flour, baking powder and baking soda. whisk well. * then once the dates become soft, blend them into a smooth paste and transfer to a bowl. add in vegetable oil and mix well. * add in your dry ingredients and whisk. * transfer the batter to a 6’inch lined tin, top it up with walnuts and bake at 180 degrees for about 50 mins or until a skewer inserted in comes out clean! try this out and believe me, you won’t believe how tasty can a date cake be! happy baking ❤️❤️❤️
recipes.caption:
✨ Date & Walnut Cake ✨

Your search for the best eggless Date Cake ends here. You need to give this one a try because it has no Maida, no added sugar and is made with whole wheat flour & tastes absolutely divine🥰

25 Dates (pitted) (197g) 
(1 + 1/2 cups) Hot Milk (375g) 
1/2 cup Vegetable Oil (95g)
1 cup Whole wheat Flour (120g) 
1/2 tsp Baking Powder 
1 tsp Baking Soda 
1/2 cup Walnuts (chopped)  50gm 

Method:
* Soak the pitted dates in Hot milk for 1 hour so that they become super soft. 
* Then in a bowl, add flour, baking powder and baking soda. Whisk well. 
* Then once the dates become soft, blend them into a smooth paste and transfer to a bowl. Add in vegetable oil and mix well. 
* Add in your dry ingredients and whisk. 
* Transfer the batter to a 6’inch lined tin, top it up with walnuts and bake at 180 degrees for about 50 mins or until a skewer inserted in comes out clean! 

Try this out and believe me, you won’t believe how tasty can a Date Cake be! 
Happy baking ❤️❤️❤️

recipes.author: marinawrightwellness
recipes.text: ingredients - 1 ripe banana (approximately 200g) - 2 cups greek yogurt - 1 teaspoon pure vanilla extract - 70g dark chocolate (70% cocoa or higher), chopped or in chips instructions 1. peel the banana and place it in a blender or food processor with the yogurt and vanilla.blend until creamy. 2. pour the mixture into molds or small cups and insert popsicle sticks into each mold or cup. place in the freezer for at least 4 hours. 3. for the chocolate coating. in a microwave-safe bowl, melt the dark chocolate in short intervals, stirring in between, until smooth and fully melted. alternatively, you can melt the chocolate using a double boiler. 4. once the ice cream is frozen solid, remove the molds or cups from the freezer and dip each ice cream pop into the melted dark chocolate, ensuring it’s evenly coated on all sides. 5. place the coated ice cream pops on a parchment-lined tray or plate and return them to the freezer for a few minutes to set the chocolate. recipes.caption:
INGREDIENTS

- 1 ripe banana (approximately 200g)
- 2 cups Greek yogurt 
- 1 teaspoon pure vanilla extract
- 70g dark chocolate (70% cocoa or higher), chopped or in chips

INSTRUCTIONS

1. Peel the banana and place it in a blender or food processor with the yogurt and vanilla.Blend until creamy.

2. Pour the mixture into molds or small cups and insert popsicle sticks into each mold or cup. Place in the freezer for at least 4 hours.

3. For the chocolate coating. In a microwave-safe bowl, melt the dark chocolate in short intervals, stirring in between, until smooth and fully melted. Alternatively, you can melt the chocolate using a double boiler.

4. Once the ice cream is frozen solid, remove the molds or cups from the freezer and dip each ice cream pop into the melted dark chocolate, ensuring it’s evenly coated on all sides.

5. Place the coated ice cream pops on a parchment-lined tray or plate and return them to the freezer for a few minutes to set the chocolate.

(Makes 4. Each ice cream contains about 140 kcal, with 10g of protein, 15g of carbs, and 4.6g of fat)

recipes.recipe_ingredients:
1 ripe banana (approximately 200g)
2 cups Greek yogurt
1 teaspoon pure vanilla extract
70g dark chocolate (70% cocoa or higher), chopped or in chips
recipes.recipe_method:
1. Peel the banana and place it in a blender or food processor with the yogurt and vanilla.Blend until creamy.
2. Pour the mixture into molds or small cups and insert popsicle sticks into each mold or cup. Place in the freezer for at least 4 hours.
3. For the chocolate coating. In a microwave-safe bowl, melt the dark chocolate in short intervals, stirring in between, until smooth and fully melted. Alternatively, you can melt the chocolate using a double boiler.
4. Once the ice cream is frozen solid, remove the molds or cups from the freezer and dip each ice cream pop into the melted dark chocolate, ensuring it’s evenly coated on all sides.
5. Place the coated ice cream pops on a parchment-lined tray or plate and return them to the freezer for a few minutes to set the chocolate.

recipes.title: Red Lentil Hummus
recipes.author: kirstykaminski
recipes.text: move aside chickpeas — for this silky smooth red lentil ‘hummus’ 🧡💪🏼 made in 15 minutes from scratch with a delicious earthy flavor and full of protein! 😍 • ingredients • 1 cup split red lentils, dry 2 cups water juice of 1 lemon 1/2 cup tahini 1 garlic clove 1 tsp salt • method • add the lentils to a sieve and rinse well to get rid of any dirt. bring 2 cups of water to a boil in a small pot, then add the lentils, reduce to a simmer and cook for 10 minutes. drain and rinse with cold water. the lentils should be soft and almost paste like. add to a blender and blend a few seconds until smooth. add the lemon juice, tahini, garlic and salt and blend again. add 2-3 tbsp of water until you’ve reached the desired consistency (it will firm up more once it gets cold). serve with paprika, cumin and a drizzle of olive oil and enjoy!
recipes.caption:
Move aside chickpeas — for this silky smooth RED LENTIL ‘HUMMUS’ 🧡💪🏼 Made in 15 minutes from scratch with a delicious earthy flavor and full of protein! 😍

• INGREDIENTS •
1 cup split red lentils, dry
2 cups water
juice of 1 lemon
1/2 cup tahini
1 garlic clove
1 tsp salt

• METHOD •
Add the lentils to a sieve and rinse well to get rid of any dirt. Bring 2 cups of water to a boil in a small pot, then add the lentils, reduce to a simmer and cook for 10 minutes. 
Drain and rinse with cold water. The lentils should be soft and almost paste like. Add to a blender and blend a few seconds until smooth.
Add the lemon juice, tahini, garlic and salt and blend again. Add 2-3 Tbsp of water until you’ve reached the desired consistency (it will firm up more once it gets cold).
Serve with paprika, cumin and a drizzle of olive oil and enjoy!

recipes.caption:
🫶🏽 The cauliflower at the store was calling my name. It was only $2, so I grabbed some to make this bowl of Maple Lime Roasted Cauliflower and Chickpeas. Just 2 sheet pans and minimal clean up. 😌

Roasted Cauliflower
1 small head of cauliflower, cut into  florets
1 tsp smoked paprika
1/2 tsp ground coriander
1/2 tsp onion powder
1/2 tsp garlic powder
1-2 tbsp avocado oil

Chickpeas
1, 15 oz can of chickpeas, drained and rinsed
1 tbsp avocado oil
1/4 cup walnuts, chopped (optional)
1/2 tsp onion powder
1/2 tsp ground coriander

Marinated Onions
1/4 medium red onion, thinly sliced into strips
1 clove garlic, grated
Zest and juice of 1 lime
1-2 tbsp maple syrup
1 tbsp red wine vinegar
1 tbsp extra virgin olive oil
1/4 cup cilantro, stems removed and minced
1/4 cup dates, chopped
Kosher salt to taste

Preheat the oven to 425F then line 2 baking sheets with parchment paper.

To 1 tray add the cauliflower along with paprika, coriander, onion powder, garlic powder and a generous pinch of salt. Drizzle with a tbsp or more of oil then toss together to evenly coat the cauliflower. Spread the cauliflower pieces out, placing pieces cut side down on the tray. Bake in the oven on the bottom rack for 30 mins, flipping the cauliflower after 20 mins.

To the 2nd tray, add chickpeas and oil. Toss to coat and bake  for 20 mins on the middle rack. Remove and allow to cool for 5-10 mins. Top with the walnuts and spices along with a pinch of salt then toss to coat. Bake for another 10 mins.

While everything bakes, prepare the marinated onions. Add the onions, garlic, lime zest and juice , maple syrup, vinegar, olive oil, cilantro, dates, and a generous pinch of salt. Using clean hands, toss the onions together until fully coated then cover and place in the fridge until everything is done baking.

Transfer the onion mixture to the tray of cauliflower and toss together to coat.

To assemble, serve the roasted cauliflower over your grain or starch of choice then top with the crispy chickpeas and walnuts. Use any of the dressing left in the bowl of marinated onions to drizzle over top then enjoy.

recipes.title: Spicy Salmon Crispy Rice
recipes.author: foodmymuse
recipes.text: spicy salmon + crispy rice…last recipe on our collab and it was delicious!! ingredients: •8 oz sushi grade salmon (chopped pretty small). •1/4 c japanese mayo. •2-3 tbsp chili oil (we used anchefta). •3 tbsp japanese mayo. •1/4 cup scallions. •1 tsp yuzu. •1.5 tsp tamari. •1 tsp sesame oil. •1.5 tbsp + 1/2 tsp cane sugar. •1.5 cup calrose or sushi rice (i cooked mine on a rice cooker, so followed those directions). •3 tbsp rice vinegar. •pinch of salt. •sesame seeds. •serranos. directions: 1. cook your rice and season with a pinch of salt, the rice vinegar and 1.5 tbsp sugar. 2. press into a large mold or a couple smaller ones for about 3/4-1 inch thickness. press in real well and let sit in the freezer for 1 hr 30 min-2 hrs. 3. mix the salmon, mayo, chili oil, tamari, sesame oil and yuzu. mix well. let sit in fridge for 15 min. 4. cut the rice into squares. 5. add some avocado oil to a pan (about 1/2 inch) and preheat on high for 2.5 min. lower to medium and fry the rice until golden, about 10 min total. do not be messing with them. yields about 12 squares. 6. pipe the salmon onto the rice, top with serrano and serve with tamari + lemon.
recipes.caption:
Spicy Salmon + Crispy Rice…last recipe on our collab and it was delicious!! 

Ingredients:
•8 oz sushi grade salmon (chopped pretty small).
•1/4 c japanese mayo.
•2-3 tbsp chili oil (we used Anchefta).
•3 tbsp japanese mayo.
•1/4 cup scallions.
•1 tsp yuzu.
•1.5 tsp tamari.
•1 tsp sesame oil.
•1.5 tbsp + 1/2 tsp cane sugar.
•1.5 cup calrose or sushi rice (I cooked mine on a rice cooker, so followed those directions).
•3 tbsp rice vinegar.
•pinch of salt.

Directions:
1. Cook your rice and season with a pinch of salt, the rice vinegar and 1.5 tbsp sugar.
2. Press into a large mold or a couple smaller ones for about 3/4-1 inch thickness. Press in real well and let sit in the freezer for 1 hr 30 min-2 hrs.
3. Mix the salmon, mayo, chili oil, tamari, sesame oil and yuzu. Mix well. Let sit in fridge for 15 min.
4. Cut the rice into squares.
5. Add some avocado oil to a pan (about 1/2 inch) and preheat on high for 2.5 min. Lower to medium and fry the rice until golden, about 10 min total. Do not be messing with them. Yields about 12 squares.
6. Pipe the salmon onto the rice, top with serrano and serve with tamari + lemon.

recipes.title: Creamy Mushroom Curry
recipes.author: aathirasethumadhavan
recipes.text: the only magic mushroom i’ll ever need… 😜 flavor bomb to another level. creamy, spicy, thicccc and just pure ❤️❤️❤️ recipe (makes 4 servings - per serving 87 kcal) ingredients diced mushrooms 200 g coconut oil 1.5 tsp 1 tak mustard seeds 5-6 curry leaves sliced onion 1 small or shallots 7-8 ginger garlic paste 1 tbsp slit green chill 1-2 sliced tomato 1 medium chilli powder 1.5 tsp turmeric powder 1 pinch coriander powder 1 tsp pepper powder 1 tsp salt and sugar to taste few squeezes of lime juice 150 ml water garam masala 1 tsp paste of 3 tbsp coconut milk and 5 cashew nuts optional - half a stock cube chopped coriander leaves for garnish method 1. splutter mustard seeds and curry leaves in hot coconut oil. 2. add in onion, chilli, ginger garlic paste and cook until golden. 3. add tomato, a pinch of salt and cook it on high until it softens. 4. add in the spices except garam masala, a few tbsp of water and cook for a few mins. 5. add the mushrooms and mix well. 6. add in remaining water and stock cube (if using)and let it come to a simmer. 7. mix in the coconut milk- cashew paste, 8. season with more salt, a pinch of sugar, garam masala and a squeeze of lime. 9. garnish with coriander leaves and enjoy while it’s hot with some steamed rice, roti, bread or even dosa! 😋 .
recipes.caption:
The only magic mushroom I’ll ever need… 😜
Flavor BOMB to another level. Creamy, spicy, thicccc and just pure ❤️❤️❤️
Recipe (makes 4 servings - per serving 87 Kcal) 
Ingredients 
Diced mushrooms 200 g
Coconut oil 1.5 tsp
1 Tak mustard seeds
5-6 curry leaves 
Sliced onion 1 small or Shallots 7-8 
Ginger garlic paste  1 tbsp 
Slit green chill 1-2
Sliced tomato 1 medium 
Chilli powder 1.5 tsp 
Turmeric powder 1 pinch 
Coriander powder 1 tsp
Pepper powder 1 tsp 
Salt and sugar to taste 
Few squeezes of lime juice 
150 ml water 
Garam masala 1 tsp 
Paste of 3 tbsp coconut milk and 5 cashew nuts
Optional - half a stock cube 
Chopped coriander leaves for garnish 

Method 
1. Splutter mustard seeds and curry leaves in hot coconut oil. 
2. Add in onion, chilli, ginger garlic paste and cook until golden. 
3. Add tomato, a pinch of salt and cook it on high until it softens.
4. Add in the spices except garam masala, a few tbsp of water and cook for a few mins.
5. Add the mushrooms and mix well. 
6. Add in remaining water and stock cube (if using)and let it come to a simmer. 
7. Mix in the coconut milk- cashew paste,
8. Season with more salt, a pinch of sugar, garam masala and a squeeze of lime.
9. Garnish with coriander leaves and enjoy while it’s HOT with some steamed rice, roti, bread or even dosa! 😋

recipes.title: Lemon Blueberry Overnight Oats
recipes.author: georginaburgess_
recipes.text: lemon blueberry overnight oats 🫐🍋😍💜 i make these every summer and somehow am only just getting round to sharing the recipe with you guys!! honestly you are gonna be obsessed 🥹 for 2 servings: 1 cup porridge oats 1 cup milk of choice (i used oat milk) 3 heaped tbsp vegan greek yoghurt / coconut yoghurt small pinch salt 1 tsp lemon zest 1 tsp vanilla extract 4 tbsp fresh lemon juice / juice of 2 small lemons 2-3 tsp maple syrup (or to taste) for the blueberry chia jam (this makes extra): 300g blueberries squeeze of lemon 2 tbsp chia seeds 1-2 tbsp maple syrup (to taste) make the overnight oats by stirring everything together in a big bowl - taste test and add more maple or lemon to your taste - then cover and leave to set for 2 hours (or overnight). make the chia jam by adding the blueberries to a pan over a low heat, along with the lemon juice and maple syrup. squish the blueberries down with a masher or back if a fork. let it simmer for 5-10 minutes until the juices have released and it’s gone a rich purple colour. take off the heat and stir in the chia seeds and let it set into a thicker jam texture. you can store this in a jar in the fridge for upto a week. later up and enjoy! 💜💜💜 . . . . . . . . . . .
recipes.caption:
Lemon blueberry overnight oats 🫐🍋😍💜

I make these every summer and somehow am only just getting round to sharing the recipe with you guys!! Honestly you are gonna be obsessed 🥹

For 2 servings:
1 cup porridge oats
1 cup milk of choice (I used oat milk)
3 heaped tbsp vegan greek yoghurt / coconut yoghurt 
Small pinch salt
1 tsp lemon zest
1 tsp vanilla extract 
4 tbsp fresh lemon juice / juice of 2 small lemons
2-3 tsp maple syrup (or to taste)

For the blueberry chia jam (this makes extra):
300g blueberries 
Squeeze of lemon 
2 tbsp chia seeds
1-2 tbsp maple syrup (to taste) 

Make the overnight oats by stirring everything together in a big bowl - taste test and add more maple or lemon to your taste - then cover and leave to set for 2 hours (or overnight).

Make the chia jam by adding the blueberries to a pan over a low heat, along with the lemon juice and maple syrup. Squish the blueberries down with a masher or back if a fork. Let it simmer for 5-10 minutes until the juices have released and it’s gone a rich purple colour. Take off the heat and stir in the chia seeds and let it set into a thicker jam texture. You can store this in a jar in the fridge for upto a week.

Later up and enjoy! 💜💜💜

recipes.caption:
Hummus is FANTASTIC!!! Don't get me wrong... 
I just think it's been pulling the weight of the whole levantine mezze on its back for far too long, and it's time for some other dishes to shine through. Enter... muhammara

Ingredients
5 Red Peppers (Seeded)
1 White Onion
2 Roma Tomatoes
2 Chilis (AND/OR 1 tsp chili powder... this can be added later depending on how spicy you like your food)
Olive Oil
Salt
Black Pepper
2 Tbsp Tomato Paste
2 tsp Cumin Seeds
2 tsp Coriander Seeds
8 Cloves Garlic
1 Tbsp Pomegranate Molasses
100g Walnuts (Chopped and Toasted)
100g Pomegranate Seeds
Parsley
1. Toss the peppers, onion, tomatoes, and chili with oil, salt, and black pepper. Then roast in the oven at 400F/200C for 25-30 mins till slightly blackened.
2. Caramelize the tomato paste in a bit of olive oil for 5 minutes.
3. Toast the cumin and coriander seeds for a couple minutes, then grind to a powder.
4. Remove any blackened veggies from the tray. (The tomatoes need extra time because they have more moisture.) Then add the garlic cloves and Put the tray back in the oven for another 15 mins
5. Peel and discard the pepper skins and then add everything EXCEPT the walnuts to a food processor. After it’s smooth, add the walnuts and pulse a few times till the spread is your desired consistency.
6. TRADITIONALLY, bread crumbs will be added to help with consistency and give the dip more body, but I prefer it to have a denser flavor, and find that by thoroughly roasting the veggies, the dip is not too wet. The pita is enough bread to fill me up.
7. Garnish with pomegranate seeds, some walnuts, parsley, and a final drizzle of pomegranate molasses. Do NOT skip the parsley. It isn’t just for color, but it’s an amazingly crisp undertone in every bite.
8. Enjoy and tag me with your review.

recipes.caption:
It’s fungi season! 🍄 Why not celebrate with some toadstool thumbprint cookies, right?! (Cookies are the best way to celebrate any ocassion, imo.)

I first shared this idea last spring, but now it’s actually mushroom hunting season, so I figured they were worth resharing for those that want to make them in a more fitting season!

We are currently getting a bunch of rain which means that the next dry day will be ripe for the foraging.

I’ve had great luck so far this year with finding about 20 pounds of hen of the woods (maitake,) in our own front yard, and then finding a bunch of turkey tail in the woods. Two powerhouse fungi 💪

I can’t wait to go out this week and see what nature provides!

Until then, I might just whip up another batch of these because they’re really SO good.

Here’s the recipe 👇

Toadstool thumbprint cookies
(Makes about 2 dozen)

1 cup butter, softened (226g)
⅓ cup sugar (70g)
⅓ cup light brown sugar, tightly packed (70g)
2 large egg yolks
1 teaspoon vanilla extract
½ teaspoon almond extract
2 cups all purpose flour (240g)
2 teaspooons cornstarch
½ teaspoon salt
½ cup sugar (for rolling)
½ cup strawberry or other red jam/preserves (105g)

Icing:
½ cup confectioners sugar
1 ½ tablespoons milk
½ teaspoon vanilla

Start by creaming together the butter and sugars in a large bowl, either with a stand mixer or hand mixer, until light and fluffy. Add in vanilla and almond extracts, as well as the egg yolks, and mix well. Add in dry ingredients and mix together slowly. The mixture will seem a bit dry and crumbly, but this is normal. Make sure to scrape the sides of the bowl down well, and feel free to use your hands to finish incorporating all the ingredients.

Using a cookie scoop or simply your hands, grab about a tablespoon of dough and roll it into a ball. Roll the ball in sugar, and then place on lined baking sheet. Flatten a bit with the bottom of a clean glass. Using your fingers, indent to make little mushrooms. Play around a bit to get it right, if necessary.

Chill in the freezer (or outside) for half an hour. While cookies are chilling, preheat oven to 375 F (190 C.)

Cont. in comments…

Using a cookie scoop or simply your hands, grab about a tablespoon of dough and roll it into a ball. Roll the ball in sugar, and then place on lined baking sheet. recipes.recipe_ingredients:
The base
2 eggs
25 g vegetable oil
25 g milk
30 g cake flour
30 g granulated sugar
5 g lemon juice
5 g vanilla extract
Cheesecake
185 g cream cheese (softened)
20 g unsalted butter (softened)
2 egg yolks
15 g granulated sugar
10 g cornstarch
130 g milk
36 g egg white
20 g granulated sugar
5 g lemon juice
5 g vanilla extract
recipes.recipe_method:
Cake Base
1. In a clean bowl, separate the eggs. Keep the egg white bowl cool in the fridge.
2. In another bowl, mix well vegetable oil and milk, add in cake flour, and mix well.
3. Preheat the oven to 302℉(150℃).
4. Take the egg white bowl out of the fridge. Add in lemon juice, granulated sugar and vanilla extract and use a hand mixer to beat until it forms soft peaks. Take a scoop of whipped egg white to fold into the batter until just combined. Pour all the batter back into the whipped egg white and gently fold it in until just combined.
5. Line the baking tray (28*28*2.6cm) with baking mat or parchment paper (don’t grease the pan), pour all the batter into the baking tray, smooth it out and give it a tap or two to break the air pockets. Send into the oven to bake for 18-20 minutes.
6. Take the cake out of the oven right away, and let it cool down on the cooling rack until cool to touch. Release the cake from edges using an icing spatula, turn it upside down and peel off the baking mat. Use a mini cheesecake mold to cut out many small cake bases. Set aside.
Cheesecake
1. In a clean bowl, mix well 2 egg yolks, cornstarch and 15g granulated sugar until well combined. Set aside. Heat the milk until simmer; pour into the egg yolks mixture while whisking quickly to mix them well so you won’t cook the egg yolks. Pour all the mixture back into the saucepan, whisk over medium heat until thickened. Set aside.
2. In another bowl, bring together softened cream cheese and butter, mix until well combined and smooth. Pour in the egg yolks mixture and whisk until well combined. Set aside.
3. In a clean bowl, bring together 36g egg white, 20g granulated sugar, lemon juice, and vanilla extract, use a hand mixer to beat until thickened, can form very very soft peaks. Sift in the batter, and gently fold it in until combined. Pour all the batter into a piping bag.
4. Preheat the oven to 185℃(365℉). Line the baking tray with parchment paper or baking mat. Line each mini cheesecake mold with cake base on the bottom and parchment paper around. Fill each mini cheesecake mold with batter.
5. Grab another baking tray, pour in enough water (enough to last in the oven for 20 minutes), place the first baking tray in it, and send into the oven to bake for 20 minutes, or until the cake surface turns golden brown.
6. Take off the cake molds when they are cool to touch.

recipes.text: khatta moong is a delicious yogurt based moong curry. you need to try it out if you haven’t already! ingredients i used: - 1/2 cup whole moong + water for soaking - salt as needed - 1/4 tsp turmeric - 1/2 cup dahi /fresh yogurt - 1 to 2 tbsp besan/ chickpea flour - 2 tbsp oil - 3/4 tsp mustard seeds - 3/4 tsp cumin seeds - 1/2 tbsp ginger, finely chopped - 1/2 tbsp garlic, finely chopped - few curry leaves - 2 red chillies - 1 to 2 green chillies, finely chopped (adjust as preferred) - salt - red chilli powder - 1/4 tsp turmeric - 1/2 tsp coriander powder - 1/2 tsp cumin powder procedure: - boil moong with salt and turmeric till soft. - in a bowl whisk together dahi and besan. add water and adjust the consistency accordingly. - heat oil in a pan and give tadka with all the remaining ingredients as mentioned above. - fry well and then add dahi besan mixture. cook well for a few mins and add the boiled moong. serve hot with rice and lots of ghee!❤️

recipes.caption:
Recipe ⬇️

Follow @theiranianvegan for more vegan Iranian recipes ☺️

🟡🍚PERSIAN CRISPY RICE // TAHDIG RECIPE🍚🟡

Tahdig literally meaning ‘bottom of the pot’ is the delicious, golden, crunchy layer formed when you cook rice the Persian way.

INGREDIENTS:
- 3 cups basmati rice
- 2 tbsp Himalayan salt
- 1/6 tsp saffron (optional)
- 3 tbsp vegetable oil

METHOD:
1. First, wash and drain the rice 3 times or until the water is not cloudy.

2. Fill a large pot with water (about 10 cups) to boil with 2 tbsp of salt. Once it has come to a boil, add the washed rice and turn the heat the low-medium heat.

3. Boil the rice for 6-7 minutes only, so that it is half cooked. Check the rice by taking a single grain and pressing it between your fingers. It should be still a little hard in the centre.

4. Immediately drain the rice in a colander, and rinse with cold water to stop the cooking process.

5. In a non-stick pot, oil the bottom of the pot with 3-4 tbsp of oil. If using saffron (recommended), mix 1/6 teaspoon ground saffron with 2 tbsp of boiling water. Let it sit for 2-3 mins.

6. Add the saffron water into the oil on the bottom of the pot and brush together make a uniform liquid.

7. Add the half-cooked rice in, spoon by spoon. Once all the rice has been added, create a mound shape by pulling up the sides of the rice. Poke some holes into the rice mound to allow steam to escape.

8. Wrap the lid of the pot in a dishcloth or a damkoni and set the lid on the pot.

9. Add in 1/6 cup of boiling water to the rice.

10. For the first 5 minutes, set the heat to medium. At this point, check to see that steam is beginning to rise in the pot.

11. Turn the heat to low, and leave it on low heat for 45 minutes-1 hour.

12. When ready to serve, take the pot off the heat for a few minutes.

13. Remove the lid. Place a large platter on top of the pot and in a swift motion, turn the platter and pot upside down.

14. If the tahdig is stuck, run the bottom of the pot under cold water.

15. Enjoy with rice and any persian stew (khoresht)!

recipes.title: Mushroom Ghee Roast
recipes.author: flavoursbymounika
recipes.text: mushroom ghee roast😍 ingredients: mushrooms - 400g ghee - 3 tbsp salt as per taste dry red chillies - 10 (adjust as per spice requirement) coriander seeds - 1 tbsp fennel seeds - 1 tbsp black pepper - 1/2 tbsp cumin seeds - 1 tbsp tamarind paste - 1 tsp soaked cashews - 10 garlic cloves - 10 ginger - 1 inch piece curry leaves - 1 sprig coriander leaves water as required i’m using spice grinder which is perfect for both wet and dry grinding. it comes with lockable safety lid with on/off switch also with high power 350w motor. product link in story! preparation method: 👉 soak dry red chilies and cashews in hot water for 15 minutes. 👉add coriander seeds, fennel seeds, cumin, seeds, and black pepper into a pan pan. dry roast them until aromatic. cool down and keep aside. 👉 in a blender add roasted seeds, soaked chillies and cashews, ginger and garlic, tamarind paste and add water to make fine paste. 👉heat a table spoon of ghee in pan and add chopped mushrooms. sauté them for 2 minutes. take out and save for later. 👉heat 2 tbsp of ghee in a pan and add ground masala paste. fry until it separates from pan. add water as per consistency and salt per taste. cook until ghee appears. add sautéed mushrooms and curry leaves and cook for 3 minutes on low flame. add chopped coriander leaves and mix well. flame off and serve it.
recipes.caption:
Mushroom Ghee Roast😍

Ingredients:
Mushrooms - 400g
Ghee - 3 tbsp
Salt as per taste
Dry red chillies - 10 
(Adjust as per spice requirement)
Coriander seeds - 1 tbsp
Fennel seeds - 1 tbsp
Black pepper - 1/2 tbsp
Cumin seeds - 1 tbsp
Tamarind paste - 1 tsp
Soaked cashews - 10
Garlic cloves - 10
Ginger - 1 inch piece
Curry leaves - 1 sprig
Coriander leaves
Water as required 

I’m using @premierkitchen.in spice grinder which is perfect for both wet and dry grinding. It comes with lockable safety lid with on/off switch also with high power 350W motor. Product link in story!

Preparation method:
👉 Soak dry red chilies and cashews in hot water for 15 minutes. 
👉Add coriander seeds, fennel seeds, cumin, seeds, and black pepper into a pan pan. Dry roast them until aromatic. Cool down and keep aside.
👉 In a blender add roasted seeds, soaked chillies and cashews, ginger and garlic, Tamarind paste and add water to make fine paste.
👉Heat a table spoon of ghee in pan and add chopped mushrooms. Sauté them for 2 minutes. 
Take out and save for later.
👉Heat 2 tbsp of ghee in a pan and add ground masala paste. Fry until it separates from pan. Add water as per consistency and salt per taste. Cook until ghee appears. Add sautéed mushrooms and curry leaves and cook for 3 minutes on low flame. Add chopped coriander leaves and mix well. Flame off and serve it.

In a blender add roasted seeds, soaked chillies and cashews, ginger and garlic, Tamarind paste and add water to make fine paste.
Heat a table spoon of ghee in pan and add chopped mushrooms. Sauté them for 2 minutes.
Take out and save for later.
Heat 2 tbsp of ghee in a pan and add ground masala paste. Fry until it separates from pan. Add water as per consistency and salt per taste. Cook until ghee appears. recipes.title: Blueberry Cheesecake Ice Cream
recipes.author: raziyyz
recipes.text: an easy, healthier substitute for ice cream… blueberry cheesecake flavour! the hype is real with this cottage cheese hack. 6 ingredients, creamy, low calorie and packed with protein.👇🏼 - cream mix: • 2 cups (16oz) cottage cheese (i use 2-4% fat) • 3 tbsp light cream cheese • 1/4 cup low calorie maple syrup or any sweetener • 1 scoop vanilla protein powder (i use myprotein whey) • optional: 1/4 tsp salt - blueberry mix: • 1 cup frozen blueberries • 1 tsp honey or any sweetener - directions: • add all “cream mix” ingredients to blender and blend until smooth • add “blueberry mix” to medium heat pot/pan and cook into jam • add half of cream mix to jar/container, followed by half blueberry mix. repeat twice for two layers. • using a fork/knife, swirl the blueberry mix to create an even flavour. • freeze for 3 hours and serve. - notes: • the higher fat content of cottage cheese you have, the less your mix will freeze solid after placing it in the freezer for longer than 3 hours. even if it does, you just need to leave it out to thaw for a few minutes and mix it around before serving. • you can use greek yogurt as a substitute for cottage cheese, but i recommend keeping it for the cheesecake flavour. • you can experiment with all different kinds of frozen fruits. i also love using raspberries. • add your toppings of choice for an extra crunch! - serving size: 3 - calories/macros (per serving): approx. 225 calories • 29g protein • 16g carbs • 4g fat - numbers may slightly vary depen
recipes.caption:
An easy, healthier substitute for Ice Cream… Blueberry Cheesecake flavour! The hype is real with this cottage cheese hack. 6 ingredients, creamy, low calorie and PACKED with protein.👇🏼
-
Cream Mix:
• 2 cups (16oz) cottage cheese (I use 2-4% fat)
• 3 tbsp light cream cheese
• 1/4 cup low calorie maple syrup OR any sweetener
• 1 scoop vanilla protein powder (I use myprotein whey)
• Optional: 1/4 tsp salt
-
Blueberry Mix:
• 1 cup frozen blueberries
• 1 tsp honey OR any sweetener
-
Directions:
• Add all “cream mix” ingredients to blender and blend until smooth
• Add “blueberry mix” to medium heat pot/pan and cook into jam
• Add half of cream mix to jar/container, followed by half blueberry mix. Repeat twice for two layers.
• using a fork/knife, swirl the blueberry mix to create an even flavour.
• Freeze for 3 hours and serve.
-
Notes:
• The higher fat content of cottage cheese you have, the less your mix will freeze solid after placing it in the freezer for longer than 3 hours. Even if it does, you just need to leave it out to thaw for a few minutes and mix it around before serving.
• You can use greek yogurt as a substitute for cottage cheese, but I recommend keeping it for the cheesecake flavour.
• You can experiment with all different kinds of frozen fruits. I also love using raspberries.
• Add your toppings of choice for an extra crunch!
-
Serving Size: 3
-
Calories/Macros (Per Serving):
Approx. 225 Calories
• 29g Protein
• 16g Carbs
• 4g Fat
-

Fresh coconut milk soaked rice gives this biryani it’s unique flavour. But using store bought coconut milk makes it equally yummy. I used 200 ml of store bought coconut milk and diluted it with water to make it 2 cups. This recipe is delicious and gets me lots of compliments.

Important Notes : Use the same cup/ glass you use to measure rice to measure coconut milk and water. Adjust water qty depending upon the type of rice you are using.

CHETTINADU  VEG BIRYANI :

Ingredients :
2 cups seeraga samba  rice or basmati rice
2 cups coconut milk 
2 bay leaves

Vegetables : 

1 onion ( thinly sliced)
1/4 cup fresh peas ( shelled)
5-6 beans ( cut into 1 “ pieces)
1 small carrot ( peeled and cut into  1 “ pieces)
1 small potato ( peeled and cut into 1” pieces) 
1/4 teaspoon turmeric powder
1/4 cup ghee

recipes.recipe_ingredients:
MARINADE
1/4 cup olive oil
1/4 cup plain whole milk yogurt
2 teaspoons paprika
2 teaspoons cumin
2 teaspoons salt
1/2 teaspoon onion powder
1 teaspoon ginger
1/2 teaspoon black pepper
1/2 teaspoon turmeric
2 to 3 teaspoons minced garlic, to taste
2 tablespoons parsley, finely chopped
2 tablespoons cilantro, finely chopped

FOR ASSEMBLY

1/4 cup black or green olives

recipes.recipe_method:
Preheat the oven to 400°F.
To make the marinade, combine olive oil, yogurt, paprika, cumin, salt, onion powder, ginger, black pepper, turmeric, minced garlic, parsley, and cilantro in a small bowl.
Add the chicken, potatoes, and lemon to a large baking dish.
Pour the marinade and toss the potatoes and chicken to evenly season it all. Also, make sure to get the marinade under the chicken skin for extra flavor.
Bake in the oven uncovered for 50 to 60 minutes until the chicken is fully cooked through to the center. To make the chicken extra golden and crispy, turn the oven to broil for 3 to 5 extra minutes.
Take out of the oven and add the olives and preserved lemons before serving!

recipes.title: Mango Sticky Rice
recipes.author: myhealthydish
recipes.text: save my mango and sticky rice recipe! i started with 2 cups short grain sweet rice, rinsed with cold water twice, then poured 2 1/2 cups cold water and cooked in my rice cooker. for the coconut sauce i used 1 can coconut milk, 1/4 of sugar and 1 tsp of salt. i simmered for 5 minutes. when the rice was done, i scooped out half the rice and saved the other half for later when i want to make more sauce. that way it doesn’t get too mushy the next day. i mix in half the sauce i made into the rice and the other half i make a slurry of 1/2 tbsp of corn starch and 2 tbsp water. reheat and stir until sauce thickens. this is also a good time to add a little more sugar if you want it sweeter. once cooled, pour thicken sauce on top, add mango and sprinkle with sesame seeds.

recipes.recipe_ingredients:
1–4 tsp red chili flakes (based on spice tolerance & heat of the flakes)

2 tbsp oil
2 tbsp soy sauce
1 tbsp black vinegar*, or rice vinegar*
2 tbsp peanut butter
Pinch of salt, to taste

recipes.recipe_method:
Bring a pot of water to boil. Once it comes to a boil, add the noodles and cook according to package instructions. Move onto next steps while the water comes to a boil.

Then, add the soy sauce, vinegar, peanut butter and salt to the bowl. Mix well with a. spoon and let it all chill out will the noodles cook.
Drain the cooked noodles, then pour the sauce over the noodles while they are still hot. If it’s too thick, add in 1-2 tbsp hot water to loosen it up. Toss to combine, garnish with some sesame seeds and/or green onions and enjoy!

recipes.text: dhaba style chicken curry - there's a reason this is one of the most popular recipes on the blog and the video was long overdue! everytime i make this recipe, i'm transported to the dhabas in raipur. heading there for diwali this year and i can't wait! oily, tangy, spicy with extra butter in the tadka - enjoy this with rotis, rice and sliced onions on the side. link to the full recipe in bio.
recipes.caption:
Dhaba Style Chicken Curry - there's a reason this is one of the most popular recipes on the blog and the video was long overdue!

Everytime I make this recipe, I'm transported to the dhabas in Raipur. Heading there for diwali this year and I can't wait!

Oily, tangy, spicy with extra butter in the tadka - enjoy this with rotis, rice and sliced onions on the side.

recipes.recipe_ingredients:
1 kg Chicken, skinless, bone-in whole chicken cut into medium sized pieces (referred to as curry cut in India)
For the marinade:
2 tablespoons Ginger Garlic Paste
1 Juice of lime
1 tablespoon Salt
For the curry:
1/4 cup Mustard Oil, see note 2
4 medium Red Onions
10 cloves Garlic
1½ inches Ginger
3 – 4 Green Chilies, use Serrano Peppers as replacement, adjust the spice as required
1 tablespoon Cumin Seeds
2 Bay leaves
½ Cinnamon stick, Stick
4 – 5 Cardamoms
8 – 10 Peppercorns
4 – 5 Cloves
4 medium Tomatoes, finely chopped
½ teaspoon Turmeric Powder
1 teaspoon Red Chili Powder, optional; adjust the spice as required
2 tablespoons Coriander Powder
1 teaspoon garam masala Powder
1 teaspoon meat masala
1 teaspoon Salt
1 1/4 cups water
For tempering:
1 tablespoon Ghee or Oil
1 tablespoon Butter
2 Green Chilies, slit lengthwise
½ inch Ginger, julienned
2 tablespoon Coriander, for garnishing
recipes.recipe_method:
Marinate the chicken pieces with ginger garlic paste, lime juice and salt. Cover and set aside while you prep everything else
Add onions, ginger, garlic and green chillies to a chopper and pulse to get a coarse mix.
Heat oil in a pressure cooker or a large heavy bottom pan. Add cumin seeds. Roughly pound all the whole spices (bay leaves, cinnamon, cardamom, peppercorns and cloves) and add to the oil.
once they start to splutter, add the onion mix. Cook the onion mix on a low flame, stirring occasionally till it is reduced to a golden brown mix and you see a thin layer of oil along the sides
Add tomatoes, salt, turmeric powder, red chili powder (if using) and coriander powder. Cook till the tomatoes start melting, and almost form a paste.
Add chicken and garam masala powder and roast for a minute or two till the chicken pieces turn pink and get coated with the masala. Add meat masala powder, 1 ¼ cups of water, mix well.
Pressure Cooker:
At this stage, if you are using a pressure cooker, place the lid and pressure cook on high till the first whistle goes off. Then reduce the flame to low and pressure cook for two more whistles and turn off the flame. If using a different kind of pressure cooker (without a whistle system), pressure cook on high for 15 minutes. Let the pressure release naturally.
Simmer for 5-10 mins on high flame, if required, to thicken the curry (chicken leaves a lot of water). I didn't need to do this.
Stovetop Method:
If you are using a heavy bottomed pan, bring the curry to a boil, reduce the heat, cover with a lid and let it cook on medium heat for 20-25 minutes. Uncover the pan, and cook for another 10-15 minutes till the curry starts to thicken. Once the curry is ready, switch off the flame.
Instant Pot Method:
If using an instant pot, place the lid and change the vent to sealing. Pressure cook on high for 8 minutes. Release pressure manually. Simmer the curry for a few minutes to achieve the desired thickness if there is too much water.
Tempering:
In another small pan, heat ghee and butter and add green chilies and ginger. Once they start to splutter, switch off the flame and mix the tadka (or tempering) into the curry. Top with coriander.
Let the curry sit for 10-15 minutes before serving. Tastes best with rotis or rice.

recipes.title: Jammy Eggs with Chili Butter
recipes.author: lindseyeats
recipes.text: let’s make: jammy eggs with chili butter & garlic yogurt! this recipe is inspired by the popular turkish eggs recipe, also know as cilbir.⁠ ⁠ this starts off with jammy eggs, a homemade chili butter (made with aleppo pepper and chili flakes!) and plain skyr. it’s served with toasted, crusty bread for the ultimate breakfast meal. ⁠ ⁠ full recipe here: https://lindseyeatsla.com/jammy-eggs-with-chili-butter-and-garlic-yogurt/⁠ ⁠
recipes.caption:
Let’s make: jammy eggs with chili butter & garlic yogurt! This recipe is inspired by the popular Turkish eggs recipe, also know as Cilbir.⁠
⁠
This starts off with jammy eggs, a homemade chili butter (made with Aleppo pepper and chili flakes!) and @icelandicprovisions plain skyr. It’s served with toasted, crusty bread for the ultimate breakfast meal. ⁠
⁠
Full recipe here: https://lindseyeatsla.com/jammy-eggs-with-chili-butter-and-garlic-yogurt/⁠
⁠
#icelandicprovisionspartner #icelandicprovisions #skyr #turkisheggs
recipes.recipe_ingredients:
1/4 cup unsalted butter
1/2 teaspoon chili flakes
1 teaspoon Aleppo pepper
1/2 tablespoon extra-virgin olive oil
2 5.3 ounce containers of yogurt or Skyr
zest and juice of 1/2 lemon
1 large garlic clove, grated
salt and pepper to taste
4 large eggs
top with chopped parsley
serve with toasted bread of your choice
recipes.recipe_method:
Make your chili butter. In a saucepan or skillet melt butter on medium-low with your olive oil.
When it is shimmering and melted, add in chili flakes and Aleppo pepper. It will bubble a bit and that’s okay! It will simmer down when you turn off the heat. Let everything cook together, brown and infuse. Mix well on low and allow it to infuse for a few minutes. Remove from heat and set aside.
Begin by making your yogurt mixture. In a bowl, mix yogurt or skyr, lemon juice, lemon zest, salt, pepper and fresh garlic. You can also choose to go the extra step to double whip in a food processor or immersion blender. Mix well and set aside.
Next, make your jammy eggs. Bring a pot to a boil, and add in your eggs gently. Set a timer for 6 1/2 minutes. Drain and rinse with cold water, or in an ice bath. Peel.
Time to assemble! On a bowl or platter, layer on your yogurt mixture. Then cut your eggs in half and add them on the plate. Finish off with your chili butter and chopped parsley. Serve with toasted bread!

recipes.title: Weekly Salsa
recipes.author: shey.cooks
recipes.text: my weekly salsa recipe 😚 i always have a big batch of this salsa in my fridge! it’s so easy it make and lasts for about a week and a half if you don’t finish it before then 😂 ingredients: 3-4 cups of cherry tomatoes 1 serrano pepper 1 garlic clove 1 cup of diced green onions 1/2 cup of diced sweet onions 1/3 cup of finely chopped cilantro (for blended) 1/3 cup of finely chopped cilantro (to be mixed in at the end) 1 teaspoon of cumin and pink himalayan salt 1/4 teaspoon of white sugar and red chilli powder (laal murchoo) 1/2 - 1 tablespoon of fresh lemon or lime juice 1. in a food processor, pulse the cherry tomatoes until it is a bit chunky and not too smooth, where it is a watery consistency. 2. ten pour into a separate bowl. in the same food processor add in cilantro, garlic, a serrano pepper and 1/3 cup of the blended tomatoes and blend until smooth. 3. add this back into the blended tomatoes. add in the chopped green onions, sweet white onions and cilantro. last add in the salt, cumin, sugar, red chilli powder and lemon juice and mix up everything until smooth. then enjoy ! . . .

recipes.title: Peanut-Miso Chickpea Salad
recipes.author: lahbco
recipes.text: peanut-miso chickpea salad 😋a plant-based sandwich i don’t think you can get sick of with school starting, folks going back into the office, and my own personal laziness in the kitchen- this chickpea salad is literally perfect for any meal prep day 🤍☁️ peanut butter and miso might be a match made in heaven, but their friends (cinnamon, cayenne, and cumin) make the relationship 10x better 😍 📲the full recipe is linked in my bio or at https://www.lahbco.com/dinner/peanutmisochickpeasalad?rq=chickpea

Peanut-Miso Chickpea Salad 😋a plant-based sandwich I don’t think you can get sick of

recipes.recipe_ingredients:
1 (15 oz) can of chickpeas, rinsed
1/4 cup peanut butter
2 tablespoon red miso paste
2 tablespoons rice vinegar
2 tablespoons maple syrup or mirin
1 teaspoon ginger powder
1 teaspoon garlic powder
1/2 teaspoon cinnamon
1/2 teaspoon cumin
1/2 teaspoon sannam chili (or chili powder)
water, to thin
1/4 cup red onion, diced
1/4 cup chopped cilantro
recipes.recipe_method:
Begin by dicing and chopping your red onion and cilantro, respectively. Set aside.
In a bowl, add your rinsed chickpeas. Using a potato masher, or fork, mash the chickpeas to the consistency of your choice. I prefer to have an even blend of mashed to partially broken chickpeas.
In a separate bowl, add the peanut butter, miso, rice vinegar, maple syrup, and spices. Mix until emulsified/combined. Taste and adjust seasonings per your preference. You may need to add water to thin if the peanut butter thickened while mixing.
Add the peanut butter-miso mixture to the mashed chickpeas. Stir to combine.
Add the red onion and cilantro. Stir until combined.
Chill for 1 hour or eat at room temperature. Some favorite ways I like to eat this salad below:
In a sandwich with toasted sourdough, leafy lettuce, tomatoes, and sriracha
In a cabbage wrap (using a whole leaf of red/green cabbage, add the salad and some scallions and sesame seeds. Roll and devour
On top of a kale salad.
Dive in!

recipes.caption:
ib: the labrador puppies i met all named after cheeses 🥺

I didn't grow up eating a lot of eggs bc my dad's allergic, so when my mom did make anda masala (a more punjabi-style one than my fusion one here), it was a treat 🍭 

Coconut Jammy Anda Masala
// INGREDIENTS //
- 1/2 tbsp coconut oil
- 1/2 tsp cumin seeds
- 1/2 tsp fennel seeds
- 4 cloves
- 10 kadi patta (also called curry leaves or sweet neem leaves)
- 5 garlic cloves, minced
- 3/4 inch ginger, grated
- 3 birds eye green chilies, finely chopped (+/-)
- 1 small onion, finely chopped
- 3 tbsp tomato paste
- 1 large tomato, finely diced
- 1/2 tsp turmeric
- 2 tsp coriander powder
- 1 to 2 tsp kashmiri red chili (+/-)
- 1/2 tsp black pepper
- Salt to taste
- 2 cups full fat coconut milk
- 1/2 tsp garam masala
- Handful of kasuri methi (dried fenugreek leaves), crushed between palms
- 4 pasture raised eggs

// RECIPE //
1️⃣ Heat up coconut oil, then add cumin, fennel, & cloves. Once they start wiggling around, quickly & carefully add kadi patta (there will be spluttering so don't stand too close!) Toast around for 30 sec.
2️⃣ Add garlic, ginger, chilies, and onion. Sauté until onions are a bit translucent.
3️⃣ Add tomato paste & cook for 3-4min to caramelize - the color will go from bright red to deep dull red.
4️⃣ Add tomatoes, turmeric, coriander, red chili powder, black pep, & salt. Cook until tomatoes are mushy.
5️⃣ Add coconut milk, mix well, & raise the heat if needed to maintain a slight simmer. Simmer for 3-4min.
6️⃣ Add garam masala, kasuri methi, & mix well for a minute. Taste for salt then turn off heat.
7️⃣ Add the eight halves of your eggs. Garnish with a sprinkle of crushed kasuri methi.

Jammy Eggs:
1️⃣ Bring a saucepan with enough water to cover the eggs to a vigorous boil.
2️⃣ Using a slotted spoon, lower in your eggs.
3️⃣ Immediately start a timer for 6min 30 sec (I personally prefer 6.5min than exactly 6min eggs, but you can try both!). Maintain a boil. 
4️⃣ Remove the eggs and dunk them in the ice bath. Let them sit for 5min then peel & enjoy!

recipes.author: pierceabernathy

recipes.caption:
Please make dried shiitake mushrooms a pantry staple. They are far less expensive and much more flavorful than most fresh shiitakes you can find. Not only can you use them after they are rehydrated but the liquid you rehydrate them in can turn into a very flavorful mushroom broth.

Ingredients: 
1 cup dried white beans, soaked overnight
1 oz dried shiitake mushrooms
6 cups water 
2 cloves garlic
1/2 small white onion 
1 1/2 tsp salt
2 tbsp olive oil 
2 tsp gochugaru or other chili pepper flakes
1 tbsp Chinese black vinegar
1 tbsp rice wine vinegar 
1 tsp sesame oil 

Cripsy shiitakes//
1/4 cup of sliced fresh shiitake mushrooms
2 tsp cornstarch
High heat oil for frying
Salt to taste

Finely chopped chives to garnish
Sesame oil to garnish
Sesame seeds to garnish

Preparation:
1. Add the dried mushrooms, soaked beans, onion, garlic, salt, and olive oil to a large pot. Cover with 6 cups water and bring to a boil. Reduce to a simmer and cook until beans are extremely tender, about 45 minutes - 1 hour. Use a slotted spoon or fine mesh skimmer to transfer the beans, mushrooms, onion, and garlic into a heat proof bowl. Return the pot to the stove with the liquid and reduce on medium-high heat until roughly 1/4 cup remains. Transfer to a heat proof bowl and set aside. 
2. Add the black vinegar, rice wine vinegar, gochugaru, sesame oil, and 2 tbsp of the reduced mushroom/bean liquid to the bowl of mushrooms and beans and stir to combine. Transfer to a food processor and process until smooth. 
3. For the fresh shiitakes, place a sieve or colander over a bowl and add the fresh mushrooms and cornstarch. Tap the sieve or colander to shake off any excess cornstarch from the mushrooms. Transfer to a generously oiled medium sized pan on medium heat and fry mushrooms on both sides until lightly browned and crisp, about 3-5 minutes. Place on a paper towel and season with salt immediately. 
4. Garnish dip with crispy mushrooms, chives, sesame oil, and sesame seeds.
